title: Base CI: platform-cli service test times out on the GitHub runner
description: First Release run on crab-shack/platform main failed in the Test step: packages/platform-cli/src/service.test.ts > 'installs, routes the everyday commands through systemctl, and uninstalls' hit vitest's default 5000ms test timeout (src/service.test.ts:113). The test boots the stand-in daemon and web servers from test-fixtures several times in one test (install-service, stop, start, restart, uninstall-service), each start allowed up to 10s, so the default 5s budget is too tight on a slow runner even though it passes locally. Fix in the base: give process-spawning tests in platform-cli an explicit, generous timeout (per test or testTimeout in the package's vitest config, e.g. 60s) sized to the internal start/stop timeouts, check the other describe blocks in that file and any other test spawning the fixtures for the same exposure, and make sure the failure message when a start genuinely fails still points at the cause. Run the platform-cli tests and pnpm lint in the base. Commit on main; do not push. Acceptance: the test declares a timeout that covers its worst-case internal waits; platform-cli tests pass locally; the next Release run on GitHub passes the Test step (Jack pushes and confirms).
notes: Fix committed on main in crab-shack/platform (not pushed): SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS=60s per-test timeout on the 4 process-spawning tests (service.test.ts x2, lifecycle.test.ts x2). GitHub verification pending Jack's push and next Release run.
close_reason: Verified by Jack: platform-cli and cap-template timeouts fixed (base commits 6d24445, 83556b4), Release run on GitHub passes the Test step.

title: Choose the base's product name, npm scope, repository name and GitHub owner
description:
Four names are needed before the platform can leave this repository, and they are Jack's to choose, not an agent's: the base's product name (the name of the platform itself, used as the repository's title, in its README and as the placeholder product name of its development distribution unless a different placeholder is chosen), its npm scope (the @scope every published platform package is named under, replacing @candy-mountain for platform-daemon, platform-web, platform-sdk, platform-config and platform-cli), the base repository's name, and the GitHub owner (the company organisation, since the registry is GitHub Packages under it and packages are private to that organisation). Candy Mountain's own packages keep @candy-mountain.

What to do: decide the four names and record them in this bead's notes, one per line, as product name, npm scope, repository name, GitHub owner. If the development distribution's placeholder product name should differ from the platform's name, record that too. Then close this bead; every phase-1 bead reads the notes before starting and is blocked until it is closed.

Acceptance: the notes carry all four names, the repository does not yet need to exist.
notes:
Decided by Jack 2026-11-09.
product name: platform
npm scope: @crab-shack (GitHub Packages requires the npm scope to equal the owner, so this is fixed, not a choice)
repository name: platform (crab-shack/platform; inferred from the product name, Jack did not name the repo separately)
GitHub owner: crab-shack (organisation created by Jack for this)
development distribution placeholder product name: platform (default, no different placeholder chosen)

Context: Candy Mountain stays on Jack's personal account (kingrea), not under crab-shack. Consequence for phase 2: Candy Mountain's CI cannot use GITHUB_TOKEN to read crab-shack packages; it needs a PAT with read:packages from a crab-shack member stored as a secret, and the same token locally in .npmrc. The base's package.json repository fields must point at crab-shack/platform so published packages attach to that repo.
Phase 4 product repo already exists: crab-shack/test-dashboard-home.
close_reason: Names decided and recorded in notes

title: Phase 5: SDK test kit and template capability
description:
Capability: a new capability can be written, tested and run against the platform from its own package alone, following a template that is itself a working capability in the repo. Covers moving what a capability's tests need into a documented test entry point (a platform started with only the platform packages and the capability under test, an actor at a chosen rung, a workspace with chosen facts, a plugin instance with fake secrets, a way to mount a layer page inside the gate), a deliberately small template capability (packages/cap-template, id template) exercising every contribution point and included in the Candy Mountain distribution only in development, the template README as the capability author's guide, and a daemon conventions document in packages/platform-daemon matching the web one in packages/platform-web/README.md. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/phase-5-sdk-test-kit-and-template.md. Decomposed 2026-11-08 into ncj.5.1 to ncj.5.9: the two test-kit entries (5.1 daemon, 5.2 web), the daemon conventions document (5.3) and the template scaffold (5.4) have no dependencies; the scaffold enters the daemon distribution at once because the workspace-wide capability package test refuses an unlisted cap-* package, and 5.8 makes it development-only afterwards.

Human test: copy the template capability to a new package name, change its id and label, add it to both apps, and confirm it appears in the sidebar under a module, its page renders behind the gate, its table exists, its event appears in the activity feed and its card on the overview. Run the new package's tests on their own with the test kit and confirm they pass without the apps present. Remove it and confirm the pipeline is green.

title: Phase 4: Packages and distributions
description:
Capability: the repo is a set of platform packages (packages/platform-daemon, packages/platform-web as a Nuxt layer, packages/platform-sdk, packages/platform-config, packages/platform-cli), a set of capability packages (one packages/cap-<id> per product capability with a daemon entry and a web entry), a plain-data packages/candy-mountain product package, and two thin apps that assemble them from the product configuration. A capability can be deleted by removing its package and one line from each app. Boundary lint moves from directory ownership to package ownership on both the web and the daemon side. Turborepo runs the build, test, lint and typecheck graph with caching. Nothing is published: every package stays private with workspace:* dependencies. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/phase-4-packages-and-distributions.md. Depends on phases 1, 2 and 3. Decomposed 2026-11-03 into ncj.4.1 to ncj.4.20; the import rules every bead obeys are in each bead's phase 4 paragraph: a capability imports the SDK and the platform-daemon root entry only, another capability only through its root entry and only when dependsOn and package.json both declare it.

Human test: run lint, typecheck, test and build through Turborepo from the root and confirm they pass and a second run is served from cache. Start both apps and repeat the v3 plan's human tests for issues, chat, bots and uptime. Delete the uptime capability package and its line from each app, run the full pipeline, start the apps and confirm Operations shows only deployments. Restore it. Add a direct import from a capability package into a platform package's internal file and confirm lint fails naming the rule.
close_reason: Phase 4 landed: packages, thin apps, Turborepo and package-boundary lint are in place; all 20 children closed 2026-11-03.

title: Phase 2: Data ownership
description:
Capability: the platform owns the workspace; each capability owns its own tables, migrations, workspace facts and activity event types; and a capability removed from the product leaves no routes, no services and no schema behind on a fresh database. Covers splitting the project table into a platform workspace plus product repository data (owned by a new service-only repository capability), renaming the platform's tables, columns, API prefix and wire types to workspace, per-capability Drizzle schema sets and migration folders applied at boot in dependency order each under its own migrations table, carrying Jack's existing database across, and facts, activity event types and notification kinds declared by the capability that provides them. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/phase-2-data-ownership.md. Depends on phase 1. Decomposed 2026-11-03 into ncj.2.1 to ncj.2.9; run ncj.2.3 (the workspace rename) alone because it touches most files in both apps.

Human test: delete the local database, start the daemon, and confirm every migration set applies in order and the boot log names each package's count. Create a project, enable modules, add a bot, run a monitor, and confirm the overview shows the same facts as before. Delete the project and confirm its bot, monitors, environments, plugin instances and activity are gone. Start from the pre-phase database copy and confirm the daemon carries it across without data loss. Remove the uptime capability from the product list, delete the database, start, and confirm no uptime table exists.
close_reason: Phase 2 landed: all nine children closed 2026-11-03.

title: Phase 3: Web shell seam
description:
Capability: the web shell is product-agnostic. It reads the product's name, colours and scope label from configuration, fills its extension points from the layers it is given, and builds with any subset of capability layers. Covers product configuration in the shell, turning the three places core knows a capability or plugin type (plugin panels and forms, the chat layer's family-specific pieces, the overview's cards) into contribution points, and an explicit layer list for distributions. The chat layer stays where it is (it moves with the shell in phase 4); this phase only makes sure nothing product-specific is left inside it. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/phase-3-web-shell-seam.md. Runs alongside phase 1.

Human test: build and run the web app and walk every page: picker, projects, modules and plugins setup including the Claude Code login panel and the Repository panel, grants, settings, the overview, a chat with a Claude Code session showing model and effort controls, and a bot session showing its worktree. Change the product name and scope label in configuration and confirm the header, picker, setup pages and gate copy all follow. Remove the uptime layer directory, run lint, typecheck and build, and confirm they pass and the app runs without it.
close_reason: All eleven phase-3 tasks closed with green gates.

title: Phase 1: Daemon registration seam
description:
Capability: the daemon starts from a list of capability definitions and a product configuration, and removing an entry from the list removes that capability's routes and services without touching anything else. Covers the runtime half of a capability (manifest plus routes, services with start and close, plugin types, MCP servers, chat families, workspace deletion hooks and dependencies), open id universes instead of closed unions in the shared package, and one product configuration object. Code does not move between packages in this phase; only the wiring changes. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/phase-1-daemon-seam.md.

Human test: start the daemon and confirm the boot log lists the same capabilities, modules and plugin types as before, every page of the web app still works, and a bot run from Slack still completes. Remove the uptime capability from the product's list and restart: the daemon boots, the uptime routes return not found, the sidebar has no Uptime entry, the Modules setup page shows the Operations module without uptime, and nothing else changed. Put it back. Add a capability definition whose manifest references a plugin type the product does not include and confirm the daemon refuses to start with a message naming both.
close_reason: All phase-1 tasks (1.1-1.19) closed with green gates; daemon boots from the product configuration and a definition list, platform start and app factory import no capability (guarded by seam.test.ts).

title: Platform extraction
description:
Candy Mountain v3 becomes the first product built on a reusable platform base without leaving its repository. At the end the repo has a clear line between platform (daemon core, web shell, SDK) and product (Candy Mountain's capabilities and plugin types): every capability is a workspace package that reaches the platform only through the SDK, and the two apps are thin distributions that list what they include. Nothing is published; the follow-on plan in .ai-docs/plans/platform-package/ moves the platform into its own repository.

Why now: the same shell (auth, secrets, plugins, capabilities, modules, grants, chat, layers) has been built three times (Digital Hub, Candy Mountain v2, v3) and the digital hub and a home dashboard are next. Extracting the base from the most complete implementation while it still builds and runs is cheaper than designing a base in an empty repo.

Hard requirements from Jack: extraction happens inside this repo first; Turborepo on top of the pnpm workspace; capabilities become unpublished workspace packages; working platform pieces move as they are with no redesign; the scope entity stays in the data model for every product; Candy Mountain keeps working at the end of every phase (lint, typecheck, test, build green and the v3 plan's human tests still pass); the layer boundary rules stay, re-pointed at the package boundary.

Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/overview.md and phase-1..5. Each phase is a child epic. Phases 1 and 3 touch different apps and run alongside each other; phase 2 needs 1; phase 4 needs 1, 2 and 3; phase 5 needs 4. Per the plan, phases 2, 4 and 5 are decomposed into tasks only once phases 1 and 3 have landed.

title: Phase 10: Platform extras
description: Capability: the platform talks back. The Overview feed gets filters and a cross-project view, Slack notifications fire on bot finish, incidents and deploys, and a native platform chat agent (Digital Hub's Hub agent, as the first Mastra agent) can navigate the app. Jack adds the LLM gateway key and model when he reaches this phase; until then the agent is declared but hidden. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-10-platform-extras.md. title: Phase 9: Operations: deployments (firm parts)
description: Capability: per project, see what is live per environment, and (later) deploy a branch through the project's vendor. This phase is deliberately open; only the firm parts are decomposed here: the Netlify and Heroku plugin types, the common live-version shape with vendor and custom-endpoint sources, and the Deployments page showing them. The deploy zone (per-environment deploy strategies for Netlify build hooks, Heroku pushes, GitHub Actions dispatch, Bitbucket pipelines, and record-only) is NOT decomposed; Jack will refine it when he reaches it, and it must write a `deploy.attempted` activity event per attempt. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-9-operations-deployments.md. Human test: Netlify configured shows the current deploy's commit and branch; a second environment from the project's own version endpoint renders the same fields.

description: Capability: per project, register things to ping, see their state and history, and get incidents when they go down. Monitors are rows, not a JSON file; the poller survives restarts without duplicates; state uses Digital Hub's hysteresis so blips do not flap. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/phase-8-operations-uptime.md. Research: .ai-docs/research/digital-hub.md section 6. title: Add the Add Issue chooser and the write-it-yourself form
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Creating an issue from the UI replaces a `bd create` incantation. The Add Issue button opens a chooser with three options: "Create with Claude Code", "Create with Codex" and "Write yourself". The first two appear only when the registry reports the matching chat capability (`chat-claude-code` or `chat-codex`) ready for the project; they are wired to a chat thread by separate work, so for now they must be rendered through one clearly-marked integration point that does nothing but is easy to connect. "Write yourself" opens a form: title, type, priority, optional labels, parent (pick from existing issues with search), description, acceptance criteria, and depends-on (pick several). Done creates the issue through the daemon and navigates to its page.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Creating an issue with a parent and two dependencies from the form is confirmed by `bd show` showing both; the page navigates to the new issue; the agent options are absent on a project with no agent plugin.
notes:
Add Issue chooser + write-it-yourself form decisions (5.2 wires the agent options; 3.6 rebuilds the list page).

FILES (apps/web/layers/issues/)
- app/components/AddButton.vue -> IssuesAddButton: no props. Renders nothing unless the registry's issues capability carries tool 'issues.write' (issuesCanWrite) and a project slug is selected. 'Add issue' button (data-testid issue-add) + one UModal with a step ref 'choose' | 'write' (reset to 'choose' on every open). On created: closes, one warning toast per response warning ('Dependency not added', description = the daemon's '<id>: <bd reason>'), a success toast 'Created <id>', then navigateTo(issuesPagePath(slug, issue.id)).
- app/components/AddChooser.vue -> IssuesAddChooser: props agentOptions: IssuesAgentCreateOption[]; emits agent(option), write. Agent buttons first (data-testid issue-add-<agentId>), then 'Write yourself' (issue-add-write).
- app/components/CreateForm.vue -> IssuesCreateForm: props slug; emits created(CreateIssueResponse), back. Loads useIssuesApi().list(slug) on mount (only mounted on the write step) for the pickers; submit = useIssuesApi().create(slug, issuesCreateRequest(data)); daemon errors show as a UAlert (message + code) at the top (data-testid issue-create-error). Buttons Back / Done at the bottom of the body.
- app/composables/useIssuesCreateWithAgent.ts -> useIssuesCreateWithAgent() { options: ComputedRef<IssuesAgentCreateOption[]>, start(option) }.
- app/utils/issue-create.ts: IssuesAgentCreateOption { capabilityId, agentId, family, label, icon }; issuesAgentCreateOptions(registry); issuesCanWrite(registry); ISSUES_PRIORITY_ITEMS; issuesPickerItems(issues) -> { label: title, value: id, description: id } minus closed issues, numeric-aware id order; IssuesCreateFormData; issuesCreateRequest(data).
- test/unit/issue-create.test.ts (6 tests).
- Mount: pages/p/[project]/issues/index.vue navbar #right slot holds the single line <IssuesAddButton />. 3.6: keep that line in the navbar right slot when rebuilding the page.

AGENT INTEGRATION POINT (for 5.2): useIssuesCreateWithAgent().start(option) is the ONLY place to change. Today it shows an info toast '<label> is coming soon'; the button already closes the modal before calling it. option carries agentId ('claude-code' | 'codex', the registry agent id that POST /projects/:slug/threads takes), family and capabilityId. 5.2: replace the body with POST threads { agentId: option.agentId } -> POST threads/:id/prompt { text: drafting prompt } -> navigate/deep-link to the thread (via the chat layer's API). Option visibility: issuesAgentCreateOptions shows an agent only when registry.capabilities has its chat capability (chat-claude-code / chat-codex) with ready === true AND chat === true (rung allows chat); fixed labels 'Create with Claude Code' (i-lucide-sparkles), 'Create with Codex' (i-lucide-square-terminal).

FORM SCHEMA (zod, UForm): title trim 1..ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH (required); type z.enum(KNOWN_ISSUE_TYPES), default 'task' (USelect); priority int 0..4, default 2 (USelect 'P0 · Critical'..'P4 · Backlog'); labels string[] (UInputTags, add-on-blur/add-on-paste, comma is the delimiter so labels can never contain commas); parentId string|null (USelectMenu, clear, virtualize, search over title + id via filter-fields ['label','value']); description and acceptanceCriteria strings <= ISSUE_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH (UTextarea autoresize); dependsOn string[] (USelectMenu multiple, same items). issuesCreateRequest trims title/text, drops empty text, de-dups labels and dependsOn, omits empty labels/parent/dependsOn; always sends type and priority.

VERIFIED: tsx daemon :7441 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, development auth) + built web .output copied to scratch :7440; temp bd workspace (bd init, prefix xt) registered as project 'tmp', modules issues + agent-hub, no agent plugins. Headless Chromium 16/16: Add issue on the list page; chooser shows only 'Write yourself' (no Claude Code / Codex options); empty title refused inline; labels via comma, Enter and blur; parent search 'Epic' narrows to 1; depends-on search by title and by id; Done -> URL /p/tmp/issues/xt-p0r.4 + 'Created' toast; 390px no overflow; Back returns to chooser; no console errors. bd show xt-p0r.4: PARENT xt-p0r, DEPENDS ON xt-st2 + xt-haw, labels api/blurred/ui, type feature, P1, description + acceptance. After inserting a healthy claude-code plugin_instances row: Claude Code option present, Codex absent, click -> 'coming soon' toast and modal closes. Epic depending on a task -> issue created, navigates, warning toast 'xt-st2: epics can only block other epics, not tasks'. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (98 files, 930 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass.
UX NOTE: UForm validates on blur, so clicking Back with an untouched title first shows 'Title is required' and shifts the Back button (a real click can miss it once).

title: Add a read-only dependency graph view for an epic
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Blocking relationships among an epic's children are hard to see in a list. Add a dependency view reachable from an epic's detail: a plain graph of the epic's descendant issues as nodes with their blocking edges, using the dependency data the layer already fetches. Nodes show short id and title and are coloured by status; clicking a node opens that issue. Keep it read-only and simple; a basic layered layout is enough. No editing of edges.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the view for a real epic shows its children and blocking edges; clicking a node opens the issue; an epic with no dependencies shows nodes without edges.
notes:
Epic dependency graph decisions.

FILES (apps/web/layers/issues): app/utils/issues-dependency-graph.ts, app/components/DependencyGraph.vue (IssuesDependencyGraph), test/unit/issues-dependency-graph.test.ts (10 tests), and a small edit to app/pages/p/[project]/issues/[id].vue. No new dependency (no dagre).

UTIL issuesDependencyGraph(epicId, issues, edges) -> IssuesDependencyGraphLayout { nodes: { issue, layer, x, y }[], edges: { from (blocker), to (blocked), path (SVG cubic d), back }[], width, height }. Nodes = every descendant of the epic via issuesParentId (BFS with seen set, so nested epics and their issues are included, the epic itself is not, parent cycles are safe), ordered with issuesSortSiblings. Edges = type 'blocks' with both ends inside, deduped, no self-loops. Layout: longest-path layering (blockers left, blocked right; DFS with a visiting set drops the edge that closes a blocking cycle, that edge is marked back and drawn dashed), columns centred vertically, one barycentre pass ordering each column by its blockers' y. Constants ISSUES_GRAPH_NODE_WIDTH 220 / NODE_HEIGHT 52 / COLUMN_GAP 56 / ROW_GAP 16 / PADDING 8. issuesGraphLabel(title, max) ellipsises. Type named ...Layout to avoid clashing with the component name.

COMPONENT IssuesDependencyGraph props slug, epicId, optional onOpenIssue(id). Data = useIssuesList(slug) (the list already carries every issue's dependencies, so no call to the /dependencies endpoint and no 200-id limit); useIssuesEvents refreshes it. Inline SVG: arrowhead marker, node = SVG <a href=issuesPagePath> with aria-label 'id: title (Status)' + <title>, short id (issuesShortId), status label, truncated title (struck when closed); colours from issuesStatusMeta via var(--ui-<colour>) (neutral -> --ui-text-dimmed, since Nuxt UI has no --ui-neutral). Plain left click / Enter -> onOpenIssue or navigateTo; modifier clicks keep the real href. Summary line 'N issues, M blocking edges' / 'no blocking dependencies between them' + status legend; scrollable bordered canvas. States: list error (issue-graph-error), skeleton, no descendants -> UEmpty 'No child issues' (issue-graph-empty). testids issue-graph, -summary, -canvas, -node (data-id), -edge (data-from/data-to).

title: Make issue fields editable in place from the detail view
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

v2's detail could not edit title, description, priority or type, which sent Jack back to the terminal. In the detail component make these editable in place, writing through the daemon's issue update endpoint: title (click to edit), description, acceptance criteria and notes (markdown editor toggled from the rendered view), type and priority (selects), labels (add and remove chips), parent (pick from existing issues with search), and assignee (the project assignee picker). Show saving and error states; on success refetch the issue. Status changes are handled by the bulk bar and a close action here with an optional reason.
acceptance_criteria: Editing title, priority and description from the UI is confirmed by `bd show`; a failed write shows an error and keeps the old value; the parent picker searches existing issues.
notes:
In-place issue editing decisions (3.9 slide-out, 3.13 bulk bar, 5.1 build on these).

FILES (apps/web/layers/issues/app): components/Detail.vue (IssuesDetail, editing added in place; props/slots run+comments/loaded/refresh unchanged), components/DetailTextSection.vue (IssuesDetailTextSection: rendered markdown <-> UTextarea editor with Save/Cancel, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter saves; props title, source, editable, saving, error, save(value)=>Promise<boolean>, emits cancel), components/ParentPicker.vue (IssuesParentPicker: USelectMenu v-model string|null, props slug, issueId? (excluded with all its descendants), placeholder, disabled, loading, defaultOpen; loads useIssuesApi().list on mount, closed issues left out, search over title+id, clear = null; CreateForm's parent field now uses it), composables/useIssuesEdit.ts, utils/issues-edit.ts, test/unit/issues-edit.test.ts (14 tests).

COMPOSABLE useIssuesEdit(slug, issueId, { onSaved(issue) }) -> { saving, failure, isSaving(target), errorFor(target), clearError(target?), save(field, current, draft) => Promise<boolean>, close(reason, force?) => Promise<boolean> }. Targets = editable field names + 'close'. One failure slot (the latest failure wins). save() diffs via issuesEditChanges; nothing changed -> true with no request; client validation (issuesEditProblem: empty/long title, long text, comma labels) -> failure code invalid_request without a request. Detail's onSaved sets data to the returned issue then calls refresh().

PURE HELPERS (utils/issues-edit.ts): issuesEditChanges(current, draft) -> UpdateIssueRequest with ONLY changed fields: title trimmed; description/acceptanceCriteria/notes trimEnd (leading indentation kept), blank -> null; labels trimmed/deduped, compared as a set, sent as the full array ([] clears); parentId/assignee blank -> null (null parent detaches, null assignee unassigns); type/priority as-is. issuesLabelsAdd/Remove/Equal, issuesLabelProblem, issuesEditProblem, issuesParentCandidates(issues, id), issuesTypeItems(current) (custom tracker types stay selectable), ISSUES_EDIT_FIELD_LABELS.

FIELD -> PATCH /projects/:slug/issues/:id: title (click h1 -> UInput, Enter saves, Esc cancels) {title}; description/acceptance/notes (all three sections shown when editable, 'Nothing yet.' when empty) {description|acceptanceCriteria|notes}; type/priority USelects in the badge row {type}/{priority}; labels: x on each chip + '+ Label' popover {labels: full set}; parent: pencil -> IssuesParentPicker (opens immediately) {parentId}, clear -> {parentId:null}; assignee: IssuesAssigneePicker {assignee} (null unassigns). Close: 'Close' popover with optional reason -> POST .../close {reason}; on a tracker_failed refusal it shows bd's message plus 'Close anyway' (force:true). No reopen/status edit here (bulk bar owns status).

ERRORS: no optimistic update. Displayed values come from the loaded issue; while a select/picker write is in flight its value comes from an inFlight draft that is dropped in finally, so a failure snaps back to the old value. Title/text editors stay open with the draft. Header fields show one closable UAlert (data-testid issue-edit-error, 'Couldn't save the <field>' + bd's message); text sections show their own alert; close errors show in the popover (issue-close-error).

HYDRATION: editable values derive from the loaded issue (computed / shown(field)), never from refs synced by a watcher (watchers do not run during SSR -> SSR showed default P2/Unassigned). Verified no 'Hydration completed but contains mismatches' on issues with non-default priority/assignee, admin and reader.

WRITE GATE: canEdit = issuesCanWrite(useProjectRegistry().registry) (issues capability carries tool issues.write). Read rung -> the old read-only display (badges, plain title, empty sections hidden, no close/label/parent/assignee controls). Daemon also refuses (403 not_granted).

TEST IDS: issue-title (h1, button inside when editable), issue-title-input/-save, issue-type/-priority (USelect when editable, badge otherwise), issue-label-add/-input/-remove, issue-assignee-picker, issue-parent-edit/-picker, issue-section-edit/-input/-save inside issue-description/-acceptance/-notes, issue-close/-close-reason-input/-close-submit/-close-error/-close-force, issue-edit-error.

VERIFIED: temp bd workspace (prefix xe) as project et with issues enabled, tsx daemon :8201 (password auth, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR) + built web :8200; reader user with a read-rung issues grant. Headless Chromium 30/30 edit (title, priority, type, description, acceptance via Ctrl+Enter, labels add/remove + comma refused, parent search by title narrows to 1 and by id, self excluded, assignee new name; bd show confirms all; empty title refused, old kept; close refused by bd with its message, then Close anyway with reason; 390px no overflow), detach 2/2 (PATCH {parentId:null}, bd shows no parent), write failure 8/8 (bd store made read-only -> 502 tracker_failed: error shown with bd's message, title/description drafts kept, priority select back to P1, bd unchanged, retry after recovery saves), reader 8/8, hydration 6/6. Stopping the daemon instead shows the app-wide 'Can't reach the daemon' screen (core behaviour), which unmounts the editors. Root lint, typecheck, test (118 files, 1124 passed), build pass.
close_reason: In-place editing of every field via PATCH, write gate, hydration fix; browser-verified 48 checks

notes: Issue detail decisions (3.9/3.11/3.12/3.15/5.1 build on these). FILES (apps/web/layers/issues): app/components/Detail.vue (IssuesDetail), app/components/DetailMarkdown.vue (IssuesDetailMarkdown), app/utils/issues-markdown.ts, app/utils/issues-display.ts, page app/pages/p/[project]/issues/[id].vue, tests test/unit/issues-markdown.test.ts (+ test/fixtures/hostile-markdown.md) and test/unit/issues-display.test.ts. apps/web/package.json gained marked ^17.0.6 (same copy @nuxt/ui's tiptap already pulls in; no new lockfile package). title: Add the slide-out with a back stack and wire row clicks to it
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Clicking a row should not leave the list. Add a right-hand slide-out hosting the detail component, opened by the list's row-open event, with the full monospace id, a copy action, an "open page" link, and a back arrow backed by a history stack (at least ten entries) so hopping through parent and dependency links inside the slide-out never loses the place. Keep the open issue id in the URL query so a reload reopens it.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a row opens the slide-out; following a parent link then back returns to the first issue; reload reopens the same issue; "open page" goes to the issue URL.
notes:
Slide-out decisions (5.1 and later issue work build on these). All in apps/web/layers/issues/app.

FILES: composables/useIssuesSlideover.ts, components/Slideover.vue (IssuesSlideover), components/DetailHost.vue (IssuesDetailHost); pages/p/[project]/issues/index.vue: openIssue(id) now calls useIssuesSlideover(slug).open(id) and <IssuesSlideover v-if=slug :key=slug :slug> is mounted in the panel body next to IssuesList/IssuesBulkBar.

useIssuesSlideover(slug: MaybeRefOrGetter<string|null>) -> { issueId (computed from route.query.issue, ISSUES_SLIDEOVER_QUERY='issue'), history (readonly ids), canGoBack, open(id) (resets stack), push(id) (current goes onto the stack; no-op for the same id), back(), close() (clears stack + query) }. Stack lives in useState('issues:slideover:history') keyed by slug, capped at ISSUES_SLIDEOVER_HISTORY_LIMIT=50. All query changes use router.replace (no browser history entries), keeping any other query params. Anything outside the list page can open the slide-out by navigating to issuesPagePath(slug) with ?issue=<id>.

IssuesSlideover props { slug }; USlideover right, sm:max-w-2xl, own #content layout: header = back arrow (disabled when stack empty), full mono id, copy (useIssuesCopyId), 'Open page' (issuesPagePath(slug,id)), close X; body scrolls and resets to top on id change. Hidden dialog title/description = issue title / id. Escape inside input/textarea/select/contenteditable is swallowed (so 3.11/3.12 inline edits cancel without closing); Escape elsewhere, overlay click and X call close(). testids: issue-slideover-header/-back/-id/-copy/-open-page/-close/-body.

IssuesDetailHost props { slug, issueId, onOpenIssue? } emits loaded: IssuesDetail + the comments slot (IssuesComments) + forwards a run slot only when given. The slide-out renders it keyed by issueId with @open-issue=push. [id].vue was NOT switched to it (other agents editing); it still wires IssuesComments itself and 3.15 mounts the epic dependency graph on the page only, so the slide-out shows no graph. Follow-up: [id].vue can swap its IssuesDetail+comments block for IssuesDetailHost.

FOR 5.1 (Run): simplest is to replace the default run slot content inside Detail.vue (covers page and slide-out). Or pass a slot from the list page: <IssuesSlideover :slug><template #run="{ issue }"><MyRun :issue /></template></IssuesSlideover> - IssuesSlideover and IssuesDetailHost both forward #run to IssuesDetail; the page would also need its own #run on IssuesDetail/IssuesDetailHost.

Headless Chromium 19/19: row click opens slide-out with URL /p/cm/issues?issue=<id>; detail + comments inside; copy -> clipboard has full id; parent link -> parent in slide-out; 12-hop walk through parent/children/dependency links then back x12 returns to the first issue, back disabled at bottom; parent then back returns; reload reopens same issue (SSR); Escape and X close and clear the query; Escape inside an edit textarea keeps it open; title link click opens slide-out not page; Open page -> /p/cm/issues/<id>; 390px no horizontal overflow; no console errors. title: Build the issues list page with epic groups, rows, filters and search
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Rebuild v2's beads page with Nuxt UI primitives. Top-level epics render as collapsible groups (open by default) with chevron, title, short id, assignee and "N open / M total"; sub-epics render recursively with indentation; the ungrouped bucket comes last. A row shows: a checkbox (selection state is kept for later bulk actions), a priority flame (P0 red-to-yellow gradient, P1 red, P2 yellow, P3 sky, P4 grey), the short uppercase id (prefix stripped) with the full id on hover and a copy action, the title struck through when closed, violet `stage:*` chips, a sky "research" chip, a status badge, a type icon and colour (bug red, feature purple, task blue, epic amber, decision teal, chore zinc), assignee, and comment count, in a monospace font. Controls: show closed toggle, ready and blocked filters (new in v3), a search over title and id, and an Add Issue button (wired separately). Clicking a row emits an open event that the slide-out (separate work) handles. Must stay responsive with several hundred issues.
acceptance_criteria: On a real project the groups, nesting, counts and order match the v2 viewer on the same repo; ready and blocked filters narrow the list; search matches title and id; show closed reveals closed epics; copying an id works.
notes:
Issues list page (3.7, 3.9, 3.13 build on these). All in apps/web/layers/issues/app.

PAGE pages/p/[project]/issues/index.vue: gate > UDashboardPanel; header = UDashboardNavbar (right slot keeps 3.14's <IssuesAddButton />) + UDashboardToolbar with <IssuesToolbar :slug>; body <IssuesList :key="slug" :slug @open="openIssue">. openIssue(id) currently navigateTo(issuesPagePath(slug, id)); 3.9 replaces that one function with opening the slide-out.

COMPONENTS
- IssuesList (components/List.vue) props { slug }, emits open(id: string), defineExpose({ refresh }). Data: useIssuesList(slug). tree = computed(issuesGroupTree(issues, { showClosed })), visible = computed(issuesFilterTree(tree, filters, issuesBlockedIds(issues))). Renders top-level groups then the ungrouped bucket ('No epic', group key ISSUES_UNGROUPED_KEY) last. States: error UEmpty with retry, skeleton while pending with no data, 'No matching issues' (Clear filters), 'No issues'.
- IssuesEpicGroup (EpicGroup.vue) recursive, props { slug, groupKey, title, epic: Issue|null, issues, epics: IssuesEpicNode[], openCount, totalCount, depth? }, emits open(id). depth 0 = bordered card, nested = border-l indent. Header: own toggle button (chevron + title, aria-expanded) then short id button (UTooltip full id, click emits open(epic.id)), (assignee), 'N open / M total'. Body UCollapsible (unmounts when closed) with rows then nested groups. No v-memo: it breaks SSR in this Vue/Nuxt build ('_cache is not defined'); rows skip re-render through prop equality instead.
- IssuesRow (Row.vue) props { slug, issue, selected }, emits open(id), toggle(id, selected). font-mono; UCheckbox; flame UIcon coloured by issuesPriorityFlameClass (P0 = gradient background through the icon mask); short id issuesShortId (text after last '-', uppercased) in UTooltip with full id; copy button (hover/focus, sm+) -> useIssuesCopyId (clipboard + toast); title is a NuxtLink to the issue page (no-prefetch): plain click bubbles to row -> open, modified click opens a tab; struck + muted when closed; violet stage:* chips and sky 'research' chip (md+); status UBadge via issuesStatusMeta (sm+, status icon below sm); type icon + label coloured by issuesTypeColorClass (bug red, feature purple, task blue, epic amber, decision teal, chore zinc); assignee (md+); comment count. Clicks on checkbox / id / copy stop propagation.
- IssuesToolbar (Toolbar.vue) props { slug }: UInput search (aria-label 'Search issues by title or id'), UFieldGroup Ready / Blocked toggle buttons (mutually exclusive), USwitch 'Show closed'.

STATE (all useState, per project, so it survives refetches and client navigation to an issue page and back; a full reload resets it)
- useIssuesListState(slug) -> { showClosed: Ref<boolean>, stateFilter: Ref<'ready'|'blocked'|null>, search: Ref<string>, filters: computed { state, search }, collapsedIds: ComputedRef<ReadonlySet<string>>, setCollapsed(key, collapsed) }. Groups are open unless their key (epic id, or ISSUES_UNGROUPED_KEY) is in collapsed. Keys issues:view:<slug>:*.
- useIssuesSelection(slug) (for 3.13) -> { ids: ComputedRef<ReadonlySet<string>>, count, isSelected(id), toggle(id, value?), select(ids[]), deselect(ids[]), set(iterable), clear() }. Backed by useState<string[]>('issues:selection:<slug>'). Rows read ids in EpicGroup and call toggle. Selection is not pruned when issues disappear (3.13/3.7 may want set([...ids].filter(present))).
- useIssuesList(slug) -> { issues (default []), status, error, refresh } = useAsyncData(issuesListKey(slug) = 'issues:list:<slug>', api.list). SSR-rendered.

FILTERS (utils/issues-list.ts, unit tests test/unit/issues-list.test.ts): issuesBlockedIds(issues) = non-closed issues with status 'blocked' or a 'blocks' dependency on a non-closed issue present in the list (missing blockers ignored). Ready = issue.ready (bd ready). issuesMatchesSearch = case-insensitive substring of title or full id (short id is a substring of the id). issuesFilterTree(tree, filters, blockedIds): returns tree untouched with no filters; otherwise filters rows at every depth and prunes groups left empty; an epic whose title/id matches the search keeps all its rows (state filter still applies) and is shown even if empty; counts stay whole-subtree counts from 3.5; ungrouped dropped when empty.

FOR 3.7: call refresh() from useIssuesList inside IssuesList (or refreshNuxtData(issuesListKey(slug))) from useIssuesEvents; collapse and selection already live in useState so they survive the refetch; useAsyncData keeps old data while refreshing (status 'pending'), so a refetch indicator can key off status. Scroll: body is UDashboardPanel's scroll container; rows keep keys (issue id) so DOM is reused.

VERIFIED (tsx daemon :7810 + built web :7811, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR; projects cm = this repo and perf = scratch bd workspace with 309 issues, nested epics, blocks edges, stage/research labels): headless Chromium 29/29. DOM group/row sequence incl. depth and 'N open / M total' identical to bd list --all --limit 0 --json + bd ready through issuesGroupTree/issuesFilterTree for default, show closed, ready, blocked and searches (title and short id) on both projects. v2 was not run; the comparison is against the ported 3.5 functions. Show closed reveals closed epic x8m.1; tooltip shows full id; copy puts full id on clipboard without navigating; checkbox selects without opening; row click opens the issue page; collapse + selection survive the round trip; 390px no horizontal overflow; no console errors. Perf (perf project, headless WSL): ~223 rows SSR; full re-render of ~220-280 rows after a filter change 150-260 ms in-page, adding/removing ~60 rows ~100 ms, selection ~70 ms incl. Playwright overhead. Per-row UTooltip costs ~25 ms per 220 rows; UButton/ULink replaced with native button/NuxtLink for speed. Virtualisation not needed at this size.
close_reason: Verified by agent; gates green except 6.2 in-flight files

title: Refresh the issues list from the daemon's change stream
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The daemon emits a per-project change event whenever the project's `.beads` directory changes. Subscribe the issues list page to that stream while it is open, refetch on each notice (coalescing bursts), preserve collapsed groups, selection and scroll position across the refetch, and reconnect if the stream drops. Show a small indicator while refetching.
acceptance_criteria: Running `bd create` and `bd close` in a terminal updates the open page within a couple of seconds without a reload; collapsed groups and selection survive the refresh.
notes: Live refresh (apps/web/layers/issues/app). utils/issues-refresh-coalescer.ts: issuesCreateRefreshCoalescer({delayMs,run,onBusy}) = trailing debounce that never overlaps runs (trigger during a run queues exactly one more; run errors swallowed). composables/useIssuesLiveRefresh.ts: useIssuesLiveRefresh(slug, refresh) -> {refreshing, lost, connected}; wraps useIssuesEvents, 300ms debounce, captures scrollTop of the nearest scrolling ancestor of [data-testid=issues-list] before refresh and restores after nextTick, refetches when connected goes false->true after having been connected (EventSource reconnect emits no event), lost=true after 10s disconnected. components/LiveStatus.vue shows 'Refreshing' spinner and 'Live updates paused, reconnecting' hint (navbar right slot of the list page). Page edit is 2 lines: const live = useIssuesLiveRefresh(slug, () => refreshNuxtData(issuesListKey(slug))) and <IssuesLiveStatus> in the navbar #right slot. Collapsed/selection are useState so survive untouched. Tests: test/unit/issues-refresh-coalescer.test.ts (4). Verified with playwright against built web + daemon on 8500/8501 and temp bd workspace: bd create visible ~1.8s, bd close hidden ~2.3s (both include bd CLI latency), collapsed group, selected checkbox and scrollTop=200 preserved. Gotcha: nuxt dev HMR from concurrent edits full-reloads the page mid-test; verify against a built copy.
close_reason: useIssuesLiveRefresh with coalescing, scroll/selection/collapse preserved; browser-verified

title: Port v2's issue grouping and ordering as tested pure functions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The grouping and order of the v2 beads page is what Jack's eyes are trained on, so it must match exactly. In the issues layer, implement pure functions over the issue list: top-level epics (an epic whose parent is not an epic) become groups; child epics nest recursively with a cycle guard; issues whose parent is not an epic fall into a final ungrouped bucket; each group carries open and total counts over all descendants; closed epics with nothing visible are hidden unless "show closed" is on. Sibling order is: hierarchical id sequence, then numeric-aware title collation, then a topological pass so an issue blocked by a sibling sorts after it. Cover with unit tests built from fixtures, including a cycle and a blocked sibling.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests pass for grouping, nesting, counts, hidden closed epics, the ungrouped bucket, and all three ordering passes; the functions have no UI dependencies.
notes:
Grouping + ordering pure functions (3.6 consumes these). Auto-imported from apps/web/layers/issues/app/utils/; no Vue/Nuxt imports (only types from @candy-mountain/shared), so tests import them directly.

ORDER app/utils/issues-order.ts
- issuesSortSiblings<T extends IssuesOrderable>(issues: readonly T[]): T[]  (new array, input untouched). IssuesOrderable = { id, title, dependencies: readonly IssueDependency[] }.
- Port of v2 lib/bead-order.ts sortBeads: (1) hierarchical id sequence = numeric parts after the first '.' (x.2 < x.2.9 < x.2.10 < x.3.1; ids with a sequence before opaque ids; non-numeric suffix = opaque); (2) Intl.Collator numeric, sensitivity base ('Phase 2' < 'Phase 2b' < 'Phase 10'); tie -> id; (3) topological pass: repeatedly take the first ranked issue whose 'blocks' deps on SIBLINGS are all placed; blockers not in the passed list are ignored; a blocking cycle takes the head.
- Deviation: collator/tie-break use fixed locale 'en' (v2 used runtime default) so SSR and hydrated order match.

TREE app/utils/issues-tree.ts
- issuesGroupTree<T extends IssuesTreeItem>(issues: readonly T[], { showClosed?: boolean } = {}): IssuesTree<T>
  IssuesTreeItem = Pick<Issue,'id'|'title'|'type'|'status'|'parentId'|'dependencies'> (pass the full Issue[] from api.list; T is preserved in nodes).
- IssuesTree<T> = { groups: IssuesEpicNode<T>[]; ungrouped: IssuesUngroupedBucket<T> | null }
- IssuesEpicNode<T> = { epic: T; issues: T[] (visible direct non-epic children, sorted); epics: IssuesEpicNode<T>[] (nested, sorted, recursive); openCount; totalCount }
- IssuesUngroupedBucket<T> = { issues: T[] (visible, sorted); openCount; totalCount }
- issuesParentId(issue): parentId ?? first 'parent-child' dependency's dependsOnId ?? null.
Rules (v2 BeadsPage.vue groups computed): epic = type 'epic', closed = status 'closed'. Top-level group = epic whose parent is not an epic id (no parent, or a non-epic parent). Child epics nest recursively with a seen-set guard. Non-epic issues whose parent is not an epic (none/missing/non-epic) go to ungrouped. Closed non-epic issues filtered out unless showClosed (filter happens BEFORE the topological pass, like v2). A closed epic with no visible issues and no visible nested epics is dropped (top-level and nested) unless showClosed. ungrouped is non-null whenever any non-epic issue is outside an epic, even if all are closed (issues may be []), matching v2 'No epic' which showed when orphans existed.
- Counts: DEVIATION from v2 per bead text: openCount/totalCount = non-epic issues across the WHOLE subtree (incl. inside hidden closed nested epics), ignoring showClosed; on every node (v2 had direct children only, top-level only). Epics themselves are not counted. open = status !== 'closed'.
- Parent cycles among epics (A->B->A, self-parent) have no root, so those epics and their issues are not shown at all (same as v2).

HOW 3.6 CALLS IT: const tree = computed(() => issuesGroupTree(issues.value, { showClosed: showClosed.value })). Render tree.groups as collapsible EpicGroup cards ('N open / M total' from openCount/totalCount, title/assignee/id from node.epic), recurse node.epics for nested sections, rows from node.issues; render tree.ungrouped last as the 'No epic' bucket when non-null. Apply ready/blocked/search filters to the input list or to node.issues as 3.6 decides (note counts come from the input passed in). Use issuesSortSiblings for any other flat sibling list.

TESTS apps/web/layers/issues/test/issues-order.test.ts (13) + issues-tree.test.ts (16), picked up by apps/web vitest include layers/*/test/**. Root lint, typecheck, test (98 files / 930 tests) pass.
close_reason: issuesGroupTree + issuesSortSiblings ported from v2, 29 tests

title: Watch each project's .beads directory and push change notifications
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack uses `bd` from terminals and agents use it from sessions, so the page must refresh itself. Watch the `.beads` directory of every project that has one (debounced, tolerant of the directory appearing or disappearing while the daemon runs), invalidate that project's list cache on change, and expose a per-project server-sent event stream that emits a "changed" notice. Keep one watcher per project regardless of how many clients listen, and stop watching archived or deleted projects.
acceptance_criteria: Running `bd create` in a project's checkout emits a changed event on the project's stream within a second or two; a burst of ten writes emits a handful of events, not ten; removing the project stops the watcher.
notes:
Issue change stream decisions (3.7 and later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Issues".

SSE ROUTE: GET /projects/:slug/issues/events (daemon path). Browser: new EventSource('/api/projects/<slug>/issues/events'); shared helper projectIssueEventsPath(slug), constants ISSUE_CHANGED_EVENT='changed', type IssueChangedEvent { projectId } (packages/shared/src/issues.ts). Wire format: ': connected' comment sent immediately (Node only flushes headers with the first body bytes), ': ping' comment every ISSUE_EVENTS_HEARTBEAT_MS=30000 (web proxy's undici fetch cuts bodies silent for 300s), and on change 'event: changed' + 'data: {"projectId":"<uuid>"}'. No payload beyond that: clients refetch the list (and open detail) on changed. Unknown slug -> 404 not_found JSON (EventSource then stops retrying). Archived projects still open a stream but get only heartbeats. Streams end when the watcher closes (daemon shutdown); client disconnect unsubscribes. Auth applies like every other route (EventSource sends the cookie same-origin).

MOUNT: issueEventRoutes(watcher, { heartbeatMs? }) in src/issues/events-routes.ts, mounted in app.ts at PROJECTS_PATH only when AppDeps.issueWatcher is given, and BEFORE issueRoutes() (otherwise /:slug/issues/:id claims 'events'). index.ts passes platform.issueWatcher.

WATCHER MODULE (src/issues/watcher.ts, re-exported from issues/index.ts): startIssueWatcher({ db, invalidate? = invalidateIssueList, debounceMs? = 250, maxWaitMs? = 1000, minIntervalMs? = 2000, reconcileMs? = 2000 }) -> IssueWatcher { subscribe(projectId, listener) -> unsubscribe; isWatching(projectId); reconcile(); signal: AbortSignal (aborted on close); close() (idempotent) }. Also exports beadsFingerprint(beadsDir) and the ISSUE_WATCH_* constants. One recursive fs.watch (Node 24 on Linux, persistent:false, no chokidar needed) per active project with a .beads dir, shared by all subscribers; on a detected change it calls invalidate(projectId) then every listener.

KEY GOTCHA (measured with bd 1.2.2): bd rewrites embedded Dolt files (manifest, journal.idx, temp manifests) on EVERY read, and bd show writes .beads/last-touched; comment/dep/label writes touch no top-level file. So raw fs events cannot distinguish reads from writes and would loop (refetch -> bd list -> event -> refetch). Events therefore only trigger a check: after the debounce the watcher computes beadsFingerprint = sha1 of issues.jsonl + each .beads/**/.dolt/noms/manifest (depth<=3, covers embeddeddolt/<db> and server-mode dolt/) + Dolt journal file size; manifest root hash and journal length only change on commits. Verified: list/ready/show/comments/dep list leave it unchanged; create/update/close/comment add/label add change it.

DEBOUNCE: trailing 250ms quiet, flushed at most 1s into a continuous burst; then notifications per project are spaced at least 2s apart (a scripted burst is many bd processes, each ~0.3-0.7s, so pure debouncing gave one event per write). Live: single bd create -> event 0.8s after start (0.25s after bd exits); ten sequential creates over 5s -> 4 events; reads -> 0 events.

PROJECT LIFECYCLE: polling, no hook in projects/*.ts. The watcher reconciles every 2s (unref'd interval; errors logged, never thrown) against listProjects(db) (active only): new/unarchived projects get a watch, archived/deleted ones are closed, a changed checkout path replaces the watch and emits changed. The same tick stats each .beads (inode) so the directory appearing, disappearing or being recreated (rm -rf + bd init: a recursive watch reports neither) is picked up; appearing/disappearing emits changed. If fs.watch throws (e.g. inotify limit) it warns once and polls the fingerprint each tick. Chose polling over an emitter so concurrent beads editing projects.ts are untouched and changes made any way (direct DB edits) are seen; cost is one SQLite query + one stat per project per 2s, and up to 2s lag on create/archive/delete.

PLATFORM: startPlatform starts it as platform.issueWatcher; platform.close() closes it before the DB. index.ts shutdown closes the watcher BEFORE server.close() since open SSE streams would otherwise keep server.close waiting forever (verified: SIGTERM with an open stream exits in ~0.3s).

TESTS: src/issues/watcher.test.ts (real temp workspaces via createTempBeadsWorkspace; bd writes run async because execFileSync would block the loop and fold events): bd create -> event + invalidate within 2s; reads -> no events; ten creates -> 1..5 events with production spacing; two subscribers share one watch, unsubscribe works; archive/unarchive/delete stop/resume; new project picked up by reconcile; .beads removed and re-inited; no-tracker/missing checkout tolerated. src/issues/events-routes.test.ts: SSE framing, changed event, heartbeat (50ms), subscribe/unsubscribe per connection, stream ends on watcher close, 404 unknown slug, createApp mounts it ahead of /:id, real bd create reaches the stream. Tests that need several events pass minIntervalMs: 0.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (56 files / 507 tests), build pass. Live: node --import tsx src/index.ts on port 5437 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR and a temp bd workspace; curl -N of the stream showed ': connected', changed after bd create, nothing for 3 list GETs, 4 events for a 10-create burst, ': ping' at 30s, no events after DELETE /projects/live, reconnect -> 404, SIGTERM with a stream open -> clean exit.
close_reason: fingerprint-based watcher + SSE stream verified live; gates green

title: Add the Issues capability manifest and layer skeleton
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Register the `issues` capability: manifest in the daemon (member of the `issues` module, no required plugins, a project-fact readiness requirement that the project has a `.beads` directory, ladder none then read then write, where write adds the editing tools) and a layer in the web app with an empty issues list view and an issue detail view at a path that carries the issue id. Add the layer's API client composable for the daemon's issue endpoints. Pages render placeholders; the real UI is separate work.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`. Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`.
acceptance_criteria: Enabling Issues on a project with `.beads` shows the Issues view; a project without `.beads` shows the soft lockout naming the missing directory; lint passes.
notes:
Issues capability + layer skeleton decisions (3.5-3.15 build on these).

MANIFEST apps/daemon/src/capabilities/manifests/issues.ts (issuesCapability), in CAPABILITIES after overview.
- One view { id 'issues', label 'Issues', icon 'i-lucide-list-todo', path 'issues' } -> /p/<slug>/issues. VIEW_PATH_PATTERN allows no params, so there is NO separate 'issue' view: the detail page is an undeclared child route /p/<slug>/issues/:id gated with view 'issues'.
- requiresPlugins [], requiresProjectFacts ['hasBeads'] (reason "The project has no .beads directory."; lockout action 'Re-check the project').
- tools: 'issues.write' and 'issues.comment', both kind 'operation', unscoped.
- ladder: none -> read (views ['issues'], no tools) -> write (views ['issues'], tools issues.write + issues.comment).
- Module: ISSUES_MODULE.capabilities = [overview read, issues write] (defaultRung 'write').

DAEMON GATE (done here): src/issues/write-routes.ts mounts requireCapability({ capability: 'issues', tool: 'issues.write' }) on POST issues, POST issues/bulk, PATCH issues/:id, POST issues/:id/close, and tool 'issues.comment' on POST issues/:id/comments + PATCH issues/:id/comments/:commentId. Refusals: module off 404 not_enabled; no .beads 409 not_ready (admin message names .beads); rung read 403 not_granted. READ routes (list/show/dependencies/comments) and the SSE stream are still UNGATED (not asked; add requireCapability({capability:'issues', view:'issues'}) later if wanted). write-routes.test.ts now enables the issues module for its project and has a test for not_enabled/not_ready.

WEB LAYER apps/web/layers/issues/
- nuxt.config.ts: components prefix 'Issues' (app/components/ not created yet).
- app/pages/p/[project]/issues/index.vue: <CapabilityViewGate capability="issues" view="issues"><UDashboardPanel id="issues"> + UEmpty placeholder. 3.6 replaces the body with a component (e.g. IssuesList) that fetches INSIDE the slot.
- app/pages/p/[project]/issues/[id].vue: same gate (view 'issues'), UDashboardPanel id="issue", navbar title = route.params.id, back button (aria-label 'Back to issues') to issuesPagePath(slug), UEmpty placeholder. 3.8 replaces the body with the detail component. Sibling of index.vue (no issues.vue parent), so both are children of core p/[project].vue; projectSwitchPath drops the :id on project switch.
- app/utils/paths.ts: issuesPagePath(slug: string, issueId?: string): string -> /p/<slug>/issues or /p/<slug>/issues/<encoded id>.
- app/composables/useIssuesApi.ts: useIssuesApi() -> object of $api calls (all slug-first, return Promises, reject with FetchError whose data is ApiErrorBody):
  list(slug) -> IssueListResponse
  show(slug, id) -> IssueResponse
  dependencies(slug, ids: readonly string[]) -> IssueDependencyListResponse (GET .../issues/dependencies?ids=a,b; max 200)
  comments(slug, id) -> IssueCommentListResponse
  create(slug, body: CreateIssueRequest) -> CreateIssueResponse
  update(slug, id, body: UpdateIssueRequest) -> IssueResponse
  close(slug, id, body: CloseIssueRequest = {}) -> IssueResponse
  bulkUpdate(slug, body: BulkUpdateIssuesRequest) -> BulkUpdateIssuesResponse
  addComment(slug, id, text) -> IssueCommentResponse
  editComment(slug, id, commentId, text) -> IssueCommentResponse
  Type IssuesApi = ReturnType<typeof useIssuesApi>. Call useIssuesApi() in setup (it uses useNuxtApp). For SSR data use useAsyncData(key, () => api.list(slug)).
- app/composables/useIssuesEvents.ts: useIssuesEvents(slug: MaybeRefOrGetter<string|null|undefined>, onChanged: (event: IssueChangedEvent) => void) -> { connected: Readonly<Ref<boolean>>, close() }. Opens new EventSource('/api' + projectIssueEventsPath(slug)) in onMounted (never SSR), listens for ISSUE_CHANGED_EVENT, reopens when slug changes, closes on scope dispose. Does NOT fire onChanged after a reconnect; 3.7 may want to refetch on connected false->true.
- README 'Views, the sidebar and the gate' gained a paragraph on param child routes.

VERIFIED: tsx daemon :6741 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, development auth) + built web (.output copied to scratch) :6740. Projects cm (this repo) and plain (empty dir), PUT modules ['issues'] on both.
