title: Show a clear state when the daemon is unreachable
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The daemon and the web app are separate processes; when the daemon is stopped the web app must not render a blank page or a wall of failed requests. Detect that the proxy cannot reach the daemon (connection refused or timeout), surface a full-page "daemon unreachable" state with the configured daemon address and a retry action, and recover automatically when the daemon returns. Ordinary API errors (4xx, 5xx from the daemon itself) are not this state.
acceptance_criteria: Stopping the daemon while the app is open shows the unreachable state within a few seconds; starting it again restores the app without a manual reload; a 500 from the daemon does not trigger the state.
notes: Daemon-unreachable decisions: MARKING: proxyToDaemon (apps/web/server/utils/daemon-proxy.ts) catches a failed upstream connection (refused/timeout; h3 proxyRequest throws only then) and answers 502 + header x-cm-daemon-unreachable: 1 + JSON {error:{code:'daemon_unreachable',message},daemonUrl}. Daemon-produced 4xx/5xx (even 502) pass through unmarked. Contract in packages/shared/src/daemon-unreachable.ts (DAEMON_UNREACHABLE_HEADER, DaemonUnreachableBody, isDaemonUnreachableResponse = status 502 AND header, isDaemonUnreachableBody). DETECTION: app/plugins/api.ts $api onResponseError calls reportDaemonError. STATE: useDaemonStatus() in app/composables/useDaemonStatus.ts -> { status: useState 'daemon-status' {unreachable, daemonUrl}, check() }; daemonUrl comes only from the unreachable response body. POLL: app/app.vue polls GET /api/health every DAEMON_POLL_INTERVAL_MS=3000 on the client always (also while healthy, so a stop between API calls is noticed); a success clears the state. UI: app/components/DaemonUnreachable.vue (full page, address, Retry now button) rendered by app.vue instead of NuxtLayout/NuxtPage while unreachable (pages remount and refetch on recovery). Verified headless chromium vs built app: shown ~1.8s after daemon kill, auto-recovered ~2.8s after restart, /api/nope 404 not triggering; daemon 500/404/502 unit-tested unmarked.
close_reason: Verified by agent; root gates green

title: Make the web app installable as a PWA
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack wants to launch Candy Mountain from an icon on desktop and Android without packaging a native app. Declare the web app installable: a manifest with name, icons, theme colour and standalone display, plus the minimal service worker needed for the browser to offer installation. The app is online-only, so the service worker must not cache API responses or make the app appear to work while the daemon is down. Non-goals: offline support, push notifications, a Tauri or Electron shell.
acceptance_criteria: Chrome on desktop and Android offers "Install"; the installed app opens in standalone mode; API calls are never served from a cache; Lighthouse's installability check passes.
notes:
PWA decisions. Hand-written, no PWA module: @vite-pwa/nuxt (1.1.1) is Workbox-based and precaches by default, which would make the app look alive with the daemon down; an install-only worker needs none of it and adds no deps.
FILES: apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest (name/short_name Candy Mountain, id/start_url/scope '/', display standalone, theme #ec4899 = pink primary, background #0f172a); apps/web/public/icons/{icon-192,icon-512,icon-maskable-512,apple-touch-icon(180)}.png = placeholder pink square with 'CM'; apps/web/public/sw.js; scripts/generate-pwa-icons.mjs (run-once generator, pure node zlib, no deps; rerun 'node scripts/generate-pwa-icons.mjs' to regenerate).
WIRING: apps/web/nuxt.config.ts app.head: manifest link, apple-touch-icon link, theme-color meta, inline script registering /sw.js on window load.
SERVICE WORKER: install/activate with skipWaiting+clients.claim; fetch listener is a no-op (never calls respondWith, no Cache API), so /api/** and everything else always hits the network. Chrome installability needs the fetch handler present. Registered in dev too (same behaviour, harmless); needs secure context: localhost or https only, so on LAN http the install prompt will not appear. To replace the icons later, overwrite the PNGs in public/icons (keep names/sizes). Caveat: if a worker is ever changed, browsers re-fetch /sw.js on navigation (served by Nitro without long cache headers by default).
VERIFIED: built server on 127.0.0.1:4447 serves manifest (application/manifest+json), all icons (image/png), sw.js (text/javascript); /projects and /settings HTML link the manifest. Not run: actual Lighthouse/Chrome install (no browser here).
close_reason: Manifest, icons, no-cache SW verified; install prompt needs a real browser (human test)

title: Add the password strategy with server-side sessions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Day to day the app runs behind Tailscale and Jack logs in with a password; the daemon's auth middleware already resolves an actor through swappable strategies, so add the password strategy. It stores a salted password hash for the admin user (set through configuration or a CLI-style command on first run, implementer's choice, but never plaintext in the database), issues a server-side session on successful login, and identifies the session by an HttpOnly cookie that the web app's Nitro proxy forwards unchanged. Provide login, logout and "who am I" endpoints; sessions expire after a configurable period. Non-goals: no UI (the login page is separate), no password reset, no multiple users.
acceptance_criteria: Logging in with the right password sets a session cookie and subsequent requests resolve the admin actor; a wrong password yields 401 without a session; logout invalidates the session; an expired session yields 401; the password hash is never returned by any endpoint; tests cover each case.
notes:
Password strategy decisions (bead 1.11 login page and 1.16 CLI rely on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Auth" > "Password strategy".

ROUTES (daemon paths; browser adds /api)
- GET /auth/strategy -> 200 { strategy: 'development' | 'password' | 'trusted-header' } (AuthStrategyResponse). PUBLIC under every strategy (added to PUBLIC_PATHS). This is how the web login page/route middleware detects the strategy signed-out.
- POST /auth/login, JSON { username, password } (LoginRequest) -> 200 { actor } (LoginResponse) + Set-Cookie. Wrong username or password -> 401 { error: { code: 'invalid_credentials', message: 'Invalid username or password' } }, no cookie, no session row. Malformed/non-JSON body or password > 1024 chars -> 400 { error: { code: 'invalid_request' } }. A login request carrying an old cm_session cookie deletes that session (rotation). Unknown usernames burn a dummy scrypt verify (no timing oracle).
- POST /auth/logout -> 204, deletes the session if the cookie names one, always clears the cookie. PUBLIC (works with an expired/missing cookie).
- login/logout exist only under the password strategy (strategy-owned routes): 404 under development, 401 under trusted-header.
- GET /auth/me unchanged: 200 { actor } or 401 'unauthenticated'.
- Shared constants (packages/shared/src/auth.ts): AUTH_STRATEGY_PATH '/auth/strategy', LOGIN_PATH '/auth/login', LOGOUT_PATH '/auth/logout', SESSION_COOKIE_NAME 'cm_session', INVALID_CREDENTIALS_ERROR_CODE 'invalid_credentials', types AuthStrategyResponse, LoginRequest, LoginResponse; AUTH_STRATEGY_NAMES now ['development','password','trusted-header'].

COOKIE
- cm_session=<32 random bytes base64url>; Max-Age=<ttl seconds>; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; plus Secure when CM_AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true (default false: Tailscale MagicDNS over plain http would drop a Secure cookie; set true behind https e.g. tailscale serve). Logout: cm_session=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax. The Nitro proxy passes Set-Cookie unchanged and $api forwards the cookie during SSR, so nothing to change in the proxy.

SESSIONS
- Table auth_sessions (named so to avoid clashing with agent sessions in phase 4): id = SHA-256 hex of the cookie token (raw token never stored), user_id FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at, expires_at, last_seen_at (ISO text); indexes on user_id and expires_at. last_seen_at written at most once a minute.
- Lifetime CM_AUTH_SESSION_TTL, default 30d, format <n>s|m|h|d, max 400d (browser cookie cap). ABSOLUTE expiry from login, no sliding renewal. Expired session -> 401 'unauthenticated' and the row is deleted; each login purges all expired rows.
- Services in src/auth/sessions.ts: createSession, resolveSession, deleteSession, deleteExpiredSessions (injectable clock).

PASSWORDS
- Table user_passwords(user_id PK FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, password_hash, created_at, updated_at); never in users, never in any response.
- Hash: node:crypto scrypt (no native dependency), N=2^17 r=8 p=1 (OWASP baseline, ~230ms), 16-byte salt, 64-byte key, stored as scrypt$N$r$p$saltB64$keyB64; verify reads params from the hash so they can be raised later. Password normalised NFKC. New passwords 8..1024 chars.
- Setting the admin password: env CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD at boot (any strategy). Different from the stored hash -> new hash + all of that user's sessions deleted (log 'Admin password set from CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD'); same -> no-op ('unchanged'), so leaving it set does not log you out on restart. Can be unset after first boot. Daemon-internal: setUserPassword(db, userId, password) (revokes sessions), applyAdminPassword(db, password), requireAdminPassword(db) in src/auth/passwords.ts. CM_AUTH_STRATEGY=password with no admin hash -> daemon refuses to start with 'The password strategy needs an admin password: start the daemon once with CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD set' (exit 1).
- CLI (1.16) can pass CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD through, or a future 'set-password' command can call setUserPassword; no CLI command was added here.

FRAMEWORK CHANGES
- AuthStrategy gained optional routes(): Hono<AppEnv>, mounted under /auth by authRoutes(strategy) (signature now takes the strategy; app.ts passes it). Password strategy publicPaths = [LOGIN_PATH, LOGOUT_PATH].
- AuthConfig has a PasswordAuthConfig member { strategy:'password', sessionTtlMs, secureCookie }. DaemonConfig gained adminPassword.

MIGRATION: drizzle/0003_auth_sessions.sql (tag 0003_auth_sessions): creates auth_sessions + user_passwords.

FOR BEAD 1.11 (login page)
- Route middleware: GET /api/auth/me; 200 -> signed in. On 401, GET /api/auth/strategy: 'password' -> redirect to login with the return URL; 'development' never 401s for /auth/me so login is naturally skipped; 'trusted-header' -> show an error, not a form.
- Login form: $api(LOGIN_PATH, { method:'POST', body:{ username, password } }); 401 with code invalid_credentials -> inline error. Username field: 'admin' is the only user (ADMIN_USERNAME).
- Logout: $api(LOGOUT_PATH, { method:'POST' }) then navigate to login. The cookie is HttpOnly, so the client cannot read it; rely on /auth/me.
- Any daemon 401 'unauthenticated' (e.g. session expired mid-use) should send the user to login.

FOLLOW-UPS NOT DONE: no login rate limiting/lockout; no sliding session renewal.

VERIFIED: new tests src/auth/password.test.ts (14), passwords.test.ts (6), config.test.ts (+3); daemon 144 tests; root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (248), build pass. Live: built daemon on 127.0.0.1:5216, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, CM_AUTH_STRATEGY=password: no admin password -> exit 1; /auth/strategy 200 password, /auth/me and /info 401 signed-out; wrong password 401 no cookie; right password 200 + cookie (Max-Age, Path=/, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax); /auth/me, /info 200 with cookie; logout 204 + Max-Age=0, cookie then 401; TTL=5s session -> 401 after expiry and row deleted; restart with same CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD -> 'unchanged' and session survives; changed password -> 'set', old session 401, old password 401, new 200; dev strategy -> /auth/strategy development, /auth/login 404.
close_reason: Verified by agent; gates green

title: Build the web app shell with the same-origin Nitro proxy and dashboard layout
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Digital Hub's browser called its server cross-origin with a spoofable header; v3 keeps the browser same-origin by having the web app's Nitro server proxy every API call to the daemon, forwarding cookies and streaming responses (server-sent events must pass through unbuffered). Build that proxy with the daemon address configurable, and the app shell on top of it: a dashboard layout with a collapsible sidebar, a header with a slot where the project picker will sit, and a content area. The sidebar renders a fixed system group (Projects, Settings) and otherwise stays empty; later work fills it from a registry. Provide a typed client helper the rest of the app uses to call the API through the proxy. Non-goals: no login page, no layers, no PWA, no real pages.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the web app shows the dashboard layout; an API call from the browser reaches the daemon only through the web app's origin; a streamed SSE response passes through the proxy without buffering (test with a sample endpoint); the daemon address is configurable.
notes:
Shell + proxy decisions (dependents rely on these):

PROXY
- Browser path /api/<rest> -> daemon <daemonUrl>/<rest> (the /api prefix is STRIPPED; query kept). Daemon routes therefore live at root, e.g. daemon GET /health is reached as /api/health. Daemon must never mount its own /api prefix.
- Files: apps/web/server/api/[...path].ts (catch-all, one line) + apps/web/server/utils/daemon-proxy.ts (proxyToDaemon, resolveDaemonUrl, toDaemonPath, API_PREFIX; explicit imports from 'h3' so it is unit-testable; h3 ^1.15.11 is now a direct web dep, same copy Nitro uses).
- Built on h3 proxyRequest: forwards method, body, all request headers incl. Cookie (h3 drops host/connection/accept-encoding etc.; Accept is re-added because h3 drops it), returns status, headers and every Set-Cookie unchanged (no domain/path rewrite, so daemon should set Path=/ cookies). Response bodies are streamed chunk by chunk (SSE verified unbuffered in dev, prod and a unit test). Client disconnect aborts the upstream fetch so the daemon sees its SSE response close. Daemon unreachable -> 502 Bad Gateway (h3 default; bead 1.10 builds the UI state on this).
- No X-Forwarded-* or actor headers are added. Every browser header passes through, so the auth bead's trusted-header strategy must not trust headers arriving via this proxy without stripping/overriding them here.
- SSE gotcha: Node fetch (undici) has a 300s bodyTimeout, so daemon SSE endpoints must send a heartbeat (e.g. ': ping' comment) at least every ~30s or long idle streams get cut.
- @nuxt/icon's endpoint moved to /_nuxt_icon (nuxt.config icon.localApiEndpoint) so /api belongs entirely to the daemon. Do not add Nitro routes under server/api/; web-only server routes go in server/routes/ outside /api.

DAEMON ADDRESS
- runtimeConfig.daemonUrl, set at runtime with NUXT_DAEMON_URL (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:4310). If empty, falls back to http://${CM_DAEMON_HOST:-127.0.0.1}:${CM_DAEMON_PORT:-4310} (IPv6 hosts bracketed), so the CLI can set CM_DAEMON_HOST/PORT once for both processes. Read per request, so no rebuild needed.

PORTS
- Web dev 4300 (nuxt.config devServer.port); daemon 4310. Prod web: node apps/web/.output/server/index.mjs with PORT/HOST (verified HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=4390). Nitro binds all interfaces by default and the proxy exposes the daemon through it, so the CLI should set HOST=127.0.0.1 until auth lands.

API CLIENT
- useApi (app/composables/useApi.ts) = createUseFetch(() => ({ $fetch: useNuxtApp().$api })): same API as useFetch, path relative to /api. Usage: const { data, status, error, refresh } = useApi<HealthResponse>(HEALTH_PATH). Types come from @candy-mountain/shared contract types passed as the generic.
- Imperative calls (mutations, event handlers): const { $api } = useNuxtApp(); await $api<T>('/projects', { method: 'POST', body }). $api is provided by app/plugins/api.ts: $fetch.create({ baseURL: '/api', headers: useRequestHeaders(['cookie']) }) so SSR forwards the browser cookie to the in-process proxy.
- Pages/layers must only use useApi / $api; never hardcode the daemon URL or /api in components. For SSE use new EventSource('/api/<path>') (same origin).

LAYOUT
- app/app.vue wraps NuxtPage in NuxtLayout. Layout file app/layouts/dashboard.vue; a page opts in with definePageMeta({ layout: 'dashboard' }) and renders a UDashboardPanel (id, #header with UDashboardNavbar title, #body content). Pages without the meta (e.g. login) get no layout.
- Structure: UDashboardGroup (storage-key cm-dashboard, flex-col) > AppHeader on top > row with UDashboardSidebar (collapsible, resizable, footer UDashboardSidebarCollapse) + page slot. The row applies [&>*]:min-h-0 because Nuxt UI sidebar/panel default to min-h-svh.
- app.config.ts: primary pink, neutral slate (v2 palette); dashboardNavbar toggle slot hidden globally because AppHeader owns the mobile sidebar toggle (UDashboardSidebarToggle, lg:hidden).

HEADER (app/components/AppHeader.vue)
- Left: mobile sidebar toggle, brand link to / (mountain-snow icon + PRODUCT_NAME). Named slots: #project (flex-1 area right of the brand: the project picker bead fills it from layouts/dashboard.vue via <template #project><ProjectPicker /></template>) and #actions (right-aligned; currently UColorModeButton; the login bead adds the logout/user action here).

SIDEBAR ENTRIES
- Types in app/utils/navigation.ts (auto-imported): NavEntry { id, label, icon (i-lucide-*), to } and NavGroup { id, label, entries: NavEntry[] }.
- SYSTEM_NAV_GROUP (same file) is the fixed System group: projects -> /projects (i-lucide-folder-git-2), settings -> /settings (i-lucide-settings). Both entries already exist; beads 1.14 and 1.15 only need to create app/pages/projects/... and app/pages/settings.vue (until then vue-router logs a 'No match found' warning for these links during SSR).
- app/composables/useNavigation.ts returns { capabilityGroups: ComputedRef<NavGroup[]> (currently []), systemGroup }. Phase 2 replaces the capabilityGroups computed with one built from the registry. app/components/AppNav.vue renders capability groups (label + entries) at the top and the System group pinned to the bottom (mt-auto), handling the collapsed state with tooltips.

TESTS / TOOLING
- New vitest project 'web' (apps/web/vitest.config.ts, node env, include test/unit/**/*.test.ts) added to root vitest.config.ts projects. test/unit is not covered by nuxt typecheck (only test/nuxt is); test/nuxt is reserved for future @nuxt/test-utils tests.
- Added deps to web: h3 ^1.15.11, @iconify-json/lucide ^1.2.147 (icons served/bundled locally, no Iconify CDN calls).
close_reason: Proxy, dashboard layout, useApi verified in dev and prod incl. SSE

title: Set up the Nuxt layer convention and lint-enforced layer boundaries
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Capabilities will each be a Nuxt layer and must not import from one another; Digital Hub proved that lint-enforced boundaries keep layers honest, and v3 wants the rules in place before any layer exists so later work only adds layers. Establish the convention: layers live in a layers directory and are auto-registered by Nuxt 4; a layer's name is its capability id; every auto-import a layer exposes carries the layer's prefix; a layer owns its own pages, components and composables; a shared `chat` layer is infrastructure, not a capability. Encode the allowed import graph in ESLint rules: capability layers may import from core and from the chat layer; the chat layer may import from core; core may import from chat; nothing may import from a capability layer. Add a throwaway example layer to prove the rules fire, then remove it or keep it as a documented template. Write a short README for the convention. Non-goals: no real capability.
acceptance_criteria: A layer importing from another capability layer fails lint with a clear message; a layer importing from core or chat passes; auto-imports without the layer prefix fail lint; the README explains how to add a layer.
notes:
Layer convention + boundary lint decisions (Phase 2+ layers rely on these). Full doc: apps/web/layers/README.md.

LAYOUT
- apps/web/layers/<capability-id>/ (lowercase kebab id = manifest id), plus one shared infra layer apps/web/layers/chat/. Everything in apps/web outside layers/ is CORE (app/, server/, test/, configs).
- Layer shape: nuxt.config.ts (components prefix only), app/pages/p/[project]/<id>/..., app/components/, app/composables/, app/utils/ (auto-imported), app/types/ (explicit imports via #layers/<id>/app/types/...), optional app/app.config.ts (defu-merged contributions, e.g. chat registration).
- Working minimal template: apps/web/test/fixtures/layered-app/layers/alpha/ (fixture app, not registered with the real app).

REGISTRATION
- Auto-discovery, no extends list: Nuxt 4.6 kit loadNuxtConfig globs layers/* and registers each dir WITH a nuxt.config.* (dirs without one are skipped; layers/README.md is ignored). Each gets alias #layers/<id> and is covered by nuxt typecheck (layers/*/app/**). apps/web/nuxt.config.ts was NOT changed.
- Verified in a scratch copy of apps/web with a demo-cap layer: components.d.ts registers DemoCapWidget (no unprefixed name), imports.d.ts has useDemoCapCount, nuxt typecheck + nuxt build pass, and the built router nests layer page p/[project]/demo-cap/index.vue as child 'demo-cap' of core's p/[project].vue -> /p/:project/demo-cap.

ADDING A CAPABILITY LAYER (exact steps)
1. Manifest in daemon; its id = layer dir name.
2. apps/web/layers/<id>/nuxt.config.ts: export default defineNuxtConfig({ components: [{ path: './components', prefix: '<PascalId>' }] })  (agent-hub -> AgentHub).
3. Pages under app/pages/p/[project]/<id>/ (or single p/[project]/<id>.vue); components in app/components; composables/utils with prefixed names.
4. pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/web exec nuxt prepare (regenerates aliases/types/ESLint globals); check .nuxt/components.d.ts + imports.d.ts.
5. pnpm lint / typecheck / test. No central edits (no extends, no lint list, no route map).

ALLOWED IMPORTS
- capability -> core, capability -> chat, chat -> core, core -> chat. Forbidden: capability -> capability, chat -> capability, core -> capability. A layer may always use its own files. Packages (incl. @candy-mountain/shared, the place for cross-capability wire types) are never restricted. Core's allowed surface = all of core (bead text); layers should use useApi/$api, useSelectedProject, projectPath etc.
- Aliases: #layers/<id>/ for own files and chat; ~/ (and @/) = core app only; never reach own layer files via ~/ (Nuxt localLayerAliases rewrites ~ inside a layer at build time but typecheck maps it to core), never create a layer file at a path that exists in core.

LINT CONFIG
- Local plugin apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs ('cm-layers'), registered in apps/web/eslint.config.mjs via withNuxt({ignores:['test/fixtures/**']}, {name:'cm/layer-boundaries', files: all js/ts/vue, rules: 4 rules = 'error'}). - Test: apps/web/test/unit/layer-boundaries.test.ts runs ESLint with the real apps/web config + settings {'cm-layers': {root: fixture}} over apps/web/test/fixtures/layered-app (11 clean files pass; violations asserted with exact messages). The settings override is the only test hook.

ROUTES (aligned with bead 1.13 notes)

title: Add actor resolution with user and role tables and the dev and trusted-header strategies
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Digital Hub had no real auth (a spoofable header) and Clanker Corner trusted a hosting edge; v3 needs one place where a request becomes an actor so nothing else in the daemon ever reads a header or cookie. Add user and role tables (seeded with one admin user and the admin role; the schema must leave room for more users and roles later) and a single auth middleware with swappable strategies, selected by configuration. Ship two strategies here: a development strategy that resolves every request as the admin, and a trusted-header strategy for a future hosted proxy that maps a configured header's value to a user. Every protected route reads the resolved actor (id, roles) from request context; unknown or missing identity yields 401. The health endpoint stays public. Non-goals: the password strategy, sessions and login UI are separate work.
acceptance_criteria: With the dev strategy every request resolves to the admin; with the trusted-header strategy a matching header resolves the user and a missing or unknown one yields 401; a protected sample route returns the actor; tests cover both strategies and the seeding of the admin user and role.
notes:
Auth decisions (dependents rely on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Auth".

TABLES (src/db/schema/auth.ts, migration drizzle/0002_auth.sql, tag 0002_auth)
- users(id text PK uuid, username text unique not null, display_name, created_at, updated_at). No credential column: the password bead adds its own (column or table).
- roles(id text PK uuid, slug text unique not null, name, created_at, updated_at). Roles are referred to by slug everywhere (actor.roles holds slugs).
- user_roles(user_id FK users ON DELETE CASCADE, role_id FK roles ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at, PK(user_id, role_id), index user_roles_role_id_idx). Role grants (2.2) should FK roles.id with ON DELETE CASCADE.
- Seed: seedAuth(db) (src/auth/seed.ts) runs in startPlatform on every boot and in openTestDatabase(); idempotent (onConflictDoNothing on users.username / roles.slug / user_roles PK). Ensures user username 'admin' (displayName 'Admin') holding role slug 'admin' (name 'Administrator'). IDs are random UUIDs generated once and stable across restarts. openTestDatabase({ seed: false }) gives an unseeded DB.

SHARED (@candy-mountain/shared, packages/shared/src/auth.ts)
AUTH_PATH '/auth', ME_PATH '/auth/me', AUTH_STRATEGY_NAMES ['development','trusted-header'], type AuthStrategyName, isAuthStrategyName, ADMIN_ROLE 'admin', ADMIN_USERNAME 'admin', UNAUTHENTICATED_ERROR_CODE 'unauthenticated', interface Actor { id, username, displayName, roles: string[] (role slugs, sorted) }, MeResponse { actor }.

READING THE ACTOR
- In any route typed new Hono<AppEnv>(): c.var.actor (Actor). Never read headers/cookies for identity. c.var.authStrategy holds the active AuthStrategyName (used by /info).
- AppEnv is now { Variables: AppVariables } with AppVariables { db, paths, authStrategy, actor }; AppDeps is { db, paths, auth?: AuthStrategy } (deps and vars are separate types now).
- Services: findActorById(db, id) / findActorByUsername(db, username) -> Actor | null (src/auth/actors.ts).
- GET /auth/me (browser: /api/auth/me) -> 200 { actor }: the protected sample route; the web header/user menu can use it.

MIDDLEWARE AND 401
- src/auth/middleware.ts authMiddleware(strategy), mounted app-wide in createApp right after the deps middleware. Every path except PUBLIC_PATHS ([HEALTH_PATH] = '/health') plus strategy.publicPaths is protected, including /info and unknown paths. Exact path match.
- No actor -> 401 { error: { code: 'unauthenticated', message: 'Authentication required' } } (ApiErrorBody). On public paths c.var.actor is unset: public routes must not read it.
- /info is PROTECTED (it exposes the data dir path); the plan only names health as public. A login page that needs to know the strategy before sign-in needs its own public route.

STRATEGIES (src/auth/strategy.ts)
interface AuthStrategy { readonly name: AuthStrategyName; readonly publicPaths?: readonly string[]; resolve(c: Context<AppEnv>): Actor | null | Promise<Actor | null> }. createAuthStrategy(config: AuthConfig) switches on config.strategy.
- development (src/auth/development.ts): every request -> findActorByUsername(db, 'admin'); 401 only if the admin row is missing.
- trusted-header (src/auth/trusted-header.ts): c.req.header(name) trimmed, exact match on users.username; missing/empty/unknown -> 401.
- createApp defaults to developmentStrategy() when deps.auth is omitted (tests rely on this; index.ts always passes the configured one).

CONFIG (src/auth/config.ts, wired into loadConfig() as config.auth)
- CM_AUTH_STRATEGY: 'development' (default) | 'trusted-header'; anything else throws at boot.
- CM_AUTH_TRUSTED_HEADER: REQUIRED with trusted-header (no default, so the name must match what the fronting proxy overwrites); validated as a token, stored lowercased.
- AuthConfig = { strategy:'development' } | { strategy:'trusted-header', header }. Boot logs 'Auth strategy: <name>'.

REGISTERING A STRATEGY (exactly)
1. Add the name to AUTH_STRATEGY_NAMES in packages/shared/src/auth.ts.
2. Add a union member to AuthConfig and a case to resolveAuthConfig (src/auth/config.ts) parsing its env vars.
3. Write src/auth/<name>.ts returning an AuthStrategy; add the case to createAuthStrategy (src/auth/strategy.ts) and export from src/auth/index.ts. TS exhaustiveness on the switch flags any missed step.

PASSWORD SEAM (bead 1.6)
- Add 'password' as above. Its resolve(c) reads the session cookie (hono/cookie getCookie; strategies are the ONLY place allowed to read cookies/headers), looks up a sessions table (new schema file + next migration, user_id FK users ON DELETE CASCADE), returns findActorById(db, session.userId) or null.
- Login/logout routes go in src/auth/routes.ts (authRoutes(), mounted at /auth). Make login reachable signed-out via the strategy's publicPaths (e.g. ['/auth/login']) rather than editing PUBLIC_PATHS, so it is public only when the password strategy is active. Set cookies with Path=/ (proxy passes Set-Cookie unchanged).
- Credentials: add a password-hash column to users or a separate credentials table; users has none today.

WEB PROXY (decision: no strip in apps/web/server/utils/daemon-proxy.ts)
- Stripping the trusted header in Nitro would break the strategy: the only topology it serves is hosted-proxy -> Nitro -> daemon, so the header has to pass through Nitro. Under development (and later password) the daemon ignores the header, so stripping adds nothing there either. Safety therefore relies on (a) trusted-header being opt-in with an explicit header name, (b) the fronting proxy overwriting that header on every request, (c) nothing but that proxy reaching Nitro or the daemon. Documented in the daemon README.
- Follow-up for whoever turns trusted-header on: apps/web/app/plugins/api.ts forwards only the cookie during SSR, so SSR $api calls would 401 under trusted-header; it would need to forward the configured header too.

VERIFIED: 67 daemon tests (new: src/auth/seed.test.ts, config.test.ts, middleware.test.ts; info.test updated); root pnpm lint/typecheck/test (106)/build pass. Built daemon, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: dev on 4810 -> /health, /info, /auth/me (admin, roles [admin]), /projects 200, forged header still admin; restart '0 migration(s) applied', still 1 user/1 role/1 link, same admin id. trusted-header (X-Forwarded-User) on 4811 -> /health 200 without header; /auth/me, /info, /projects 401 without header or with unknown user; admin and an inserted user 'jack' resolve (jack roles []); missing header env or bogus strategy -> boot exits 1.
close_reason: Auth middleware, dev + trusted-header strategies, users/roles seeded; gates green

title: Add SQLite through Drizzle with migrations and a configurable data directory
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

All three predecessors used raw SQL with hand-rolled CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS and no migrations, and v2 also scattered state across JSON files; this hurt every time a schema changed. The daemon must own exactly one SQLite database managed through Drizzle, with migrations generated from the schema and applied automatically on daemon start. Introduce a single configurable data directory (environment variable with a sensible default under the user's home, never inside any repository) that holds the database and, for later work, secrets, worktrees, agent config homes and logs; moving to another machine must be a copy of that directory. Create the directory tree on start. Provide a small, reusable way for later features to get the database handle and the data-directory paths. Non-goals: no application tables beyond what proves the migration path works.
acceptance_criteria: Starting the daemon on an empty data directory creates it and the database with migrations applied; a second start is a no-op; a new migration added to the schema is applied on the next start; the data directory location is configurable and documented; a test covers migration-on-start.
notes:
Database plumbing decisions (later beads depend on these). Full how-to in apps/daemon/README.md.

DRIVER
- better-sqlite3 ^13.0.3 + drizzle-orm ^0.45.4 (latest stable) + drizzle-kit ^0.31.11 (dev). Why better-sqlite3: synchronous, the most battle-tested Drizzle SQLite driver; Drizzle's node:sqlite driver exists only in the 1.0 beta/rc line, and libsql is async-only. Mastra (bead 1.4) may still use @mastra/libsql LibSQLStore pointed at the same file (url file:<data dir>/candy-mountain.db): WAL mode + busy_timeout 5000 let two connections share it, and Drizzle migrations only touch tables in drizzle/.
- Native build: pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds has 'better-sqlite3: true' (prebuilt binary for Node 22/24; without the entry install fails with ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS). Stays external in the tsdown bundle (resolved from node_modules at runtime).

DATA DIRECTORY
- Env CM_DATA_DIR (~ expanded, relative paths resolved against cwd). Default: $XDG_DATA_HOME/candy-mountain if XDG_DATA_HOME is absolute, else ~/.local/share/candy-mountain. NOT ~/.candy-mountain: v2 still uses that on this machine.
- config.ts: DaemonConfig now { host, port, dataDir }; resolveDataDir(env) is exported.
- src/data-dir.ts: dataPaths(root) -> { root, database, secrets, worktrees, agentHomes, logs, run }; ensureDataDir(root) mkdirs all with mode 0700 and returns the paths. Layout: <root>/candy-mountain.db, secrets/, worktrees/, agent-homes/, logs/, run/ (pid files). Need a new subdir? Add it to DataPaths + the ensureDataDir list.
- Move machines = copy the directory with the daemon stopped (WAL -wal/-shm files exist while running).

DB HANDLE
- src/platform.ts startPlatform(dataDir, { migrationsFolder? }) -> { paths, db, appliedMigrations, close }. Called once in src/index.ts at boot; closed on SIGINT/SIGTERM after the server closes. Boot logs '<data dir> (N migration(s) applied)'.
- src/db/index.ts: openDatabase(file, opts) sets pragmas (WAL, synchronous NORMAL, foreign_keys ON, busy_timeout 5000), runs drizzle migrate, returns { db, appliedMigrations, close }. Exports type Db = BetterSQLite3Database<typeof schema>, schema namespace, MIGRATIONS_DIR.
- createApp(deps: AppDeps = { db, paths }) (src/app.ts) now REQUIRES deps; a middleware sets c.var.db and c.var.paths. Route modules type themselves with new Hono<AppEnv>() (AppEnv exported from app.ts). Services take db: Db as a parameter; there is no global singleton.
- Drizzle sync API: db.select().from(t).all()/.get(), db.insert(t).values(...).run(), db.transaction(tx => ...) is synchronous.

SCHEMA AND MIGRATIONS
- Schema files: apps/daemon/src/db/schema/<name>.ts, each re-exported from src/db/schema/index.ts (drizzle.config.ts points at that index). Only table so far: platform_meta (key text PK, value text, updated_at text), a tiny key/value table proving the migration path; free for later use.
- Migrations: apps/daemon/drizzle/ (NNNN_tag.sql + meta/_journal.json + snapshots), committed. Runtime finds them via src/package-root.ts (PACKAGE_ROOT = one level above src/ or dist/, so the same path works under tsx, vitest and the bundled dist/index.mjs). The built daemon must run from the repo checkout (drizzle/ is not copied into dist/).
- Add a table: (1) create src/db/schema/<name>.ts with sqliteTable(...), add export * from './<name>' to schema/index.ts; (2) pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/daemon db:generate --name <short_name>; (3) review + commit the SQL; the next daemon start applies it. Never edit an applied migration. Also: db:check (folder consistency), db:studio (opens the configured db).
- src/db/schema.test.ts fails if the schema has changes without a generated migration (diffs latest snapshot vs schema via drizzle-kit/api).
- Gotcha: Drizzle's SQLite migrator only applies migrations whose journal 'when' is newer than the last applied one. If two parallel beads each generate a migration, the later merger must delete theirs and re-run db:generate after rebasing, or one migration is silently skipped. Migration tags/indices also collide, so parallel beads adding tables should expect to regenerate.

TESTS
- src/testing/index.ts: openTestDatabase() -> in-memory (':memory:') migrated PlatformDatabase (call close()); createTempDataDir() -> { root (non-existent dir inside a fresh mkdtemp), cleanup() } to use with startPlatform(root).
- src/platform.test.ts covers: empty dir -> tree + db + all migrations applied (0700 root); second start applies 0 and keeps data; a newly added migration is applied on the next start (copies drizzle/ to temp and appends a journal entry).

VERIFIED: pnpm lint, typecheck, test (13 tests), build pass; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ok. Built daemon with CM_DATA_DIR=<empty scratch dir>: tree created, '1 migration(s) applied', health ok; second start '0 migration(s) applied'; added a real schema table, drift test failed as expected, db:generate made 0001, rebuilt daemon applied it ('1 migration(s) applied', table present); probe reverted. tsx dev entry also resolves migrations.
close_reason: Drizzle + better-sqlite3, migrations at boot, CM_DATA_DIR verified

title: Build the encrypted write-only secrets store
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Plugins, bots and auth will hold tokens and keys that must never leave the daemon in plaintext and must survive a move to another machine. Build a secrets store modelled on Candy Mountain v2's: values encrypted with AES-256-GCM under a master key supplied by the operator (environment variable, 32 bytes, documented), written atomically with restrictive file permissions or into the platform database as ciphertext (implementer's choice), and keyed by an owner (for example a plugin instance or a bot) plus a secret name. The API is write-only: callers can set, check whether a value is set, delete, and obtain the decrypted value only through an internal daemon-side accessor that is never reachable from an HTTP route. Deleting an owner must delete all of its secrets. Redact secret values from errors and logs. Non-goals: no OAuth, no rotation, no UI.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests prove set/is-set/delete/get-internal behaviour, that a wrong master key fails to decrypt, that deleting an owner removes its secrets, and that no exported HTTP-facing function returns a secret value; the store lives under the daemon's data directory.
notes:
Secrets store decisions (dependents rely on these). Full how-to in apps/daemon/README.md ## Secrets.

MODULE
- apps/daemon/src/secrets/ : index.ts re-exports master-key.ts + store.ts. Import from './secrets' (or '../secrets').
- Exports: MasterKey, SECRETS_KEY_ENV ('CM_SECRETS_KEY'), createSecretsStore, SecretsStore, SecretsWriter, SecretsLockedError, SecretDecryptError, InvalidSecretIdError.

OBTAINING THE STORE
- startPlatform(dataDir, { secretsKey?: MasterKey, migrationsFolder? }) now returns { paths, db, appliedMigrations, secrets, close }. src/index.ts passes config.secretsKey. Use platform.secrets daemon-side.
- Standalone: createSecretsStore(dir: string, key: MasterKey | undefined): SecretsStore (mkdirs dir 0700).
- NOT wired into createApp/AppDeps yet (no HTTP routes this bead). When routes need it, add `secrets: SecretsWriter` to AppDeps and pass platform.secrets.writeOnly. Never put the full store (with get) in c.var; services that need plaintext receive the full SecretsStore as a constructor/function parameter.

API (all synchronous)
- set(owner, name, value: string): void  (non-empty string; throws SecretsLockedError without key)
- isSet(owner, name): boolean
- delete(owner, name): boolean  (true if something was removed; removes empty owner dir)
- deleteOwner(owner): number  (count removed; rm -r the owner dir). Call it when deleting a plugin instance/bot/etc.
- get(owner, name): string | undefined  (INTERNAL, daemon-side only; throws SecretsLockedError without key, SecretDecryptError on wrong key/corrupt/moved file)
- unlocked: boolean  (false when no key; useful for health/readiness)
- writeOnly: frozen SecretsWriter view {unlocked,set,isSet,delete,deleteOwner}, no get. The only form HTTP-facing code may hold.
- owner and name: /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:@-]{0,127}$/ else InvalidSecretIdError (blocks path traversal). Suggested owners: 'plugin:<instanceId>', 'bot:<id>'.

MASTER KEY
- Env CM_SECRETS_KEY: exactly 32 bytes, standard base64 (44 chars with '=' padding; padding optional). Generate: openssl rand -base64 32. Same encoding as v2's CM_SECRETS_KEY.
- config.ts: DaemonConfig.secretsKey: MasterKey | undefined (MasterKey.parse). MasterKey keeps bytes in a #private field; toJSON/toString/inspect print [redacted], so logging config is safe.
- Unset at boot: daemon starts, logs a warning, store is locked (set/get throw SecretsLockedError; isSet/delete/deleteOwner work). Malformed (not base64 / not 32 bytes): loadConfig throws, daemon exits 1 at boot; message never echoes the input.
- Key must be kept outside the data dir and backed up; move = copy data dir + same key.

CRYPTO + FILE LAYOUT
- AES-256-GCM, random 12-byte IV per write, AAD = owner + '\0' + name (a file moved to another owner/name fails to decrypt).
- <dataDir>/secrets/<owner>/<name>.json, JSON {version:1, iv, tag, data} (base64). Files 0600, dirs 0700. Atomic write: temp file '<name>.json.<pid>.<rand>.tmp' opened 'wx' 0600, fsync, rename. No database tables or migrations.

REDACTION
- Errors carry owner/name only, never the value; decrypt failures drop the underlying cause. The store itself logs nothing.

TESTS
- createSecretsStore(join(createTempDataDir().root, 'secrets'), MasterKey.generate()); or startPlatform(temp.root, { secretsKey: MasterKey.generate() }). Use MasterKey.parse(base64) when two stores must share a key. See src/secrets/store.test.ts.
close_reason: Verified by agent; gates green except 1.12 in-flight files
