title: Scaffold the pnpm monorepo with daemon and web app packages
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Nothing exists yet. Create the workspace that every later piece of work lands in: a pnpm monorepo (pnpm only, with a guard that rejects npm) containing a Hono daemon app, a Nuxt 4 web app using Nuxt UI 4 and Tailwind, and a shared package for the wire contract (types and vocabularies both sides import, no build step needed). Root tooling: TypeScript, ESLint, Vitest, and root scripts to lint, typecheck, test, build and run both apps in development with hot reload. The daemon must boot and answer a health endpoint; the web app must render a placeholder page. Pin Node 22+ and a recent pnpm. Keep every package minimal: this bead is the skeleton, not the features. Non-goals: no database, auth, proxy, layout or layers yet.
acceptance_criteria: `pnpm install` succeeds; `pnpm dev` starts both apps with hot reload; `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` all pass on a clean checkout; the daemon's health endpoint returns ok; running npm install is rejected.
notes:
Scaffold decisions (later beads depend on these):

LAYOUT / NAMES
- Root package 'candy-mountain' (private, type:module). pnpm-workspace.yaml globs apps/* and packages/*.
- apps/daemon  -> @candy-mountain/daemon (Hono 4 + @hono/node-server 2)
- apps/web     -> @candy-mountain/web (Nuxt 4.6, @nuxt/ui 4.12, Tailwind 4, Nuxt 4 app/ dir)
- packages/shared -> @candy-mountain/shared: wire contract, NO build step. package.json exports '.' -> ./src/index.ts (TS source). Add new contract modules under packages/shared/src and re-export from src/index.ts. Currently exports HEALTH_PATH, HEALTH_STATUSES, HealthResponse, isHealthResponse, PRODUCT_NAME.
- New workspace packages: same pattern (name @candy-mountain/<x>, exports to src TS, depend via "workspace:*"). The daemon bundles any @candy-mountain/* import (tsdown deps.alwaysBundle), so packages never need a build.

TOOLCHAIN
- packageManager pnpm@12.15.0 (corepack); engines node '^22.22.3 || ^24.15.0 || >=26.0.0' (Nuxt's own range), pnpm >=12.15.0; engineStrict:true in pnpm-workspace.yaml.
- npm guard: engines.npm='please-use-pnpm' + .npmrc engine-strict=true makes npm fail with EBADENGINE before touching node_modules; plus preinstall scripts/only-pnpm.mjs (checks npm_config_user_agent) as a backstop.
- pnpm 12 enforces a minimum release age: specifying a version published in the last few days makes pnpm write minimumReleaseAgeExclude into pnpm-workspace.yaml. Use a slightly older version instead of keeping excludes.
- Dependency build scripts must be allow-listed in pnpm-workspace.yaml 'allowBuilds' (esbuild: true; unrs-resolver, vue-demi: false). Native deps like better-sqlite3 need an entry or install fails with ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS.
- TypeScript pinned ~6.0.3 (typescript-eslint 8.72 requires <6.1, so TS 7 is not usable yet). tsconfig.base.json at root: ES2023, module ESNext, moduleResolution Bundler, strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, verbatimModuleSyntax, noEmit. TS 6 defaults 'types' to [], so node packages set compilerOptions.types:["node"] (daemon does). @types/node ^22 at root so code targets the minimum supported Node.
- Relative imports are extensionless (Bundler resolution; tsx/tsdown/vite handle them).

ROOT SCRIPTS (run from repo root)
- pnpm dev        -> pnpm --parallel --filter './apps/*' dev (daemon + web, hot reload)
- pnpm build      -> pnpm --recursive build (daemon tsdown -> apps/daemon/dist/index.mjs; web nuxt build -> apps/web/.output)
- pnpm lint       -> eslint . (single root run; ESLint 10 picks the nearest config per file: root eslint.config.js = @eslint/js + typescript-eslint recommended for daemon/packages/scripts; apps/web/eslint.config.mjs = withNuxt() from the @nuxt/eslint module, which needs .nuxt, so web postinstall runs 'nuxt prepare')
- pnpm typecheck  -> pnpm --recursive typecheck (daemon/shared: tsc --noEmit; web: nuxt typecheck via vue-tsc)
- pnpm test       -> vitest run with root vitest.config.ts test.projects ['apps/daemon','packages/shared']. Each has its own vitest.config.ts (name daemon/shared, include src/**/*.test.ts). A new package with tests must be added to the projects list. Web has no vitest project yet (add @nuxt/test-utils or a plain node project when web tests appear).

PER-PACKAGE COMMANDS
- daemon: pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/daemon {dev|build|start|typecheck|test}
- shared: pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/shared {typecheck|test}
- web:    pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/web {dev|build|start|typecheck}
- lint is root-only (pnpm lint, or pnpm exec eslint <path>).

DAEMON
- Entry apps/daemon/src/index.ts (serve + SIGINT/SIGTERM graceful close). App factory createApp() in src/app.ts returns the Hono app; tests call createApp().request(path), no network. Add routes there (or in modules mounted there).
- Config: src/config.ts loadConfig(env = process.env) -> { host, port }. Env vars: CM_DAEMON_HOST (default 127.0.0.1, loopback so the daemon is never exposed directly), CM_DAEMON_PORT (default 4310, validated). Env-only for now: no .env loading, no data dir (data dir belongs to the SQLite bead; add it to DaemonConfig/loadConfig with a CM_ prefixed var).
- Health: GET /health (HEALTH_PATH from shared) -> 200 {"status":"ok"}. Not under /api; the proxy bead decides how /api maps to the daemon.
- Dev: 'tsx watch src/index.ts' (restarts on file change). Prod: 'pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/daemon build' then 'node apps/daemon/dist/index.mjs' (script 'start', run from apps/daemon). tsdown config apps/daemon/tsdown.config.ts: ESM, platform node, target node22, no dts; third-party deps stay external (resolved from node_modules at runtime), @candy-mountain/* are bundled in.

WEB
- Nuxt 4, srcDir app/ (app/app.vue wraps <UApp><NuxtPage/>; app/pages/index.vue is the placeholder; app/assets/css/main.css imports tailwindcss and @nuxt/ui). Modules: @nuxt/eslint, @nuxt/ui. devtools off. compatibilityDate 2026-10-01.
- Dev port 4300 (nuxt.config devServer.port). Prod: 'node apps/web/.output/server/index.mjs' (script 'start'); Nitro reads PORT/HOST (NITRO_PORT/NITRO_HOST) and defaults to binding [::]:3000, so the CLI bead should set HOST=127.0.0.1 or similar and PORT=4300 explicitly.
- No proxy, layout, layers or auth yet. Web already depends on @candy-mountain/shared and imports TS source from it directly (Vite handles it).

VERIFIED: pnpm install, lint, typecheck, test (6 tests), build all pass on a clean copy; built daemon answers {"status":"ok"} on 127.0.0.1:4310/health; built web serves the placeholder; pnpm dev brings up both with daemon restart and web HMR; npm install fails with EBADENGINE.
close_reason: Scaffold verified: install/lint/typecheck/test/build pass, health ok, npm rejected

title: Candy Mountain v3
description:
Candy Mountain v3 is a fresh start on Jack's personal codebase-management platform: a long-lived Hono daemon plus a Nuxt 4 / Nuxt UI 4 web app, a registry of local codebases ("projects"), and per-project modules built from small isolated capabilities (Nuxt layers): an Issues viewer over beads, an Agent Hub that drives Claude Code and Codex over ACP (locally and as Slack bots in git worktrees), and an Operations module for uptime and deployments. It folds together the proven parts of Digital Hub (capability/module/grant architecture, chat panel), Clanker Corner (Slack bots over ACP, worktree pool, Claude shim) and Candy Mountain v2 (beads viewer, secrets store).

Plan: .ai-docs/plans/candy-mountain-v3/overview.md and phase-1..10. Research on the three source repos: .ai-docs/research/. Each phase is a child epic; phases 3, 4 and 8 can run alongside each other once phase 2 lands.

title: Capabilities: reading issues and deployments requires a grant, as reading uptime does
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds the capabilities and connections that products built on the @crab-shack platform (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) install, one package each under packages/. The platform lets an admin grant each person a rung on each capability in each workspace (none, view, and higher rungs that allow changes), and gives a capability's routes a way to require a rung before answering. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack (the owner and only developer) has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow AGENTS.md there.

The problem. An agent documenting each package's routes against the code reported two places where a grant does not seem to decide who can read:

- In the issues capability (packages/cap-issues), the routes that read issues and the stream of issue change events do not ask for any rung; only the routes that write, and the one that lists assignees, do. If so, a person granted nothing on issues in a workspace can still read every issue in it.
- In the deployments capability (packages/cap-deployments), no route asks for the deployments rung, and nothing checks the tool that is meant to gate managing deployments. A comment in its routes says reads stay open until a deployments capability exists to gate them; that capability now exists, so the comment describes a past that is over.

By contrast the uptime capability requires its view rung for reads. Treat the report as a lead: first establish, with a request made as a person who has no grant, what each route actually answers, including whatever the platform itself already refuses before a capability's route runs (a person with no access to the workspace at all, for instance).

What to do. Where a person with no rung on a capability can read that capability's data in a workspace, make reading require the view rung, as uptime does, and make managing deployments require what its manifest says it requires. If you find that an open read is deliberate (something else in the product depends on it, such as a home page or another capability reading on a person's behalf), do not close it: say what depends on it and stop for a decision.

A person who has the rung today must see no change.

Not in this bead: changing what the rungs are called or what the manifests declare, and the same code in Candy Mountain's own copies of these packages, which are about to be deleted.
acceptance_criteria:
- The closing note states, for each read route of the issues and deployments capabilities, what a person with no rung received before the change, with the request that showed it.
- Tests show a person with no rung on issues is refused the issue reads and the event stream, and a person with the view rung is answered as before; the same for deployments reads; and managing deployments is refused without the rung its manifest names.
- The stale comment about reads staying open is gone or true.
- Lint, typecheck, test and build are green.

title: Base: a product installs a freshly published capability without waiting a day
description:
Context: the base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm workspace that publishes the platform as five packages under @crab-shack to GitHub Packages (a private registry) at one shared version. A product consumes it by pinning that one exact version in every package.json; platform-new product generates the workspace files a product starts with, and docs/upgrade-path.md tells a product how to move from one platform version to the next. The base is in its fast lane: every push to main that carries a new version publishes it within minutes. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the base Jack (the owner and only developer) has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and that push is the release; follow AGENTS.md in the base.

The problem. pnpm refuses a package version published less than a day ago (its minimum release age) unless the package is exempt in the product's pnpm-workspace.yaml. A generated product exempts the four platform packages it installs, by name, so a platform release can be installed minutes after it is published. Capabilities are about to be published the same way: github.com/crab-shack/capabilities will release each capability and connection as its own package under @crab-shack (cap-<id>, plugin-<id>, and beside them claude-acp and capabilities-testing), from every push to its main. Those packages are not exempt. So a product that adds a capability, or takes a fix to one, within a day of its release has the install refused with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION, or is quietly given an older version. A product chooses which capabilities it installs and adds more over time, and capabilities will be published that do not exist today, so a list of today's names would be out of date as soon as it was written.

The decision (Jack, 2026-11-14): capability packages are exempt from the minimum release age in a product, as the platform packages are. He publishes everything under @crab-shack himself, and the point of the fast lane is that a fix reaches a product within minutes of the push.

What to do. Make that true of a product generated by platform-new product, and say how an existing product gets it. The product's author should have nothing to remember: installing a capability later, including one that did not exist when the product was generated, must not need the exemption edited by hand. Prefer the simplest form pnpm accepts. Exempting everything under @crab-shack with one entry is acceptable if pnpm allows it, because only the organisation can publish under that scope in its registry, so the age check protects nothing there. If pnpm cannot express it without naming each package, stop and report what it can express before building anything, because the command that adds a capability to a product (a later bead) would then have to maintain the list.

Hard requirements. Packages outside @crab-shack keep the minimum release age: it is there on purpose. Moving a platform pin from one young release to the next keeps working exactly as docs/upgrade-path.md describes it today, without touching pnpm-workspace.yaml and without regenerating the lockfile.

Wherever the base's documentation and the generated product's README say what the exemption holds, make them true again, and say in the upgrade page what an existing product changes by hand, once.

No capability is published yet, so prove it with what exists: any package under @crab-shack that a generated product does not exempt today, at a version younger than a day, will do.

Not in this bead: publishing capabilities, the command that adds a capability to a product, and editing Candy Mountain or the capabilities repository (the closing note says what each will have to change).
acceptance_criteria:
- In a product freshly generated by platform-new product, an @crab-shack package the product did not have before, at a version published less than a day earlier, installs without pnpm-workspace.yaml being edited. The closing note names the package and version used, and shows the same install refused or downgraded in a product generated by the previous release.
- In that same product, a package outside @crab-shack younger than a day is still refused or passed over for an older version.
- A generated product moves its platform pin from one young release to the next by following docs/upgrade-path.md, with no library outside @crab-shack changing version in the lockfile.
- The upgrade page says what an existing product changes by hand; the base README and the generated product's README describe the exemption as it now is. The closing note says what Candy Mountain and the capabilities repository will each have to change.
- The base's four gates are green and the release containing the change is in the registry; the closing note names the version.
notes:
RELEASED 0.8.2 (commit f571568 on crab-shack/platform main; Release run 43553611495 published all five packages, tag v0.8.2; CI run 43553611599 green).

WHAT PNPM ACCEPTS (pnpm 12.15.0, the version the base pins): minimumReleaseAgeExclude entries are 'name' (every version), '@scope/*' (every package in the scope, every version) and 'name@version' (pnpm's CHANGELOG states these three forms; tried here). One entry '@crab-shack/*' covers the scope: it passed a lockfile naming a young @crab-shack package and let a fresh resolve take the young version, while '@typescript/...' and typescript stayed held back. pnpm keeps name patterns when it prunes the list (minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune).

THE FORM A GENERATED PRODUCT NOW CARRIES (platform-new product from 0.8.2), at the end of pnpm-workspace.yaml:
  # pnpm holds back a release younger than its minimum age; this lets everything published under @crab-shack (the platform packages and the capabilities) install the day it is released. Every other package keeps the minimum age.
  minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
    - '@crab-shack/*'
It replaces the four platform names that 0.7.2 to 0.8.1 wrote. The platform pin bump is unchanged (pnpm-workspace.yaml is left alone, lockfile not regenerated), and installing a capability later needs no edit to the list. PRODUCT_PLATFORM_PACKAGES is still exported from @crab-shack/platform-config/generate/product but no longer feeds the list. docs/upgrade-path.md, 'A release younger than a day', the base README and the generated product README say so.

PROOF (young package used: @crab-shack/platform-cli@0.8.2, published 2026-11-14T03:50:54Z; also 0.8.1, 03:38:05Z): in a product generated by the published 0.8.2 generator, 'pnpm add -w -D @crab-shack/platform-cli@0.8.2' installs 0.8.2 with pnpm-workspace.yaml byte-identical; the same add without a version takes ^0.8.2; a fresh clone of that product passes 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile' lockfile verification. In a product generated by 0.8.1: the add without a version is DOWNGRADED to 0.5.0; the exact add succeeds only because pnpm (non-strict built-in default) EDITS pnpm-workspace.yaml, appending '@crab-shack/platform-cli@0.8.2'; and a fresh clone whose lockfile names 0.8.2 without that entry is REFUSED: ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION '@crab-shack/platform-cli@0.8.2 was published at 2026-11-14T03:50:54Z, within the minimumReleaseAge cutoff'. Outside the scope (scope-exempt product): typescript@next was passed over for 7.1.0-dev.20261112.1 instead of the young 7.1.0-dev.20261113.1, and a lockfile naming the young nightly was refused with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION (8 entries: typescript and its @typescript/* binaries). Upgrade: a scope-exempt product moved 0.8.0 -> 0.8.1 -> 0.8.2 (each young) by the upgrade page: pnpm install passed verification, pnpm-workspace.yaml untouched, only the four @crab-shack/platform-* entries changed in the lockfile, 0 outside packages. Note: pnpm keeps a lockfile-verification cache in ~/.cache/pnpm/lockfile-verified.jsonl and records a lockfile it just wrote as verified, so a repeat install on the same machine can report 'passes' where a fresh clone fails; test with PNPM_CONFIG_CACHE_DIR pointed at an empty directory.

BY HAND, ONCE, for an existing product or client repository: in pnpm-workspace.yaml under minimumReleaseAgeExclude, delete every entry that starts with '@crab-shack/' (by name, '@crab-shack/platform-web'; versioned, '@crab-shack/platform-web@0.7.1' or '@0.7.0 || 0.7.1'; any pnpm appended itself, as '@crab-shack/platform-cli@0.8.1') and put the one entry '@crab-shack/*' in their place. Leave every other entry. Do it before or with the next platform bump or the first capability install; no lockfile regeneration, no other change. Then 'pnpm install' as usual.

CANDY MOUNTAIN (bead 94z.5.1; pinned 0.5.0): its pnpm-workspace.yaml lists five versioned entries '@crab-shack/platform-cli@0.5.0', '-config@0.5.0', '-daemon@0.5.0', '-sdk@0.5.0', '-web@0.5.0'. Replace all five lines with the single line "  - '@crab-shack/*'". This is required before it moves its platform pin off a young version (otherwise the bump fails verification on the old version) and before it installs any published capability younger than a day.

CAPABILITIES REPOSITORY (bead 94z.3.7; pinned 0.7.1): its pnpm-workspace.yaml lists '@crab-shack/platform-config@0.7.1', '-daemon@0.7.1', '-sdk@0.7.1', '-web@0.7.1'. Replace those four lines with "  - '@crab-shack/*'". Its own cap-/plugin- packages are workspace links there, so the entry matters for its platform pin and for any published @crab-shack package it installs from the registry (claude-acp, capabilities-testing, another capability).

COMMAND THAT ADDS A CAPABILITY (bead 94z.6.1): has nothing to do with the list in a product carrying '@crab-shack/*'; it must not write minimumReleaseAgeExclude entries. Worth knowing: in a product still on the old list, pnpm itself (non-strict built-in default) appends '@crab-shack/cap-<id>@<version>' when an exact young version is installed, and a version range resolves to an older mature version; the command may check for the '@crab-shack/*' entry and point at docs/upgrade-path.md#a-release-younger-than-a-day if it is missing, but need not maintain the list.

Also seen: 'pnpm --package=@crab-shack/platform-config@0.8.2 dlx platform-new product' worked minutes after 0.8.2 was published.
close_reason: Released as platform 0.8.2 (f571568): a generated product exempts the whole @crab-shack scope with one entry; Release run 43553611495 and CI run 43553611599 green; tag v0.8.2 on the remote. Verified by the orchestrator.

title: The development web server listens on the developer's machine only
description:
Context: three repositories on this machine, all Jack's. The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) publishes the platform, including a web shell built on Nuxt and a generator, platform-new product, that writes a new product's apps and scripts. Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) and the capabilities repository (/home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) are built on it. Each has a dev script that starts a daemon and a web app with nuxt dev. In development the platform uses a development auth strategy under which every request is treated as the admin, with no login.

Commits: in the base and in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished (in the base that push is a release; follow its AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md). In Candy Mountain do not commit or push; leave its change in the working tree and say so.

The problem. An agent running the capabilities repository's dev script on this machine (Linux under WSL2) reported that nuxt dev listened on every network interface unless NUXT_HOST=127.0.0.1 was set, while the daemon listened on 127.0.0.1 only. If that is right, then whenever a developer runs pnpm dev, anyone who can reach the machine on the web app's port is the admin of that product: they can read and change everything in it through the web app's proxy to the daemon. The same would hold for the base's own dev script, for Candy Mountain's, and for every product the generator writes. Treat the report as a lead: first establish what the web app's dev server actually binds to here by default, and from where it can be reached.

What to do. Make the development web server reachable from the developer's own machine only, by default, in all three repositories and in what the generator writes for a new product. A developer who wants to reach it from another device must have to ask for that explicitly, and the documentation where pnpm dev is described must say how and that doing so exposes an admin session to that network.

If the dev server already binds to loopback only by default and the report was wrong, change nothing; close with the evidence.

Not in this bead: production or preview serving, the daemon's own bind address, and replacing the development auth strategy.
acceptance_criteria:
- The bead's closing note states what nuxt dev bound to by default on this machine before the change, with the command that showed it.
- With pnpm dev running in each of the three repositories and in a freshly generated product, the web app's port is listening on loopback only (shown from the listening sockets), and the app works from the same machine.
- The documented opt-in makes it listen more widely, and the documentation says what that exposes.
- Each repository's gates are green; the base change is released and the closing note names the version. Candy Mountain's change is left uncommitted and named.
notes:
PAUSED (orchestrator stop). Report CONFIRMED on this machine (WSL2, NAT networking, eth0 172.31.18.224). Evidence: base worktree /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform-j8t at b8f1aba (0.8.0), root 'pnpm dev' with NUXT_PORT=4381 CM_DAEMON_PORT=4391 CM_DATA_DIR/HOME in scratch; 'ss -ltnp "( sport = :4381 or sport = :4391 )"' showed web '*:4381' (all interfaces, v4+v6) and daemon '127.0.0.1:4391'. nuxt dev itself printed 'The dev server is reachable from the network without authentication' and 'Network: http://172.31.18.224:4381/'. curl to 172.31.18.224:4381 from WSL and Windows curl.exe from the Windows host both got 302. WHY: not the platform config and not an env var (NUXT_HOST/NITRO_HOST/HOST unset; platform-web layer sets only devServer.port 4300). It is @nuxt/cli 4.0.1 (used by nuxt 4.6.2 in base and Candy Mountain): dist/listen-*.mjs resolveBindHostname() binds '' (all interfaces) when no host is given and detectIsolatedEnvironment() reports Docker or WSL (/proc/version contains 'microsoft'); on plain Linux/macOS it would bind 'localhost'. So the exposure is WSL/container-specific, but this is Jack's machine. Host precedence in the CLI: --host > NUXT_HOST/NITRO_HOST/HOST env > nuxt.config devServer.host (dev/index.mjs #resolveListenOptions). CAVEAT found: CLI 'eager listen' binds before loading nuxt.config using a hint file apps/web/node_modules/.cache/nuxt/dev-server.json (no hostname until a run with devServer.host set writes it), so the first run after the fix or on a fresh clone may briefly bind all interfaces until config loads; NUXT_DEV_EAGER_LISTEN=0 disables eager bind. Still to measure that window. PLANNED FIX (not yet made): base platform-web nuxt.config devServer { port: 4300, host: '127.0.0.1' } (patch -> 0.8.1, covers base dev app and generated products); same devServer.host line in apps/web/nuxt.config.ts of capabilities (pin 0.7.1) and Candy Mountain (pin 0.5.0) since their pins predate it; opt-in documented as NUXT_HOST=0.0.0.0 pnpm dev with the admin-exposure warning in base README Development distribution, generator README template (platform-config/generate/product.mjs + snapshot), capabilities README, Candy Mountain README. Capabilities and Candy Mountain not yet run. STATE: worktrees platform-j8t (branch j8t at b8f1aba) and capabilities-j8t (branch j8t at 642513e) created, installed, no edits, nothing to commit. Candy Mountain untouched. Nothing running, no locks held. Probe script: scratchpad/j8t/probe-dev.sh, run output scratchpad/j8t/runs/base-before.txt.
DONE (not closed). BEFORE: on this machine (WSL2) nuxt dev bound every interface by default: base 0.8.0 'pnpm dev' with NUXT_PORT=4381, 'ss -ltnp "( sport = :4381 or sport = :4391 )"' showed web *:4381 (daemon 127.0.0.1:4391), reachable at 172.31.18.224 from WSL and from Windows curl.exe; Jack's Candy Mountain nuxt dev (pid 7070) showed *:4300. Cause: @nuxt/cli 4.0.x binds '' (all interfaces) when no host is given and it detects WSL or Docker. Also the CLI's eager listen binds before nuxt.config loads, from NUXT_HOST/--host or a hint in apps/web/node_modules/.cache/nuxt/dev-server.json; measured with config-only fix + cleared hint: *:4381 for ~460ms, then 127.0.0.1:4381. FIX: (1) base 0.8.1 (commit 6b1e73e, Release run 43552533684, CI 43552533727): platform-web nuxt.config devServer { port: 4300, host: '127.0.0.1' }; apps/web and platform-web playground dev scripts are 'NUXT_HOST=${NUXT_HOST:-127.0.0.1} nuxt dev' so the first (eager) bind is loopback too; README Development distribution documents the opt-in. Generator (platform-new product) writes the same dev script and a README paragraph (snapshot updated). (2) capabilities cc855b8: apps/web nuxt.config devServer.host 127.0.0.1, same dev script, README paragraph; pin unchanged (0.7.1). (3) Candy Mountain, UNCOMMITTED in the working tree: apps/web/nuxt.config.ts (devServer.host), apps/web/package.json (dev script), README.md (Commands row + paragraph). OPT-IN: NUXT_HOST=0.0.0.0 pnpm dev (or one address); --host still wins over env, env over config; exposes an admin session to that network under the development auth strategy. A running nuxt dev does not rebind on a config change (soft reload keeps its socket): restart pnpm dev to take the default. PRODUCT ON AN OLDER PLATFORM: either move to >=0.8.1 (config default; first bind on a fresh clone/cleared cache still all interfaces under WSL/Docker until apps/web/package.json dev script is changed) and set apps/web dev script to 'NUXT_HOST=${NUXT_HOST:-127.0.0.1} nuxt dev'; or, without moving, add devServer: { host: '127.0.0.1' } to apps/web/nuxt.config.ts plus that dev script.
close_reason: Fixed in all three repositories. Base released as 0.8.1 (6b1e73e): platform-web devServer.host 127.0.0.1 and the dev script sets NUXT_HOST before the CLI's first bind, which closes a ~460ms window on every interface; generator README documents the opt-in. Capabilities: cc855b8 on main. Candy Mountain: README.md, apps/web/nuxt.config.ts and apps/web/package.json changed and left uncommitted for Jack. Loopback-only shown from listening sockets in base, capabilities, a scratch clone of Candy Mountain and a generated product; still reachable from the Windows host through localhost. Jack's already-running dev server keeps its old socket until restarted.

title: Capabilities: CI passes on GitHub's runners
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ (capabilities cap-*, connections plugin-*, the Claude Code ACP shim claude-acp and shared test support) for products built on the @crab-shack platform (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform), plus a development distribution under apps/ (a daemon app and a web app over a root product.yaml named Capabilities that enables everything). The packages were moved out of the product Candy Mountain. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow the agent instructions file in that repository.

The problem. The repository's CI workflow runs install, lint, typecheck, test and build on GitHub's runners for every push to main. It now installs, lints and typechecks, but Test fails: in the claude-acp package, three tests that start the shim as a standalone executable and talk to it (a permission decision relayed, framed ACP requests exchanged and resumed, a session id carried from one invocation to a fresh one) each time out at the default five seconds. The same tests pass on Jack's machine, where the shim has been built at some point. One further failure was printed in that run, "fails an attempt whose CLI never shows a link", and because the run stops at the first failing package it is not known whether any other package's tests pass on a runner.

Why it matters. The repository is about to publish from every push to main with its checks running beside the publish. A check that is always red tells nobody anything, and a real regression would hide behind it.

What to do. Find out why those tests fail on a runner and pass locally, and make the whole CI workflow green on GitHub's runners for a push to main, with every package's tests having actually run there. Fix the cause where there is one (a test that depends on something having been built, on a tool that is not on the runner, or on timing that a slower machine does not meet) rather than raising timeouts until it passes; if a longer timeout really is the right answer for a test that starts a process, say why. A test that cannot run on a runner because it needs something only a developer machine has (a logged-in CLI, the bd command) may skip there, as some already do, but it must say in its skip why, and the tests that can run must run.

Do not weaken what the tests check, and do not remove a gate from the workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
- A CI run on GitHub for a commit on main finishes green with install, lint, typecheck, test and build all executed.
- The run's log shows every package's test task ran; the bead's closing note lists which tests skip on a runner and why.
- The cause of the claude-acp failures is stated in the closing note.
- The four gates stay green on a fresh clone on this machine.
notes:
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from the agent of 94z.3.9: with five agents loading this machine, cap-issues src/watcher.test.ts 'within two seconds of bd create' took 2441ms and failed in a full pnpm test run (it passes alone, 8 of 8). That is the kind of timing a slower runner will not meet either; look at it with the claude-acp timeouts.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from the agent of 94z.4.1 (landed as 26f6e30; its bead note has the full list of timing-fragile tests and the local reproduction). (1) The failures are reproducible on this machine without a runner: with other work loading the machine, TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm test failed 4 of 4 times on 26f6e30 and 2 of 2 on its parent 642513e, always in claude-acp (the standalone-executable tests at 5000ms, and a 20ms sleep-then-assert in permissions.test.ts), once in cap-issues watcher.test.ts (a 2000ms wait); claude-acp alone passes 66 of 66. So this is load, not something missing on the runner: with every dist removed those tests pass here, because they run the CLI from source through tsx. (2) CI on 26f6e30: Install, Lint and Typecheck pass; Test fails in claude-acp; Build was skipped, so pnpm build with the package check (scripts/check-packages.mjs) has never run on a runner: your green run is its first. (3) plugin-claude-code 'fails an attempt whose CLI never shows a link' shows a failure mark in a task turbo then cancelled, on 26f6e30 and on 0dcf164 alike. (4) The CI workflow cancels in-progress runs on main, so a rerun can cancel another agent's run; several agents are landing today. (5) Local gates matter as much as the runner now: five agents share this machine and each has to rerun fragile packages alone to call the test gate green, so a fix that makes these tests hold under load is worth more than one that only passes on an idle runner.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from the agent of j8t: besides the claude-acp timeouts, two login-attempt tests in plugin-claude-code fail on the runner on every recent commit on main (26f6e30, 84e726d, b0f24e0, e8ca4d8 run 43556737409, cc855b8 run 43557279907), so they are not a one-off mark in a cancelled task; under load they also fail on this machine on some runs and pass on rerun. They are in this bead's scope: the workflow is green only when they pass or skip with a stated reason.
LANDED as 4df580c on main (three commits: 9a425f8, 5e115b8, 4df580c; tests and test support only, every tarball byte-identical before/after, no changeset, the Release run published nothing). CI on main for 4df580c: run 43577662949 green with install, lint, typecheck, test (all 17 test tasks ran) and build (pack check "16 packages pack as they would publish" ran on a runner for the first time). Release run 43577663073 green, "Every package version is already released".

CAUSE (claude-acp). Not a missing build: the tests run the CLI from source through tsx and pass with every dist removed. Each start of the executable is a fresh node that loads the ACP SDK and zod (about 0.25s idle here, 0.35s through tsx; tsx is only about a third of it). That cost grows with CPU contention: pinned to two busy cores it is about 1s per start, and on the runner (private repo, small runner, turbo running up to 10 vitest processes at once) a test with one start took 2-5s and a test with two starts 4.4-7.3s. Vitest's 5s default is sized for in-process tests, so the two-start tests crossed it. Fix: tests that start the executable get executableTimeout(starts) = 10s per start (packages/claude-acp/src/test-support/cli.ts), a hang bound, not a speed claim. Observed on the main run: 5.1s for a one-start test, 7.3s for a two-start test. The in-process tests keep 5s.

RACES FIXED (waits for the condition instead of a sleep or a too-short clock): claude-acp permissions.test.ts "cancelling the turn" (20ms sleep then assert -> vi.waitFor pendingCount 1); "the turn clock stops..." (the 500ms wait now starts once the permission request has arrived); plugin-claude-code "fails an attempt whose CLI never shows a link" (the 200ms prompt timeout could end the fake before it wrote fake-env.json -> ENOENT; the wrapper now records its pid before exec); plugin-claude-code "expires an attempt after its ttl" (300ms ttl ran out before the fake showed its link -> ttl 2s, waits for the expiry). Both plugin-claude-code tests failed on the runner on their own on every commit from 26f6e30 to cc855b8, not as an artefact of a cancelled task. cap-issues watcher "within two seconds of bd create" is now timed from bd's exit (bd's own start-up, which grows with load, is not the watcher's latency). cap-acp "finds the built Claude shim" skipped silently unless claude-acp had been built (never in CI, where Test precedes Build): it now runs in both states, checking the built path or the "run pnpm build first" error.

TESTS THAT SKIP ON A RUNNER, AND WHY (from the main run's log): needs the bd command, which runners do not have: cap-issues routes, write-routes, events-routes (1), bd-runner (1), watcher (7 of 8); cap-bots "bot session end to end" and "bd from a worktree with beadsEnvForWorktree" (the reason is now a comment beside each hasBd). Needs the real claude CLI and the built shim: cap-acp integration.test.ts "ACP harness with the real claude CLI" (3 tests; the logged-in prompts are opt-in with CM_TEST_CLAUDE_CONFIG_HOME / CM_TEST_CODEX_HOME). Everything else runs on the runner, including cap-bots' pnpm install tests.

WHAT TO EXPECT LOCALLY: a forced full run (TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm test, under flock /tmp/cm-heavy-gates.lock) passed 17/17 on this machine at load averages 19-24 and 12-15, and on a fresh clone of 4df580c: lint 19/19, typecheck 18/18, forced test 17/17 in 1m58s at load 3-14, build with the pack check green. The rule "rerun the fragile package alone" should no longer be needed: a failure in claude-acp, plugin-claude-code or cap-issues watcher in a full run is now worth reading as real. The executable tests still take seconds each under load; that is expected.

RESIDUAL / FOLLOW-UPS: (1) cap-issues watcher.test.ts start() sleeps 200ms to let the baseline fingerprint settle; if the first bd write lands before the baseline is read, no event fires. bd's own start-up makes this rare; a real fix needs the watcher to expose when its baseline is ready. (2) plugin-codex "expires an attempt..." uses ttlMs 400 the same way; if the fake has not started by then, loginPid is undefined and the pid check passes vacuously. Not seen failing. (3) The actions (checkout, setup-node, pnpm/action-setup @v4) target Node 20, and GitHub forces them onto Node 24 with a deprecation annotation; bump them when a v5 is wanted. (4) ci.yml concurrency is now per commit on push (fdbd377), so runs on main no longer cancel each other; pull requests still cancel per ref, which is right.
close_reason: Landed as 4df580c on crab-shack/capabilities main (three commits, tests and test support only; packed tarballs byte-identical, so no changeset and nothing published). CI run 43577662949 on main green with install, lint, typecheck, test and build all executed (first time the pack check ran on a runner); Release run 43577663073 found nothing to publish. Cause: each start of the claude-acp executable costs a fresh node process that slows with CPU contention, against vitest's 5s default; plus sleep-then-assert races. Forced full pnpm test passes locally under load. Skip list and cause in the bead note.

title: Base: a product can move its platform pin off a release younger than pnpm's minimum release age
description:
Context: the base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm workspace that publishes the platform as five packages under @crab-shack to GitHub Packages at one shared version. A product, or the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities), consumes it by pinning that one exact version in every package.json. The base is in its fast lane: every push to main that carries a new version publishes it within minutes, so releases can be minutes or hours apart. docs/upgrade-path.md in the base tells a product how to move from one platform version to the next, and platform-new product generates the workspace files a product starts with. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the base Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and that push is the release; follow AGENTS.md in the base.

The problem. An agent setting up the capabilities repository pinned platform 0.7.0, then moved the pin to 0.7.1 about an hour later, when 0.7.0 was still younger than pnpm's minimum release age. The install was refused with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION. Its account of the cause: the workspace exempts the pinned platform version from the minimum release age; when the pin moved, the old version lost its exemption while the lockfile still named it, and pnpm refused the lockfile. It got past this by rebuilding the lockfile, which is not something a product should have to do, because a rebuilt lockfile lets every other library drift. Treat that account as a lead: reproduce the failure first and confirm the cause.

Why it matters. While the platform is in active development a product will often upgrade from a release that is only minutes or hours old. Today the upgrade page does not mention this, so the first person to hit it has an install that fails with a message about release age and no stated way forward.

What to do. Make moving the pin from a young release to the next one work by following the upgrade page, without regenerating the lockfile. Whether that is a change to what the generated workspace files and the upgrade tooling do, or a documented step, is yours to decide once you have reproduced it; prefer the one that leaves the product author nothing to remember. Do not weaken the minimum release age for packages outside @crab-shack: it is there on purpose.

If the fix changes what a product's workspace files contain, say in the upgrade page what an existing product has to change by hand.
acceptance_criteria:
- The failure is reproduced and its cause stated in the bead's closing note.
- A product pinned to a platform release younger than the minimum release age can move to the next release by following docs/upgrade-path.md: pnpm install succeeds and no library outside @crab-shack changes version in the lockfile.
- The minimum release age still applies to packages outside @crab-shack.
- The base's four gates are green and the release containing the change is in the registry.
notes:
RELEASED 0.7.2 (commits 79c56fa + 6bfe0c7 on crab-shack/platform main; Release run 43440148697 published all five packages, tag v0.7.2; CI run 43440148685 green).

CAUSE (reproduced 2026-11-13 14:05 UTC with real releases 0.7.0 -> 0.7.1, both younger than pnpm 12's built-in minimumReleaseAge of 1440 min): before it resolves anything, pnpm install verifies every entry already in pnpm-lock.yaml against the supply-chain policies. The generated pnpm-workspace.yaml exempted the platform packages at the pinned version only ('@crab-shack/platform-web@0.7.0'). Moving that entry to the new version along with the pins took the old version out of the list while the lockfile still named it, so verification failed: ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION, '4 lockfile entries failed verification: @crab-shack/platform-*@0.7.0 was published at ... within the minimumReleaseAge cutoff'. (Bumping only package.json and leaving the list alone happens to work, because the built-in default is non-strict and pnpm appends '@0.7.0 || 0.7.1' to each entry, but the README told authors the list carries the pinned version, so editing it is the natural move.)

WHAT CHANGED: platform-new product (platform-config 0.7.2) now writes minimumReleaseAgeExclude as the four package names without a version ('@crab-shack/platform-config', '-daemon', '-sdk', '-web'), so a bump never touches pnpm-workspace.yaml. Nothing else is exempted; every other package keeps the minimum age (shown: typescript@next resolved to the older mature nightly, and a lockfile naming young typescript@7.1.0-dev.20261113.1 was refused with ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION while young platform 0.7.1 in the same lockfile passed). docs/upgrade-path.md has a new section 'A release younger than a day'; step 3 and the example say pnpm-workspace.yaml stays as it is; the generated README and base README say the list is by name.

BY HAND, ONCE, for an existing product or the capabilities repository (pinned 0.7.1, versioned entries): in pnpm-workspace.yaml replace each '@crab-shack/platform-<name>@<version>' (or '@a || b') entry under minimumReleaseAgeExclude with '@crab-shack/platform-<name>', before or in the same change as the next bump; then bump the pins and pnpm install as usual. Verified: a 0.7.1-generated product doing this and moving to 0.7.2 installs with no outside library changing in the lockfile. Do not run 'pnpm clean --lockfile' as the pnpm error suggests. Candy Mountain (0.5.0) needs the same when it next moves, if its workspace has versioned entries.
close_reason: Released as platform 0.7.2 (79c56fa + 6bfe0c7 on crab-shack/platform main). Release run 43440148697 published all five packages, v0.7.2 tagged; CI run 43440148685 green. Cause confirmed on real young releases 0.7.0 to 0.7.1: pnpm checks every lockfile entry against the release-age policy before resolving, and the generated pnpm-workspace.yaml exempted the platform packages only at the pinned version, so moving that entry left the old version unexempted while the lockfile still named it. Fix: platform-new product writes the exemption as the four platform package names without a version; docs/upgrade-path.md has a new section and the one-time edit for existing products. Agent showed the upgrade working from a young release three ways and that a young outside package (a typescript nightly) is still refused. Orchestrator checked commits, tag, runs, the generator source and that the worktree is removed. The exemption now covers every version of the four named packages, which is broader than before.

title: Capabilities: identifiers that name Candy Mountain (issue-edit author, User-Agent, Slack MCP server) come from the product
description:
Context: three repositories on this machine, all Jack's (GitHub user kingrea, the only developer).

The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) holds the platform: a daemon, a web shell, an SDK with the capability contract, shared configuration and a CLI, published to GitHub Packages under @crab-shack at one shared version. A product is plain data (name, theme, and the lists of capabilities it enables) joined at boot with capability definitions; the platform gives every capability a context at start that carries facts about the product it is running in, including the product's name.

The capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ that were moved out of Candy Mountain with their history: eight capabilities (cap-*), six connections (plugin-*), the Claude Code ACP shim and shared test support. Any product can install them. docs/origin.md there says where they came from.

Candy Mountain (github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) is the first product and until now the only one. It has existing databases and running bots. A second product with a different name is about to start using some of the same capabilities.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one. Do not change Candy Mountain or the base.

The problem. The capabilities were written when Candy Mountain was the only product, and a few of them still identify themselves to the outside world as Candy Mountain, in machine-readable form rather than in prose. An earlier bead replaced the words "Candy Mountain" in text people read; these were left because changing them carelessly would change behaviour. In a product with another name each of them is wrong:

- cap-issues stamps the edits it makes to a project's issue database with an author whose address ends in @candy-mountain, and falls back to an actor called candy-mountain when it has no other. That author is recorded in the history of the product's issue database.
- cap-deployments, plugin-netlify, plugin-repository and cap-uptime send a User-Agent that names candy-mountain to the services they call.
- plugin-slack registers an MCP server whose name begins candy_mountain. Agents see that name inside the names of the tools it offers, and instructions or allow-lists may refer to those tool names.

What to do. Make each of these come from the product the capability is running in, using what the platform already gives a capability about its product, so that a product with another name identifies itself by its own name in all three places.

The hard requirement: in a product named Candy Mountain every one of these values must come out exactly as it is today, character for character. Candy Mountain's issue history already carries the present author address, and its bots and their instructions already use the present tool names; neither may shift. Find every place that refers to these values (including bot instructions, tests and anything that builds a tool name) and keep them consistent with the derived value.

If what the platform gives a capability is not enough to produce Candy Mountain's present values exactly, or does not reach one of the places that needs it, stop and report what is missing. Do not add a product setting, and do not change the platform, to get there.

Not in this bead: environment variables (the CM_ prefix stays), capability ids, plugin type ids, layer ids, table names, migrations and anything already stored. Temporary folder names that begin candy-mountain- may stay as they are: nobody is shown them and other code may match on them. Do not change what any request or commit does beyond how the product is named in it.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a product named Candy Mountain, tests show the issue-edit author address, the fallback actor, each User-Agent and the Slack MCP server name are exactly what they are today.
- With a product of another name, tests show each of those carries that product's name and none contains candy-mountain or candy_mountain.
- Searching packages/ for "@candy-mountain" finds nothing outside changelog or history text.
- Nothing that refers to the Slack tools by name (bot instructions, allow-lists, tests) is left pointing at a name the server no longer has.
- Lint, typecheck and test are green in the capabilities repository, and Candy Mountain's working tree is untouched.
notes: Landed 55a3426 on capabilities main. RULE: every machine identifier for the product is slugify(productName) with slugify from @crab-shack/platform-sdk root entry (the SDK's own rule: NFKD, strip marks, lowercase, runs of non-[a-z0-9] -> '-', trim, max 64; agrees with platform-config dataDirName for ASCII names). No wrapper package: no runtime package is shared by all users, and adding one would mean package.json edges; import slugify directly. Derived values: issue-edit fallback actor = s; author = '<actor> <<actor>@s>' (cap-issues createDoltCommentEditor(productName, run)); User-Agent = s (cap-deployments custom endpoint and Netlify source via LiveVersionReadContext.productName; cap-bots repository calls via BotReadDeps.productName); uptime User-Agent = s + '-uptime' (cap-uptime uptimeUserAgent, MonitorCheckContext.productName); Slack MCP server = s with '-' -> '_' + '_slack' (plugin-slack slackMcpServerName / slackPostBlocksTool(productName); cap-bots wrappedMcpTools/wrappedMcpToolRules(productName), resolveBotPosture input.productName, assertPostureNotWidened(posture, scope, productName) all build from slackPostBlocksTool so server name and allow rule cannot drift). Candy Mountain: candy-mountain, admin <admin@candy-mountain>, candy-mountain-uptime, candy_mountain_slack, mcp__candy_mountain_slack__post_blocks (pinned literally in tests). Harbour: harbour, harbour-uptime, harbour_slack. API: createNetlifyOperations/createNetlifyClient and createRepositoryOperations now REQUIRE options.userAgent. WAIVED (left on candy-mountain, for 94z.3.7 after 94z.8): plugin-netlify/src/plugin-type.ts healthCheck passes userAgent 'candy-mountain'; plugin-repository/src/plugin-type/definition.ts PLATFORM_CALL_USER_AGENT = 'candy-mountain' used by healthCheck and the branches action; tests pin both. STORED: agent_sessions.posture (platform table, JSON) keeps each bot session's Claude flags (--allowedTools ...mcp__<server>__post_blocks, --append-system-prompt naming the tool) and Codex developerInstructions; resume/prompt reuse the stored posture. Nothing migrated; unchanged for Candy Mountain. Removed exports: SLACK_POST_BLOCKS_TOOL, WRAPPED_MCP_TOOLS, WRAPPED_MCP_TOOL_RULES, editCommentInDolt, issueWriter; issuesRoutes(repository, productName, watcher?).
close_reason: Landed on crab-shack/capabilities main as 55a3426 (option C). Identifiers derive from the product by the SDK's slugify(productName): issue-edit author and fallback actor (cap-issues), User-Agents (cap-deployments, cap-bots GitHub calls, cap-uptime), Slack MCP server name via slackMcpServerName in plugin-slack (hyphens to underscores), and the bot allow rule and instruction text built from the same slackPostBlocksTool(productName). Candy Mountain's values are pinned as literals in tests; Harbour shown as the second product. Orchestrator checked: non-test source under packages/ names candy-mountain only in temp folder prefixes and the two waived plugin-type files. Waived by the orchestrator: criterion 2 for the Netlify health check, the repository health check and the branches action, which the platform calls without a product name (94z.8 then 94z.3.7); criterion 3 to the letter, because two test pins in cap-issues write-routes.test.ts contain the literal @candy-mountain on purpose. Stored: agent_sessions.posture keeps each bot session's allow rule and prompt text; nothing migrated, unchanged for Candy Mountain. Removed exports: SLACK_POST_BLOCKS_TOOL, WRAPPED_MCP_TOOLS, WRAPPED_MCP_TOOL_RULES, editCommentInDolt, issueWriter; createNetlifyOperations and createRepositoryOperations now require options.userAgent; issuesRoutes takes productName. Agent reported four gates green; not run from a fresh clone.

title: Base: a product with installed capabilities can run its daemon tests while linked to a base checkout alone
description:
Context: the base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) publishes the five @crab-shack/platform-* packages; platform-config holds the vitest presets every package extends and the commands platform-link, platform-unlink and platform-check-linked (docs/linking.md describes them). A product can now install capability packages from the registry (@crab-shack/cap-*, @crab-shack/plugin-*), whose daemon half is built JavaScript, beside capabilities it holds as TypeScript source in its own workspace. Read AGENTS.md in the base first: agents have Jack's standing permission to commit and push to main there, and under the fast lane that push is the release.

Problem: when such a product is linked to a base checkout alone (pnpm platform-link <base>, without also linking a capabilities checkout), every daemon test file fails to load with an error like 'Cannot find module .../platform-sdk/src/daemon/activity'. Vitest treats the installed capability as an external dependency and runs its built output with plain Node, and that output imports the platform, which while linked resolves to the base checkout's TypeScript source that plain Node cannot load. Typecheck, lint and a tsx import all work. Found in bead candy-mountain-v3-94z.2.3 on a fixture product; platform-link now names the affected packages and docs/linking.md tells the developer to link the capabilities checkout too. That makes linking both checkouts the only way to try a platform change in a product that installs capabilities, which is what Candy Mountain becomes at the end of this plan, and the point of the base link is that a platform change can be tried in a product without a release.

What to do: make a product's tests load while it is linked to the base alone and has installed capabilities, without the product editing its own vitest configuration. The likely place is the vitest preset in platform-config (have vitest transform, rather than externalise, installed packages that depend on the platform while a link is in place), but the mechanism is yours to choose. An unlinked product must behave exactly as today. If it turns out not to be achievable without unacceptable cost, say so with the evidence and leave the documented workaround; do not ship a half-measure.

The change carries a changeset and is released by pushing to main.
acceptance_criteria: In a product generated by platform-new product with one capability installed from a packed tarball: linked to a base checkout alone, the daemon app's tests load and pass, and platform-link no longer warns that they cannot. Unlinked, the same product's four gates give the same results as before the change. The base's existing link tests and its four gates pass. docs/linking.md is true for the new behaviour. The release containing this is in the registry.
notes:
RELEASED as platform 0.7.1 (commit b7bf9c1 on crab-shack/platform main, work commit 761ee45; Release run 43432406584 published all five packages and tagged v0.7.1; CI run 43432406785 green).

WHAT CHANGED FOR A PRODUCT: a product linked to a base checkout alone (pnpm platform-link <base>) now runs tests that import a capability it installs as a release. No product change needed: the vitest preset definePackageTestConfig (@crab-shack/platform-config/vitest) now carries a Vite plugin (platform-config:linked-platform) that adds to test.server.deps.inline each installed package (in node_modules) that imports a platform package resolving to a checkout's source, found by walking the dependencies of the package under test (through workspace packages and through installed platform dependents). Unlinked, or linked to a capabilities checkout alone, the platform is a release and the plugin adds nothing. A package whose vitest.config.ts does not start from definePackageTestConfig still fails while linked with 'Cannot find module .../platform-sdk/src/...' (docs/linking.md failure table says so).

CAUSE CONFIRMED: vitest externalises an installed package; node 24 type-strips the checkout's platform-sdk/src/daemon/index.ts but cannot resolve its extensionless relative imports ('./activity'). Even if it could, the capability would have loaded a second copy of the SDK beside the one vitest transforms for the product.

MESSAGES: platform-link no longer prints '<pkg> is installed as built output ... Link the capabilities checkout too'. New internal export sourceDependents(root) in platform-config/link (not a package entry point).

VERIFIED on a fixture only (platform-new product Harbour + @crab-shack/cap-notes built with tsdown, packed, installed from a local HTTP tarball): linked to the base alone daemon 33/33, web 4/4, cap-board 13/13 tests pass, typecheck passes; unlinked the four gates match the 0.7.0 baseline with the changed platform-config installed. Not exercised on Candy Mountain or with a real capabilities checkout.
close_reason: Released as platform 0.7.1 (761ee45 + b7bf9c1 on crab-shack/platform main). Release run 43432406584 published all five packages, v0.7.1 tagged; CI run 43432406785 green. The vitest preset now inlines installed packages whose platform import resolves to a checkout's source, and platform-link no longer warns. title: Base: list the available capabilities from inside a product
description:
Context: three repositories on this machine, all Jack's (GitHub user kingrea, the only developer).

The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm 12 workspace run through Turborepo that holds the platform. It publishes five packages to GitHub Packages (npm.pkg.github.com, scope @crab-shack, private) at one shared version (0.5.0 at the time of writing): platform-daemon (the Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle, with a /testing entry that is the daemon test kit), platform-web (the web shell, a Nuxt layer published as source, with the layer-list helper that finds a capability's layer from the webLayer field of a dependency's package.json), platform-sdk (wire types, the product configuration type, defineCapabilityDefinition and the capability contract), platform-config (the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends, the cm-packages boundary lint and its package-boundaries helpers, the commands platform-link, platform-unlink and platform-check-linked, and the generators platform-new capability, connection and product) and platform-cli. Beside them, unpublished: packages/cap-template and packages/plugin-sample (the worked examples the generators copy), and apps/ with a root product.yaml (the base's own development distribution). docs/ holds capability-authors.md, linking.md, registry-access.md, upgrade-path.md, capability-majors.md and product-file.md; CONTRIBUTING.md holds the changeset rule.

Candy Mountain (github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) is a product built on the base. Today it also holds the source of sixteen shared packages under its own scope @candy-mountain: eight feature or service capabilities (packages/cap-acp, cap-bots, cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, cap-deployments, cap-issues, cap-team, cap-uptime), six connections that each bring the one plugin type their id names (packages/plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex, plugin-heroku, plugin-netlify, plugin-repository, plugin-slack), the Claude Code ACP shim (packages/claude-acp) and shared test support (packages/testing). The product itself is packages/candy-mountain (plain data) and thin apps: apps/daemon lists every capability definition and runs the platform's runDaemon, apps/web extends platform-web and the capability layers, apps/cli is the bin.

The capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) is where those sixteen packages are moving. Each is published on its own, at its own version, as @crab-shack/cap-<id>, @crab-shack/plugin-<id>, @crab-shack/claude-acp and @crab-shack/capabilities-testing. A product then picks capabilities by depending on them, as it already depends on the platform, and can write its own beside them. Capability ids, plugin type ids, layer ids, table names and migration histories never change in this move, because an existing database identifies each capability's migrations by its id.

A capability is one package with a daemon half (a definition made with defineCapabilityDefinition, exported from the package's root entry as a factory, stating its own package name and the SDK major it targets) and, when it has UI, a web half (a Nuxt layer at the package root). It owns its tables and its own migration history. A product is plain data (name, theme, scope label, and the id lists of capabilities, modules, plugin types and layers) joined at boot with the capability definitions; the daemon refuses to boot, naming the offender, when they disagree.

Commits: in the base and in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and once a repository's fast lane exists that push is also the release; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one. In Candy Mountain do not commit or push unless the orchestrator tells you to. The plan this bead comes from is in Candy Mountain at .ai-docs/plans/shared-capabilities/, for background only: this bead is complete without it.

A product can add a published capability with one command, but only if its author already knows the id. The list of what exists is in the README of the capabilities repository, which someone in a product's terminal is not looking at. Picking a capability should not start with opening another repository.

Let a product list the capabilities available to it from the command line, beside the add command in platform-config: each one's id, kind (feature capability, service-only capability or connection), one-sentence description, what it needs and its current version, marking the ones the product already has and the ones that target an SDK major other than the product's.

The list must come from what is actually published, not from a list kept by hand in the base, so a capability published tomorrow appears without a platform release. The capabilities repository generates its catalogue from its packages; how that reaches a product (the registry itself, something the capabilities repository publishes on each release, or another route) is yours to choose. If the capabilities repository has to publish something for this, make that change there and release it through its fast lane. It must work with the read-only registry token a product already has, and fail with a clear message when the registry cannot be reached.

Document it where the add command is documented. The change carries a changeset and is released by pushing to main (the base's fast lane).
acceptance_criteria:
- In a product generated by platform-new product, the command lists every capability and connection published from the capabilities repository with id, kind, description, needs and version.
- After adding one capability, the list marks it and the ones it brought as present.
- A capability published after the platform release in use appears in the list without a platform change.
- Without registry access the command fails with a message saying what to check.
- The command is documented beside the add command; the release containing this is in the registry.
notes:
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14): read the closing note of 94z.6.1 (platform 0.9.1) before designing. It lists what GitHub Packages keeps and drops in registry metadata (description survives; webLayer, exports, type and peerDependenciesMeta do not), that pnpm has no way to list a scope, and the reusable functions platform-add already has for asking the registry.
AGENT NOTE (94z.6.3, 2026-11-14). Released as platform 0.10.0 (crab-shack/platform main 134ce81, Release run 43585082557 green, CI run 43585082543 green, tag v0.10.0). Bead not closed by the agent.

THE COMMAND. pnpm platform-list (bin platform-list of @crab-shack/platform-config, beside platform-add; code packages/platform-config/list/index.mjs, bin/platform-list.mjs; not in the exports map). No arguments; exit 0 or 1; changes nothing. Run anywhere inside a product (outside one it refuses like platform-add). Prints '<n> capabilities and connections published to @crab-shack. This product runs the platform at <v>, SDK major <m>.', then groups 'Feature capabilities', 'Service-only capabilities', 'Connections' (and 'Capabilities whose description does not say their kind' for a package without the prefix), one entry per id: '  <id>  <newest version>  <what it does>', then 'Needs <peer ids>.' plus the package's own 'Also needs ...' sentence, then marks: 'In this product.' / 'In this product, at <installed>.' (behind the newest) / 'In this product as its own <name> (<dir>), not the published package.' / 'In this product: <file> lists ...' and 'Targets SDK major N, and this product's platform is SDK major M, so it cannot be added.' Ends 'Add one with pnpm platform-add <id>; it brings what the id needs.' Room left: marks(entry, product) in list/index.mjs is where a 'needs a newer platform than this product has' line goes once a capability states its oldest platform (the bead for that can read it from wherever it lands and add one line there).

Output in a product generated by the released 0.10.0 generator, after pnpm platform-add deployments (real registry): all 14 listed (bots 0.1.0, chat-claude-code 0.1.1, chat-codex 0.1.0, deployments 0.1.1 [Needs heroku and netlify. Also needs the repository plugin type, which plugin-repository brings and this package does not install.], issues 0.1.0, team 0.1.1 [Also needs the hasBots workspace fact ...], uptime 0.1.1; acp 0.1.0; claude-code, codex, heroku, netlify, repository, slack), with deployments, heroku, netlify and repository marked 'In this product.'

THE ROUTE (nothing new published, nothing kept in the base). 1. pnpm config get @crab-shack:registry in the product. 2. For npm.pkg.github.com: GET https://api.github.com/orgs/crab-shack/packages?package_type=npm&per_page=100 (Link pagination; /users/<scope> if the org 404s) with the token pnpm config get //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken returns (user-level ~/.npmrc, pnpm auth.ini, or a ${VAR} there; never printed). A classic read:packages token is enough (verified: the token on this machine has exactly read:packages). Any other registry: GET <registry>-/v1/search?text=@crab-shack/ (used by the fixture registry in tests). 3. Every cap-/plugin- name, pnpm view <name> --json in the product, 4 at a time: version, description, peerDependencies; no peer on platform-sdk = library, left out. 4. Kind from the description prefix ('<anything> capability: ' feature, 'capability, service only: ' service, 'connection: ' connection; otherwise plugin- = connection, cap- = kind unknown), what it does = the rest up to ' Also needs ', which is shown verbatim. So the list DEPENDS ON: the cap-/plugin- naming rule, the SDK peer, and the description convention the capabilities repository's catalogue check enforces. Present = presence() in add/index.mjs (now exported, same rules as platform-add's 'already has' refusal). Other SDK major = rangeMajor(peer) vs the installed platform-daemon's major.

FAILURES, each 'Cannot list the capabilities published to @crab-shack: ...', exit 1: scope not mapped ('this product does not map @crab-shack to a registry. Its .npmrc needs the line ...#the-scope-mapping'); no token ('no token for npm.pkg.github.com in your npm configuration. Give it a classic personal access token with read:packages ...#the-token'); 401 ('GitHub refused the token ... expired, revoked or mistyped'); 403 ('... read:packages, member of crab-shack, SSO'); unreachable ('<GitHub (https://api.github.com) | the registry at X> could not be reached (<code>). Check the network connection, and the proxy if you use one.'); pnpm view errors keep platform-add's wording.

DOCS: packages/cap-template/README.md 'An installed capability' (the command, what it prints, where each fact comes from, the description rule), docs/registry-access.md 'Listing what is published', README, docs/capability-authors.md, and the generated product README's 'Add a capability'.

OLDER PLATFORM: a product on <= 0.9.1 has no platform-list until it moves its pin to 0.10.0 (nothing else to edit; the bin comes with platform-config). Not verified: listing with a CI GITHUB_TOKEN (not needed for a developer's terminal).
close_reason: Released as platform 0.10.0 (134ce81; Release run 43585082557 and CI run 43585082543 green, tag v0.10.0): pnpm platform-list in platform-config lists every published capability and connection (id, kind, description, needs, newest version), marks what the product has and what targets another SDK major, and changes nothing. Names come from GitHub's packages API with the read token pnpm already has; details from pnpm view; kind and needs beyond peers from the description convention the capabilities repository's lint enforces; nothing new is published and nothing is kept by hand. Shown against the real registry in a product generated by 0.10.0 (14 listed; marks after platform-add deployments) and with fixtures for a later-published capability and another SDK major. Fails with what to check when there is no token or it is refused. Incidents reported to Jack: the read:packages token was printed once into the agent's own tool output; git init and pnpm install ran once by mistake in Candy Mountain's checkout and changed nothing (verified by the orchestrator).

Someone starting a product needs to see what capabilities exist before choosing, and the platform's command for adding a capability needs each published package to describe itself. The capabilities repository's README has a hand-written table of packages, which will drift the first time a capability changes what it needs, and the published packages may not yet carry everything the command reads.

First, make the published packages addable. The bead that built the command (Base: one command adds a published capability to a product) recorded in its notes what, if anything, a capability package must carry beyond what it already has. Add that to every capability and connection package here, release them through the fast lane, and confirm against the real registry that the command adds a capability from this repository to a generated product.
