The README's package table is produced from the packages themselves: for each published capability and connection, its id, its kind (feature capability, service-only capability or connection), one sentence on what it does, what it needs, and its current version. A check that runs with the repository's gates fails when the committed table is out of date, so it cannot drift. The support packages are listed separately from the capabilities.

Keep the generated part clearly marked in the README so hand-written sections around it are left alone.
acceptance_criteria:
- In a product generated by platform-new product, running the platform's add command for chat-claude-code against the real registry installs it with the ACP runtime and the Claude Code and repository connections, and the product's gates pass.
- The README's catalogue lists every published capability and connection with id, kind, description, needs and version, and matches the packages.
- Changing a package's description or needs without regenerating makes the repository's gates fail with a message saying how to regenerate.
- Any package change was released through the fast lane.
notes:
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from 94z.6.1 (platform 0.9.1; read its bead note first, it says what platform-add reads from a package). (1) What a capability needs is not only its peers: a manifest can require a plugin type its package does not peer on (cap-deployments requires 'repository' and peers only on heroku and netlify) or a workspace fact another capability declares (cap-team requires 'hasBots', which only cap-bots declares, and bots depends on team, so team alone cannot boot). Orchestrator decision: no new peer rule, because a product may supply a plugin type itself and the daemon names the gap at boot; but the catalogue and each package's self-description must show these needs, taken from the manifest, so that someone choosing a capability sees them before installing. (2) platform-add loads a definition as the root export named <id in camelCase>Definition called with no argument; all fourteen follow it today, and the author's guide now states it as a rule: consider holding it in scripts/check-packages.mjs. (3) GitHub Packages returns a package's description but drops webLayer, exports, type and peerDependenciesMeta from registry metadata, and pnpm cannot list a scope; anything the catalogue needs from the registry has to survive that.
AGENT NOTE (94z.6.2, 2026-11-14). Landed and released; bead not closed by the agent.

COMMITS ON crab-shack/capabilities main: f3d2634 (the change, with the changeset unapplied) and ea50458 (release commit: versions, changelogs, regenerated table). Release run 43583095510 green, published exactly @crab-shack/cap-deployments@0.1.1 and @crab-shack/cap-team@0.1.1 and tagged both; CI run 43583095461 green (Lint ran the catalogue check on the runner with nothing built). Main checkout fast-forwarded to ea50458.

HOW THE CATALOGUE IS GENERATED. Two steps in scripts/catalogue/:
- gather.mjs, gatherCatalogue(root) -> { capabilities, support, problems }. Registers tsx (root devDependency, new) and imports each non-private cap-/plugin- package's workspace root entry (exports['.'] = src/index.ts), calls the export <camelId>Definition with no argument. Per capability: id, package, version, kind (manifest -> feature; no manifest and pluginTypes -> connection; neither -> service), description (package.json description minus its kind prefix, up to ' Also needs '), webLayer, readme path, sdkMajor, brings {pluginTypes, workspaceFacts}, needs {peers (cap-/plugin- peer ids), pluginTypes (requiresPlugins), anyPluginTypes, workspaceFacts (requiresWorkspaceFacts), beyondPeers: each requirement nothing in the package's transitive peer closure supplies, with 'from' = the ids that bring/declare it}. Support packages: package, version, description, readme. ~3 s, nothing built needed.
- render.mjs renders that into README.md between <!-- catalogue:start --> and <!-- catalogue:end -->: Id | Package (linked to its README) | Kind | Web layer | What it does | Needs | Version, a generated legend, then the support packages table. Hand-written text around it unchanged except the paragraph under it, whose sentence about the old Needs column (peers only) became wrong and was reduced to the peer/one-copy point, plus the factory-name rule.
- scripts/catalogue.mjs: no argument (pnpm catalogue) writes; --check fails when README differs, printing the expected lines and 'Run `pnpm catalogue` and commit README.md.'; --json prints the gathered facts.

WHAT IS CHECKED (pnpm lint ends with node scripts/catalogue.mjs --check; any problem fails it, ending 'Fix them, then run `pnpm catalogue` and commit README.md.'): the root entry exports <camelId>Definition, callable with no argument, returning id = package id, package = package name, sdkMajor = major of the platform-sdk peer; cap- vs plugin- name matches the kind; a connection brings the plugin type its id names; the description starts 'Crab Shack capability: ' / 'Crab Shack capability, service only: ' / 'Crab Shack connection: ' by kind; every manifest requirement no peer supplies is named in the description after ' Also needs ', and ' Also needs ' appears only when there is such a requirement. scripts/check-packages.mjs (end of pnpm build, so also before every publish) now also loads each capability's BUILT root entry (publishConfig.exports) the same way, so a published package that platform-add could not load fails the build (proved by renaming the export in a built dist: 'fails to load its root entry dist/index.js ...').

PACKAGE CHANGE (patch, released): the manifest-only needs are now in the registry-visible description. cap-deployments 0.1.1: '... Also needs the repository plugin type, which plugin-repository brings and this package does not install.' cap-team 0.1.1: '... Also needs the hasBots workspace fact, which only cap-bots declares; cap-bots installs this package with it.' No peer added (orchestrator decision). The catalogue shows them as 'not installed with it: the `repository` plugin type, which `repository` brings' / 'the `hasBots` workspace fact, which `bots` declares'.

WHAT A RELEASE HAS TO RUN. Nothing new to remember: version-packages is now 'changeset version && node scripts/catalogue.mjs', so it rewrites the table's versions with the bump (also in the gated lane, whose changesets/action runs pnpm version-packages). Running bare 'changeset version' leaves the table behind and pnpm lint fails. AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and README (Gates, New capabilities, fast lane step 1) say so. Also folded in the orchestrator's SECOND CORRECTION: on 0.x a patch is a fix or backwards-compatible addition and a minor only for a break (reason given); landing is change commit, then a separate release commit, never amend or rebase after versioning, and if origin/main moves, drop the release commit (git reset --hard HEAD~1), rebase, version again. CONTRIBUTING.md has a new section 'The package catalogue'. A change to a description, peers or definition runs pnpm catalogue and commits README in the change commit.
Proof in a throwaway clone (scratch, never pushed): with this changeset plus an extra cap-acp minor, pnpm version-packages bumped acp 0.2.0 and patched bots, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, claude-code, codex, deployments, team, rewrote all eight versions in the table; catalogue --check and full pnpm lint green on that release commit; unreleased.mjs listed exactly those eight. Bare 'changeset version' instead left the check failing with the stale rows.

FIRST ACCEPTANCE CRITERION, SHOWN. In an empty scratch dir: pnpm --config.@crab-shack:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com --package=@crab-shack/platform-config@0.9.1 dlx platform-new product 'Shack Demo' --scope @shack-demo; git init; pnpm install; pnpm platform-add chat-claude-code -> installed cap-chat-claude-code 0.1.1 with plugin-repository 0.1.1, cap-acp 0.1.0 (and claude-acp 0.1.0 under it), plugin-claude-code 0.1.0, one copy each; definitions.ts and product.yaml edited; lint, typecheck, test (daemon 33, web 4, board 13), build all green. Nothing in the packages had to change for the command.

FOR 94z.6.3. The facts are gathered once, in scripts/catalogue/gather.mjs (gatherCatalogue), and 'node scripts/catalogue.mjs --json' prints them as { capabilities: [...], support: [...] } with the shape above; the README is only a rendering of that. Nothing new is published. From the registry alone (pnpm view): version, peerDependencies, and the description, whose prefix now reliably gives the kind and whose ' Also needs ' sentence gives the manifest-only needs (both enforced by the check); webLayer and the definition are not there.

NOT DONE / NOTICED. README line 3 still says the platform pin is 0.7.1 while every package.json pins 0.8.2 (hand-written, left alone). The catalogue's 'What it does' is plain text from package.json, so the backticks the old hand-written table had (`.beads`, `claude`) are gone. The workspace-fact closure is computed over this repository's packages only; a product that declares hasBots itself is not something the catalogue can know.
close_reason: Landed as f3d2634 + ea50458 on crab-shack/capabilities main: the README package table is generated from the packages (scripts/catalogue: gather, render), pnpm lint fails when it is stale and says how to regenerate, and pnpm version-packages regenerates it so a release keeps versions current. Needs come from the manifest as well as peers. check-packages also loads each built definition the way platform-add does. cap-deployments and cap-team published at 0.1.1 (descriptions now name what their manifests need); Release run 43583095510 and CI run 43583095461 green. platform-add chat-claude-code shown against the real registry in a product generated by 0.9.1, gates passing. CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md carry the corrected bump and landing rules.

Commits: in the base and in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and once a repository's fast lane exists that push is also the release; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one. In Candy Mountain do not commit or push unless the orchestrator tells you to. The plan this bead comes from is in Candy Mountain at .ai-docs/plans/shared-capabilities/, for background only: this bead is complete without it.

Adding a capability to a product is four edits in four files: a dependency line in the daemon app and in the web app, an import and an entry in the daemon's definitions, and ids in the product description. Each is checked, so a missed one names itself, but it is a chore, and a capability that needs others multiplies it. Capabilities are now published as @crab-shack/cap-<id> and @crab-shack/plugin-<id>, and Jack wants picking one to feel like installing a package.

Give products one command, shipped in platform-config beside platform-new, that adds a published capability by id. It installs the package at its current version, pinned exactly as products pin everything, makes every edit the product needs, and does the same for everything that capability needs and the product does not have yet, saying what it added. Afterwards the product's gates pass and the capability's pages are reachable once it is in a module.

It refuses, with the reason and without changing anything: a capability that does not exist in the registry, one the product already has, and one whose SDK major is not the product's.

Two things it does not decide: which module a feature capability appears under, and any setting that has no default. Like platform-new, it ends by printing what is left to do.

It must work for a product generated by platform-new product, which is described by a root product.yaml and lists its definitions in the daemon app. A product described another way (Candy Mountain keeps a TypeScript product package) gets the installs and whatever edits can be made safely, and is told plainly which edits remain.

The command has to learn about a capability without a human reading its source: its id, its layer, the plugin type a connection brings, the capabilities it needs, and how its definition is exported. Much of that is already in a published package or follows from the naming rules (the layer id is in the manifest, needed capabilities are peer dependencies, a connection's plugin type is its id). Use what is there. If something is missing, define the smallest addition a capability package must carry, document it in the author pages, and add it to the template and the sample connection so generated capabilities have it; say in this bead's notes exactly what published capabilities must add, because another bead adds it in the capabilities repository.

Removing a capability stays the documented manual reverse; do not build a remove command. Document the command in the author's guide where adding a capability is described. Test against packed fixtures, not the live registry. The change carries a changeset and is released by pushing to main (the base's fast lane).
acceptance_criteria:
- In a product generated by platform-new product, adding a fixture capability that needs two others installs all three at exact versions, edits both apps, the definitions and product.yaml, prints what it added and what remains, and the product's lint, typecheck and tests then pass.
- Once the capability is put in a module, its page renders in the running product.
- Running the command again for the same id refuses and changes nothing; so does an unknown id, and so does a capability targeting another SDK major, each with its reason.
- In a product without a product.yaml, the command installs, edits what it safely can and lists the remaining edits.
- The author's guide documents the command; this bead's notes say what, if anything, published capabilities must carry; the release containing this is in the registry.
notes:
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from 94z.7 (platform 0.7.2): pnpm refuses a lockfile entry younger than a day unless the package is exempt in pnpm-workspace.yaml (minimumReleaseAgeExclude). Since 0.7.2 the generator writes the four platform packages there by name, without a version, and a pin move no longer touches the list; docs/upgrade-path.md in the base ('A release younger than a day') has the one-time edit for a repository whose entries still carry a version. The same age check applies to a capability package a product adds: one published less than a day before is refused unless it is exempt. The command that adds a capability has to leave the product able to install it; how (naming the package in the list, or otherwise) is for this bead to settle, without exempting anything outside @crab-shack.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), Jack's decision: capability packages are exempt from pnpm's minimum release age in a product. Bead 94z.9 (which this bead now depends on) makes a generated product exempt them without a per-capability edit; read its closing note before designing. If it reports that the exemption still needs a package named, the command that adds a capability has to keep that list right; otherwise the command leaves pnpm-workspace.yaml alone.
AGENT NOTE (94z.6.1, 2026-11-14). The command exists and is released. Bead not closed by the agent.

RELEASES. Platform 0.9.0 (origin/main 918a2c6, Release run 43559520942, CI run 43559520890) shipped the command as the agent's work stood when a usage limit stopped it: complete in code, tests and docs, but not yet proved against real capabilities. The audit afterwards found one defect in it, fixed in 0.9.1 (origin/main 223c2a2, Release run 43580656178, CI run 43580656205). Use 0.9.1 or later.

THE COMMAND. `pnpm platform-add <id>[@<version>]`, bin `platform-add` of @crab-shack/platform-config beside platform-new (code: packages/platform-config/add/index.mjs; not in the package's exports map). One argument: a capability id (issues), or a package name (@crab-shack/cap-issues), either with an exact version (issues@1.2.0); no flags. Exit 0 or 1. Run anywhere inside a product. In order:
1. Finds the product: the pnpm workspace root, the app under apps/ that depends on @crab-shack/platform-daemon (required) and the one on platform-web; the platform version from the installed platform-daemon.
2. Asks the registry with `pnpm view <name>[@<spec>] --json` run in the product, so the product's .npmrc decides the registry; it reads only `version` and `peerDependencies`. For an id it asks for @crab-shack/cap-<id> and @crab-shack/plugin-<id>. For every cap-/plugin- package among the peers that the product lacks it asks for the newest version in the peer range, recursively.
3. Refuses, before changing anything, each message ending "Nothing was changed.": "No capability '<id>' in the registry: @crab-shack/cap-<id> and @crab-shack/plugin-<id> are not published there."; "The product already has the capability '<id>': <package>, installed at <v>." (also the product's own packages/cap-<id>, and ids product.yaml or definitions.ts already list, such as overview); "<package> <v> targets SDK major N, and this product runs the platform at <v>, SDK major M." (also for a need: "...; <requirer> needs it."); a need the registry lacks; a need the product has at a version outside the range ("move that pin first"); a need whose id one of the product's own packages carries; a package with no peer on platform-sdk ("is not a capability package").
4. Adds every package to `dependencies` of both apps at its exact version and runs `pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile`. If the install fails it restores both package.json files, pnpm-lock.yaml and pnpm-workspace.yaml.
5. Reads `webLayer` from each installed package.json, and loads each installed definition in a child `node` process from the daemon app (`import(<package>)`, the export `<id in camelCase>Definition`, called with no argument) for: the plugin types it brings, whether it has a manifest, its rungs and view paths, the settings without a default, the plugin types its manifest requires (requiresPlugins and every alternative in requiresAnyPlugins), the workspace facts it declares and requires.
6. (0.9.1) For each plugin type a manifest requires that the product does not supply, adds the connection that brings it, named by the plugin type: <scope>/plugin-<type>, with what that needs, in a further install round.
7. Edits apps/daemon/src/definitions.ts (an import and a DEFINITIONS entry each, before 'platform-agent') and product.yaml (capabilities, pluginTypes, layers; text spliced in, comments and layout kept, the result re-parsed and compared before it is written), reruns the web app's postinstall (nuxt prepare), and prints "Added ...", "It needs N capabilities the product did not have, added with it:", "Changed:", and "What remains:".
What remains is always: the module each feature goes in (with its rungs; a connection or service-only capability goes in none), each setting declared without a default, the gates, pnpm dev. First in that list, when they apply: an edit it could not make, a required plugin type no connection could be added for, a required workspace fact nothing installed declares.
It never writes pnpm-workspace.yaml. If the file lacks the '@crab-shack/*' release-age entry it prints one note pointing at docs/upgrade-path.md#a-release-younger-than-a-day (seen in a Candy Mountain clone: pnpm appended three by-version entries itself and the install went through).

WHAT PUBLISHED CAPABILITIES MUST ADD: NOTHING. The command reads what the sixteen packages at 0.1.0 already carry, and all fourteen capabilities were added with it from the real registry into one product (gates green, daemon boots 17 capabilities, one copy of each). What it relies on, all true today:
- the name: cap-<id> or plugin-<id>, the id being the definition's id; a plugin- package brings the plugin type its id names;
- a peer dependency on @crab-shack/platform-sdk naming one major (it is also how a capability is told from a library: capabilities-testing and claude-acp are not capabilities);
- every capability it needs as a peerDependency (cap-/plugin- name);
- `webLayer` in package.json when it has a layer;
- the root entry exports the definition factory as <id in camelCase>Definition, callable with no argument, importable under plain Node from the installed dist. This name was a habit of the template; the author's guide now states it as a rule ("The definition is a factory"). A package that breaks it is still installed and listed in product.yaml, and the command prints the import to write by hand.
The registry (GitHub Packages) keeps only these manifest fields per version: name, version, description, scripts, dependencies, devDependencies, peerDependencies, files, repository, bin, dist. It DROPS webLayer, exports, type and peerDependenciesMeta. So nothing custom can be read before installing; anything a tool must know beforehand has to be in the name, the description or the dependency fields.

TWO FINDINGS ABOUT THE PUBLISHED PACKAGES (not required by the command, but they decide whether one add leaves a product that boots):
- cap-deployments 0.1.0 requires the plugin type 'repository' in its manifest but does not peer on plugin-repository. 0.9.0 left such a product unable to boot; 0.9.1 adds plugin-repository by the naming rule. It is still worth deciding in the capabilities repository whether a package should peer on every connection whose plugin type its manifest requires: only then can the need be seen before installing (by the catalogue and by `pnpm view`).
- cap-team 0.1.0 requires the workspace fact 'hasBots', which only cap-bots declares, and cap-bots depends on cap-team, so team cannot name bots. `pnpm platform-add team` alone gives a product the daemon refuses ("Capability 'team' requires workspace fact 'hasBots', which no definition declares."); 0.9.1 says so first under What remains, but cannot know which capability declares a fact. Adding bots (which brings team) works.

A PRODUCT DESCRIBED ANOTHER WAY (no root product.yaml; tried in a scratch clone of Candy Mountain at platform 0.5.0): it installs, pins both apps, edits apps/daemon/src/definitions.ts when it has the generator's shape (Candy Mountain's has), and prints the ids to add to the product's own capabilities, pluginTypes and layers, the module step and the settings. In Candy Mountain every one of the fourteen ids is already carried by a workspace package, so the command refuses each ("already has ... (packages/cap-issues)"): moving Candy Mountain to the published packages (94z.5.1) is not a job for this command.

GENERATED PRODUCTS' OWN TESTS. Chosen: the generator stops writing tests that restate the product file, rather than the command editing tests (the module step, which is the person's, would break them again). Seven assertions in apps/daemon/src/product.test.ts and apps/web/test/unit/distribution.test.ts now hold only that the starting capability is among what the product boots. A product generated before 0.9.0 makes the edit once: docs/upgrade-path.md, "Tests a generated product carries".

FOR 94z.6.2 (packages describe themselves, catalogue). Nothing has to be added for platform-add. Worth holding in scripts/check-packages.mjs, since the command depends on them: the built root entry exports <id in camelCase>Definition; calling it with no argument returns a definition whose id is the package's id; every plugin type and workspace fact the manifest requires is supplied by the package itself or by a capability among its peers (false today for cap-deployments and cap-team, see above). The catalogue can take the kind from the definition (manifest: feature; no manifest and plugin types: connection; neither: service only), which the registry cannot tell apart for a cap- package; `description` is the one free-text field the registry returns, and the sixteen already start it "Crab Shack capability:", "Crab Shack capability, service only:" or "Crab Shack connection:".

FOR 94z.6.3 (list from inside a product). It sits beside this command in packages/platform-config (bin + a module like add/). Reusable from add/index.mjs: pnpmView(root, name, spec) (undefined for a 404 or no matching version; throws AddError with the registry's words, credentials redacted, for anything else, pointing at docs/registry-access.md), redact(text), and the product discovery inside readProduct (not exported yet). `pnpm view <name> --json` gives version, description and peerDependencies per package with the product's read-only token; GitHub Packages offers no way to list a scope's packages through pnpm, so the list of names has to come from somewhere the capabilities repository publishes. "Already in the product" is workspacePackages(root) from package-boundaries (kind capability, by capabilityId); "another SDK major" is rangeMajor(peerDependencies['@crab-shack/platform-sdk']) against the installed platform-daemon's major. On this machine the scope's registry line is in each project's .npmrc, not at user level, so `pnpm dlx` in an empty directory needs `--config.@crab-shack:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`.

PNPM FINDINGS. With the registry dropping peerDependenciesMeta, vue becomes a required peer of every layer package in the metadata; a generated product still ends with one copy of each capability (checked with all fourteen). Rebuilt tarballs served under a version pnpm has already seen are taken from its metadata cache: point PNPM_CONFIG_CACHE_DIR at an empty directory when testing against a local registry.
close_reason: Released as platform 0.9.1 (223c2a2; Release run 43580656178 and CI run 43580656205 green, tag v0.9.1): pnpm platform-add <id>[@version] in platform-config adds a published capability and what it needs to a generated product, refuses without changing anything, and reports what remains for a product described another way. 0.9.0 (the agent's work in progress, pushed during the usage-limit stop) had one defect, fixed in 0.9.1: a capability whose manifest requires a plugin type its package does not peer on (cap-deployments needs repository) left the daemon unable to boot. Proved against packed fixtures and the real registry. Capability packages need to carry nothing new. Products should pin 0.9.1, not 0.9.0.

title: Rehearse the shared-capabilities human test and hand Jack the checklist
description:
Context: three repositories on this machine, all Jack's (GitHub user kingrea, the only developer).

The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm 12 workspace run through Turborepo that holds the platform. It publishes five packages to GitHub Packages (npm.pkg.github.com, scope @crab-shack, private) at one shared version (0.5.0 at the time of writing): platform-daemon (the Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle, with a /testing entry that is the daemon test kit), platform-web (the web shell, a Nuxt layer published as source, with the layer-list helper that finds a capability's layer from the webLayer field of a dependency's package.json), platform-sdk (wire types, the product configuration type, defineCapabilityDefinition and the capability contract), platform-config (the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends, the cm-packages boundary lint and its package-boundaries helpers, the commands platform-link, platform-unlink and platform-check-linked, and the generators platform-new capability, connection and product) and platform-cli. Beside them, unpublished: packages/cap-template and packages/plugin-sample (the worked examples the generators copy), and apps/ with a root product.yaml (the base's own development distribution). docs/ holds capability-authors.md, linking.md, registry-access.md, upgrade-path.md, capability-majors.md and product-file.md; CONTRIBUTING.md holds the changeset rule.

Candy Mountain (github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) is a product built on the base. Today it also holds the source of sixteen shared packages under its own scope @candy-mountain: eight feature or service capabilities (packages/cap-acp, cap-bots, cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, cap-deployments, cap-issues, cap-team, cap-uptime), six connections that each bring the one plugin type their id names (packages/plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex, plugin-heroku, plugin-netlify, plugin-repository, plugin-slack), the Claude Code ACP shim (packages/claude-acp) and shared test support (packages/testing). The product itself is packages/candy-mountain (plain data) and thin apps: apps/daemon lists every capability definition and runs the platform's runDaemon, apps/web extends platform-web and the capability layers, apps/cli is the bin.

The capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) is where those sixteen packages are moving. Each is published on its own, at its own version, as @crab-shack/cap-<id>, @crab-shack/plugin-<id>, @crab-shack/claude-acp and @crab-shack/capabilities-testing. A product then picks capabilities by depending on them, as it already depends on the platform, and can write its own beside them. Capability ids, plugin type ids, layer ids, table names and migration histories never change in this move, because an existing database identifies each capability's migrations by its id.

A capability is one package with a daemon half (a definition made with defineCapabilityDefinition, exported from the package's root entry as a factory, stating its own package name and the SDK major it targets) and, when it has UI, a web half (a Nuxt layer at the package root). It owns its tables and its own migration history. A product is plain data (name, theme, scope label, and the id lists of capabilities, modules, plugin types and layers) joined at boot with the capability definitions; the daemon refuses to boot, naming the offender, when they disagree.

Commits: in the base and in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and once a repository's fast lane exists that push is also the release; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one. In Candy Mountain do not commit or push unless the orchestrator tells you to. The plan this bead comes from is in Candy Mountain at .ai-docs/plans/shared-capabilities/, for background only: this bead is complete without it.

Candy Mountain now runs on capabilities published from the capabilities repository, and Jack has to confirm that for himself before the old way is considered gone. His time is better spent confirming than discovering, so run the whole test first and hand him a checklist that already works.

The test, on a copy of a real pre-existing Candy Mountain data directory (never the original):
- The repository has no cap-* or plugin-* folder.
- Candy Mountain starts and the daemon's boot log shows no migration applied.
- Every existing plugin instance shows healthy; a chat thread starts on Claude Code and on Codex; a bot runs; the uptime and deployments pages read as before.
- Linked to the capabilities checkout, a label changed there appears in Candy Mountain; after unlinking, git status is clean.
- That change, pushed to the capabilities repository with a patch bump, appears in the registry within minutes without a pull request; Candy Mountain moved to that one new version shows the label in a build.

Run each step. Where one fails, find the cause and either fix it where it belongs (the capabilities repository or the base, released through their fast lanes; never a patch in Candy Mountain) or, if it is more than a small fix, file a bead for it and say so. Revert the label change at the end, as a further release.

Write the checklist for Jack as a note on this bead: each step as a command or a click with what he should see, the versions everything is on, and anything that needed fixing along the way.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every step above was run and its result recorded.
- A checklist Jack can follow is in this bead's notes, with exact commands and expected results.
- Anything that failed is either fixed and released, or filed as a bead that the notes name.
notes:
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from 94z.6.1: on this machine the @crab-shack registry line is not in the user-level npm configuration, so 'pnpm dlx platform-new product' run in an empty directory needs --config.@crab-shack:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com (inside a product the scope is already mapped). The human test's 'freshly generated product' step meets this: rehearse it exactly as Jack will type it, and put the working command in his checklist. Products should pin platform 0.9.1, not 0.9.0 (0.9.0 has a defect in platform-add).
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14, late), from 94z.5.1 (read its bead note and closing reason first). (1) Jack's real data directory (~/.local/share/candy-mountain) holds 4 workspaces, 2 organisations, modules, grants and 1 user, and NO plugin instances, bots, threads or monitors, no stored secrets and no agent homes. So 'every existing plugin instance shows healthy; a chat thread starts; a bot runs' cannot be rehearsed on a copy of it as written. Rehearse the no-migration, nothing-lost steps on a copy of the real directory, and the instance, thread and bot steps on a directory made by the old build (94z.5.1 left one, synthetic, with its scripts: scratch 94z-5-1/seed2, old-build/, scripts/ under the orchestrator's scratchpad; its note says how it was made). Write Jack's checklist for what his directory really holds, and say plainly which steps need him to connect a real account first. (2) 94z.5.1 ran every daemon that touched a data directory inside a no-network sandbox (its scripts/jail.sh) and without CM_SECRETS_KEY; keep to that for any copy of real data. (3) Candy Mountain is on platform 0.9.1 with the capabilities at the versions in 94z.5.1's note; its working tree is uncommitted and Jack's to commit: never commit, stash, reset or check out there, and show the commit guard by running the check itself, never git commit. (4) The capabilities repository's development distribution has a stand-in mode (pnpm build, then pnpm dev:stand-ins) where every capability can be exercised with no accounts; it is not Candy Mountain, but it is where 'a chat thread starts on Claude Code and on Codex; a bot runs' can be seen working on the published code paths.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14, late), three more things. (1) Platform 0.10.0 is out with pnpm platform-list beside platform-add; the 'freshly generated product' step should be generated by 0.10.0 and can show the list before and after the add. Candy Mountain itself is on 0.9.1; moving it is not part of this bead. (2) When you land the label change in the capabilities repository, also correct the third line of its README, which still says the platform pin is 0.7.1 (every package.json pins 0.8.2); it is documentation, so it rides along without its own changeset. (3) NEVER run a command that prints a credential: no 'pnpm config get' or 'npm config get' on an auth key, no cat, grep or head of ~/.config/pnpm/auth.ini, ~/.npmrc or any .npmrc, no 'env' dumps. An agent printed Jack's registry token into its own output today that way. To check that access works, run the command that needs it (pnpm view <package> version) and look at its exit code.

Candy Mountain now installs its capabilities from the registry at exact versions, like the platform. Its README explains how to take a new platform version and how to link to a local base checkout, but says nothing yet about doing either for a capability, and the link to a capabilities checkout has only ever been tried against a test fixture.

Add to the README, beside what it says about the platform:
- Taking a new version of a capability: change its version wherever Candy Mountain lists it, then pnpm install. Capabilities have independent versions, so one can move without the others. - The README covers the three points with commands that run as written.

notes:

title: Capabilities: the fast-lane release flow, and the first publish
description:
Context: three repositories on this machine, all Jack's (GitHub user kingrea, the only developer).

The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm 12 workspace run through Turborepo that holds the platform. It publishes five packages to GitHub Packages (npm.pkg.github.com, scope @crab-shack, private) at one shared version (0.5.0 at the time of writing): platform-daemon (the Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle, with a /testing entry that is the daemon test kit), platform-web (the web shell, a Nuxt layer published as source, with the layer-list helper that finds a capability's layer from the webLayer field of a dependency's package.json), platform-sdk (wire types, the product configuration type, defineCapabilityDefinition and the capability contract), platform-config (the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends, the cm-packages boundary lint and its package-boundaries helpers, the commands platform-link, platform-unlink and platform-check-linked, and the generators platform-new capability, connection and product) and platform-cli. Beside them, unpublished: packages/cap-template and packages/plugin-sample (the worked examples the generators copy), and apps/ with a root product.yaml (the base's own development distribution). docs/ holds capability-authors.md, linking.md, registry-access.md, upgrade-path.md, capability-majors.md and product-file.md; CONTRIBUTING.md holds the changeset rule.

Candy Mountain (github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) is a product built on the base. Today it also holds the source of sixteen shared packages under its own scope @candy-mountain: eight feature or service capabilities (packages/cap-acp, cap-bots, cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, cap-deployments, cap-issues, cap-team, cap-uptime), six connections that each bring the one plugin type their id names (packages/plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex, plugin-heroku, plugin-netlify, plugin-repository, plugin-slack), the Claude Code ACP shim (packages/claude-acp) and shared test support (packages/testing). The product itself is packages/candy-mountain (plain data) and thin apps: apps/daemon lists every capability definition and runs the platform's runDaemon, apps/web extends platform-web and the capability layers, apps/cli is the bin.

The capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) is where those sixteen packages are moving. Each is published on its own, at its own version, as @crab-shack/cap-<id>, @crab-shack/plugin-<id>, @crab-shack/claude-acp and @crab-shack/capabilities-testing. A product then picks capabilities by depending on them, as it already depends on the platform, and can write its own beside them. Capability ids, plugin type ids, layer ids, table names and migration histories never change in this move, because an existing database identifies each capability's migrations by its id.

A capability is one package with a daemon half (a definition made with defineCapabilityDefinition, exported from the package's root entry as a factory, stating its own package name and the SDK major it targets) and, when it has UI, a web half (a Nuxt layer at the package root). It owns its tables and its own migration history. A product is plain data (name, theme, scope label, and the id lists of capabilities, modules, plugin types and layers) joined at boot with the capability definitions; the daemon refuses to boot, naming the offender, when they disagree.

Commits: in the base and in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and once a repository's fast lane exists that push is also the release; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one. In Candy Mountain do not commit or push unless the orchestrator tells you to. The plan this bead comes from is in Candy Mountain at .ai-docs/plans/shared-capabilities/, for background only: this bead is complete without it.

The capabilities repository's packages are versioned and publishable but nothing publishes them. Jack wants nothing between a change and a release while the capabilities are in active development: his blocker in the base was waiting for the gates, opening and merging a pull request, then merging a generated release pull request. The base now has a fast lane that removes those waits, with a switch to bring the gate back. Give this repository the same lane, built the same way, so there is one release habit across both. Read how the base does it (its workflows, the Releasing section of its README, CONTRIBUTING.md and its agent instructions file) and copy it, changing only what differs here: packages have independent versions, so a release publishes just the packages whose versions changed, and there is no shared version tag.

While the fast lane is on:
- A push to main is the release: no pull request, no generated release pull request, and the versions stated in the push are published without a further human step.
- Lint, typecheck and tests run on every push and report, beside the publish rather than before it. Only a package that does not build stops a publish.
- Nobody has to pull an automated commit before pushing again.
- Publishing from a laptop is the documented fallback.

One documented switch restores the gated flow (checks gate the publish, changes arrive by pull request), and the repository starts with the gate off. Enforcing pull requests on a private repository needs a paid GitHub plan the organisation does not have, so say that this half is a convention for now.

Fill the Releasing section of the README with both positions of the switch, and add to the agent instructions file that a push to main is the release and what a change to a package must carry. Create either file if it is not there yet.

Then make the first publish through the lane: all sixteen packages at 0.1.0. Products' CI must be able to read them: Candy Mountain, which is outside the organisation, reads with a personal token, and repositories inside the organisation need access granted per package. Do what an agent can and leave Jack an exact list of anything that needs clicking in GitHub's settings as a note on this bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- All sixteen packages are in the organisation's registry at 0.1.0, private, published by the workflow.
- Pushing a change to one capability with a patch bump publishes that package's new version and no other, with no pull request opened or merged; a second push from the same clone without pulling succeeds.
- A push whose tests fail still publishes and its checks show as failed; with the switch in the gated position the same push publishes nothing.
- A push with no version change publishes nothing and fails nothing.
- From Candy Mountain's checkout, pnpm view of one of the packages succeeds with Jack's existing token.
- The README's Releasing section and the agent instructions describe the lane, the switch and the laptop fallback; anything Jack must do by hand is listed in this bead's notes.
notes:
LANDING PROCEDURE (capabilities repo, from now on; release flow fdbd377 is on main and all 16 packages are at 0.1.0 in GitHub Packages, published by Release run 43557796360). Every push to main is a release: the Release workflow publishes every package version in the pushed commit whose <name>@<version> tag is not on the remote. Lane: fast (RELEASE_LANE unset). Do NOT pull/reset/touch the main checkout /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities (it holds unpushed local merges from another tool); take origin/main after git fetch as the truth and drop the 'pull --ff-only' step from landing scripts.
(A) CHANGE THAT TOUCHES A PUBLISHED PACKAGE (anything a package under packages/ ships: src outside tests, web layer app/ and nuxt.config.ts, migrations, package README, package.json dependencies/peerDependencies/exports/files etc.):
1. On your branch, commit the change plus an UNAPPLIED changeset .changeset/<short-name>.md naming only the packages you changed: front matter '"@crab-shack/<pkg>": patch' (minor for a breaking change or addition before 1.0; never major), body written for a product that installs the package.
2. git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main; run the four gates (heavy ones under flock /tmp/cm-heavy-gates.lock). Rerun them if a later rebase brings anything in.
3. Take /tmp/capabilities-land.lock (e.g. a holder: flock /tmp/capabilities-land.lock bash -c 'while [ -e <sentinel> ]; do sleep 3; done' in the background) and hold it to the end of step 6. git fetch origin; if origin/main moved, release the lock and go back to 2.
4. pnpm version-packages (bumps the named packages, patch-bumps dependents whose range a minor leaves, writes CHANGELOG.md, deletes the changeset). Commit that (amend or a second commit). Run node scripts/unreleased.mjs: it must list exactly the versions your changeset produced and nothing else. The pushed tip must hold NO .changeset/*.md besides config.json (a leftover fails the release) and must hold the bumped versions + changelogs (+ pnpm-lock.yaml if dependencies changed).
5. git push origin HEAD:main.
6. Wait for the Release run of that sha (gh run list --repo crab-shack/capabilities --commit <sha>; gh run watch <id> --repo crab-shack/capabilities --exit-status). It must be green and its 'Build and publish' step must list only your versions; then check the CI run for the same sha. Release the lock. If the Release run fails part-way, gh run rerun <id> --failed; never delete package versions, never publish from a laptop; stop and report.
(B) CHANGE THAT TOUCHES ONLY APPS, TESTS, DOCS, CI, scripts/, OR ONLY A PACKAGE'S devDependencies (e.g. the platform pin; Jack/orchestrator decision: a product receives nothing different, so no changeset): no changeset. Same steps 2, 3, 5, 6, and in step 4 node scripts/unreleased.mjs must print 'Every package version is already released.' (if it lists anything, someone left an unreleased version: stop and report). The Release run then ends green after 'Find unreleased versions' with publish skipped.
NOTE: the workflow writes only tags to the remote, never commits, so a second push needs no pull. AGENTS.md (Landing a change) says the same; it reaches main with this bead's next push.
LANDING PROCEDURE, CORRECTION (supersedes the line in the previous note about the main checkout): the main checkout /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities is back to normal. Put 'git -C /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities pull --ff-only' back as the LAST step of landing, after the Release run for your sha has finished and before releasing /tmp/capabilities-land.lock. If that pull fails because the checkout is not clean or not on main, leave it alone and report it. Branch saved/local-merges-2026-11-14 there is not to be built on, merged or deleted.
FOR JACK, BY HAND (an agent cannot: the gh token has no read:packages scope and package settings have no API):
1. Check the 16 packages show 'Private' at https://github.com/orgs/crab-shack/packages (published with --access restricted by the workflow; visibility not readable by the agent).
2. Per-package read access for an org repository that installs them: none needed today (the only other org repos are crab-shack/platform, which does not install them, and crab-shack/test-dashboard-home, which is empty). When a product repo inside crab-shack starts installing them: for each package it installs, https://github.com/orgs/crab-shack/packages/npm/<package>/settings -> 'Manage Actions access' -> 'Add Repository' -> the repo -> role Read. Package names: cap-acp, cap-bots, cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, cap-deployments, cap-issues, cap-team, cap-uptime, claude-acp, plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex, plugin-heroku, plugin-netlify, plugin-repository, plugin-slack, capabilities-testing.
3. Candy Mountain's CI (outside the org): kingrea/candy-mountain-v3 has no workflow and no Actions secret today. When it gets CI: create a classic PAT with only read:packages (https://github.com/settings/tokens -> Generate new token (classic)), then https://github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3/settings/secrets/actions -> New repository secret CRAB_SHACK_PACKAGES_TOKEN, used as NODE_AUTH_TOKEN as the platform's docs/registry-access.md shows. Locally nothing is needed: pnpm view from the checkout already works with the existing token.
4. Only if the gated lane is ever used for real: https://github.com/organizations/crab-shack/settings/actions -> Workflow permissions -> tick 'Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests' (the repo-level setting already reports it allowed; the Version Packages PR path was not exercised, the gated proof stopped at Test as intended).
Nothing else needs clicking: the workflow created all 16 packages with GITHUB_TOKEN and has written to them again since (cap-uptime 0.1.1, cap-chat-claude-code 0.1.1).
DONE (not closed). Release flow fdbd377: .github/workflows/release.yml (fast + gated jobs, copied from the base minus SDK_VERSION check and v<version> tag; Install steps get NODE_AUTH_TOKEN because this repo installs the platform from the registry), scripts/unreleased.mjs (base's, unchanged), ci.yml concurrency per sha on push, README Releasing section (both lane positions, partial-publish rerun, laptop fallback, token, reading from a product), CONTRIBUTING.md (lanes; devDependency-only change needs no changeset), AGENTS.md (fast lane, what a package change carries, landing steps, in 03b0d97). Switch: repo variable RELEASE_LANE on crab-shack/capabilities, unset = fast (current). gh variable set RELEASE_LANE --body gated / gh variable delete RELEASE_LANE. A re-run of a Release run re-reads the variable (proved: gated attempt 1, fast attempt 2 of run 43580391662).
Registry now: all 16 at 0.1.0 (Release run 43557796360, fdbd377); cap-uptime 0.1.1 (run 43580162242, 590b7e9, real change: zod ^4.6.7); cap-chat-claude-code 0.1.1 (run 43580391662 attempt 2, c6073d9, real change: unused drizzle-orm dropped); plugin-netlify and plugin-repository 0.1.1 were published by 94z.3.7 (13d9125), not by this bead.
Proofs: patch -> only that package (43580162242 lists only cap-uptime@0.1.1; no PR). Second push c6073d9 from the same clone with no fetch/pull succeeded. Failing tests: c6073d9 carried a test failing on purpose; gated: Release 43580391662 attempt 1 failed at Test, nothing published, no PR; CI 43580391654 red; after deleting the variable, attempt 2 of the same run (fast) published cap-chat-claude-code@0.1.1 with CI still red. No version change: 03b0d97 (removes the failing test) Release 43580893580 green, publish skipped, CI 43580893602 green; also 4df580c (94z.3.8) Release 43577663073. pnpm view @crab-shack/cap-acp from Candy Mountain's checkout: 0.1.0, exit 0.
LANDING PROCEDURE, SECOND CORRECTION (orchestrator, 2026-11-14 late). (1) In step 4, commit the result of pnpm version-packages as a SECOND commit (message 'Release <package> <version>[, ...]'); do not amend it into the change, and do not rebase after running it. The changelog entry names the commit that added the changeset, and amending leaves it naming a commit that is not on main (this happened to capabilities-testing 0.1.1). If origin/main moves after you have versioned, discard the version commit, rebase, and run version-packages again. (2) Size of a bump while the packages are on 0.x, replacing '(minor for a breaking change or addition before 1.0)': patch for a fix AND for a backwards-compatible addition; minor only for a change that breaks a product or a capability that depends on the package. On 0.x a caret range accepts patches only, so a minor forces a release of every package that needs the one bumped; that cost is for breaks, not for additions. CONTRIBUTING.md is being brought into line by bead 94z.6.2.
close_reason: Release flow on crab-shack/capabilities main (fdbd377, docs completed in 03b0d97): a push to main publishes every package version whose tag is not on the remote; RELEASE_LANE=gated restores the gate; fast lane is the current position. First publish through the workflow: all sixteen at 0.1.0 (Release run 43557796360). Proofs: cap-uptime 0.1.1 published alone and a second push needed no pull; with the lane gated a push with a failing test published nothing, and the same push published cap-chat-claude-code 0.1.1 with red checks once the lane was fast; a push with no version change published nothing and failed nothing; pnpm view succeeds from Candy Mountain. Landing procedure and Jack's by-hand list are in the bead notes. Not verified: package visibility (Jack to confirm Private), a real part-way publish followed by a rerun, the gated lane's Version Packages pull request.

The plan this bead comes from is in Candy Mountain at .ai-docs/plans/shared-capabilities/, for background only: this bead is complete without it.

The sixteen shared packages are now published from the capabilities repository as @crab-shack/cap-<id>, @crab-shack/plugin-<id>, @crab-shack/claude-acp and @crab-shack/capabilities-testing, but Candy Mountain still builds from its own copies under packages/. While both exist the source lives twice and a fix has to be made twice. Make Candy Mountain a thin product that installs the published packages, which is also the proof that the move worked.

Before deleting anything, confirm that the capabilities repository lacks nothing: it records the Candy Mountain commit the packages were taken from, so compare Candy Mountain's copies now against that commit and carry any later change over to the capabilities repository (released through its fast lane) first.

Then Candy Mountain depends on each published package at an exact version, as it does on the platform, and its own copies of the sixteen packages are deleted. Move it to the platform release that checks installed capability packages, and make its checks use that, so a capability that is installed but not listed in the daemon's definitions, or listed but not installed, still names itself. Its built daemon must start under plain Node with the installed capabilities, and its web app must find their layers.

What remains in Candy Mountain is the product: its description, its apps, its brand assets and the tests that are about Candy Mountain as a product. Tests that exercise capabilities together now live in the capabilities repository's development distribution; remove Candy Mountain's copies of those rather than keeping two, and keep the ones that check Candy Mountain's own lists and boot.

The thing to prove is that existing data keeps working. A Candy Mountain database created before this change must start on the new build without applying any migration and without losing anything: plugin instances, logins, threads, bots, uptime history. Ids and migration histories were kept byte for byte in the move for exactly this reason. Try it on a copy of a real data directory, never on the original.

A problem found in a published capability or in the platform is fixed there and released, never patched, vendored or overridden in Candy Mountain. Update the README's layout and platform sections for the new shape.
acceptance_criteria:
- Candy Mountain has no packages/cap-*, packages/plugin-*, packages/claude-acp or packages/testing, and no workspace: dependency on them; each is an exact-version dependency on the @crab-shack package.
- pnpm install, lint, typecheck, test and build are green.
- The built daemon (node, not tsx) starts on a copy of a pre-existing Candy Mountain data directory with a boot log that shows no migration applied, and existing plugin instances, threads and bots are present.
- pnpm dev serves every capability's pages as before.
- Removing one capability from the daemon's definitions makes the tests fail naming it.
- Any change made to Candy Mountain's copies after the move is present in the capabilities repository.
- The README describes the new shape.
notes:
Orchestrator note (from 94z.2.1, platform 0.6.0): Candy Mountain's own apps/daemon/src/capability-packages.test.ts still has its checks inline and its folder rule strips @candy-mountain/, so it would wrongly flag an installed @crab-shack capability. Replace the inline checks with one call, as the base's copy does: capabilityPackageProblems(packages, { daemon: packages.get('@candy-mountain/daemon')!, listed: Object.keys(DEFINITIONS), definitions: capabilityDefinitions() }) from @crab-shack/platform-config/package-boundaries; it returns { placement, registration, dependencies, sdk, kind }. Needs platform >= 0.6.0. Also (from 8by.4.13): apps/daemon/src/settings.ts imports BOTS_SETTINGS from @candy-mountain/cap-bots and needs repointing to @crab-shack/cap-bots.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from 94z.7 (platform 0.7.2): pnpm refuses a lockfile entry younger than a day unless the package is exempt in pnpm-workspace.yaml (minimumReleaseAgeExclude). Since 0.7.2 the generator writes the four platform packages there by name, without a version, and a pin move no longer touches the list; docs/upgrade-path.md in the base ('A release younger than a day') has the one-time edit for a repository whose entries still carry a version. Candy Mountain (0.5.0) has five versioned entries, platform-cli among them: make that edit when its pin moves. The same age check applies to the @crab-shack/cap-* and plugin-* packages Candy Mountain will install: any published less than a day before is refused unless exempt, and the list was deliberately not widened to the whole @crab-shack scope. Say in your report how you exempted them.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), Jack's decision: capability packages ARE exempt from pnpm's minimum release age in a product, as the platform packages are. This replaces the earlier note's 'the list was deliberately not widened': bead 94z.9 changes what platform-new product writes and documents, in the base's docs/upgrade-path.md, what an existing product changes by hand. title: Capabilities: Changesets with a version per package
description:
Context: three repositories on this machine, all Jack's (GitHub user kingrea, the only developer).

The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm 12 workspace run through Turborepo that holds the platform. It publishes five packages to GitHub Packages (npm.pkg.github.com, scope @crab-shack, private) at one shared version (0.5.0 at the time of writing): platform-daemon (the Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle, with a /testing entry that is the daemon test kit), platform-web (the web shell, a Nuxt layer published as source, with the layer-list helper that finds a capability's layer from the webLayer field of a dependency's package.json), platform-sdk (wire types, the product configuration type, defineCapabilityDefinition and the capability contract), platform-config (the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends, the cm-packages boundary lint and its package-boundaries helpers, the commands platform-link, platform-unlink and platform-check-linked, and the generators platform-new capability, connection and product) and platform-cli. Beside them, unpublished: packages/cap-template and packages/plugin-sample (the worked examples the generators copy), and apps/ with a root product.yaml (the base's own development distribution). docs/ holds capability-authors.md, linking.md, registry-access.md, upgrade-path.md, capability-majors.md and product-file.md; CONTRIBUTING.md holds the changeset rule.

Candy Mountain (github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) is a product built on the base. Today it also holds the source of sixteen shared packages under its own scope @candy-mountain: eight feature or service capabilities (packages/cap-acp, cap-bots, cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, cap-deployments, cap-issues, cap-team, cap-uptime), six connections that each bring the one plugin type their id names (packages/plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex, plugin-heroku, plugin-netlify, plugin-repository, plugin-slack), the Claude Code ACP shim (packages/claude-acp) and shared test support (packages/testing). The product itself is packages/candy-mountain (plain data) and thin apps: apps/daemon lists every capability definition and runs the platform's runDaemon, apps/web extends platform-web and the capability layers, apps/cli is the bin.

The capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) is where those sixteen packages are moving. Each is published on its own, at its own version, as @crab-shack/cap-<id>, @crab-shack/plugin-<id>, @crab-shack/claude-acp and @crab-shack/capabilities-testing. A product then picks capabilities by depending on them, as it already depends on the platform, and can write its own beside them. Capability ids, plugin type ids, layer ids, table names and migration histories never change in this move, because an existing database identifies each capability's migrations by its id.

A capability is one package with a daemon half (a definition made with defineCapabilityDefinition, exported from the package's root entry as a factory, stating its own package name and the SDK major it targets) and, when it has UI, a web half (a Nuxt layer at the package root). It owns its tables and its own migration history. A product is plain data (name, theme, scope label, and the id lists of capabilities, modules, plugin types and layers) joined at boot with the capability definitions; the daemon refuses to boot, naming the offender, when they disagree.

Commits: in the base and in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and once a repository's fast lane exists that push is also the release; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one. In Candy Mountain do not commit or push unless the orchestrator tells you to. The plan this bead comes from is in Candy Mountain at .ai-docs/plans/shared-capabilities/, for background only: this bead is complete without it.

The capabilities repository's packages are ready to publish but nothing manages their versions. Products will pin exact versions of individual capabilities, so each package needs its own version line and its own changelog: a migration in one capability must not look like a release of the others, and a product must be able to take one fix without moving everything.

Set up Changesets in the capabilities repository, as the base uses it, with these differences:
- Every published package is versioned independently. There is no fixed or linked group.
- A release of one capability must not by itself release another. Capabilities name each other as peer dependencies; configure Changesets so that a capability which needs another is only bumped when the other's new version falls outside the range it declares.
- The apps of the development distribution are private and are neither versioned nor tagged.
- Access is restricted and the base branch is main.

Add root scripts for adding a changeset, applying pending changesets to versions and changelogs, and building then publishing, named as the base names its own. Write a CONTRIBUTING.md stating the rule: every change to a published package carries a changeset; while the packages are on 0.x a breaking change takes a minor bump and its changeset text says what a product has to change.

Do not publish anything and do not write a release workflow; another bead does both.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a changeset for one capability, the status command lists that package only, and applying it changes that package's version and changelog and no other package's version.
- With a patch changeset for a capability that others need, applying it bumps none of the others.
- The development distribution's apps are never versioned.
- CONTRIBUTING.md states the rule; the gates are green.
notes: LANDED e8ca4d8 on capabilities main. Config: .changeset/config.json (changelog @changesets/cli/changelog, access restricted, baseBranch main, no fixed/linked, updateInternalDependencies patch, privatePackages version:false tag:false, ___experimentalUnsafeOptions onlyUpdatePeerDependentsWhenOutOfRange:true). Root scripts: pnpm changeset; pnpm version-packages (= changeset version, no SDK sync step); pnpm release (= pnpm build && changeset publish; NOT run, no workflow yet). @changesets/cli 3.0.3 root devDependency; lockfile diff is additions only. No pending changeset on main; all packages 0.1.0. BEHAVIOUR (run in a throwaway copy, changesets 3.0.3): patch of cap-acp/plugin-repository bumps only that package. Minor of cap-acp (0.1.0 -> 0.2.0, outside ^0.1.0) bumps cap-bots, cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex by PATCH, changelog 'Updated dependencies - @crab-shack/cap-acp@0.2.0'; their package.json change only in version (workspace:^ stays literal in source; pnpm pack writes ^0.2.0 into the tarball, verified). Cascade is not transitive beyond range: cap-bots needs plugin-claude-code ^0.1.x, its 0.1.1 is in range so no further bumps. Never a major cascade in 3.0.3 (determine-dependents is range-based already). The experimental option only affects apply: without it a dependent's changelog also lists in-range peer siblings' bumps (e.g. plugin-claude-code@0.1.1 under cap-bots). Apps (private) are never versioned or listed. NOTES FOR 94z.4.3: (1) publish with pnpm so workspace: ranges are rewritten (changeset publish uses pnpm publish under pnpm); a tarball published by npm would keep workspace:^ and be broken. Peers become ^<sibling's version at pack time>, so release in one run with versions applied together; a dependent packed after the sibling bump narrows to the new version (^0.1.1), fine. (2) devDependencies workspace:* become exact versions, harmless. (3) 'changeset status' compares to main via git; needs origin/main fetched in CI (fetch-depth 0). (4) changeset version does not touch pnpm-lock (specifiers unchanged). (5) README Releasing section still unwritten; README only points at CONTRIBUTING.md. (6) cap-issues watcher.test.ts 2000ms test failed in full run and alone under load avg 20, passed alone later (94z.3.8).
close_reason: Landed as e8ca4d8 on crab-shack/capabilities main: Changesets 3.0.3 with independent versions, private apps neither versioned nor tagged, peer dependents bumped only when out of range; root scripts changeset, version-packages, release; CONTRIBUTING.md. Shown in a throwaway copy: a patch of a needed capability bumps nothing else; a minor of cap-acp patch-bumps its five dependents and pnpm writes the new peer range at pack time. Four gates green after the rebase. Nothing published; every package still 0.1.0.

The packages in the capabilities repository are private, unversioned and export TypeScript source to each other. That works inside one workspace but not for a product that installs them from the registry: plain Node cannot run TypeScript from node_modules, so a product's built daemon could not start, and nothing says what a published package contains.

Give all sixteen packages a publishable shape, without publishing yet. Follow what the base's own packages do, since the two must feel the same to a product: inside the workspace a package still exports source, so nothing has to be built to work here; what gets published has the daemon half built with type declarations, the web layer as source (a Nuxt layer is consumed as source), and the migrations as files on disk, where the package finds them at run time whether it is running from source, from an install, or bundled into a product's daemon.

An installed package must work in a product exactly as the workspace package does: its definition starts under plain Node in a built daemon, its layer is found through the webLayer field and extended by the product's web app, and its migrations are found and applied. A capability's test support stays out of its main entry, as now.

A capability that needs another declares it as a peer dependency, so that a product ends up with exactly one copy of each capability however many others need it; two copies would mean two sets of service keys and two migration sets. The platform packages are peers too, with the SDK peer naming the one major the capability targets, as it already does. Installing a capability without something it needs must fail at install or at boot with a message naming what is missing, never silently.

Each package starts at version 0.1.0, publishes to GitHub Packages with restricted access, and says in its manifest what it is in one sentence.

Prove it without the registry: pack the packages and install the tarballs into a scratch product generated by platform-new product.
acceptance_criteria:
- pnpm build produces, for every package, exactly what would be published; packing a package yields the built daemon half with declarations, the layer source where it has one, and its migrations, and no tests or test support in the main entry.

- Installing cap-chat-claude-code alone, without what it needs, fails with a message naming what is missing.
- The product holds one copy of each capability.
- Inside the capabilities repository nothing needs building for lint, typecheck, test or pnpm dev, and all four gates are green.

(c) scripts/proof.sh and scripts/alone.sh again for final logs. LEARNED, NOT WRITTEN ANYWHERE ELSE YET.
- A capability that peers on @nuxt/ui or nuxt (optional or not) is installed TWICE in a product whose daemon app has a build tool whose rolldown differs from the one nuxt's own peer range picks (a fresh product with tsdown ^0.23.2 gets rolldown 1.3.2 beside nuxt's 1.2.19): pnpm resolves Nuxt's peer graph per app. With vue as the only web peer there is one copy. That is why the layers' type-only imports of @nuxt/ui are deliberately undeclared; the check script allows exactly that (type-only, from layer files, of @nuxt/ui and nuxt). Experiment in scratch e3/.
- pnpm 12 defaults: blockExoticSubdeps is on, so a tarball product needs blockExoticSubdeps: false plus an override pointing @crab-shack/claude-acp (a dependency of cap-acp) at its tarball; autoInstallPeers is on, so a missing peer is fetched from the registry silently once it is published (the boot check is the guarantee, not the install). A project that pins an older platform keeps it: another project's missing peer resolved to the pinned 0.7.0, not the newest 0.7.1.
- A product lists each capability and what it needs in BOTH apps' dependencies (cap-acp too, though it has no layer); listing only layer packages in the web app makes pnpm auto-install the rest for the web app.

- Peer range 0.x accepts platform 0.8.0, so 94z.3.7 need not change it; it also would not refuse a platform too old for a capability.
