A feature capability (@candy-mountain/cap-<id>, has a manifest) requires plugin types and depends on connection packages for their services. A service-only package that brings no plugin type keeps the cap- prefix. Target layout: plugin-repository and plugin-slack (renames of cap-repository and cap-slack), plugin-claude-code, plugin-codex, plugin-heroku and plugin-netlify (new), cap-acp (new, service-only, id acp: the ACP runtime, depending on threads and repository), with cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex, cap-deployments and cap-bots depending on them. Capability ids, plugin type ids, layer ids, table names, routes and stored data do not change unless a bead says so. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. Gates: pnpm lint, pnpm --recursive --workspace-concurrency=1 typecheck (parallel typechecks are killed for memory on this machine), pnpm test and pnpm build green. Do not commit.


Problem: the ACP runtime is inside cap-chat-claude-code: the harness that spawns ACP agent processes (over the claude-acp workspace package), the session manager that runs sessions over the platform's THREAD_SESSIONS store and takes launchers per family, the decision service and its store, and the session and decision routes, all bound to the ACP_SESSIONS, ACP_HARNESS and ACP_DECISIONS service keys. chat-codex registers its launcher on that manager and bots reads sessions and decisions from it, so both depend on a chat page capability to run an agent. The next beads move the claude-code and codex plugin types into connection packages that must register launchers on the manager without depending on a chat capability, so the runtime has to sit below them.

What to build: a new service-only capability package @candy-mountain/cap-acp with definition id acp that owns the ACP runtime: harness, session manager, decisions, the session and decision routes, the three service keys, the launcher registration mechanism, and whatever shared launch types and environment allowlist the launchers and bots use from the runtime today. It depends on the platform's threads definition (for the session store) and on repository (for the working directory service), exactly as chat-claude-code does now for these pieces. cap-chat-claude-code keeps its manifest, the claude-code plugin type, its launcher and family, and its chat UI, and depends on acp; it registers the claude-code launcher on the manager it now obtains as a service. cap-chat-codex and cap-bots switch their imports to cap-acp's root entry for everything that moved and declare acp in dependsOn and package.json; nothing else about them changes in this bead. The product lists acp in its capabilities, apps/daemon registers the definition, and the definition's close order keeps the existing behaviour that decisions stop before sessions and sessions before the harness. Routes keep their paths and gating. Tests move with the code they test; the daemon's testing helpers for ACP follow.

Non-goals: the plugin types stay where they are; the chat capabilities' web layers do not change; no new routes or services.

Acceptance: cap-chat-claude-code's definition no longer provides any ACP_* key and cap-acp's does; cap-chat-codex and cap-bots import nothing ACP-related from cap-chat-claude-code. Starting the daemon with the Candy Mountain product lists acp among started capabilities before chat-claude-code, chat-codex and bots. Every existing session, decision and bot test passes where it now lives. Root gates green.
close_reason: Extracted the ACP runtime (harness, sessions, decisions, routes, ACP_* keys) into service-only @candy-mountain/cap-acp (id acp); chat-claude-code, chat-codex and bots depend on it; gates green bar the known slack-notifications failures

Problem: the package boundary lint decides what a package is from its name prefix, and only @candy-mountain/cap-<id> counts as a capability package. title: Base: capability definitions declare product-level settings, validated at boot
description:
Context: two repositories on this machine. The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform; other git worktrees of it may sit beside it) is a pnpm 12 workspace run through Turborepo that holds the platform: packages/platform-daemon (a Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle: database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces, registries, grants, threads, the platform agent, startPlatform, createApp, runDaemon, and a /testing entry that is the test kit a capability's daemon tests import), packages/platform-web (the web shell as a Nuxt layer package, with the contribution points, the layer-list helpers a web app's Nuxt config calls with the product's layer ids, the cm-layers lint and a /test kit), packages/platform-sdk (wire types and the product configuration type on a Node-free root entry; defineCapabilityDefinition and the capability contract on the /daemon entry), packages/platform-config (address and data-directory resolution, the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends, the cm-packages boundary lint and its package-boundaries helpers, and the platform-link, platform-unlink and platform-check-linked commands a product runs) and packages/platform-cli (start, stop, status, logs, install-service for a distribution). These five are published together at one shared version (a Changesets fixed group; 0.3.1 at the time of writing) to GitHub Packages as private @crab-shack/platform-* packages: the daemon-side ones as built output, platform-web as source. Beside them: packages/cap-template (id template, private and never published: the deliberately small capability that exercises every contribution point and is the worked example an author copies; its README is the capability author's guide) and apps/, the base's own development distribution (apps/product, a plain-data product package; apps/daemon; apps/web) that runs the platform with the template and is what the base's tests boot. The READMEs of platform-daemon and platform-web are the conventions documents for a capability's daemon half and web half; docs/ holds registry-access.md, linking.md and upgrade-path.md; CONTRIBUTING.md holds the changeset rule.

Candy Mountain (github.com/kingrea/candy-mountain-v3, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) is a product built on the base: capability packages under its own scope @candy-mountain/ (packages/cap-<id>, feature capabilities with a manifest; packages/plugin-<id>, connection packages, each service-only and bringing the one plugin type its id names), a plain-data product package (packages/candy-mountain) and thin apps (apps/daemon lists every capability definition and runs runDaemon over the product; apps/web extends platform-web and the capability layers; apps/cli). It installs the five platform packages from the registry pinned at one exact version (0.3.0 at the time of writing) in every package.json. A product is pointed at a local base checkout with pnpm platform-link and back with pnpm platform-unlink (docs/linking.md in the base); a linked state is never left behind or committed.

A capability is one package with a daemon half (a definition made with defineCapabilityDefinition, exported from the package's root entry as a factory) and, when it has UI, a web half (a Nuxt layer at the package root, declared by a webLayer id in its package.json). The daemon boots a product: plain-data product configuration (name, description, theme, scope label and URL prefix, and the id lists of capabilities, modules, plugin types and layers) joined with the capability definitions and module definitions, and it refuses to boot, naming the offender, when they disagree.

This bead belongs to the phase of the platform-package work whose goal is that a capability built for the wrong SDK major is refused with a clear message, a capability's product-level settings are declared and checked at boot, a product can be described by one file, and a new capability or a new product starts from a generator instead of a blank directory. Standing decisions, not to revisit: packages are private and never public; the five platform packages share one version line and semver is meant; capabilities stay unpublished workspace packages inside each product, under the product's own scope; a defect in the base is fixed in the base and released, never worked around in a product.

Working rules: the gates are pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck (serial on purpose; parallel typechecks are killed for memory on this machine, so never raise its concurrency), pnpm test and pnpm build, green in every repository the bead touches. Other agents may be working in the same checkouts and running installs and gates at the same time; follow whatever locking and branch arrangement the person who assigned this bead gave you. A change to a published platform package carries a changeset as the base's CONTRIBUTING.md describes. Do not commit, push, or open or merge pull requests in either repository unless whoever assigned this bead tells you to; otherwise leave the work in the working tree and report the changed files. Work this bead depends on may not be on the base's main branch yet; whoever assigned the bead tells you where it is.

Problem: a capability's product-level settings are not declared anywhere. Candy Mountain's bots capability reads its worktree limits from environment variables deep inside the capability, other capabilities read theirs ad hoc or take them as untyped factory options, and nothing checks a value until the code that uses it runs. A product that wants a capability tuned a certain way has to write TypeScript, and a teammate who wants the same tuning copies code. For products to be described as data (a separate bead adds a product file with a settings block per capability), the daemon has to know what settings each capability accepts and refuse wrong ones before it starts.

What to build, in the base: extend the capability definition contract so a definition declares the shape of its product-level settings, with defaults, and receives the validated settings through its start context. The product handed to the daemon carries the settings, keyed by capability id, as plain data with no functions in it. The daemon validates every capability's settings against its declared shape at boot, before anything touches disk, and refuses to start with a message naming the capability and the offending key when a value is missing without a default, has the wrong type, or is not a key the capability declares. A capability that declares no settings accepts an absent or empty block and nothing else, and a settings block for a capability the product does not include is refused as well. The refusal must read like the existing product and module boot errors. Every value a capability can declare must be something a plain data file can hold, because the product file will be the usual source.

Give the mechanism a real user in the base: the template capability declares one small setting with a default whose effect a person can see in the running development distribution, and the development distribution supplies settings in code for now. If a second worked example package exists in the base when you arrive, it declares an empty settings shape. Anything you add to a worked example package in the base must follow its existing naming forms, because those packages are copied and renamed mechanically to start new capabilities. The daemon test kit lets a capability's tests start a platform with chosen settings for the capability under test. Describe how to declare and read settings in the daemon conventions (the definition, what is refused at boot, what the platform keeps stable) and in the capability author's guide.

Defaults and non-goals: settings are per product and per capability, one block per capability id; not per module and not per workspace. Per-workspace configuration stays in plugin instances and capability tables. Factory options that are code (test fakes, callbacks) stay as they are and are not part of the declared shape. Do not add a file reader, a YAML parser or a generator. Environment variable resolution for ports and the data directory stays in platform-config. Settings are not exposed to the web app or over the API by the platform; a capability that wants one visible serves it itself. Do not convert any Candy Mountain capability; that is a separate bead after the release. Choose the validation approach (a schema library capability packages already depend on, or hand-written validators like the module registry's) and justify it in the handoff; the SDK's root entry must stay Node-free and must gain no dependency a browser bundle would carry. The change is additive, so a capability that declares nothing keeps working and the changeset is a minor.
acceptance_criteria: A definition can declare settings with defaults. Booting with a value of the wrong type, an undeclared key, a missing value that has no default, or a block for a capability the product does not include refuses to start, and the message names the capability and the key. Booting with no block for a capability that declares defaults starts with those defaults. A capability that declares no settings refuses a non-empty block. The template declares one setting; changing its value where the development distribution supplies it visibly changes the running app, and a wrong value there stops the daemon at boot. A capability's tests can start the test kit's platform with chosen settings. The daemon conventions and the author's guide describe declaring and reading settings. A minor changeset is present. The four gates are green in the base.

title: Type every untyped $api(...) call in the web packages so nuxt typecheck stops depending on check order
description: apps/web nuxt typecheck is order-sensitive: an untyped $api(path, options) call over a string path makes TypeScript infer the result through Nitro's MatchedRoutes conditional types, and TypeScript 6.0.3 caches a stack-depth overflow in the relation map (relationCount = 16e6 - relation.size >> 3; relation.set(id, Failed | StackDepthOverflow)) and replays it as TS2321 'Excessive stack depth comparing types'. Which files were checked before the call decides whether it overflows: ncj.4.10 bisected it to one layer unit test (packages/cap-chat-claude-code/test/unit/chat-claude-code-setup.test.ts) entering the program through a nuxt typescript.tsConfig.include of test/**, and typing packages/cap-repository/app/plugins/repository.ts:3 as $api<T>(...) only moved the identical error to packages/platform-web/app/composables/usePlugins.ts:48. Fix: give every $api( call without an explicit type argument one ($api<void> for DELETE/POST calls whose body is unused, $api<T> otherwise): platform-web app/composables/usePlugins.ts:48, app/components/AppLogout.vue:15, app/components/projects/ProjectsOrganisations.vue:98, app/pages/projects.vue:92/96/105; cap-repository app/plugins/repository.ts:3 (nuxtApp.$api<T>(path, options) instead of the as Promise<T> cast); cap-team app/components/Manager.vue:57; cap-deployments app/components/Manager.vue:69; cap-uptime app/components/Board.vue:91; the bots layer app/components/Manager.vue:99. Then cap-chat-claude-code can restore the typescript.tsConfig.include of test/** in its nuxt.config.ts (and drop app/utils and test from its tsconfig include) so its layer tests are typechecked by apps/web like the other cap packages (ncj.4.8 shape). Acceptance: grep -rnE '\$api\(' over packages/platform-web/app, packages/platform-web/layers, packages/cap-*/app and apps/web/layers finds no call without a type argument; root pnpm typecheck green with the include restored.
notes: 2026-11-08 (ncj.5.2): every untyped $api( call in the listed web files now carries an explicit type argument (<unknown> for DELETE/POST calls whose body is unused; nuxtApp.$api<T>(path, options) in plugin-repository); the acceptance grep finds none. Remaining for this bead: restore cap-chat-claude-code's typescript.tsConfig.include of test/** and drop app/utils and test from its tsconfig include.
close_reason: Restored test/** typescript.tsConfig.include in cap-chat-claude-code nuxt.config.ts, dropped app/utils and test from its tsconfig include; no untyped $api( calls remain; typecheck, lint, test, build green with no TS2321.

title: packages/platform-cli takes the product and the apps' paths from the distribution
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace. apps/daemon is a Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle: src/platform.ts boots a Product (the shared product configuration joined with a list of runtime capability definitions, built in src/candy-mountain.ts from src/definitions.ts) and src/app.ts mounts each started definition's routes; a definition is made with defineCapabilityDefinition in src/capabilities/definition.ts (id, optional manifest, dependsOn, pluginTypes, sessionFamilies, provides, and start(context) returning services, workspace and platform routes, MCP servers, chat families, notification channels, onWorkspaceDeleted and close; context.service resolves only keys a declared dependency binds); src/seam.test.ts fails when platform.ts or app.ts import a product folder. apps/web is a Nuxt 4 app: each capability's UI is a layer under apps/web/layers/, registered by glob in this repo or from the product configuration's layer list with CM_WEB_LAYERS=product through apps/web/layer-list.mjs, which also resolves layer packages (a dependency whose package.json says "webLayer": "<id>"); apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the directions capability -> core and capability -> chat only; core offers contribution points (plugin panels, plugin icons, chat family pieces, overview home card slots) and the scope word only through its SCOPE helper. packages/shared holds the wire types both apps import and the product configuration (CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT in src/product.ts: name, theme, scope label and URL prefix, and the capability, module, plugin type and layer ids) with no Node or DOM types; packages/config resolves ports and the data directory; packages/claude-acp and apps/cli complete the workspace. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table; phases 1 and 3 have landed). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (still named projects in the daemon's tables, the /projects API prefix and the shared wire types; the UI word comes from the product's scope label) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation and readiness, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads and the session store (the platform-owned threads definition), Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections (the service-only slack capability), Slack routing, decisions and handoffs (owned by bots), uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, slack, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent, plus the platform's threads. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Declared dependencies today: chat-claude-code on threads; chat-codex on chat-claude-code; bots on chat-claude-code, chat-codex and slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. Nothing is published: every package stays private with workspace:* dependencies. pnpm lint, pnpm --recursive --workspace-concurrency=1 typecheck (parallel typechecks are killed for memory on this machine), pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record in it any decision a later bead must know.

Phase 4 shape, fixed for every bead in it. Target layout: packages/platform-daemon (platform start, the app factory, the platform routes and services, the platform-owned definitions threads, overview and platform-agent, the platform schema set and its migrations; one public root entry), packages/platform-web (a Nuxt layer package holding the shell, the chat and overview layers, the Nitro proxy, the contribution points, the layer-list and scope-route helpers and the cm-layers lint plugin), packages/platform-sdk (what packages/shared was: the wire types that cross the platform line, the product configuration type, and the define helpers and contract types for capabilities, manifests, plugin types, service keys, facts, event types and schema sets; no runtime services), packages/platform-config (what packages/config was: runtime address and data dir resolution, plus the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends), packages/platform-cli (what apps/cli was, taking the product and the apps' paths from the distribution), packages/claude-acp (unchanged), one packages/cap-<id> per product capability (issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, slack, team, uptime, deployments, repository) with a daemon entry exporting its definition factory and service keys and a web entry that is its Nuxt layer (package.json "webLayer": "<id>"), a small packages/candy-mountain product package holding the product configuration and module definitions as plain data, and the thin apps/daemon and apps/web. Import rules, obeyed from the first move and enforced by lint beads later: a capability package imports @candy-mountain/platform-sdk and, on the daemon side, the root entry of @candy-mountain/platform-daemon; on the web side it uses the platform-web layer through the existing capability-to-core direction; never a subpath of any platform package; another capability package only through that package's root entry and only when the importing capability's definition names it in dependsOn and its package.json lists it; a platform package never imports a capability package; the apps import root entries only. Package names keep the @candy-mountain scope. Nothing is published: every package is private, dependencies are workspace:*, no publishConfig, no registry, no changesets. Each package carries its own test, lint, typecheck and build scripts so the Turborepo pipeline runs them per package; a moved test moves with its code.

apps/cli finds the repository from its own path, reads the Candy Mountain product configuration from a file it owns, and runs the daemon from apps/daemon/dist and the web from apps/web/.output. Make the CLI a platform package, @candy-mountain/platform-cli, whose entry takes the product configuration, the daemon and web locations and the data directory resolution from whoever calls it, with every command, the supervisor, systemd unit generation and the log and pid handling moving as they are. apps/cli becomes the thin candy-mountain bin that calls the package with Candy Mountain's product and this repository's paths. The CLI's README describes the split. Non-goals: new commands; renaming environment variables.
acceptance_criteria: The package's tests run on their own and import no app. The candy-mountain bin starts, stops and reports status exactly as before, and a test shows another product name and paths flowing into unit files and messages. All gates pass.
close_reason: apps/cli -> @candy-mountain/platform-cli with runCli(argv, distribution, host?); apps/cli is a thin bin via candyMountain(repoRoot) distribution. Names derive from dataDirName(product.name); Rock Candy test proves another product flows through. Lint/build green; typecheck/test only failed in daemon packages mid-move by ncj.4.6, to be re-confirmed when 4.6 lands.

title: packages/cap-deployments: deployments, environments and the netlify and heroku plugin types as one package
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace. apps/daemon is a Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle: src/platform.ts boots a Product (the shared product configuration joined with a list of runtime capability definitions, built in src/candy-mountain.ts from src/definitions.ts) and src/app.ts mounts each started definition's routes; a definition is made with defineCapabilityDefinition in src/capabilities/definition.ts (id, optional manifest, dependsOn, pluginTypes, sessionFamilies, provides, and start(context) returning services, workspace and platform routes, MCP servers, chat families, notification channels, onWorkspaceDeleted and close; context.service resolves only keys a declared dependency binds); src/seam.test.ts fails when platform.ts or app.ts import a product folder. apps/web is a Nuxt 4 app: each capability's UI is a layer under apps/web/layers/, registered by glob in this repo or from the product configuration's layer list with CM_WEB_LAYERS=product through apps/web/layer-list.mjs, which also resolves layer packages (a dependency whose package.json says "webLayer": "<id>"); apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the directions capability -> core and capability -> chat only; core offers contribution points (plugin panels, plugin icons, chat family pieces, overview home card slots) and the scope word only through its SCOPE helper. packages/shared holds the wire types both apps import and the product configuration (CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT in src/product.ts: name, theme, scope label and URL prefix, and the capability, module, plugin type and layer ids) with no Node or DOM types; packages/config resolves ports and the data directory; packages/claude-acp and apps/cli complete the workspace. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table; phases 1 and 3 have landed). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (still named projects in the daemon's tables, the /projects API prefix and the shared wire types; the UI word comes from the product's scope label) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation and readiness, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads and the session store (the platform-owned threads definition), Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections (the service-only slack capability), Slack routing, decisions and handoffs (owned by bots), uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, slack, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent, plus the platform's threads. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Declared dependencies today: chat-claude-code on threads; chat-codex on chat-claude-code; bots on chat-claude-code, chat-codex and slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. Nothing is published: every package stays private with workspace:* dependencies. pnpm lint, pnpm --recursive --workspace-concurrency=1 typecheck (parallel typechecks are killed for memory on this machine), pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record in it any decision a later bead must know.

Phase 4 shape, fixed for every bead in it. Target layout: packages/platform-daemon (platform start, the app factory, the platform routes and services, the platform-owned definitions threads, overview and platform-agent, the platform schema set and its migrations; one public root entry), packages/platform-web (a Nuxt layer package holding the shell, the chat and overview layers, the Nitro proxy, the contribution points, the layer-list and scope-route helpers and the cm-layers lint plugin), packages/platform-sdk (what packages/shared was: the wire types that cross the platform line, the product configuration type, and the define helpers and contract types for capabilities, manifests, plugin types, service keys, facts, event types and schema sets; no runtime services), packages/platform-config (what packages/config was: runtime address and data dir resolution, plus the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends), packages/platform-cli (what apps/cli was, taking the product and the apps' paths from the distribution), packages/claude-acp (unchanged), one packages/cap-<id> per product capability (issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, slack, team, uptime, deployments, repository) with a daemon entry exporting its definition factory and service keys and a web entry that is its Nuxt layer (package.json "webLayer": "<id>"), a small packages/candy-mountain product package holding the product configuration and module definitions as plain data, and the thin apps/daemon and apps/web. Import rules, obeyed from the first move and enforced by lint beads later: a capability package imports @candy-mountain/platform-sdk and, on the daemon side, the root entry of @candy-mountain/platform-daemon; on the web side it uses the platform-web layer through the existing capability-to-core direction; never a subpath of any platform package; another capability package only through that package's root entry and only when the importing capability's definition names it in dependsOn and its package.json lists it; a platform package never imports a capability package; the apps import root entries only. Package names keep the @candy-mountain scope. Nothing is published: every package is private, dependencies are workspace:*, no publishConfig, no registry, no changesets. Each package carries its own test, lint, typecheck and build scripts so the Turborepo pipeline runs them per package; a moved test moves with its code.

Move the deployments capability into packages/cap-deployments: its daemon folders deployments and environments, the netlify and heroku plugin types, its schema set and migrations, its web layer apps/web/layers/deployments as the package's layer, its tests, and the wire types in the SDK that only this capability's daemon and web halves share (the SDK keeps what the platform reads). The package exposes a daemon entry exporting the definition factory and a web entry that is the layer. apps/daemon's definition list and apps/web's layer list and dependencies point at the package. Obey the phase 4 import rules. Non-goals: other capabilities; the thin app rewrite.
acceptance_criteria: No deployments, environments, netlify or heroku code remains under apps/. The package's tests run on their own through the pipeline. Environments, live versions and the deployments page behave as before. Removing the package's line from each app and running the pipeline passes, with no environments table in a fresh database; restore it afterwards. All gates pass.
close_reason: Landed uncommitted: packages/cap-deployments (deployments, environments, netlify and heroku plugin types, schema set, web layer, wire types); already on the 4.19 layerPackageConfig lint shape. All root gates green; removal verified in a scratch copy. Decisions in phase-4-decisions.md. Filed candy-mountain-v3-6rw for a Mastra-table test flake.

title: packages/platform-daemon holds the daemon's platform half behind one public entry
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace. apps/daemon is a Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle: src/platform.ts boots a Product (the shared product configuration joined with a list of runtime capability definitions, built in src/candy-mountain.ts from src/definitions.ts) and src/app.ts mounts each started definition's routes; a definition is made with defineCapabilityDefinition in src/capabilities/definition.ts (id, optional manifest, dependsOn, pluginTypes, sessionFamilies, provides, and start(context) returning services, workspace and platform routes, MCP servers, chat families, notification channels, onWorkspaceDeleted and close; context.service resolves only keys a declared dependency binds); src/seam.test.ts fails when platform.ts or app.ts import a product folder. apps/web is a Nuxt 4 app: each capability's UI is a layer under apps/web/layers/, registered by glob in this repo or from the product configuration's layer list with CM_WEB_LAYERS=product through apps/web/layer-list.mjs, which also resolves layer packages (a dependency whose package.json says "webLayer": "<id>"); apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the directions capability -> core and capability -> chat only; core offers contribution points (plugin panels, plugin icons, chat family pieces, overview home card slots) and the scope word only through its SCOPE helper. packages/shared holds the wire types both apps import and the product configuration (CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT in src/product.ts: name, theme, scope label and URL prefix, and the capability, module, plugin type and layer ids) with no Node or DOM types; packages/config resolves ports and the data directory; packages/claude-acp and apps/cli complete the workspace. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table; phases 1 and 3 have landed). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (still named projects in the daemon's tables, the /projects API prefix and the shared wire types; the UI word comes from the product's scope label) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation and readiness, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads and the session store (the platform-owned threads definition), Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections (the service-only slack capability), Slack routing, decisions and handoffs (owned by bots), uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, slack, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent, plus the platform's threads. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Declared dependencies today: chat-claude-code on threads; chat-codex on chat-claude-code; bots on chat-claude-code, chat-codex and slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. Nothing is published: every package stays private with workspace:* dependencies. pnpm lint, pnpm --recursive --workspace-concurrency=1 typecheck (parallel typechecks are killed for memory on this machine), pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record in it any decision a later bead must know.

Phase 4 shape, fixed for every bead in it. Target layout: packages/platform-daemon (platform start, the app factory, the platform routes and services, the platform-owned definitions threads, overview and platform-agent, the platform schema set and its migrations; one public root entry), packages/platform-web (a Nuxt layer package holding the shell, the chat and overview layers, the Nitro proxy, the contribution points, the layer-list and scope-route helpers and the cm-layers lint plugin), packages/platform-sdk (what packages/shared was: the wire types that cross the platform line, the product configuration type, and the define helpers and contract types for capabilities, manifests, plugin types, service keys, facts, event types and schema sets; no runtime services), packages/platform-config (what packages/config was: runtime address and data dir resolution, plus the tsconfig, ESLint and vitest presets every package extends), packages/platform-cli (what apps/cli was, taking the product and the apps' paths from the distribution), packages/claude-acp (unchanged), one packages/cap-<id> per product capability (issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, slack, team, uptime, deployments, repository) with a daemon entry exporting its definition factory and service keys and a web entry that is its Nuxt layer (package.json "webLayer": "<id>"), a small packages/candy-mountain product package holding the product configuration and module definitions as plain data, and the thin apps/daemon and apps/web. Import rules, obeyed from the first move and enforced by lint beads later: a capability package imports @candy-mountain/platform-sdk and, on the daemon side, the root entry of @candy-mountain/platform-daemon; on the web side it uses the platform-web layer through the existing capability-to-core direction; never a subpath of any platform package; another capability package only through that package's root entry and only when the importing capability's definition names it in dependsOn and its package.json lists it; a platform package never imports a capability package; the apps import root entries only. Package names keep the @candy-mountain scope. Nothing is published: every package is private, dependencies are workspace:*, no publishConfig, no registry, no changesets. Each package carries its own test, lint, typecheck and build scripts so the Turborepo pipeline runs them per package; a moved test moves with its code.

The daemon's platform half still lives in apps/daemon/src beside the product capabilities. Move it into packages/platform-daemon: the data directory, the database opener and the platform schema set with its migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries and plugin instances, grants, registry computation and readiness, settings, activity, notifications, threads, the agent MCP host, Mastra, the platform-owned definitions threads, overview and platform-agent, the platform routes, the app factory, platform start, boot and the product assertion. The package's root entry exports what a distribution needs (start, the app factory, the product type and its assertion) and what capabilities build on (route helpers and gates, actor and workspace lookups, plugin instance resolution, activity append, the platform service keys and whatever else a product definition imports today); package.json exports allows only that entry. The product's capability folders stay in apps/daemon/src for this bead and import the platform through the package root only, every relative import into a platform folder rewritten, which is the forcing function for the entry being complete. The package carries its own tests; its test support takes explicit definitions and never knows Candy Mountain, while the product-aware test helpers stay in apps/daemon. The migrations folder must resolve from source and from the built output. The seam test becomes a guard inside the package that it imports no app code. Non-goals: capability packages; the thin app shape (apps/daemon keeps its entry, product composition and capability folders until later beads).
acceptance_criteria: apps/daemon imports nothing from the package's src, only the package name. A test in the platform package boots a platform with no product definitions and serves its own routes. The daemon builds and runs with the same boot log, and the built daemon finds its migrations. Every moved test passes in the package. All gates pass.
close_reason: Landed uncommitted: platform-daemon root entry complete, apps/daemon imports package name only, product-agnostic test support, migrations resolve from source and dist (boot verified), no-product route test added; lint/test/build green, typecheck green except apps/web (ncj.4.7 in flight). Decisions in phase-4-decisions.md.

comments.author: kingrea
comments.text: 2026-11-03 evening: agent stopped mid-move at Jack's request. State: platform folders already git-mv'd from apps/daemon/src into packages/platform-daemon/src (activity, etc.); apps/daemon/src keeps the product folders plus candy-mountain.ts, definitions.ts, modules.ts, config.ts, index.ts, package-root.ts, testing/. Last note from the agent: the package's test harness opens its own DB with platform tables only and the app wrapper needs to hand in Candy Mountain's, so it was adding an openDatabase option. Typecheck/test were red in platform-daemon and daemon when stopped. Decisions from landed beads: .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/phase-4-decisions.md. Resume by reading git status for packages/platform-daemon and finishing the root entry + tests.

apps/daemon has one Drizzle schema (src/db/schema) and one migration folder (drizzle/) for every table in the system, applied under one migrations table by src/db/index.ts. A capability cannot carry its tables with it, and the platform cannot boot a product without some capability's tables. The capability definition contract gains an optional declaration of the capability's schema and migrations folder. Generation: one documented way to generate a migration for a single set (a drizzle-kit config per set or a script taking the set id; your choice), and the schema drift test (src/db/schema.test.ts) checks every set against its own folder's latest snapshot. In this bead the platform set is today's whole drizzle/ folder and schema, and no capability declares a set: prove the mechanism with fixture sets in tests. Non-goals: moving any table (a later bead); carrying an existing database across.
acceptance_criteria: Tests apply two fixture sets, the second referencing the first's table, in order under separate migrations tables with per-set counts, and a second open applies nothing. The projects table and the Project wire type carry both what every product needs (identity, slug, name, colour, organisation, archived state) and what only Candy Mountain needs (the repository source and the verification facts about the path). The platform must own a workspace without the repository, so a product without repositories runs the same platform. Add a product capability definition with id repository, service-only like slack (no manifest, no views or ladder, absent from the catalog and grants, listed in the product configuration's capabilities), that owns: a table of repository records keyed by workspace id (source and verification, at most one per workspace, removed with the workspace), path normalisation and verification (today apps/daemon/src/projects/verification.ts and the source handling in projects.ts), routes under the workspace prefix to read, set, check and reverify a workspace's repository, the repository wire types in packages/shared, and a service it provides (a service key) answering a workspace's repository path to other capabilities. The registry's repository facts keep working by reading the repository record for now (a later bead turns facts into declarations). The web: only the repository layer changes, since the previous bead moved every path and verification piece into it; it saves the repository through the new routes from the form's after-save hook and checks a path through the check route. The existing numbered migration history gains one generated migration that creates the repository table, copies every project's source and verification into it and drops the two columns; do not squash or reorganise the migration folder. title: Move the repository path field, path check and verification facts out of core into the repository layer
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace. apps/daemon is a Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle: src/platform.ts boots a Product (the shared product configuration joined with a list of runtime capability definitions, built in src/candy-mountain.ts from src/definitions.ts) and src/app.ts mounts each started definition's routes; a definition is made with defineCapabilityDefinition in src/capabilities/definition.ts (id, optional manifest, dependsOn, pluginTypes, sessionFamilies, provides, and start(context) returning services, workspace and platform routes, MCP servers, chat families, notification channels, onWorkspaceDeleted and close; context.service resolves only keys a declared dependency binds); src/seam.test.ts fails when platform.ts or app.ts import a product folder. apps/web is a Nuxt 4 app: each capability's UI is a layer under apps/web/layers/, registered by glob in this repo or from the product configuration's layer list with CM_WEB_LAYERS=product through apps/web/layer-list.mjs, which also resolves layer packages (a dependency whose package.json says "webLayer": "<id>"); apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the directions capability -> core and capability -> chat only; core offers contribution points (plugin panels, plugin icons, chat family pieces, overview home card slots) and the scope word only through its SCOPE helper. packages/shared holds the wire types both apps import and the product configuration (CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT in src/product.ts: name, theme, scope label and URL prefix, and the capability, module, plugin type and layer ids) with no Node or DOM types; packages/config resolves ports and the data directory; packages/claude-acp and apps/cli complete the workspace. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table; phases 1 and 3 have landed). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (still named projects in the daemon's tables, the /projects API prefix and the shared wire types; the UI word comes from the product's scope label) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation and readiness, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads and the session store (the platform-owned threads definition), Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections (the service-only slack capability), Slack routing, decisions and handoffs (owned by bots), uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, slack, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent, plus the platform's threads. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Declared dependencies today: chat-claude-code on threads; chat-codex on chat-claude-code; bots on chat-claude-code, chat-codex and slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. Nothing is published: every package stays private with workspace:* dependencies. pnpm lint, pnpm --recursive --workspace-concurrency=1 typecheck (parallel typechecks are killed for memory on this machine), pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record in it any decision a later bead must know.

Core's Projects page and project form (apps/web/app/pages/projects.vue, app/components/projects/ProjectsFormModal.vue, ProjectsList.vue and ProjectsVerificationFacts.vue) read and write the repository source path and show the path verification facts (exists, has beads, git repo, remote). Those are Candy Mountain's product data: a home dashboard's workspace has no path. The next daemon bead moves source and verification out of the platform workspace into a repository capability with its own API, and that move must touch one layer, not the shell. Prepare the web now, with no daemon or shared-type change: core gains contribution slots on the workspace form (extra fields with their own validation and a hook that runs after the workspace is created or updated, with the saved workspace) and on the workspace list row (extra detail), in the spirit of the overview card slots in apps/web/app/utils/project-home.ts and the plugin panel registry. The repository layer (apps/web/layers/repository, a plugin-type layer today) contributes the path field with its check button, the path shown on the row and the verification facts, still reading and writing today's project API. Afterwards core knows nothing about paths, beads directories, git or remotes; the scope-copy guard and layer prefix rules apply as usual; the Projects page looks and behaves exactly as today. Non-goals: the daemon, packages/shared, the daemon's data split.
acceptance_criteria: A grep of core (apps/web/app, apps/web/server, apps/web/shared) finds no reference to the source path, verification or the repository facts. The repository layer's tests cover the field, the check and the facts, and a unit test shows the form and the row render without them when nothing is contributed. Creating, editing, checking and listing a project in the browser works as before. The layer README documents the two new slots. All gates pass.
close_reason: Core Projects page gains form-field and list-row contribution slots; the repository layer contributes the path field, path check, row path, facts and re-check action

title: Daemon and shared link builders read the scope URL prefix from the product configuration
description: Context: see bd show candy-mountain-v3-ncj.1.14 for the shared context paragraph and the product configuration; see bd show candy-mountain-v3-ncj.3.3 notes for how the web app now derives every scoped route and link from PRODUCT.scope.urlPrefix. Bead 3.3 found that URLs written by the daemon still hard-code /p/: packages/shared projectViewRoute (registry.ts), chatThreadLink (threads.ts), uptimeMonitorLink (uptime.ts); apps/daemon/src/slack/handoffs.ts (around line 140) and apps/daemon/src/notifications/dispatcher.ts (around line 87). These feed the registry view 'to' paths (sidebar), platform-agent navigate actions, and activity and notification links, so under another prefix they point at a route that no longer exists. Make each builder take the prefix from the product configuration the daemon starts from (1.14), threading it where shared helpers are pure (a prefix argument or a factory bound once at boot), with no behaviour change for Candy Mountain. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups).
acceptance_criteria: grep of packages/shared and apps/daemon for '/p/' finds no link builder; a unit test shows a different prefix flowing through projectViewRoute, chatThreadLink, uptimeMonitorLink, handoff links and notification links; lint, typecheck, test, build green.
notes: Shared builders take the prefix first: projectViewRoute(prefix, slug, path), chatThreadLink(prefix, slug, threadId), uptimeMonitorLink(prefix, slug, monitorId); no factory. Daemon threads a required scopeUrlPrefix: string through CapabilityContext, NotificationDispatcherDeps, AppVariables (c.var), ThreadServiceOptions (now required options), RegistryInput, RegistryLoadDeps, PlatformTurnContext, IncidentTrackerDeps, SlackHandoffsDeps; bound in startPlatform and createApp from product.config.scope.urlPrefix. Handoff fallback projectViewRoute(prefix, encodeURIComponent(slug), 'bots'); dispatcher fallback projectViewRoute(prefix, slug, ''). Only doc comments still show /p/ (shared activity.ts, product.ts, daemon README). apps/web imports none of the shared builders. Gates at hand-back: typecheck/build green; lint + 11 tests red only from in-flight 1.11 - re-verify after 1.11 and check threadServiceFor still receives scopeUrlPrefix.
close_reason: Done by subagents; full workspace lint, typecheck, test (1518 passed), build green.

description:

Capability ids: overview, issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record any decision a later bead must know in it.

The web app globs apps/web/layers/* to register its layers and apps/web/layers/README.md forbids an extends list, because inside this repo the directories are the list. A distribution in another repo will install layers as packages and must be able to name them. packages/shared now exports a product configuration listing the layer ids the product includes. Keep the glob for development inside this repo and add the ability for the web app to be given an explicit layer list (the product configuration's layer ids resolved to directories or package names), so that a listed layer that is missing fails the build with a message naming it and an unlisted directory is not registered when the explicit list is in use. Teach the boundary lint (apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs) that a layer can be a package as well as a directory, with ownership still coming from where a file lives (a package root owns its files the way a layer directory does today), and extend the fixture-based lint test in apps/web/test for the package case. Update the README. Non-goals: actually turning any layer into a package (phase 4); the daemon.
acceptance_criteria: The web app builds as today with the glob; with the explicit list in use it builds with exactly the listed layers and fails naming a missing one (tested); the lint resolves ownership for a package-backed layer in the fixture app and each rule still fires there; the README describes both modes; lint, typecheck, test and build green.
notes: Glob (layers/*) stays the default; CM_WEB_LAYERS=product makes nuxt.config.ts build extends from PRODUCT.layers via layerListConfig(PRODUCT.layers, root) in apps/web/layer-list.mjs; unlisted layers/* dirs are dropped in modules:before; a listed id that cannot be resolved (or exists both as dir and package, or a package without nuxt.config) fails the build naming it. Explicit extends entries are [realDir, { meta: { name: id } }] so package layers get the #layers/<id> alias; list order = layer priority. Layer package identification (phase 4 relies on it): package.json field webLayer: '<id>', listed in the web app's dependencies/devDependencies, nuxt.config.* at package root; discovery is packageLayers(root) in layer-list.mjs, shared by Nuxt and the lint. Lint: files under a package layer root belong to that layer (package wins over a same-id dir); #layers/<id> resolves into the package; importing a layer package by name is checked like a layer import. Fixture package test/fixtures/delta-layer linked from test/fixtures/layered-app/package.json. test/unit/layer-list.test.ts requires CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT.layers to equal the layers/* directories - a new layer must be added to the product list. Lint DEFAULT_ROOT is apps/web; must point at the distribution's web root when the plugin moves into a package. Explicit mode still typechecks layers/*/app/** (Nuxt tsconfig), so typecheck in glob mode.
close_reason: Done by subagent; lint, typecheck, build green in both modes; tests green except the Slack flake tracked in ncj.1.16.

title: Give the chat layer a contribution point for family-specific pieces and move model and effort controls out
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace: apps/daemon (Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle; src/platform.ts starts every background service and src/app.ts mounts every route by hand), apps/web (Nuxt 4 app; each capability's UI is a Nuxt layer under apps/web/layers/<capability-id>, apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the boundaries), packages/shared (wire types both apps import), packages/config, packages/claude-acp and apps/cli. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under the plan in .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (today called projects) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads with native agent families, Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections, routing, decisions and handoffs, uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record any decision a later bead must know in it.

The chat layer (apps/web/layers/chat) is platform: it renders threads for any agent family, including the native platform agent, and a home dashboard will want it. Today its agent panel renders model and effort controls in the prompt bar and a model-and-effort divider in the transcript, which belong to the ACP session families (claude-code and codex), and a bot worktree card, which belongs to bots (a separate bead moves the card). Give the chat layer a contribution point for family-specific transcript and prompt-bar pieces, keyed by the thread's family, registered from a Nuxt plugin in the contributing layer in the same way rail entries register today, so the chat layer renders whatever was registered for the current thread's family and knows no family by name. Move the model and effort controls, the divider and their utils and tests out of the chat layer and register them from the chat-claude-code and chat-codex layers (both exist). Layers cannot import each other, so decide whether the two layers each carry their own copy or the chat layer keeps a family-agnostic options control that a family's layer feeds; either is acceptable as long as the chat layer contains no reference to claude-code, codex, bots, worktrees or ACP. Model and effort behaviour for Claude Code and Codex threads is unchanged. Non-goals: the bot worktree card; the daemon.
acceptance_criteria: The chat layer has a documented contribution point (README updated) and no reference to claude-code, codex, bots, worktrees or ACP (a test or grep guard enforces it); a Claude Code thread and a Codex thread show model and effort controls and the divider exactly as before; a platform agent thread shows none; moved tests pass; lint, typecheck, test and build green.
notes: Contribution point: chatFamilyRegister(family, { id: <layer id>, aboveTranscript?: Component, promptBar?: Component }) in apps/web/layers/chat/app/utils/chatFamilies.ts (auto-imported; call from the contributing layer's Nuxt plugin with defineAsyncComponent(() => import('#layers/<id>/app/components/X.vue'))); same id re-registers; several layers per family render in registration order; read side chatFamilyPieces/chatFamilyComponents. AgentPanel resolves family from RegistryAgent.family; aboveTranscript renders after ChatBotWorktree (until 3.8) and before ChatTranscript; promptBar renders in ChatPromptBar #options slot. Each piece gets thread: ChatFamilyThread { slug, agentId, agent, threadId, thread, sessions, working (read-only refs); draft + setDraft(fields); setSessionDividers(labels); update(body) (PATCH, keeps replaced session log, refreshes); refresh() }; the panel clears draft/dividers when threadId or agentId changes. Model/effort piece, composable, util and test now duplicated in chat-claude-code (ChatClaudeCodeModelEffort) and chat-codex (ChatCodexModelEffort); dedupe later if a shared non-platform home appears. Guard test apps/web/layers/chat/test/unit/families.test.ts forbids claude/codex/acp words in the chat layer and bot/worktree outside BOT_CARD_PENDING. For 3.8: in bots Nuxt plugin call chatFamilyRegister(f, { id: 'bots', aboveTranscript: <Card> }) for each BOT_FAMILIES entry; card detects bot via thread.agent.value?.kind === 'bot' / .bot, fetches per-thread bot state itself (today from ChatThreadResponse.bot via useChatThread, same useAsyncData key), calls thread.refresh() after close; then delete ChatBotWorktree.vue + its line in AgentPanel.vue, the bot computed and close() in useChatThreads.ts (or relocate), and empty BOT_CARD_PENDING. Open: ChatThreadResponse.bot / useChatThreads().close are product fields in platform code - 3.8 or phase 4 decides their home.
close_reason: Done by subagent; lint, typecheck, test (1440 passed), build green.

Core's Nuxt plugin apps/web/app/plugins/plugin-panels.ts registers the Claude Code panel and the Claude Code setup form from components in core, and the login flow they use (a composable and a setup util with its unit test) lives in core too, so the shell knows a product plugin type. Create the chat-claude-code layer (no pages; the capability has no views) and move the panel, the form, the login composable, the setup util and their tests into it with the layer's prefix, registering the panel and form from the layer's own Nuxt plugin through the existing registrations. The login flow (start login, submit code, revoke, executable check) and the form's behaviour inside the add/edit modal are unchanged. Non-goals: the Codex panel; chat model and effort controls.
acceptance_criteria: Core contains no Claude Code panel, form, login composable or setup util and no reference to the claude-code plugin type; the Plugins page shows the Claude Code panel and the add/edit modal shows its form exactly as before; moved tests pass under the layer; lint, typecheck, test and build green.
notes: Layer chat-claude-code (prefix ChatClaudeCode): ChatClaudeCodePanel (app/components/Panel.vue), ChatClaudeCodeForm (app/components/Form.vue), Nuxt plugin app/plugins/chat-claude-code.ts registers panel+form for 'claude-code'. Login composable moved to layers/chat-claude-code/app/composables/useChatClaudeCodeLogin.ts (exports useChatClaudeCodeLogin, type ChatClaudeCodeLoginOutcome); only this layer may use it (capability->capability and chat->capability are forbidden). Setup util layers/chat-claude-code/app/utils/chat-claude-code-setup.ts exports chatClaudeCodePathToSave, chatClaudeCodeExecutableSummary, chatClaudeCodeSetupReady, CHAT_CLAUDE_CODE_AUTH_MODE_OPTIONS; test under layers/chat-claude-code/test/unit. Follow-up: CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT.layers (packages/shared/src/product.ts) must gain chat-claude-code and chat-codex once 3.6 lands (assign to 3.10). Gates at hand-back: lint clean, layer tests pass; typecheck/test/build red only from in-flight 1.12 - re-verify after 1.12.

Every scoped page lives at /p/<slug>/... because the web app's pages directory is literally named p and core's route helpers in apps/web/app/utils/project-scope.ts hard-code the segment; the boundary lint's page rule also assumes the p/[project] directory. packages/shared now exports a product configuration carrying the scope URL prefix (p for Candy Mountain). Make the prefix come from the configuration: links built by core, the route param resolution, the last-opened cookie redirect and the switch-project path logic all use the configured prefix, and a product configured with another prefix serves its pages there. Layers keep writing their pages under the existing directory shape so no layer changes; rewriting the generated routes is the implementer's choice. The boundary lint keeps enforcing that a layer's pages sit under its own id below the scoped directory. Non-goals: the scope label in copy; renaming anything project-named in code.
acceptance_criteria: With the prefix changed in configuration, every scoped page and every link core builds use the new prefix and the old one answers not found (covered by a unit test of the route helpers and a page test); the default configuration keeps /p/ exactly as today; layer directories are unchanged; lint, typecheck, test and build green.
notes: Mechanism: apps/web/scope-routes.mjs exports SCOPE_PAGES_DIR='p' and scopeRoutes(pages, prefix); nuxt.config.ts pages:extend hook rewrites top-level '/p' and '/p/...' routes to '/<PRODUCT.scope.urlPrefix>...' (no-op for p, throws on a bad prefix); route names stay p-project-*. Pages stay on disk under app/pages/p/ in core and every layer. PROJECT_ROUTE_PREFIX in app/utils/project-scope.ts derives from PRODUCT; projectPath/projectSwitchPath are the only way to build scoped links. Lint uses SCOPE_PAGES_DIR for the on-disk check and says '/<scope prefix>/' in messages (plugin cannot load TS product config). Test test/unit/scope-routes.test.ts loads the real page tree with loadNuxt. Verified by a real build with prefix w. GAP (filed as ncj.1.17): daemon and shared link builders still hard-code /p/ (shared registry.ts projectViewRoute, threads.ts chatThreadLink, uptime.ts uptimeMonitorLink; daemon slack/handoffs.ts, notifications/dispatcher.ts).
close_reason: Done by subagents; full workspace lint, typecheck, test (1484 passed), build green.

packages/shared now exports a product configuration (name, theme colour as a Nuxt UI colour name plus a hex, scope label and URL prefix, included ids). The web shell still hard-codes the product: the header imports a name constant, apps/web/app/app.config.ts sets the primary colour to pink, apps/web/nuxt.config.ts writes the theme-color hex, and apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest carries the name, short name, description and colours by hand. Make the shell read all of these from the product configuration so that changing the configuration changes the header, the page titles, the primary colour, the theme-color meta and the PWA manifest (generate or serve the manifest from the configuration rather than keeping a hand-written copy; icons may stay static files for now). The daemon's info route also carries the name; the shell may read it for display but the build-time values come from the shared configuration. Nothing in apps/web may import a product name constant afterwards. Non-goals: the scope label and URL prefix (separate beads); layers.
acceptance_criteria: Changing the name and colours in the shared configuration and rebuilding changes the header, document titles, primary colour, theme-color meta and the served web manifest (a unit test covers the manifest content); no file under apps/web imports a product name constant; the service worker keeps working; lint, typecheck, test and build green.
notes: Single web seam: apps/web/shared/utils/product.ts exports PRODUCT: Readonly<ProductConfig> (= CANDY_MOUNTAIN_PRODUCT); Nuxt 4 shared/ dir so it is auto-imported in app code, templates and Nitro; nuxt.config.ts, app.config.ts and vitest tests import it by relative path. Lint treats the file as core, any layer may use it. Manifest: static public/manifest.webmanifest deleted; Nitro route server/routes/manifest.webmanifest.ts returns webManifest(PRODUCT) (server/utils/web-manifest.ts, test test/unit/web-manifest.test.ts); short_name = name, background_color #0f172a is a shell constant. Added required ProductConfig.description ('Codebase management platform') in packages/shared/src/product.ts. apps/web no longer imports PRODUCT_NAME (daemon + CLI still do; 1.14 and a CLI follow-up remove it). For 3.2/3.3: use PRODUCT.scope.label.* and PRODUCT.scope.urlPrefix via the same auto-import; app/utils/project-scope.ts still hard-codes PROJECT_ROUTE_PREFIX='/p' (3.3); projects.vue delete copy still says project (3.2). Title template added on orchestrator ruling (acceptance names document titles). Title template lives in apps/web/app/app.vue via useHead (titleTemplate fn); nuxt.config app.head is JSON-serialised by Nuxt so functions there are dropped silently - any head function must go in app.vue or a plugin.

packages/shared now exports a product configuration whose scope label says what the product calls a workspace (Candy Mountain says project) with the casings and plural the UI needs. The platform pages in apps/web/app still write the word project into their copy: the picker (add, select, search, manage), the projects page and its forms and confirm modal, the modules and plugins setup pages and their scope descriptions, the gate's needs-setup, not-enabled and not-available states, the grants page, the activity page, the navigation's system group and the organisation grouping copy. Make every such string read the label from the configuration through one shell-side helper that handles casing and plural, so the configuration alone changes the copy. Capability layers (issues, bots, team, uptime, deployments, overview, chat) are product and may keep saying project; leave them alone. notes: SCOPE (auto-imported from apps/web/app/utils/scope-label.ts; pure utils import './scope-label') is the only way core writes the scope word: singular, plural, singularTitle, pluralTitle, aSingular (a/an by spelling - add an article field to ScopeLabel if a product needs otherwise), count(n); scopeWords(label) is the pure builder. packages/shared fixes capability ids, module ids, plugin type ids, agent session families and activity event types as closed string unions with matching guard functions, and both apps import them. A closed union means adding a capability to a product edits the shared base, which defeats a reusable platform. Types stay strict where they can: a capability manifest remains generic over its own view, tool and rung ids, and wire types keep an id field typed as string. The decision is that chat-claude-code owns the ACP session service and offers it through its definition; chat-codex and bots declare a dependency on chat-claude-code and reach the service only that way (their conversions are separate beads). Move the ACP harness, the session manager, the decision service, the session and decision routes, the claude-code plugin type and its login attempt lifecycle into the chat-claude-code definition, and register the claude-code chat family through the definition so the platform thread service runs Claude Code threads without naming the family. The thread service stays platform and must work for any registered family. The agent MCP host stays platform; the session manager keeps receiving its MCP servers from it. Keep every posture and never-bypass guarantee exactly as it is. Non-goals: converting chat-codex or bots; moving files between packages.
