title: Boot the daemon from the capability definition list, with uptime as the first converted capability
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace: apps/daemon (Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle; src/platform.ts starts every background service and src/app.ts mounts every route by hand), apps/web (Nuxt 4 app; each capability's UI is a Nuxt layer under apps/web/layers/<capability-id>, apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the boundaries), packages/shared (wire types both apps import), packages/config, packages/claude-acp and apps/cli. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under the plan in .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (today called projects) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads with native agent families, Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections, routing, decisions and handoffs, uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record any decision a later bead must know in it.

The daemon now has a runtime capability definition contract (manifest plus workspace and platform routes, services with start and close, plugin types, MCP servers, chat families, workspace deletion hooks, offered services and dependencies; read the define helper and its tests in apps/daemon/src/capabilities), but platform start (apps/daemon/src/platform.ts) and the app factory (apps/daemon/src/app.ts) still wire every capability by hand. Make the daemon walk a list of definitions instead: platform start validates the list, starts services in dependency order and closes them in reverse, and registers plugin types, MCP servers (into the platform agent MCP host) and chat families (into the platform thread service, replacing the nativeFamilies map) from it; the app factory mounts each definition's routes. Workspace deletion runs each definition's deletion hooks in reverse dependency order before the platform deletes the workspace row (today the project delete route calls bot and plugin instance cleanup directly; plugin instance cleanup is platform and stays). The boot log names the capabilities, modules and plugin types registered.

Convert uptime as the proof: its monitor routes, monitor source routes, scheduler and incident tracker become its definition, and nothing in platform start or the app factory names uptime any more. Removing uptime from the list must leave the daemon booting with its routes answering not found and everything else unchanged. Every other capability keeps its hand-wiring in this bead: the list and the hand-wiring coexist until each capability's own conversion bead removes its hand-wiring. The platform agent keeps working through the family registration (its definition is written in a separate bead; a temporary platform-side registration is acceptable here). Non-goals: converting any other capability; product configuration.
acceptance_criteria: A daemon test starts a platform with the uptime definition and serves uptime routes with its services running, then starts without it and gets not found on those routes with every other route unchanged. A test shows a list missing a declared dependency refuses boot naming both sides. Deleting a project runs definition deletion hooks in reverse dependency order (tested). Existing daemon tests pass. The boot log lists capabilities, modules and plugin types. Lint, typecheck, test and build green.
notes: Boot walk startCapabilities(context) in apps/daemon/src/capabilities/start.ts returns StartedCapabilities { started, workspaceRoutes, platformRoutes, mcpServers, chatFamilies, notificationChannels, services(id), onWorkspaceDeleted(workspace) (dependents first), close() (reverse) }. Definition list lives in apps/daemon/src/definitions.ts (capabilityDefinitions(options), CAPABILITY_DEFINITIONS) - outside capabilities/ to avoid an ESM cycle; CAPABILITIES (manifests only, capabilities/manifests/index.ts) stays for registry-only consumers and must be kept in sync by hand until 1.14 replaces both with the product object. platform.ts: PlatformOptions.capabilities: CapabilityRegistryEntry[]; definitions start after hand-wired Slack connections and before the MCP host; MCP host gets [slackMcpServer, ...runtime.mcpServers]; dispatcher gets channels: runtime.notificationChannels (tried in order before built-in Slack path); Platform.runtime replaces uptimeScheduler/uptimeIncidents; close() = notifications, then void runtime.close() (sync hazard: make platform close async when an async DB-touching close is converted), then the rest. app.ts: AppDeps.runtime (workspaceRoutes mounted under PROJECTS_PATH after hand-wired, platformRoutes at their path, chatFamilies merged with AppDeps.nativeFamilies - a family in both throws; nativeFamilies goes in 1.11); projectRoutes(secretsReader, { onWorkspaceDeleted }) runs hooks before bot/plugin cleanup, a throw keeps the project. CONVERSION RECIPE (1.3-1.11): (1) move capabilities/manifests/<id>.ts to src/<cap>/manifest.ts, re-point import in manifests/index.ts, keep in CAPABILITIES; (2) add src/<cap>/definition.ts exporting <id>Definition(options) = defineCapabilityDefinition({ id, manifest, dependsOn?, pluginTypes?, provides?, start(context) }) - start sync, services from context.db/paths/secrets/capabilities/modules/pluginTypes/agentMcp.serversFor, other caps via context.service(KEY) (direct deps only), return { services: [bindService(KEY, v)] (exactly provides), workspaceRoutes, platformRoutes: [{path, routes}], mcpServers, chatFamilies, notificationChannels, onWorkspaceDeleted, close }; options via factory arg; optionally export <id>Routes() for route-only tests; (3) export from src/<cap>/index.ts; swap the bare manifest for <id>Definition(options.<id>) in capabilityDefinitions() and add to CapabilityDefinitionOptions; (4) delete hand-wiring in platform.ts/app.ts; platform consumers read platform.runtime.services('<id>').get(PLATFORM_KEY); workspace cleanup moves into onWorkspaceDeleted; (5) tests pass runtime: <id>Routes() to createApp or startPlatform(temp.root, { capabilities: [...] }) + createApp({ runtime: platform.runtime }). Example: apps/daemon/src/uptime/definition.ts + manifest.ts; tests start.test.ts, boot.test.ts.

title: Define the runtime capability definition contract with boot-time validation
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is a pnpm workspace: apps/daemon (Hono daemon over SQLite via Drizzle; src/platform.ts starts every background service and src/app.ts mounts every route by hand), apps/web (Nuxt 4 app; each capability's UI is a Nuxt layer under apps/web/layers/<capability-id>, apps/web/layers/README.md is the conventions document and the local ESLint plugin cm-layers in apps/web/eslint/layer-boundaries.mjs enforces the boundaries), packages/shared (wire types both apps import), packages/config, packages/claude-acp and apps/cli. The repo is being split in place into a reusable platform base and a Candy Mountain product under the plan in .ai-docs/plans/platform-extraction/ (overview.md holds the platform/product line and the decisions table). Platform means what every product needs: the data directory, database and migrations, secrets, auth, workspaces (today called projects) and organisations, the capability, module and plugin type registries, module enablement, grants, registry computation, platform settings, the activity feed, the notification dispatcher, chat threads with native agent families, Mastra and the platform agent, the agent MCP host, the overview capability, the web shell and the CLI. Product means Candy Mountain's own: issues and assignees, ACP sessions with the claude-code and codex plugin types, worktrees, bots and bot sessions, team, Slack connections, routing, decisions and handoffs, uptime, environments and deployments with the netlify and heroku plugin types, and the repository plugin type. Capability ids: overview, issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent. Module ids: issues, agent-hub, operations. Plugin type ids: repository, claude-code, codex, netlify, heroku, slack. Working pieces move as they are: no redesign and no behaviour change beyond what this bead asks. pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test and pnpm build must be green when the bead is done. Do not commit. Finish with a fenced handoff block (outcome, summary, pull_request, issues, follow_ups) and record any decision a later bead must know in it.

Today a capability's manifest (apps/daemon/src/capabilities/manifests) declares only views, tools, agents, jobs and requirements; the daemon's platform start and app factory then hand-wire that capability's routes and background services by importing them by name, so removing a capability means editing the platform. Give each capability a single runtime definition that carries its manifest plus everything the daemon needs to run it: routes mounted under a workspace (today the /projects/:slug prefix) and at the platform level, long-running services with a start and a close so shutdown order stays correct, the plugin types it brings, MCP servers it offers to agent sessions, the chat families it runs (a runner the platform thread service calls for that family), hooks to run when a workspace is deleted, and declared dependencies on other capabilities.

A definition must be able to offer named services to other definitions, reachable only through the dependency declaration, and to platform services that need them without the platform importing the capability. Three platform consumers exist today and must be served by the contract: the agent MCP host collects MCP servers (today it is handed the Slack MCP server directly), the notification dispatcher delivers through Slack (today it imports the Slack plugin and reads bot tokens itself) and so needs a delivery channel a capability can offer, and the thread service runs native families (today through a nativeFamilies map). A definition must also be allowed to be service-only, with no views and no ladder and therefore absent from the capability catalog and the grants pages, because Slack connections become such a definition in a later bead. Platform-owned capabilities (overview, platform-agent) use the same contract as product ones.

Validation runs before anything touches disk, as manifests are validated today: a bad definition stops boot with a message naming the capability; a list containing a dependency on a capability not in the list, a dependency cycle, or a duplicate id is refused with a message naming both sides; a manifest referencing a plugin type that neither the list nor the product supplies is refused naming the capability and the plugin type. The capability registry accepts definitions and keeps answering manifest questions as it does today, so nothing downstream of the registry changes.

This bead is the contract, its define helper, its validation and their unit tests. It does not change how the daemon boots (a separate bead walks the list) and moves no capability's code. Non-goals: schema and migration ownership, workspace fact and activity event declarations (a later phase), product configuration.
acceptance_criteria: A definition for any existing capability can be written with the define helper and shared types alone. Unit tests cover each refusal above with a message naming the capability, and both sides for dependency and plugin type errors. Existing manifest and registry tests pass unchanged. Daemon behaviour is unchanged.
notes: Contract in apps/daemon/src/capabilities/definition.ts. CapabilityDefinition { id; manifest?; dependsOn?: string[]; pluginTypes?: AnyPluginType[]; provides?: ServiceKey[]; start?(context: CapabilityContext): CapabilityRuntime } via defineCapabilityDefinition(def); errors CapabilityDefinitionError. CapabilityRuntime { services?: ServiceBinding[]; workspaceRoutes?: Hono<AppEnv>[] (mounted under workspace prefix, handlers keep /:slug/...); platformRoutes?: {path, routes}[]; mcpServers?: AgentMcpServerDefinition[]; chatFamilies?: Partial<Record<family, NativeFamilyRunner>>; notificationChannels?: NotificationChannel[]; onWorkspaceDeleted?(workspace); close?() } - start sync, close may be async. CapabilityContext { db, paths, secrets, registries, agentMcp.serversFor, service(KEY) } where service resolves only keys bound by a DIRECT declared dependency. Named services: KEY = serviceKey<T>('name'); provider lists provides:[KEY] and returns services:[bindService(KEY, value)]; boundServices(def, runtime) checks both directions; platform reads offered services from the per-capability BoundServices map using platform-owned keys. Service-only = omit manifest; excluded from registry.list()/byId()/has() (catalog, modules, grants) but in registry.definitions(). createCapabilityRegistry accepts a mixed list of manifests and definitions + { pluginTypeIds } for types supplied outside the list; assertCapabilityDefinitions + orderCapabilityDefinitions (deps first, list order otherwise) in registry.ts. Fixtures: fixtureDefinition(id, overrides) (manifest:null = service-only), fixtureCapabilityContext(db, overrides) in capabilities/fixtures.ts. Per-capability options: export a factory like uptimeDefinition(options); the contract has no options field on purpose. Follow-ups for 1.2/1.4/1.6/1.11 are in the bead's handoff (see bd remember platform-extraction-decisions-a).

title: Let Codex bot sessions write to the main checkout's beads directory
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon. Bead 6.4 routes bd in a worktree to the main checkout via BEADS_DIR, and 6.13 adds beadsDir to the Claude write-auto sandbox allow list, but Codex sessions run under the adapter's workspace-write sandbox which only allows writes inside the worktree. CodexLaunchOptions (apps/daemon/src/acp/families.ts) has no writable-roots field and the posture verifier (src/posture/verify.ts) refuses unknown codex keys, so a bd write under workspace-write currently surfaces as an escalation decision. Add a codex.writableRoots option emitted as CODEX_CONFIG sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots, allow it in the posture mapping (6.7) and verifier for write scopes only (never for read-only), and have 6.13 pass beadsDir for Codex bots.
acceptance_criteria: A Codex bot session in write-confirm or write-auto scope has the main checkout's .beads directory as a writable root in CODEX_CONFIG; read-only scope never gets writable roots; posture tests and bot-session tests cover both; auto-review modes stay refused.
notes:
Codex writable roots for bot sessions.
API: CodexLaunchOptions.writableRoots?: string[] (acp/families.ts). Absolute paths only, deduped; non-empty in a mode other than workspace-write (incl. the read-only default) -> AcpLaunchError; assertCodexLaunchOptions runs the same check. Emitted as CODEX_CONFIG sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots AND as FamilyLaunch.additionalDirectories, which acp/session.ts sends as ACP additionalDirectories on session/new and session/load.
WHY BOTH: codex-acp 2.3.0 sends the mode's sandboxPolicy (workspaceWrite, writableRoots: []) with every turn/start, and app-server documents turn sandboxPolicy as 'Override the sandbox policy for this turn and subsequent turns', so CODEX_CONFIG writable_roots alone would be replaced on the first turn. The adapter adds session additionalDirectories back into every turn's policy (addAdditionalDirectoriesToSandboxPolicy) and into config writable_roots (mergeSandboxWorkspaceWriteRoots). Side effect: the adapter marks that dir as a trusted project and scans it for skills.
POSTURE: resolveBotPosture({ beadsDir? }) (absolute or invalid_input); codexPosture adds writableRoots: [beadsDir] for write-confirm/write-auto only. Verifier: writableRoots allowed only when mode is workspace-write (write scopes), non-empty array of absolute, normalised paths whose basename is .beads; anything else 'widened'. Unknown keys still refused; model/reasoningEffort still refused for bots.
BOT SESSIONS: service.ts passes beadsDir: beads?.beadsDir. Shared AgentSessionPosture.codex gained writableRoots? (REST parsePosture never copies it). Posture is stored on the session row so resumes keep it.

title: Gate session SSE and prompt routes by project access and chat rung
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon. Bead 4.6 exposed /projects/:slug/sessions/:id/{events,prompt,cancel,decisions} to any signed-in actor who knows a session id; bead 4.9 noted that only the /threads routes are gated by the chat rung. Add gating: a session may be read or driven only by its owning actor (actor_id) or an admin, and the chat rung of the session's family capability must allow chat (use requireCapability / gateChat from src/registry). Decision routes from 4.7 get the same rule. Keep bot sessions (6.13) in mind: they have no human owner, so allow admins. Tests cover a foreign actor getting 404, a below-rung actor getting 403, and the owner succeeding.
acceptance_criteria: A different non-admin actor cannot list, stream, prompt, cancel or answer decisions on someone else's session; an actor whose chat rung is none is refused; the owner and the admin succeed; existing session tests still pass.
notes:
Session access gating (6.13 bot sessions, 4.11 decision cards, 7.4 Slack rely on this).

HELPER: apps/daemon/src/sessions/access.ts (exported from '../sessions'):
- familyCapability(capabilities, family) -> CapabilityId|undefined: the capability whose manifest has an agent with that family (chat-claude-code / chat-codex).
- gateSessionFamily(deps, actor, project, family) -> GateResult: gateChat on that capability; capability_unknown 404 when no capability runs the family.
- canAccessSession(actor, session): session.actorId === actor.id || isAdmin(actor). Admins see every session so bot sessions (synthetic actor) stay reachable.
- requireSessionAccess(sessions) -> Hono middleware for routes with :slug and :id: unknown slug -> ProjectError 404; missing session, other project, or not canAccessSession -> SessionError not_found 404 (existence never revealed); then gateSessionFamily refusal -> ApiErrorBody with the gate's code/status (not_enabled 404, not_granted 403, not_ready 409). Admin still goes through the gate (top rung, but enablement and readiness apply).

ROUTES (shapes unchanged): sessionRoutes GET :id, POST :id/prompt, POST :id/cancel, GET :id/events, and decisionRoutes GET :id/decisions, POST :id/decisions/:decisionId all mount requireSessionAccess per route (not via a wildcard, so the two sub-apps never double-run it). POST /:slug/sessions gates the body family after validation (bad family/posture still 400 first; a family that is not ready -> 409 not_ready before the never-bypass posture check in manager.create). GET /:slug/sessions returns only the actor's own sessions (admin: all) of families the actor may chat with; refused with the first family refusal only when no family is allowed (same rule as GET /threads).

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE: session/decision routes now need the agent-hub module enabled and the family plugin ready (stored health), like the /threads routes. The manager's family_unavailable 422 is now only reachable via direct manager use (REST hits not_ready first).

TESTS: src/sessions/sessions.test.ts 'session access' (foreign non-admin 404 on all six per-session routes + empty list; chat rung none -> 403 not_granted on all routes incl. list/create, even own session; owner and admin prompt/get/decisions/cancel/stream succeed, admin reaches a 'bot:reviewer' session). Fixtures in sessions and decisions tests now enable agent-hub and mark plugin health healthy; the family_unavailable test asserts the manager directly plus REST not_ready. No migration.

VERIFIED: vitest sessions+decisions+threads 39/39; root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (98 files, 930 pass, 3 skipped), build all pass.

FOLLOW-UP: apps/daemon/README.md '## Durable agent sessions' does not yet mention the access rule (left untouched to stay in scope).
close_reason: requireSessionAccess: owner-or-admin + chat gate on session and decision routes; gates green

title: Clean up agent homes on instance delete and refresh health after login or revoke
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon plugin instances (bead 2.5) and the claude-code (4.4) and codex (4.5) plugin types, which own per-instance config homes under <dataDir>/agent-homes/<type>/<instanceId>. Two gaps: (1) deleting a plugin instance or its project leaves the home on disk with credentials; add an optional per-type onDelete hook to the plugin type definition and call it from deletePluginInstance and deleteProjectPluginInstances, with both types removing their home. (2) Instance actions (start-login success, submit-code, revoke) cannot update the stored health, so readiness (2.6) is stale until POST /test; add a health-refresh or health-reset capability to PluginActionContext (e.g. ctx.refreshHealth() runs the type's health check and stores it) and call it at the end of those actions in both types. Keep the action extension point otherwise unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Deleting a claude-code or codex instance (or its project) removes the home directory; after a successful login action the stored health is healthy without calling /test; after revoke it is unhealthy; tests cover both types.
notes:
Agent home cleanup + health refresh decisions (4.8 panel and any future type with on-disk state depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md (Claude Code, Codex, Plugin instances, Instance actions).

ONDELETE HOOK (src/plugins/definition.ts): PluginType gains optional onDelete?(ctx: PluginDeleteContext<S>): void | Promise<void>, PluginDeleteContext { instance: PluginInstance (wire shape), paths: DataPaths, secrets: PluginSecrets<S> (read-only, this instance) }. assertPluginType rejects a non-function ('onDelete must be a function.'). Runs BEFORE the row and secrets are deleted; a throw propagates and the instance stays (retryable; better than credentials orphaned on disk with no row). Unregistered type -> no hook.
SERVICE (src/plugins/instances/instances.ts): deletePluginInstance and deleteProjectPluginInstances are now ASYNC and take PluginInstanceDeleteDeps = PluginInstanceDeps & { secretsReader, paths } (c.var + secretsReader satisfies it; Platform too). deleteProjectPluginInstances runs every instance's hook, then deletes rows, then secrets; returns the count. projectRoutes now takes secretsReader (app.ts passes deps.secretsReader ?? locked) and DELETE /projects/:slug awaits it. instanceHarness deps gained paths (dataPaths(root)).
claude-code onDelete: claudeLoginAttempts.cancel(id) (kills the open login process) then removeConfigDir. codex onDelete: attempts.cancel(id) then removeCodexHome.

REFRESH/RESET (src/plugins/actions.ts PluginActionContext): refreshHealth(): Promise<PluginInstanceHealth | null> = refreshPluginInstanceHealth(deps, id): runs testPluginInstance (re-reads the instance, same config/secrets/instance/paths, same updatedAt guard and storage); returns the stored health, or null when the instance changed (instance_changed) or was deleted (not_found) mid-check, nothing stored; other errors throw. It closes over deps, not the request, so it is safe to call after the request ends. resetHealth(): void = resetPluginInstanceHealth(deps, id): sets health/healthCheckedAt null without bumping updatedAt. Both service functions are exported from src/plugins/instances.
CALL SITES: claude-code submit-code awaits refreshHealth() on the 'accepted' outcome (logged_in AND failed; not on 400/404/409 errors); claude-code revoke awaits it in BOTH modes (login mode would otherwise keep a stale healthy; both checks are CLI-free after revoke: missing dir / missing token). codex: CodexLoginTarget gains onLoggedIn?: () => Promise<unknown>; start-login passes ctx.refreshHealth; the registry awaits it (errors swallowed) after codex login status confirms and BEFORE marking the attempt 'succeeded', so a client that sees succeeded reads fresh health. Not called on failed/expired/close. codex revoke awaits refreshHealth() after removing the home.

4.8 PANEL NO LONGER NEEDS: POST /plugins/:id/test after claude submit-code, after either revoke, or after codex login-status reports 'succeeded'. Just re-read GET /plugins/:id (or the action response + GET) for instance.health. Revoke now leaves health unhealthy (not null). /test is still for the token path (PATCH config/secrets resets health to null) and manual re-checks.

TESTS: instances.test.ts (hook order/args for both deletes, throwing hook keeps instance, refresh/reset/null after delete), definition.test.ts (non-function onDelete), claude-code.test.ts (stored health after submit-code success/failure without /test, unhealthy after login-mode and token-mode revoke, DELETE /plugins/:id kills attempt + removes dir, project delete removes only that project's dir), codex.test.ts (stored healthy after succeeded without /test, unhealthy after revoke, DELETE removes home + kills attempt, project delete removes only its home).
VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (79 files, 727 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass. No schema/migration.
OPEN: narrow race: a codex login completing while a revoke runs could store healthy after revoke's unhealthy (no updatedAt bump on either); resetHealth has no caller yet.
close_reason: onDelete hook + refreshHealth/resetHealth; homes removed on delete, health fresh after login/revoke; gates green

title: Apply the platform agent's navigate and start-chat actions in the browser
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The platform agent's tools return actions rather than performing them. In the chat layer, recognise action events in a platform-agent thread: a navigate action routes to the named view for the named project (through the registry's view paths) and a start-chat action creates a thread with the named agent and opens it in the panel. Show each applied action as a small card in the transcript. Ignore actions from any other agent.
acceptance_criteria: Asking the agent to open uptime for a project navigates there; asking it to start a chat with Claude Code opens a new thread with that agent; an action in a non-platform thread is ignored.
notes:
Platform agent browser actions (all in apps/web/layers/chat).

SEGMENTER (utils/chatTranscript.ts): new item kind 'action' ChatActionItem { key, seq, at, session (divider key of its part: 'current' = CHAT_TRANSCRIPT_CURRENT for the live session, a session id for history, '' with no dividers), toolCallId, action: PlatformClientAction } pushed for each client_action row whose action passes chatIsClientAction (unknown kinds dropped). It breaks text joining like any other item. Transcript's current part id now uses the exported CHAT_TRANSCRIPT_CURRENT.

PURE LOGIC (utils/chatClientActions.ts, tests test/unit/clientActions.test.ts, 10): ChatActionState applying|applied|failed|earlier|ignored; ChatActionLedger { since, outcomes: toolCallId -> {state} } per session; chatActionsApply(agentId) = agentId === PLATFORM_AGENT_ID; chatActionsToApply(rows, ledger, agentId) = client_action rows with at > ledger.since and toolCallId not in outcomes, deduped; chatActionState; chatNavigatePath(action, registry) = registry view 'to' when registry.project.slug === action.projectSlug and the view exists, else action.to; chatActionLabel -> 'Opened Issues for Alpha', 'Started a chat with Claude Code', ignored 'Did not open ...', failed 'Could not ...' (names from registry views/project/agents, ids as fallback).

APPLY ONCE: useChatClientActions(threadAgentId, session, sessionRows) (deviation: takes the session {id,lastActivityAt} too). Ledgers in useState('chat-client-actions') keyed by session id, so a remounted panel / replayed SSE never repeats. useState does not survive a reload, so the ledger's 'since' = the session's lastActivityAt when this tab first saw it (daemon clock vs daemon clock; appendSessionEvent bumps lastActivityAt on every row): after a reload or a deep link in a fresh tab every replayed row is <= since and shows as 'earlier', never applied. For a thread created in the panel, AgentPanel.send calls actions.follow(created.session) right after create so the ledger starts before the first prompt (otherwise the thread GET can land after a fast action row and swallow it). navigate -> navigateTo(chatThreadLink(threadId, path)) when same project (keeps the platform thread open), else navigateTo(path). open_thread -> threadId ? showThread(agentId, threadId) : useChatThreads(slug).create({ agentId }) then showThread(agentId, id). Failure -> outcome failed + error toast. Non-platform threads (threadAgentId from current.thread.agentId) never apply; their cards say ignored. stateOf(item): ignored unless platform; history parts -> earlier; current -> ledger state or earlier.

UI: ChatActionCard (components/ActionCard.vue) small bordered row: compass / message-square-plus icon, label, badge Applied (success) / Failed (error) / Ignored (neutral, tooltip 'Only the platform agent can steer the app.'), spinner while applying, none for earlier. Test ids chat-action (data-state, data-action-kind, data-tool-call-id), chat-action-label, chat-action-state; row data-kind='action'. ChatTranscript prop actionState?: (item) => ChatActionState (default ignored). AgentPanel: 3 lines (composable call, :action-state, follow after create).

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: unit tests (chat layer 33). Live: daemon from source on 127.0.0.1:10200 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR/CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth), stub gateway (test-support startStubGateway(scriptedReply)) on :10202, PUT /settings/platform base URL/model/fake key, project alpha (issues + agent-hub, real bd init in a scratch git repo, claude-code instance set healthy in sqlite), built web on :10201. Headless Chromium 17/17: 'open issues' in a new platform thread navigates /p/alpha/setup/plugins -> /p/alpha/issues?thread=<platform> with card 'Opened Issues for Alpha' Applied; deep link back on setup/plugins does not navigate again (card earlier); 'chat with claude-code' creates one claude-code thread and the panel shows it (page stays); back to the platform thread in the same tab: cards earlier+applied, no extra thread; reload re-applies neither; a client_action row inserted via sqlite into the claude-code session (newer than its lastActivityAt, so it would apply in a platform thread) shows 'Did not open Issues for Alpha' Ignored and does not navigate; 390px no overflow; no console errors. No uptime view exists yet (no uptime manifest/layer), so 'open issues' stood in for 'open uptime'. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (132 files, 1257 passed, 3 skipped), build pass.

OPEN: two tabs on the same platform thread would both apply a live action (ledgers are per tab). A failed action is not retried. The card does not link to the opened thread/view.
close_reason: Platform agent navigate/start-chat actions applied once per tool call in platform threads only; reload-safe; gates green

title: Add LLM gateway key and platform agent model settings
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The platform agent needs an LLM, and Jack will supply it later. Add two platform settings: an LLM gateway key (a secret in the secrets store, shown only as set) with the gateway base URL, and the platform agent's model id. Store them in a platform settings table, expose them over REST (admin only), and extend the Settings page with a form for them. The daemon must boot and behave normally with both unset.
acceptance_criteria: Saving a key shows it as set and never returns it; the model id persists; the daemon boots with nothing set.
notes:
Platform LLM settings (no new table/migration; uses platform_meta).
ROUTE: GET/PUT /settings/platform (PLATFORM_SETTINGS_PATH in @candy-mountain/shared platform-settings.ts), admin only (requireAdmin). Mounted in app.ts only when AppDeps.secrets (SecretsWriter) is passed; index.ts passes platform.secrets.writeOnly.
RESPONSE PlatformSettings: {gatewayBaseUrl: string|null, modelId: string|null, gatewayKeySet: boolean, secretsUnlocked: boolean}. Key never returned.
PUT UpdatePlatformSettingsRequest: {gatewayBaseUrl?, modelId?, gatewayKey?}; omitted=unchanged, null or blank=clear. gatewayBaseUrl must be http(s) URL. Errors: 400 invalid_request, 403 forbidden, 409 secrets_locked (setting a key with no CM_SECRETS_KEY).
KEYS in platform_meta: llm.gatewayBaseUrl, platformAgent.modelId. SECRET: owner platform:llm-gateway name api-key.
PHASE 10 ACCESSOR: resolveLlmGatewayConfig(db, platform.secrets) from apps/daemon/src/settings -> {baseUrl, modelId, apiKey|undefined}; needs the full SecretsStore (throws SecretsLockedError if locked and a key file exists? no: get throws when no master key). Hide the agent when modelId is null.
CODE: apps/daemon/src/settings/{platform-settings,routes,index}.ts + platform-settings.test.ts; web: Platform agent card in apps/web/app/pages/settings.vue (replaced 'More settings'); README section Platform settings.
Verified: daemon tests, live curl PUT/GET via daemon and web proxy, SSR /settings, persistence across restart, boot with no key/unset.
close_reason: Platform settings via platform_meta + secrets store, Settings form; verified live

title: Add the native platform chat agent on Mastra with rung-gated tools
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

This is the first native agent and proves the Mastra path end to end. Register the `platform-agent` capability (standalone, granted to every role, ladder none then chat) and a Mastra agent whose instructions are built per request from the actor's registry for the selected project (what modules, views and agents exist and what the actor may do) and whose model comes from the platform settings through the configured gateway. Memory threads live in the platform database keyed by actor. When no gateway key or model is configured the agent is omitted from the registry's chat agents so the rail hides it. Tools: open a view, start a chat with another agent, and describe what the platform can do; each tool is gated by the actor's rung for the target capability and returns a refusal as a value (which the agent relays) rather than throwing. The first two tools return actions for the browser to apply (navigate, open a thread) rather than performing them. Non-goals: any other tool.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Without a key the rail shows no platform agent; with a key and model it appears for the admin; asking it to describe the platform answers from the registry; the open-view and start-chat tools return typed actions; a view the actor cannot see yields a refusal the agent relays; tests mock the model.
notes:
Platform agent decisions (10.8 browser actions, future native agents build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Platform agent' and the in-process paragraph at the end of '## Chat threads'.

MANIFEST src/capabilities/manifests/platform-agent.ts (appended to CAPABILITIES): id platform-agent, standalone (in no module, so a candidate for every project), no views/jobs, requiresPlugins [], requiresPlatformFacts ['llmGateway'], tools open_view / start_chat / describe_platform (kind 'tool', unscoped), ladder none -> chat (chat: true, all three tools), everyoneRung 'chat', agent { id 'platform' (PLATFORM_AGENT_ID), label 'Platform', family 'platform', avatar 'i-lucide-mountain' }.

GRANT MECHANISM = manifest flag, not seeded grants: CapabilityManifest.everyoneRung?: rung name (shared capabilities.ts; defineCapability param typed to the ladder's rung names). resolveRoleRungs (src/grants/resolve.ts) raises every capability to its everyoneRung BEFORE applying grants, so every role (existing or future, even with zero grants) holds chat on platform-agent; grants can raise but not lower it; admin still top rung; fail-closed path still resolves none. assertCapability rejects everyoneRung 'none' or a rung not on the ladder. GET /grants roles[].rungs therefore shows platform-agent: chat for every role.

READINESS / HIDING: new platform facts beside project facts: shared PLATFORM_FACT_IDS ['llmGateway'], PlatformFactId, CapabilityManifest.requiresPlatformFacts, ReadinessReason kind 'platform-fact' { fact, message }. src/registry: readiness.ts PlatformFacts (Partial record, missing = false) + capabilityReadiness(cap, plugins, facts, platformFacts = {}); load.ts platformFacts(deps) = gatewayBaseUrl set AND modelId set AND secrets.isSet(platform:llm-gateway/api-key) (only isSet, never decrypts, so it works with secrets locked); RegistryInput.platformFacts? optional; gate.ts passes it too. Effect: with any of the three unset the capability is not ready -> absent from registry.agents (rail hides it), admin sees the reason 'No LLM gateway is configured; set the gateway base URL, key and model id on the Settings page.', thread create/prompt/options refused not_ready 409. Base URL is required as well as key+model because Mastra needs the URL to build the OpenAI-compatible provider.

SESSION FAMILY: shared AGENT_SESSION_FAMILIES gained 'platform' (name 'Platform agent'); no schema change (family column is untyped text). src/sessions/manager.ts seam: NativeTurn { emit(payload), signal }, NativeTurnRunner, SessionManager.run(id, text, runner): session_busy unless idle/live, appends prompt row, status prompting, runs the runner in the background, then turn_end { stopReason 'end_turn' | 'cancelled' (signal aborted) | 'error' (runner threw; an error row phase 'prompt' precedes it) } and status idle; returns at once with status prompting (HTTP 202 like prompt). cancel(id) aborts a native turn's signal and awaits it; close() aborts all native turns first. launchFor refuses family 'platform' with family_unavailable 422 ('run in-process; prompt them through their chat thread') so the plain /sessions prompt route cannot drive it.

THREAD SEAM: src/threads/service.ts NativeFamilyTurn (NativeTurn + project, actor, thread, session, text), NativeFamilyRunner, NativeFamilyRunners = Partial<Record<AgentSessionFamily, NativeFamilyRunner>>; ThreadServiceOptions.native; ThreadService.prompt(thread, text, actor) (routes pass c.var.actor) picks options.native[session.family] and calls sessions.run, else sessions.prompt as before; threadServiceFor(db, sessions, options?) (first call wins). AppDeps.nativeFamilies?: NativeFamilyRunners (app.ts passes it to threadServiceFor). threads/options.ts catalog(): family 'platform' offers no models/efforts (4.15's catalog otherwise defaults to Claude's). Everything else (working/unread via status subscription, SSE replay, thread title, mark-read, 404 for other actors' threads) is unchanged and verified live.

AGENT MODULE apps/daemon/src/platform-agent/: context.ts PlatformTurnContext { actor, project, capabilities (registry), registry: RegistryResponse, access(capabilityId) -> CapabilityAccess (memoised per turn), model { baseUrl, modelId, apiKey } } carried in Mastra RequestContext under PLATFORM_TURN_KEY ('platformTurn'); turnOf(requestContext) throws outside a turn. agent.ts createPlatformAgent({ storage }) -> one Mastra Agent (id 'platform') whose instructions/model/tools are DynamicArguments resolved per turn from that context; memory = @mastra/memory Memory({ storage, options: { lastMessages: 30, generateTitle: false, semanticRecall: false, workingMemory: { enabled: false } } }). instructions.ts platformInstructions(turn): actor, admin flag, project, enabled modules, views (id/label/route/ready), chat agents (minus itself), capabilities+rungs, and the rules (relay refusals verbatim, browser applies actions, never claim to have navigated, say issue never bead). runner.ts createPlatformAgentRunner(deps: RegistryDeps & { secretsReader: SecretsStore, mastra }, { flushIntervalMs = 150, maxSteps = 6 }) -> NativeFamilyRunner. mastra.ts: createMastra(paths, { agents?: (storage) => Record<id, Agent> }) -> { mastra, storage, close }; index.ts registers { platform: createPlatformAgent({ storage }) } and passes nativeFamilies: { platform: runner } to createApp. Default createMastra(paths) still registers no agents (mastra.test.ts unchanged). Deps added to the daemon: @mastra/memory 1.39.0, zod 4.6.7.

GATEWAY: each turn calls resolveLlmGatewayConfig(db, platform.secrets); if any of baseUrl/modelId/apiKey is missing it writes error { phase 'start' } and ends the turn (normally unreachable because the chat gate already refuses not_ready). Model config = { providerId: 'llm-gateway', modelId, url: baseUrl, apiKey, api: 'chat' }: Mastra's router builds an OpenAI-compatible provider on that base URL, so the gateway must serve POST <baseUrl>/chat/completions (streaming SSE) with Bearer <key>; the model id is sent verbatim. No env var, no network at boot.

TOOL CONTRACTS (shared platform-agent.ts; pure functions openView/startChat/describePlatform in tools.ts, wrapped by createTool with zod input schemas): every tool first checks the actor's own rung on platform-agent (checkTool) then the target. Results are values, never throws: PlatformToolRefusal { refused: true, code: GateRefusalCode | 'not_found' | 'invalid_request', reason } or PlatformToolAction { refused: false, action, summary }. open_view({ viewId }): finds the manifest owning the view (not_found otherwise), checkView on the actor's access to that capability (not_enabled/not_granted/not_ready refusals verbatim, e.g. "Rung 'none' of 'overview' does not show view 'overview'."), action { kind: 'navigate', to: projectViewRoute(slug, path), projectSlug, viewId, capabilityId }. start_chat({ agentId }): invalid_request for 'platform' itself or an agent without a family, not_found for unknown, checkChat on the agent's capability, action { kind: 'open_thread', agentId, threadId?: undefined } (the browser creates the thread). describe_platform(): PlatformDescription { refused: false, project, actor { displayName, admin }, modules, views (id/label/capabilityId/to/ready), agents (minus itself), capabilities (id/label/rung/ready/reasons messages) } straight from the actor's registry.

EVENT ROWS the runner writes (so the 4.11 transcript renders them unchanged): streamed text as 'text' { role: 'agent' } rows sliced at most every 150 ms (consecutive rows join in the transcript); 'tool_call' { toolCall: { toolCallId, title ('Open view' | 'Start chat' | 'Describe platform'), kind: 'other', status: 'in_progress', rawInput } }; 'tool_result' { update: { toolCallId, status: 'completed' | 'failed', rawOutput: the full tool result, content: [{ type: 'content', content: { type: 'text', text: summary | 'Refused: <reason>' } }] } }; NEW KIND 'client_action' { toolCallId, action: PlatformClientAction } emitted right after the tool_result whenever the result carried an action; 'error' { phase: 'prompt' } on a model error; then the manager's 'turn_end'. Unknown kinds fall into the transcript's default branch, so client_action is invisible until 10.8 renders it.

WHAT THE CHAT UI NEEDS (10.8): the platform agent is an ordinary registry agent (family/avatar set), so the rail and ChatAgentPanel already work (verified: registry agents lists it when ready). 10.8 should watch the session events for kind 'client_action' in a thread whose agentId === PLATFORM_AGENT_ID, apply navigate via navigateTo(action.to) (or resolve action.viewId/projectSlug through the registry views) and open_thread via useChatPanel().startThread(action.agentId) (threadId is reserved for a daemon-created thread), apply each only once (dedupe by seq/toolCallId, also on SSE replay: decide whether replayed actions re-apply; suggest only applying rows newer than the last seq seen when the panel opened), and render the row as a small card. PlatformClientAction, PLATFORM_CLIENT_ACTION_KINDS, PLATFORM_AGENT_ID are exported from @candy-mountain/shared.

TESTS src/platform-agent/platform-agent.test.ts (8): startPlatform + createMastra with the agent + createPlatformAgentRunner + createApp({ nativeFamilies }); the model is a stub OpenAI-compatible server (test-support.ts startStubGateway(scriptedReply): picks a tool from 'open <viewId>' / 'chat with <agentId>' / 'describe', answers from the tool result, both streaming and non-streaming) configured through PUT /settings/platform. title: Add per-project notification rules and the dispatcher
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack wants Slack to tell him when things happen. Add notification rules per project: for each of the event types bot finished (`bot.handoff`), incident opened, incident closed, deploy succeeded and deploy failed (both from `deploy.attempted` with its outcome), an on/off flag and a destination (a channel id or a Slack member id for a direct message). Build a dispatcher that observes activity events as they are appended and, for each matching enabled rule, sends a short message with the event title and a link into the app, using the project's first bot with Slack keys when one exists and otherwise the platform-level Slack plugin instance; when neither is available record a delivery failure on the rule and keep going. Never send twice for one event. REST to read and set rules.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.
acceptance_criteria: With "notify when a bot finishes" on, a completed bot turn delivers one Slack message with a link to the thread; an incident opening delivers to the configured channel; with no Slack identity the rule shows a delivery failure; tests cover matching and single delivery.
notes:
Per-project notification rules + dispatcher (10.5 UI and 7.6/8.x/9.x producers depend on these).

FILES: apps/daemon/src/notifications/{config,rules,dispatcher,routes,index}.ts + notifications.test.ts (14 tests); packages/shared/src/notifications.ts (exported from index). Minimal edits: activity/events.ts (subscribeActivityEvents), config.ts (+notifications), platform.ts (platform.notifications, PlatformOptions.notifications, close), app.ts (notificationRoutes on /projects), index.ts, config.test.ts, README.md (## Notifications, CM_WEB_URL row). No migration, no table.

SHARED (@candy-mountain/shared notifications.ts): NOTIFICATION_KINDS ['bot.finished','incident.opened','incident.closed','deploy.succeeded','deploy.failed'], NotificationKind, NOTIFICATION_KIND_LABELS (UI labels), NotificationDestination = {channelId} | {memberId}, NotificationRule { enabled, destination|null, lastFailureAt|null, lastFailureReason|null, lastDeliveredAt|null }, NotificationRules = Record<kind, rule>, NotificationRulesResponse { rules }, UpdateNotificationRulesRequest { rules: Partial<Record<kind, { enabled?, destination? }>> }, NotificationRuleUpdate, NOTIFICATION_ERROR_CODES ['invalid_request'], projectNotificationsPath(slug) = /projects/<slug>/notifications, DEPLOY_OUTCOMES ['succeeded','failed'] + DeployOutcome. Channel/member id validation reuses the existing SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_PATTERN (bots.ts, [CG][A-Z0-9]{2,}) and SLACK_MEMBER_ID_PATTERN (team.ts, [UW][A-Z0-9]{2,}); NOT re-exported from notifications.ts (that made the shared export * index ambiguous and broke both builds).

STORAGE: platform_meta key notifications.<projectId> = JSON NotificationRules (missing/malformed kinds read as defaults); notifications.delivered.<projectId> = JSON array of the last 500 delivered event ids (DELIVERED_RING_SIZE). Blobs are not removed on project delete (small, uuid-keyed).

ROUTES (admin only via route-level requireAdmin, so other /projects routes are unaffected): GET /projects/:slug/notifications -> { rules } (every kind present, defaults off). PUT same path body { rules: { <kind>: { enabled?, destination? } } } -> { rules }: merge semantics, omitted kinds unchanged, a kind that is present gets lastFailureAt/lastFailureReason cleared; destination null allowed only while disabled. Errors 400 invalid_request (bad JSON/shape, unknown kind, enabled w/o destination, both ids, bad id pattern), 403 forbidden, 404 not_found. Mounted unconditionally in app.ts.

DISPATCHER: startNotificationDispatcher(deps { db, pluginTypes, secrets, secretsReader, slack: Pick<SlackConnections,'web'> }, { webUrl?, timeoutMs? (10s), fetch?, log? }) -> { notify(event), idle(): Promise, close() }. Started by startPlatform as platform.notifications (PlatformOptions.notifications; index.ts passes config.notifications), closed first in platform.close(). It subscribes via subscribeActivityEvents(db, listener) added to src/activity/events.ts (WeakMap keyed by Db so test platforms never cross-talk; listener errors are console.error'd and never fail the append). Matching: bot.handoff -> bot.finished; incident.opened/closed -> same; deploy.attempted -> deploy.succeeded when payload.outcome==='succeeded', deploy.failed when 'failed', else nothing. Enabled rule with destination -> claim event id in the delivered ring BEFORE sending (at-most-once: a crash between claim and post loses the message rather than repeating it; no catch-up on restart; ids older than the ring could in theory repeat if re-emitted, nothing re-emits). Sender order: project's first bot by lower(name),createdAt with slackBotToken set -> platform.slack.web(botId).operations; else global slack plugin instance (resolvePluginInstance(deps, projectId, 'slack'), createSlackOperations(slackConfig(cfg), createPluginSecrets(...))); else failure 'No Slack identity: ...'. Message text: '<escaped title>\n<ABSURL|Open in Candy Mountain>', ABSURL = CM_WEB_URL + event.link, or /p/<slug> when link is null. memberId -> conversations.open then chat.postMessage; channelId -> chat.postMessage. Success stamps lastDeliveredAt and clears failure; any error (no identity, SecretsLockedError, SlackApiError e.g. channel_not_found, token redacted) records lastFailureAt + lastFailureReason on that kind's rule and continues.

CM_WEB_URL: new env (resolveNotificationSettings in src/notifications/config.ts; DaemonConfig.notifications.webUrl), default http://127.0.0.1:4300, must be http(s), trailing slash stripped, invalid value stops boot. README Configuration row added.

10.5 UI should: GET projectNotificationsPath(slug) to render the five kinds (NOTIFICATION_KIND_LABELS) each with an on/off switch, a destination type (channel/DM) + id input, and show lastDeliveredAt / lastFailureReason; PUT only the kinds the user changed ({ rules: { kind: { enabled, destination } } }); expect 400 messages prefixed with the kind. The failure clears when the rule is saved again.

PRODUCERS (7.6 bot handoff, 8.x incidents, 9.x deploys): bot.handoff events must carry link = thread path (/p/<slug>/agents/<threadId>) so the DM opens the thread; incident events should link to the monitor page; deploy.attempted MUST set payload.outcome to 'succeeded' | 'failed' (DEPLOY_OUTCOMES) or no notification is sent. Titles are sent as-is (mrkdwn-escaped), keep them one line.

TESTS: src/notifications/notifications.test.ts stubs fetch (never real Slack): REST defaults/merge/persist, validation + 403/404, kind mapping, bot DM with thread link via bot token, incident to channel via global plugin, first-bot-with-keys preference, no-identity failure recorded + cleared on next success/PUT, Slack error reason, exactly-once incl. across dispatcher restart, ring trim, disabled/unmatched/closed ignored, other-Db isolation, platform wiring. Live (tsx script, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, port 9541): PUT/GET/400/404, in-process incident.opened append -> lastFailureReason recorded, PUT clears, rules persist across restart. Slack base URL is hardcoded in plugins/slack/client.ts so the delivery path is tests-only.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (119 files, 1139 passed, 3 skipped), build (daemon tsdown + web) all pass.
close_reason: Rules in platform_meta, dispatcher with at-most-once delivery, CM_WEB_URL; 14 tests; live-verified

title: Add the global Slack plugin type for platform notifications
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Notifications need a Slack identity when a project has no bot. Add the `slack` plugin type: global scope only (the one global plugin in v3), secret is a bot token, config is a default channel id. Health means the token can call Slack's auth test. Expose a daemon-side operation to post a message (text or blocks) to a channel or as a direct message to a member id.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: A platform-level instance with a valid token reports healthy; the post operation delivers a message; a project scope is rejected; tests mock Slack.
notes:
Slack plugin type decisions (10.4 notifications and phase 7 depend on these).

FILES: apps/daemon/src/plugins/types/slack.ts (type + SlackConfig + slackConfig()), apps/daemon/src/plugins/slack/{client.ts, operations.ts, index.ts, slack.test.ts}. Registered in PLUGIN_TYPES (types/index.ts) and re-exported from apps/daemon/src/plugins/index.ts (export * from './slack'). Daemon-only; nothing added to @candy-mountain/shared. No Drizzle schema/migration, no new dependency (global fetch).

TYPE: id 'slack', scopes ['global'] only, singleInstance true. Config: defaultChannelId (string, OPTIONAL, pattern [CG][A-Z0-9]+, e.g. C0123456789) - optional because notification rules carry their own destination; postMessage falls back to it. Secret: botToken (required; xoxb- Bot User OAuth Token, scopes chat:write + im:write). Health = auth.test ok -> {healthy:true, detail:'Connected to <team> as @<user>.'}; bad token -> reason 'Slack auth.test failed: invalid_auth (the bot token is invalid or has been revoked).'; no token -> 'No Slack bot token is set.' (no request made). healthCheck has an explicit Promise<PluginHealth> return annotation: without it TS reports a circular type (type -> operations -> SlackConfig -> type).

PROJECT SCOPE REJECTION: enforced by scopes ['global'] plus 2.5's instance rule (type.scopes.includes(scope)); 2.5 is not built yet, so the test asserts at type level that scopes is ['global'] and excludes 'project'. 2.5 should add an instance-level test for a project-scoped slack instance.

OPERATIONS: createSlackOperations(config: SlackConfig, secrets: PluginSecrets<'botToken'>, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal, fetch?: typeof fetch }): SlackOperations (frozen) with
- authTest(): Promise<SlackIdentity {teamId, team, userId, user, url}>
- openDirectMessage(memberId): Promise<string> (DM channel id via conversations.open {users})
- postMessage(message: SlackMessage): Promise<SlackPostedMessage {channel, ts}>. SlackMessage = ({channel} | {memberId} | {}) & { text?, blocks?: readonly SlackBlock[] } (channel+memberId together is a compile error and a runtime invalid_request). memberId must match ^[UW][A-Z0-9]+$ and triggers conversations.open first; returned channel is the D... id. Neither -> config.defaultChannelId, else invalid_request. Needs non-blank text or >=1 block; blocks: array of objects each with string type, max SLACK_MAX_BLOCKS=50; block contents are Slack's to validate. text is sent alongside blocks as notification fallback when given.
Low-level: createSlackClient(token, options) -> { call<T>(method, body), error(...) } for phase 7 to build more methods on (chat.update, etc.) with a project bot's token.

ENDPOINTS: POST https://slack.com/api/{auth.test, conversations.open, chat.postMessage}, JSON body, headers Authorization: Bearer <token>, Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8. Every request gets options.signal; an abort rethrows the AbortError unchanged.

ERRORS: SlackApiError (name 'SlackApiError') {method, code: SlackErrorCode, slackError?, status?, retryAfterSeconds?}; codes: no_token | invalid_request (local validation, no request made) | unavailable (fetch threw or HTTP 5xx) | rate_limited (HTTP 429 with Retry-After, or Slack error 'ratelimited') | invalid_response (non-JSON / missing fields) | slack_error (ok:false). Message 'Slack <method> failed: <error> (<hint>).' with hints for invalid_auth/not_authed/token_revoked/token_expired/account_inactive, channel_not_found, not_in_channel, is_archived, user_not_found, user_disabled, missing_scope (names the needed scope). Token is redacted ('[redacted]') from every message; checkPluginHealth also redacts.

WHAT TO IMPORT (from apps/daemon/src/plugins or ./plugins/slack): slackPluginType, slackConfig (narrow stored config, throws 'Invalid Slack config: ...'), SlackConfig, createSlackOperations, SlackOperations, SlackMessage, SlackDestination, SlackBlock, SlackPostedMessage, SlackIdentity, SlackApiError, SlackErrorCode, createSlackClient, SlackClient, SlackClientOptions, SLACK_MAX_BLOCKS. 10.4 dispatcher: find the single global slack instance, secrets = createPluginSecrets(platform.secrets, instanceId, slackPluginType), createSlackOperations(slackConfig(instance.config), secrets).postMessage({ memberId | channel, text, blocks }). Phase 7 bot keys: createSlackClient(botToken) or createSlackOperations({}, { get: () => token }).

TESTS: plugins/slack/slack.test.ts (18 tests) mocks Slack with vi.stubGlobal('fetch') in-memory workspace; no real Slack calls.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (48 files, 395 tests), build all pass.
close_reason: slack plugin type + post operations, 18 mocked tests; gates green

title: Fill the live-version shape from the Netlify and Heroku plugins
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. Add two more live-version source kinds for environments: Netlify and Heroku, each reading the current deploy through the project's plugin instance and filling the common shape (commit, branch, deployed at, link). An environment using a vendor source must be rejected when the project has no healthy instance of that plugin, and the live-version answer must report the plugin reason when the instance later becomes unhealthy.
acceptance_criteria: A Netlify environment shows the current deploy's commit and branch; a Heroku environment shows its release; without the plugin the environment cannot be saved; tests mock the plugin operations.
notes:
Netlify + Heroku live-version sources (9.5 depends on these). How-to in apps/daemon/README.md '## Environments and live versions'.

FILES: apps/daemon/src/environments/plugin-sources.ts (NETLIFY_SOURCE id 'netlify', HEROKU_SOURCE id 'heroku', fields [] for both, so there are no settings and liveSourceSettings is stored as {}), registered in builtin-sources.ts: LIVE_VERSION_SOURCES = [custom-endpoint, netlify, heroku] (the order of GET /live-version-sources). Re-exported from environments/index.ts. Tests: environments/plugin-sources.test.ts (8) using instanceHarness(PLUGIN_TYPES) plus vi.stubGlobal('fetch') with an in-memory Netlify site and Heroku app; instances are made healthy or unhealthy with the real testPluginInstance against the stub. No migration, no shared change.

CONTRACT CHANGE: LiveVersionSource.validate is now (settings, { projectId, deps: PluginInstanceDeps }) => {field,message}[] (LiveVersionValidateContext in sources.ts). createEnvironment/updateEnvironment now take deps: PluginInstanceDeps (c.var satisfies it) instead of db as the first argument; update validates inside its transaction with deps.db = tx.

VALIDATION RULE: saving an environment with kind netlify/heroku (POST, or PATCH that changes the kind or sends settings) needs resolvePluginInstance(deps, projectId, type) to exist with stored health.healthy === true. Otherwise 422 invalid_settings with field '' and one of: 'The Netlify plugin is not set up for this project; add it on the Plugins page.' | 'The Netlify plugin has not been tested since it last changed; test it on the Plugins page.' (health null, the same as readiness) | 'The Netlify plugin is unhealthy: <stored health reason>' (same for Heroku). A rename-only PATCH does not re-check.

READ: the same check runs first. If it fails, that message is the environment's error and no vendor call is made, so an instance that later tests unhealthy (or is deleted) shows its reason. Otherwise the read calls create*Operations(config(instance.config), createPluginSecrets(deps.secretsReader, instance.id, type), { signal, fetch: ctx.fetch }). Vendor errors (NetlifyApiError/HerokuApiError messages, key redacted) become the environment's error. Stored health is not updated by a read.

MAPPING. Netlify getCurrentDeploy(): version = commitSha (left out for a commitless CLI/drag-and-drop deploy), branch, deployedAt (published_at, else created_at), link = deployUrl, the deploy permalink, chosen because it pins the exact live build; when that is null, getSite().url costs one extra request. null deploy -> {}. Heroku getCurrentRelease(): version = commitSha ?? 'v'+version, deployedAt = createdAt, link = appUrl, never a branch. null release -> {}.

FOR 9.5: kind picker from GET /api/live-version-sources (netlify/heroku have no fields, so no settings form). Show a 422 invalid_settings message as-is in the save form; it tells the user to set up or test the plugin on the Plugins page. Live cards: ok -> render version/branch/deployedAt/link if present (Heroku never has branch; Netlify may lack version; {} = nothing deployed yet). Not ok -> the error string, which may be a plugin-health message pointing at the Plugins page.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (128 files, 1215 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass.
close_reason: Netlify and Heroku live-version sources done; root gates green; notes stored
