title: Add the Heroku plugin type
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Deployments need to read Heroku. Add the `heroku` plugin type: project scope, config is the app name, the secret is an API key. Health means the key can read the app. Expose a daemon-side operation that returns the app's current release (version, commit sha if the release carries one, description, created at, app URL) for the live-version source.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: A valid key reports healthy and the operation returns the current release; a wrong key reports unhealthy; tests mock the API.
notes:
Heroku plugin type decisions (9.4 depends on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Plugin types' > '### Heroku'.

FILES: apps/daemon/src/plugins/types/heroku.ts (herokuPluginType + HerokuConfig + herokuConfig() parser), apps/daemon/src/plugins/heroku/{client.ts, operations.ts, index.ts, heroku.test.ts}. Registered in PLUGIN_TYPES (types/index.ts) and re-exported from apps/daemon/src/plugins/index.ts (export * from './heroku'). Daemon-only; nothing in @candy-mountain/shared. No Drizzle schema/migration, no new dependency (global fetch).

TYPE: id 'heroku', scopes ['project'], singleInstance true. Config: appName (string, required, pattern [a-z][a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9]). Secret: apiKey (required; Heroku API key or authorization token, sent as Bearer). healthCheck has an explicit Promise<PluginHealth> annotation (avoids the type -> operations -> HerokuConfig circularity). Health = getApp() succeeds -> {healthy:true, detail:"Can read Heroku app 'x'."}; wrong key -> reason "Heroku returned 401 for app 'x': Invalid credentials provided (the API key is invalid or has expired)."; unknown/inaccessible app -> 404 reason with hint '(check the app name and the API key's access)'; no key -> 'No Heroku API key is set.' (no request made).

OPERATIONS: createHerokuOperations(config: HerokuConfig, secrets: PluginSecrets<'apiKey'>, options?: {signal?: AbortSignal, fetch?: typeof fetch}): HerokuOperations (frozen; never throws itself) with
- getApp(): Promise<HerokuApp {id, name, webUrl: string|null}>
- getCurrentRelease(): Promise<HerokuRelease | null>, HerokuRelease = {version: number, commitSha: string|null, description: string, createdAt: string (ISO 8601, Heroku's created_at), appUrl: string|null (app web_url), status: 'succeeded'|'failed'|'pending'}. null = app never released. Picks the release with current:true among the newest 10, else newest succeeded, else newest (so a failed newer release-phase is skipped). commitSha: GET the release's slug (or OCI image when slug is null) and read its commit; null when neither exists or the build has no commit.
Low-level: createHerokuClient(apiKey, options) -> {get<T>(path, subject, headers?), error(code, message, extra)} for later deploy strategies.

ENDPOINTS (base https://api.heroku.com, headers Accept: application/vnd.heroku+json; version=3, Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>, every request gets options.signal; an abort rethrows the AbortError unchanged): GET /apps/{app}; GET /apps/{app}/releases with Range: 'version ..; order=desc, max=10' (200/206 both ok); GET /apps/{app}/slugs/{slugId}; GET /apps/{app}/oci-images/{imageId}. getCurrentRelease = 3 requests (app + releases in parallel, then slug/image).

ERRORS: HerokuApiError (name 'HerokuApiError') {code: HerokuErrorCode, herokuError? (Heroku's body id), status?, retryAfterSeconds? (Retry-After header)}; codes: no_token | unauthorized (401) | forbidden (403) | not_found (404) | rate_limited (429) | unavailable (fetch threw or 5xx) | invalid_response (non-JSON, missing app id/name, releases not an array, release missing version/created_at/known status) | heroku_error (other 4xx). Message 'Heroku returned <status> for <subject>: <Heroku message> (<hint>).'. The API key is redacted ('[redacted]') from every message; checkPluginHealth also redacts. Nothing retries.

FOR 9.4: import { createHerokuOperations, herokuConfig, herokuPluginType, HerokuApiError, type HerokuRelease } from '../plugins' (or '../plugins/heroku'); build with createHerokuOperations(herokuConfig(instance.config), createPluginSecrets(platform.secrets, instance.id, herokuPluginType), { signal }). Map to live-version: version/commit = commitSha ?? 'v'+version, deployed at = createdAt, link = appUrl; Heroku releases carry no branch (leave it unset). Tests: stub fetch (see heroku.test.ts stubHeroku) or mock the operations.
close_reason: Verified by agent against real bd / mocked API; gates green except in-flight files

title: Define environments and the common live-version shape with a custom endpoint source
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

What is live must look the same whatever vendor serves it. Add a per-project environment table with REST: name, a live-version source kind, and source settings. Define the common live-version shape once: version or commit, branch, deployed at, and a link, each optional. Implement the first source kind, a custom version endpoint: the environment stores a URL the project itself exposes and a mapping from paths in that endpoint's JSON response to the four fields; the daemon fetches it with a short timeout and fills the shape. Expose an endpoint that returns the live version for every environment of a project, with per-environment errors rather than failing the whole answer. Leave room for a deploy strategy on the environment (a nullable kind and settings, unused for now).
acceptance_criteria: An environment pointing at a local fake endpoint with a mapping renders the four fields; an unreachable endpoint reports an error for that environment only; tests cover the mapping.
notes:
Environments + live-version decisions (9.4 and 9.5 depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Environments and live versions'.

TABLE environments (src/db/schema/environments.ts): id uuid PK, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, name, live_source_kind (registry id), live_source_settings JSON (normalised validated values), deploy_kind text NULL, deploy_settings JSON NULL (both unused, always null; reserved for the deploy zone), created_at, updated_at. Unique index (project_id, name); the service also refuses case-insensitive duplicates (409 name_taken). List order = creation order (created_at, rowid). MIGRATION drizzle/0016_environments.sql (tag 0016_environments, after 0015_uptime_monitors); db:check + schema drift test pass.

SHARED (packages/shared/src/environments.ts, exported from index): LIVE_VERSION_SOURCES_PATH '/live-version-sources', projectEnvironmentsPath(slug), projectEnvironmentPath(slug,id), projectLiveVersionsPath(slug); ENVIRONMENT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH 100; LIVE_VERSION_SOURCE_ID_PATTERN /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/. LiveVersion { version?, branch?, deployedAt? (ISO 8601), link? (absolute http(s)) }; LIVE_VERSION_FIELDS; LiveVersionResult = {ok:true, version: LiveVersion} | {ok:false, error: string}. Settings fields reuse the monitor field kinds: LiveVersionSourceField = MonitorOptionField, LiveVersionSettings = MonitorOptions, validateLiveVersionSettings(fields, input) -> {ok, settings}|{ok:false, errors:{field,message}[]} (usable by web forms). LiveVersionSourceInfo {id,label,description,fields} + liveVersionSourceInfo() strip helper. Environment {id, projectId, name, liveSourceKind, liveSourceSettings, deployKind: null, deploySettings: null, createdAt, updatedAt}. CreateEnvironmentRequest {name, liveSourceKind, liveSourceSettings?}; UpdateEnvironmentRequest = Partial. EnvironmentListResponse {environments}, EnvironmentResponse {environment}, LiveVersionSourceListResponse {sources}, EnvironmentLiveVersion {environmentId, environmentName, liveSourceKind, checkedAt, live: LiveVersionResult}, LiveVersionsResponse {environments: EnvironmentLiveVersion[]}. ENVIRONMENT_ERROR_CODES.

REGISTRY (apps/daemon/src/environments/sources.ts): interface LiveVersionSource extends LiveVersionSourceInfo { validate?(settings) -> {field,message}[] (cross-field rules, runs after field rules on every write); read(ctx) -> Promise<LiveVersion> (throw to report an error; message becomes that environment's error) }. ctx = LiveVersionReadContext { settings, project: Project, signal, fetch, deps: LiveVersionDeps } where LiveVersionDeps = PluginInstanceDeps & { secretsReader } i.e. { db, pluginTypes, secrets, secretsReader }. defineLiveVersionSource(source) asserts on import (id pattern, label/description, read/validate functions, field names camelCase+unique, kinds, patterns, bounds, defaults) -> LiveVersionSourceError; createLiveVersionSourceRegistry(sources) -> {list, ids, byId, get, has}, rejects duplicates. builtin-sources.ts: LIVE_VERSION_SOURCES = [CUSTOM_ENDPOINT_SOURCE], LIVE_VERSION_SOURCE_REGISTRY (built at load, so a bad source fails boot). The runner (service.readEnvironmentLiveVersion) wraps every read in a 15s cap (LIVE_VERSION_READ_TIMEOUT_MS -> 'No answer within 15s.'), catches throws, reports an unregistered stored kind as 'The live-version source "x" is not available.', and normalises output via normaliseLiveVersion (trims, drops empties, deployedAt -> ISO or dropped, link must be absolute http(s)).

CUSTOM ENDPOINT (custom-endpoint.ts): id 'custom-endpoint', label 'Version endpoint'. Fields: url (required, http(s), <=2048), versionPath, branchPath, deployedAtPath, linkPath (optional, <=200; at least one required; each must parse). readCustomEndpoint(settings, {signal?, fetch?, timeoutMs?}): GET with 5s timeout (CUSTOM_ENDPOINT_TIMEOUT_MS), accept: application/json, redirect:'manual' and follows only same-hostname http(s) redirects (max 5), caps body at 1 MiB, JSON.parse. Paths (json-path.ts parseJsonPath/readJsonPath): dotted a.b, bracket [0] / ["k.e.y"] / ['k'], optional leading $, all-digit dotted key indexes arrays, own properties only. Missing path -> field omitted; no mapped path found -> error 'None of the mapped paths were found...'. version: string or number; branch: string; deployedAt: ISO string or Unix s/ms number; link: string, relative resolves against the (final) endpoint URL. Errors: '<host> returned HTTP N.', '<host> did not return JSON.', 'No response from <host> within 5s.', 'Could not reach <host>: ECONNREFUSED.', redirect/size messages. Matches digital-hub's /api/debug ({commit, branch, buildStartedAt}) via mapping; placeholders suggest those keys.

HOW 9.4 ADDS netlify/heroku: create e.g. src/environments/netlify-source.ts with defineLiveVersionSource({ id: 'netlify', label: 'Netlify', description, fields: [], read: async ({ project, signal, deps }) => { const instance = resolvePluginInstance(deps, project.id, 'netlify'); if (!instance) throw new Error('The Netlify plugin is not set up for this project.'); const deploy = await createNetlifyOperations(netlifyConfig(instance.config), createPluginSecrets(deps.secretsReader, instance.id, netlifyPluginType), { signal }).getCurrentDeploy(); return deploy ? { version: deploy.commitSha ?? undefined, branch: deploy.branch ?? undefined, deployedAt: deploy.deployedAt ?? undefined, link: deploy.deployUrl ?? undefined } : {} } }) and append it to LIVE_VERSION_SOURCES in builtin-sources.ts (same for heroku: version = commitSha ?? 'v'+version, deployedAt = createdAt, link = appUrl, no branch). Settings fields can stay empty (the plugin instance holds the config). No migration needed.

ROUTES (mounted in app.ts; browser uses /api prefix). AUTH: writes requireAdmin (403 forbidden); reads open to any signed-in actor (same model as uptime; gate on a deployments capability rung when one exists). GET /live-version-sources -> {sources}. GET /projects/:slug/environments -> {environments}; POST -> 201 {environment}; GET/PATCH /projects/:slug/environments/:id -> {environment} (omitted unchanged; settings replace whole; kind change without settings validates {}); DELETE -> 204. GET /projects/:slug/live-versions -> {environments: EnvironmentLiveVersion[]} read in parallel, always 200 for a known project; per-environment {ok:false,error}. environmentRoutes(secretsReader, {sources?, fetch?}) and liveVersionSourceRoutes(sources?) take injectable registries. Errors: invalid_request 400, not_found 404 (also other project's env / unknown project), name_taken 409, unknown_source 422 (lists known ids), invalid_settings 422 ('field: problem ...').

FOR 9.5 (Deployments page): GET /api/live-version-sources to build the kind picker and render settings fields (validateLiveVersionSettings client-side; placeholders/descriptions on fields); GET/POST /api/projects/:slug/environments, PATCH/DELETE /api/projects/:slug/environments/:id for management (admin); GET /api/projects/:slug/live-versions for the per-environment cards (render version/branch/deployedAt/link when ok, the error string otherwise; checkedAt for 'checked at'). Can take up to ~5s (custom endpoint) / 15s (cap), so load it separately from the environment list.

TESTS: src/environments/{json-path,custom-endpoint,environments}.test.ts (19) with a local fake endpoint server (fake-endpoint.ts helper): mapping incl. nested/bracket/indexed paths, missing fields, wrong types, none found, HTTP error, non-JSON, oversize, same-host redirect ok / other-host refused / loop, timeout, ECONNREFUSED; registry validation; CRUD + error codes + 403 for viewers; project cascade; live-versions with one ok + unreachable + 404 env; throwing/hanging/unregistered sources. VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (126 files, 1200 passed), build pass; built daemon curl-checked on port 9873 (fake endpoint on 9871, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR): 17 migrations applied, CRUD, 409/422s, live-versions returned the four fields for Production and 'Could not reach 127.0.0.1:9879: ECONNREFUSED.' for Staging only.
close_reason: environments table, live-version source registry, custom-endpoint source, per-env error isolation; 19 tests

title: Add the Netlify plugin type
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Deployments need to read Netlify. Add the `netlify` plugin type: project scope, config is the site id, the secret is a personal access token. Health means the token can read the site. Expose a daemon-side operation that returns the site's current production deploy (commit sha, branch, deployed at, deploy URL) for the live-version source.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: A valid token reports healthy and the operation returns the current deploy; a wrong token reports unhealthy with the reason; tests mock the API.
notes:
Netlify plugin type decisions (9.4 depends on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Plugin types' > '### Netlify'.

FILES: apps/daemon/src/plugins/types/netlify.ts (netlifyPluginType, NetlifyConfig, netlifyConfig() parser throwing 'Invalid Netlify config: ...'); apps/daemon/src/plugins/netlify/{client.ts, operations.ts, index.ts, netlify.test.ts}. Registered in PLUGIN_TYPES (types/index.ts) and re-exported from apps/daemon/src/plugins/index.ts (export * from './netlify'). Daemon-only: nothing added to @candy-mountain/shared (no browser needs the raw deploy shape; 9.3 owns the common live-version wire shape). No Drizzle schema/migration, no new dependency.

TYPE: id 'netlify', scopes ['project'], singleInstance true. Config: siteId (string, required, pattern [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.-]*; the site's API ID or its netlify.app domain, both accepted by the Netlify API). Secret: token (required; Netlify personal access token, sent as Authorization: Bearer). Health = GET /api/v1/sites/{siteId} succeeds -> {healthy:true, detail:'Can read the site <name> (<url>).'}; wrong token -> reason 'Netlify returned 401 for site <id>: <Netlify message> (the token is invalid or has expired)'; unknown site -> 404 with hint '(check the site ID and that the token's account can see the site)'; no token -> 'No Netlify token is set for site <id>.' (no request). healthCheck has explicit Promise<PluginHealth> annotation (avoids circular type, as Slack).

OPERATIONS: createNetlifyOperations(config: NetlifyConfig, secrets: PluginSecrets<'token'>, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal, fetch?: typeof fetch }): NetlifyOperations (frozen; never throws itself; token read once).
- getSite(): Promise<NetlifySite { id, name, url: string|null (ssl_url ?? url), adminUrl: string|null }>
- getCurrentDeploy(): Promise<NetlifyDeploy | null>, NetlifyDeploy = { id: string, state: string (Netlify state, 'ready' when live; 'unknown' if absent), commitSha: string|null (commit_ref), branch: string|null, deployedAt: string|null (ISO 8601 from published_at, else created_at), deployUrl: string|null (deploy_ssl_url ?? deploy_url, the permalink to that exact deploy) }. Source: site.published_deploy; if absent/null, GET /api/v1/sites/{id}/deploys?production=true&state=ready&per_page=1; empty list -> null (never published). commitSha/branch null for CLI/drag-and-drop deploys.
Low-level: createNetlifyClient(token, subject, options) -> { get(path), error(...) } for later endpoints (e.g. build hooks for the deploy zone).

ENDPOINTS: base https://api.netlify.com/api/v1; GET only; headers Accept: application/json, Authorization: Bearer <token>, User-Agent: candy-mountain; site id URL-encoded in the path. Every request gets options.signal; an abort rethrows the original AbortError unwrapped.

ERRORS: NetlifyApiError (name 'NetlifyApiError') { code: NetlifyErrorCode, status?, retryAfterSeconds? }. Codes: no_token (no request) | unauthorized (401) | forbidden (403) | not_found (404) | rate_limited (429; retryAfterSeconds from Retry-After or X-RateLimit-Reset; message ends '(retry in N s)') | unavailable (5xx or network failure 'Could not reach Netlify: ...') | api_error (other non-2xx) | invalid_response (non-JSON, site without id, deploy without id, deploy list not an array). Message shape 'Netlify returned <status> for site <siteId>: <body.message or statusText> (<hint>)'. Token replaced with [redacted] in every message; checkPluginHealth also redacts. No retries, no pagination.

WHAT 9.4 IMPORTS (from apps/daemon/src/plugins or ./plugins/netlify): netlifyPluginType, netlifyConfig, NetlifyConfig, createNetlifyOperations, NetlifyOperations, NetlifyDeploy, NetlifySite, NetlifyApiError, NetlifyErrorCode. Wiring: createNetlifyOperations(netlifyConfig(instance.config), createPluginSecrets(platform.secrets, instance.id, netlifyPluginType), { signal }).getCurrentDeploy() -> map to the common live-version shape: commit = commitSha, branch = branch, deployedAt = deployedAt, link = deployUrl (or getSite().url for the site's public URL); null -> nothing live. Heroku (9.2) shape for comparison: { version, commitSha, description, createdAt, appUrl, status }.

TESTS: plugins/netlify/netlify.test.ts (18 tests) stubs global fetch with an in-memory Netlify (site 3970e0fe-..., token nfp_good-token-123); covers registration/scope/singleInstance/boot, config validation, healthy, wrong token (401 reason), unknown site (404), no token (no request), redaction (network error + echoed body), getSite, published_deploy, deploys-list fallback URL, never published -> null, commitless deploy, site domain id, 429 retry, 502/non-JSON/missing id, injected fetch, abort passthrough. No real network calls.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (56 files, 507 tests), build all pass. One earlier full-suite run had a timing flake in src/issues/watcher.test.ts ('folds a burst of ten writes', expected 6 <= 5; not this bead's code) that passed in isolation and on rerun.
close_reason: netlify type + operations, 18 mocked tests; gates green

title: Add the Uptime capability and page with monitor cards and forms
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. title: Schedule monitors on their own intervals with one poller per monitor
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Checks must keep running across restarts without ever running twice. Build the scheduler: on daemon start, load every enabled monitor and schedule it on its interval (staggered so they do not all fire at once); creating, editing (interval or target) or disabling a monitor reschedules it without a restart; deleting stops it. Each check runs the type's checker and stores a check row (monitor, time, ok, status, latency, error), keeping a bounded history per monitor (prune beyond a configurable count or age). Guard against overlapping runs of the same monitor and against duplicate schedulers in development hot reload.
acceptance_criteria: Two monitors with different intervals fire at their own cadence; editing an interval changes the cadence without a restart; a slow check does not overlap with the next; after a restart each monitor has exactly one schedule; history is pruned; tests use fake timers.
notes:
Uptime scheduler decisions (8.4 incidents/hysteresis and the 8.x Uptime page build on these). Full how-to in apps/daemon/README.md '## Uptime monitors' (Scheduling paragraph).

TABLE uptime_checks (src/db/schema/uptime-checks.ts): id integer PK (rowid), monitor_id FK uptime_monitors ON DELETE CASCADE, checked_at text ISO (= check START, from MonitorCheckResult.checkedAt), ok int boolean, status text enum up|degraded|down, http_status int NULL, latency_ms int, detail text NULL. Index uptime_checks_monitor_id_checked_at_idx (monitor_id, checked_at). MIGRATION drizzle/0017_uptime_checks.sql (tag 0017_uptime_checks, after 0016_environments); db:check + schema drift test pass.

STORAGE (src/uptime/checks.ts): type UptimeCheck = row type {id, monitorId, checkedAt, ok, status, httpStatus, latencyMs, detail}. recordMonitorCheck(db, monitorId, result, {historyMax, historyMaxAgeMs}) inserts + prunes in one transaction. pruneMonitorChecks(...). listMonitorChecks(db, monitorId, limit=50 (MONITOR_CHECKS_LIST_DEFAULT), clamped 1..1000) -> NEWEST FIRST (checked_at desc, id desc). latestMonitorCheckAt(db, monitorId).

SERVICE HOOK (src/uptime/service.ts): onMonitorChange((db, change) => void) -> unsubscribe; change = {kind:'saved', monitor} | {kind:'deleted', monitorId}; emitted after createMonitor, updateMonitor (after commit; setMonitorEnabled goes through it) and deleteMonitor. Listener gets the db written to; module-level set, listener errors are logged.

SCHEDULER (src/uptime/scheduler.ts): startUptimeScheduler({ db, key?, ownerFile?, sources?, fetch?, log? }, { historyMax?, historyMaxAgeMs?, timeoutMs?, staggerWindowMs? = MONITOR_STAGGER_WINDOW_MS 15000 }) -> UptimeScheduler { scheduled(): ids, nextCheckAt(id): ISO|null, onCheck(listener) -> unsubscribe, reload(), close() }. One setTimeout chain per monitor (unref'd), fixed rate from the planned due time. First due = last stored check + interval (cadence survives restarts); none/overdue -> now + sha1(id) % min(interval, 15s). Hook: new interval counts from last check; changed target/sourceType/options aborts the in-flight check (result discarded) and rechecks within the stagger; disable/delete unschedules. Each tick re-reads the monitor (findMonitor) so a cascade-deleted (project deleted) or out-of-band-disabled monitor is dropped. Overlap guard: a tick that finds the previous check running is skipped. Checks aborted by the scheduler itself (edit, delete, close) are never stored. Single instance: module-level registry by key (Platform passes paths.root) closes the previous one in-process; ownerFile (Platform: <data>/run/uptime-scheduler.owner) holds the newest scheduler's token, an older process's next tick sees a foreign token, warns 'Another uptime scheduler took over this data directory; this one stops polling.' and halts; close() removes the file only if it still owns it. PLATFORM: platform.uptimeScheduler, PlatformOptions.uptime; closed first in platform.close(). index.ts passes config.uptime.

ENV (src/uptime/config.ts, DaemonConfig.uptime = UptimeSettings {historyMax, historyMaxAgeMs}): CM_UPTIME_HISTORY_MAX default 500 (1..100000), CM_UPTIME_HISTORY_MAX_AGE default 30d (Ns/m/h/d, <=366d). Pruning runs per monitor on each stored check.

FOR 8.4: subscribe with platform.uptimeScheduler.onCheck(({ monitor, check }) => ...) - called after each check is STORED, check is the UptimeCheck row (includes id), listener may be async (rejections logged). To rebuild state on boot without a false incident, read listMonitorChecks(db, monitorId, N) (newest first) rather than waiting for new checks. Hysteresis should use check.status ('down' = failure, 'degraded' or latencyMs over threshold = degraded), not ok alone. Note history may be pruned to CM_UPTIME_HISTORY_MAX, so do not rely on more than that many rows.

VERIFY: src/uptime/scheduler.test.ts 11 fake-timer tests (two cadences 30s/45s, stagger by hash, interval edit, target edit cancels+discards in-flight, slow 75s check on 30s interval -> no overlap (runs at 0,90,180), disable/delete/enable/project delete, other-db isolation, in-process restart -> one timer per monitor + cadence from last check, cross-process owner takeover, pruning by count and age, close clears all timers). Root lint/typecheck/test (1226 pass)/build pass; db:check ok. Live: dist daemon on 10732 + stub on 10731, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: A(30s)/B(45s) staggered ~1.7s/~9.9s, cadence exact, PATCH interval 60 -> next at last+60, disable B stopped it, CM_UPTIME_HISTORY_MAX=3 kept 3 rows, 503 stored down 'Expected status 200, got 503.'; real daemon SIGTERM+restart -> /a hits 3.5,33.5,63.5,93.5 and /b 18.4,63.4,108.4 (no duplicates, cadence kept), owner file removed on clean stop; two overlapping scheduler processes -> older one halted at its next tick, no duplicate hits.

OPEN: monitors of archived projects still run (listEnabledMonitors does not filter archived); decide in 8.4/8.5 whether archive should pause them.
close_reason: Uptime scheduler with uptime_checks table (0017), per-monitor timers, cadence after restart, single owner per data dir, history pruning; gates green

title: Derive monitor state with hysteresis and open and close incidents
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A single blip must not flap a monitor. Derive each monitor's state from its recent checks the way Digital Hub does: down when the newest three checks all failed; degraded when any check in the recent window failed or latency exceeded two seconds; up otherwise; unknown with no history. Rebuild state from stored history on start so a restart never produces a false transition. Open an incident (monitor, opened at, reason) on the transition to down and close it (closed at) on recovery to up; both write activity events (`incident.opened`, `incident.closed`) linking to the monitor. Leave an optional thread-reference field on the incident for a later investigation thread; nothing investigates automatically. Expose state, recent checks and incidents (per monitor and project-wide) over REST.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.
acceptance_criteria: Three consecutive failures open one incident; recovery closes it; a single failure shows degraded without an incident; restarting with a down monitor keeps the open incident and opens no second one; the Overview feed shows both events; tests cover the transitions.
notes:
DONE (awaiting orchestrator close). Migration 0019 (uptime_incidents) landed earlier; no schema changes after it.

Daemon: src/uptime/state.ts (deriveMonitorState, monitorStatus, reconcileMonitorIncident), incidents.ts (findOpenIncident, listIncidents, openIncident, closeIncident, setIncidentThread), tracker.ts (startIncidentTracker, wired in platform.ts after the scheduler; reconciles every polled monitor at start, then on each scheduler.onCheck), routes.ts (state routes). Shared types/paths/constants in packages/shared/src/uptime.ts.

State rule: newest 3 checks all status=down -> down; any check in that 3-window not 'up' or latency > 2000 ms -> degraded; else up; no checks -> unknown. Only status=down counts toward down (vendor 'degraded' and slow never open incidents). Recovery reads degraded until 3 good checks in a row, so an incident closes on the 3rd good check. Incidents are reconciled against the stored open incident (partial unique index on monitor_id WHERE closed_at IS NULL), never a remembered state, so restarts never open a second one. Activity: incident.opened (title '<name> is down: <reason>', payload {incidentId, monitorId, monitorName, reason, openedAt}) and incident.closed (title '<name> is back up', payload {incidentId, monitorId, monitorName, openedAt, closedAt, durationMs}); both link to uptimeMonitorLink(slug, id) = /p/<slug>/uptime?monitor=<id> -> 8.5 should open the monitor's drawer from ?monitor=.

Archived projects (decision 72 follow-up): PAUSED. listEnabledMonitors/findPolledMonitor join projects and skip archived; projects.ts gained onProjectArchiveChange which the scheduler uses to reload. An incident open at archive time stays open until the project is unarchived and the monitor recovers. Disabling a monitor likewise leaves its open incident open.

REST (all GET, any signed-in actor; under /projects/:slug; path helpers in shared):
- /monitors/:id/status?recent=N (0..200, default 30) -> MonitorStatusResponse {status: MonitorStatus}  [projectMonitorStatusPath]
- /monitors/:id/checks?limit=N (1..1000, default 50) -> MonitorCheckListResponse {checks: MonitorCheckRecord[]} newest first  [projectMonitorChecksPath]
- /monitors/:id/incidents?status=open|closed&limit=N (1..200, default 50) -> IncidentListResponse {incidents: MonitorIncident[]} newest opened first  [projectMonitorIncidentsPath]
- /uptime/status?recent=N -> UptimeStatusResponse {monitors: MonitorStatus[]} (every monitor of the project incl. disabled, ordered by name)  [projectUptimeStatusPath]
- /uptime/incidents?status=open|closed&monitor=<id>&limit=N -> IncidentListResponse (project-wide)  [projectUptimeIncidentsPath]
Shapes: MonitorStatus {monitor: Monitor, state: 'up'|'degraded'|'down'|'unknown' (MONITOR_STATES), lastCheck: MonitorCheckRecord|null, openIncident: MonitorIncident|null, recentChecks: MonitorCheckRecord[] newest first}. MonitorCheckRecord {id:number, monitorId, checkedAt, ok, status:'up'|'degraded'|'down', httpStatus:number|null, latencyMs, detail:string|null}. MonitorIncident {id, projectId, monitorId, openedAt, closedAt:string|null (null = open), reason, threadId:string|null}. Errors: ApiErrorBody, 400 invalid_request for bad query values, 404 not_found for unknown monitor/project.
No route sets threadId yet (setIncidentThread exists daemon-side for a later investigation-thread bead).

Gates: daemon vitest 91 files / 912 passed (3 skipped); daemon tsc clean; shared tsc clean; eslint on uptime, projects, platform.ts, shared uptime.ts clean.
close_reason: Monitor state with hysteresis, incidents + activity events, REST routes; archived projects pause polling; tests green

title: Add uptime monitors as per-project rows with REST
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Digital Hub kept monitors in a JSON file that needed a restart to change. Add a monitor table owned by a project: name, source type, target (URL), interval in seconds (minimum enforced), enabled flag, and type-specific options stored as validated JSON. Define the source type model as an open registry in the daemon where each type declares its id, label, its option fields and (in separate work) its checker; register the ids `http` (options: expected status, optional response substring), `statuspage`, `statusio` and `statping` now. REST: list, create, update, delete, enable and disable, validated against the type's options. Non-goals: polling, UI.
acceptance_criteria: Creating an HTTP monitor with an expected status persists; an unknown type or an interval below the minimum is rejected; the type registry lists the four types with their option fields; tests cover validation.
notes:
Uptime monitor decisions (8.2, 8.3 and the 8.x Uptime page rely on these). Full how-to in apps/daemon/README.md '## Uptime monitors'.

TABLE uptime_monitors (src/db/schema/uptime-monitors.ts): id uuid PK, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, name, source_type (registry id), target (absolute http(s) URL, <=2048), interval_seconds int, enabled int boolean, options JSON (normalised validated values), created_at, updated_at; index on project_id. MIGRATION drizzle/0015_uptime_monitors.sql (tag 0015_uptime_monitors, after 0014_team_members); schema drift test + db:check pass.

SHARED (packages/shared/src/uptime.ts, exported): MONITOR_SOURCES_PATH '/monitor-sources', projectMonitorsPath(slug), projectMonitorPath(slug,id); MONITOR_INTERVAL_MIN_SECONDS 30, MAX 86400, DEFAULT 60; MONITOR_NAME_MAX_LENGTH 100, MONITOR_TARGET_MAX_LENGTH 2048; MONITOR_SOURCE_ID_PATTERN /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/, MONITOR_OPTION_NAME_PATTERN camelCase. Fields: MonitorOptionField = MonitorStringField {kind:'string', name, label, description?, required?, placeholder?, pattern? (anchored RegExp source), maxLength?, default?} | MonitorIntegerField {kind:'integer', ..., placeholder?, min?, max?, default?}; MONITOR_OPTION_FIELD_KINDS. MonitorOptions = Record<string,string|number>. validateMonitorOptions(fields, input) -> {ok:true, options}|{ok:false, errors:{field,message}[]} (trims, empty=absent, fills defaults, digit strings accepted for integers, unknown keys rejected) - usable by web forms. MonitorSourceInfo {id,label,description,targetLabel,targetPlaceholder?,fields} + monitorSourceInfo() strip helper. Monitor {id, projectId, name, sourceType, target, intervalSeconds, enabled, options, createdAt, updatedAt}. CreateMonitorRequest {name, sourceType, target, intervalSeconds?, enabled?, options?}; UpdateMonitorRequest = Partial. MonitorListResponse {monitors}, MonitorResponse {monitor}, MonitorSourceListResponse {sources}. MONITOR_ERROR_CODES.

REGISTRY (apps/daemon/src/uptime/sources.ts): type MonitorSource = MonitorSourceInfo today. defineMonitorSource<const S>(source) asserts on import (id pattern, non-blank label/description/targetLabel, field names camelCase + unique, known kind, label set, pattern compiles, maxLength/min/max integers, min<=max, default passes validation) -> MonitorSourceError. createMonitorSourceRegistry(sources) -> {list(), ids(), byId(), get() throws, has()}; rejects duplicate ids. builtin-sources.ts: HTTP_SOURCE (expectedStatus integer 100-599 default 200; responseContains string optional max 500), STATUSPAGE_SOURCE (componentId required; target = https://<page>/api/v2/components.json), STATUSIO_SOURCE (componentId, containerId required; target = https://api.status.io/1.0/status/<page id>), STATPING_SOURCE (serviceId integer >=0 required; target = https://<page>/api/services). MONITOR_SOURCES array and MONITOR_SOURCE_REGISTRY (built at module load, so a bad source fails boot). Vendor id fields use pattern [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ max 64. BEAD 8.2: turn MonitorSource into an interface extending MonitorSourceInfo with a check(ctx) method (keep it out of the wire info; monitorSourceInfo already strips extras), add the checker to each built-in definition, and add a 'must be a function' assertion in assertMonitorSource. Digital Hub readers to port live in ~/work/baby-bunting/digital-hub/apps/mastra/src/mastra/uptime/{statuspage,statusio,statping,vendor}.ts.

SERVICE (src/uptime/service.ts): listMonitors(db, projectId) (by lower(name)), listEnabledMonitors(db) (all projects, for the 8.3 scheduler), findMonitor/getMonitor(db, projectId, id), createMonitor(db, projectId, req, sources=MONITOR_SOURCE_REGISTRY), updateMonitor(db, projectId, id, req, sources) (omitted unchanged; options replaces whole; sourceType change without options validates {} against the new type), setMonitorEnabled(db, projectId, id, bool), deleteMonitor, monitorSourceOf(sources, id). title: Implement the check runners for HTTP and the vendor status-page types
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Each monitor type needs a checker that performs one check and returns ok or not, the HTTP status if any, latency, and an error message. Implement: `http` (GET the target with a five-second timeout and manual redirect handling; ok when the status matches the expected one and, if set, the body contains the substring); `statuspage` (Atlassian Statuspage status API: ok when the overall indicator is none); `statusio` (ok when the overall status is operational); `statping` (ok when the service reports online). Register each with its type in the monitor type registry. Never follow redirects to unexpected hosts; never log response bodies.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests with mocked HTTP cover ok, wrong status, missing substring, timeout and each vendor's degraded response; a real check against a local fake service works.
notes:
Check runners (8.3 scheduler and 8.4 hysteresis/incidents build on these). Full how-to in apps/daemon/README.md '## Uptime monitors' (Checks paragraph).

FILES: src/uptime/check.ts (types + probe helper), src/uptime/checkers.ts (checkHttp, checkStatuspage, checkStatusio, checkStatping), sources.ts (MonitorSource is now interface extends MonitorSourceInfo { check: MonitorCheck }; assertMonitorSource fails 'check must be a function.' so a source without a checker stops boot), builtin-sources.ts (check wired on each), service.ts runMonitorCheck, check.test.ts (17 tests), uptime.test.ts updated. No migration. Types live in the daemon only (not shared); if the UI needs MonitorCheckResult, move the type to packages/shared/src/uptime.ts.

RESULT MonitorCheckResult { ok: boolean (=== status 'up'), status: 'up'|'degraded'|'down', httpStatus: number|null (final response; null when nothing answered), detail: string|null (null when up; never the body or target URL; target credentials/query redacted), latencyMs (int, includes body read), checkedAt (ISO, at start) }. This is ONE check's verdict, no hysteresis.

CONTEXT MonitorCheckContext { target, options, signal?, fetch?, timeoutMs? }. MonitorCheck resolves for every outcome, never rejects. runMonitorCheck(monitor: Pick<Monitor,'sourceType'|'target'|'options'>, { sources?=MONITOR_SOURCE_REGISTRY, signal?, fetch?, timeoutMs? }) -> Promise<MonitorCheckResult>; unknown sourceType or a throwing checker -> down (latencyMs 0, httpStatus null). No scheduling.

PROBE (shared by all 4): GET, redirect:'manual', headers Accept + User-Agent candy-mountain-uptime, MONITOR_CHECK_TIMEOUT_MS 5000 via AbortSignal.timeout combined with caller signal (AbortSignal.any), timeout covers body read (reader cancelled on abort). Body capped MONITOR_MAX_BODY_BYTES 2 MB (down 'larger than 2 MB'). Redirects 301/302/303/307/308 followed up to MONITOR_MAX_REDIRECTS 5, only same hostname (http->https upgrade allowed, https->http refused) else down 'Redirected to another host (<host>)...'. Failures -> down with detail: 'Timed out after 5 s.', 'DNS lookup failed for <host>.' (ENOTFOUND/EAI_AGAIN), 'Connection refused.', 'Connection reset.', 'Connection timed out.', 'TLS certificate problem (<code>).', 'Request failed (<code>).', 'The response is not JSON.'. Caller signal aborted -> down 'Check cancelled.' (8.3: if your own signal aborted, discard the result rather than store it).

HTTP: up when status === expectedStatus (default 200) and, if responseContains set, body includes it; else down 'Expected status X, got Y.' / 'The response does not contain the expected text.'. A 3xx expectedStatus disables redirect following. Body only read when responseContains set.

VENDORS (feed non-2xx -> down 'The status feed returned N.'; not JSON / wrong shape (zod) / missing component -> down):
- statuspage: target /api/v2/components.json or /api/v2/summary.json; components[].id === componentId, .status: operational|under_maintenance -> up; degraded_performance|partial_outage -> degraded; major_outage -> down; unknown string -> degraded "Unrecognised status 'x'.". Detail is status with underscores as spaces.

title: Expose a thread-scoped MCP tool that lets the bot post Block Kit
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

This is the pattern for every "wrapped MCP server scoped to an agent" in Candy Mountain: the agent sees a narrow tool while the daemon holds the credentials and the scope. Build a small MCP server the daemon runs for a bot session (stdio or local HTTP, implementer's choice) exposing one tool that posts a Block Kit payload to the current Slack thread. The daemon validates the payload (well-formed blocks, size limits, no raw tokens), posts it with the bot's credentials, and refuses anything outside the current thread. Register the server with the agent at session start through the harness (Claude Code and Codex both accept MCP server configuration), and allow the tool in the posture for every write scope. Non-goals: any other tool.
acceptance_criteria: Asking the bot to post a formatted message results in a Block Kit message in the thread; a payload naming another channel is refused; the tool is absent from a plain console session that is not a bot.
notes:
Wrapped-MCP pattern (7.7). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Daemon-hosted MCP tools'. NO migration, no tables, no shared-type changes.

FILES: new apps/daemon/src/agent-mcp/{host.ts, tools.ts, index.ts}, src/slack/{block-kit.ts, mcp.ts, mcp.test.ts (8 tests)}; edited src/acp/{families.ts, harness.ts, index.ts}, src/sessions/manager.ts (one hook in startAndPrompt), src/posture/{claude.ts, posture.ts, verify.ts}, src/bot-sessions/service.ts (one line), src/platform.ts, src/slack/index.ts, README.md.

TRANSPORT: startAgentMcpHost({ db, servers }) = platform.agentMcp. Stateless Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1:<port 0, opened lazily on first serversFor>, path /mcp/<server>/<sessionId>, POST only (GET/DELETE 405), one JSON response per request (no SSE, no Mcp-Session-Id), batches answered, notifications 202. Methods: initialize (echoes 2025-11-25|2025-06-18|2025-03-26|2024-11-05, else newest), ping, tools/list, tools/call. Auth: random 32-byte base64url bearer per server+session per daemon boot (in memory only); 401 otherwise; 403 on any Origin header or Host != 127.0.0.1:<port> (DNS rebinding); appliesTo(session) re-checked on every request (404 once out of scope). Body cap 1 MiB. Checked with the real @modelcontextprotocol/client 2.4.0 StreamableHTTPClientTransport (connect, listTools, callTool) from a scratch script.

SERVER DEFINITION: AgentMcpServerDefinition { name, appliesTo(session), tools: AgentMcpTool[] { name, title?, description, inputSchema, annotations?, call(args, { session, signal }) -> { text, isError? } } }. Thrown errors become isError results.

REGISTRATION PER FAMILY (launch-time only, never in the stored posture, because port+token change per boot): SessionManagerDeps.mcpServers(session) -> LaunchMcpServer[] { name, url, bearerToken, tools } (platform wires it to agentMcp.serversFor) is awaited in startAndPrompt on every launch/resume and passed as StartSessionOptions.mcpServers -> FamilyLaunchOptions.mcpServers, validated by assertLaunchMcpServers (name /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,47}$/, unique; url http://127.0.0.1:<port> only, no userinfo; token /^[\w-]{32,128}$/; tools non-empty /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/). Claude Code: appended after the posture flags as --strict-mcp-config (if absent) + --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{name:{type:"http",url,headers:{Authorization:"Bearer .."}}}}' (last, since the flag is variadic). Codex: CODEX_CONFIG.mcp_servers.<name> = { url, http_headers:{Authorization}, enabled_tools: tools, default_tools_approval_mode: 'approve' } (verified with the bundled codex 0.164 binary: `codex -c mcp_servers.x={...} mcp get x` parses it as streamable_http with approve; values are auto|prompt|writes|approve). ACP session/new mcpServers stays [] (the claude shim refuses them; codex-acp's own path cannot set an approval mode).

POSTURE: tool names in src/agent-mcp/tools.ts: WRAPPED_MCP_TOOLS = [SLACK_POST_BLOCKS_TOOL { server: 'candy_mountain_slack', tool: 'post_blocks' }], claudeMcpToolRule -> 'mcp__candy_mountain_slack__post_blocks', WRAPPED_MCP_TOOL_RULES. resolveBotPosture({ mcpTools?: WrappedMcpTool[] }) refuses unknown tools (PostureError invalid_input) and adds their rules to the stored --allowedTools after Bash(bd *) in every write scope (read-only, write-confirm, write-auto); Codex posture unchanged (approval comes with the registration). assertPostureNotWidened now refuses any mcp__ allow rule not in WRAPPED_MCP_TOOL_RULES; --mcp-config in stored flags is still refused; --strict-mcp-config still required. Bot sessions pass mcpTools = [SLACK_POST_BLOCKS_TOOL] only when holder.kind === 'slack'.

TOOL post_blocks (src/slack/mcp.ts slackMcpServer({ db, slack: Pick<SlackConnections,'web'> }, { fetch? })): appliesTo = posture.bot.holder.kind === 'slack' (plain and console sessions get nothing: no --mcp-config, no allow rule). Thread = findSlackThreadBySession(session.id), must be state open, same bot id, holder id == slackThreadHolderId(thread); never from the agent. VALIDATION validateSlackBlocksPost(args, { channel, threadTs }) in src/slack/block-kit.ts: keys only text|blocks|channel|thread_ts (reply_broadcast, username, as_user... refused); channel/thread_ts optional but must equal the thread's; text required, <= 3000; blocks 1..SLACK_MAX_BLOCKS (50), <= 30,000 chars JSON, depth <= 12; types section|header|divider|context|actions|image|markdown|rich_text with required fields (section text<=3000 or fields 1..10; header plain_text<=150; context 1..10 elements; actions 1..25; rich_text elements; image image_url|slack_file + alt_text<=2000; markdown text<=12000); action_id/block_id 1..255 and not starting 'cm-' (SLACK_RESERVED_ID_PREFIX, covers cm-decision buttons); <!channel>/<!here>/<!everyone> and rich_text broadcast elements refused; strings matching Slack xox?-/xapp-, GitHub gh?_/github_pat_, sk-/sk-ant-, AKIA, PEM private keys refused. Posts chat.postMessage { channel, thread_ts, text, blocks } with the bot's token via slack.web(botId); SlackApiError -> isError text. PlatformOptions.agentMcp = { fetch?, slack? } are test seams.

TESTS src/slack/mcp.test.ts: validation accept/refuse table; posture for all 3 scopes (+ widening check, foreign mcp rule, --mcp-config, unknown tool); launch args for both families + loopback-only validation; host auth (wrong token, other session's URL, Origin, GET 405, out-of-thread refusal); e2e through startPlatform + startSlackRouter with a fake claude that reads --mcp-config and calls the tool: mention -> Block Kit chat.postMessage in C01LISTED/1.1 with the exact blocks; reply naming C02OTHER -> isError, no post; plain console session -> no MCP config.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: daemon vitest 94 files 933 passed 3 skipped; root pnpm typecheck and lint pass.
UNVERIFIED (human test): a logged-in claude CLI actually loads the inline --mcp-config http server and runs the allowed tool without a prompt, incl. in plan mode (read-only scope); Codex runs it without an approval prompt; real Slack accepts the blocks. A persona whose front matter sets tools: must list mcp__candy_mountain_slack__post_blocks to see the tool.
close_reason: Daemon-hosted Streamable HTTP MCP host + post_blocks tool scoped to the session's Slack thread; registered per launch for Claude and Codex; 933 tests, root lint+typecheck pass

title: Parse the structured handoff block from a final message
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Every Slack bot is asked to end a turn with a fenced handoff block, and the platform renders it rather than trusting the model to write Block Kit. Write a pure parser: given the final assistant message, find the handoff block, parse its fields, validate the outcome value, normalise "none" to empty, and return either the parsed handoff or a reason it was missing or malformed. Tolerate surrounding prose and minor whitespace differences.

Shared names: The structured handoff format is fixed: a fenced code block whose info string is `handoff`, containing one `key: value` line per field with keys `outcome` (one of done, partial, blocked), `summary` (one line), `pull_request` (URL or none), `issues` (comma-separated issue ids or none), and `follow_ups` (semicolon-separated or none).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover a well-formed block, a block with extra prose around it, a missing block, an unknown outcome, and missing optional fields.
notes: Exports from packages/shared/src/handoff.ts (re-exported in index.ts): HANDOFF_OUTCOMES ['done','partial','blocked'], types HandoffOutcome, Handoff {outcome, summary, pullRequest: string|null, issues: string[], followUps: string[]}, HandoffFailureReason, HandoffParseResult, parseHandoff(message). Result: {ok:true, handoff} | {ok:false, reason:'missing'|'malformed'|'unknown_outcome'|'missing_outcome'|'missing_summary', message}. Rules: fenced block (backtick or tilde, indent ok) with info string exactly 'handoff' (case-insens); last such block wins; CRLF/indent/trailing ws tolerated; keys and outcome case-insensitive; unknown keys ignored; blank lines ignored; non key:value line or unclosed fence => malformed; 'none' (any case) or empty => null for pull_request, [] for lists; issues split on comma, follow_ups on semicolon, trimmed; absent optional fields default empty; outcome and summary required (summary 'none' counts as missing).
close_reason: parseHandoff in packages/shared with 14 tests; lint green

title: Render the handoff as a Block Kit card and record the activity event
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

At the end of a bot turn in Slack, run the handoff parser on the final message. When it parses, post a Block Kit card with outcome, summary, pull request link, issues touched (each as the short id) and follow-ups, plus a "mark done" button that closes the session like the "done" verb; when it is missing or malformed, post the raw final text instead. In both cases append a `bot.handoff` activity event to the project with the summary (or first line), the pull request link if any, the issue ids, and a link to the thread in the chat panel.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.
acceptance_criteria: A completed bot turn shows the card with summary, PR link and issue id; a turn without a block posts the raw text; the Overview feed shows the handoff event with the link; mark done releases the worktree.
notes:
Slack handoff card + bot.handoff activity (7.6). How-to: apps/daemon/README.md '## Slack handoffs'. No migration, no new tables.

FILES: apps/daemon/src/slack/handoffs.ts (startSlackHandoffs({db, slack, botSessions, sessions}, {fetch?, now?, log?}) -> {onTurnEnd, idle, close}), src/slack/handoff-message.ts (slackHandoffMessage({handoff, prose, turnId, closed:{by}|null}) -> {text, blocks}; SLACK_HANDOFF_DONE_ACTION='cm-handoff:done'; issueShortId = after last '-', upper-cased, same as web issuesShortId), src/slack/done.ts (slackDoneText, closeSlackThreadSession({db, botSessions}, thread, {at, signal}) -> text|null; router done() now uses it, behaviour unchanged), src/platform.ts (platform.slackHandoffs, PlatformOptions.slackHandoffs; router onTurnEnd = handoffs.onTurnEnd then PlatformOptions.slackRouter.onTurnEnd), packages/shared/src/handoff.ts gained stripHandoff(message) (removes the last handoff block; parser refactored to findHandoffBlock, behaviour same). BEHAVIOUR: onTurnEnd: cancelled -> nothing. completed + parseHandoff ok -> chat.update message.ts with {text, blocks} (markdown block = turn text minus handoff block, divider, outcome+summary section, fields PR (<url|#n>) + issue short ids, follow-ups bullets, actions button value=turnId with confirm); message null -> chat.postMessage claimed first in platform_meta 'slack-handoff:<turnId>'. Missing/malformed -> message untouched (it already is the raw text). Completed or failed -> one bot.handoff event, deduped on json_extract(payload,'$.turnId'): title '<bot name>: <summary | first non-fence line of the last agent message after the last tool step>' (<=200), link = chat.getPermalink of the card message (fallback /p/<slug>/bots), payload {turnId, botId, sessionId, slackThreadId, channel, threadTs, slackUrl, turnOutcome, outcome, summary, pullRequest, issueIds, followUps}. LINK DECISION: Slack bot sessions have no chat_threads row (chat threads are per web actor; Slack actor is slack:<member>), so there is no chat-panel thread to link; the Slack permalink is the closest. Activity.vue NuxtLink handles the external URL.
MARK DONE: subscribe kinds ['interactive'], block_actions with action_id cm-handoff:done; turn -> thread; botId and channel must match; presser and opener pass mayMemberTalkToBot; if thread open and on the turn's session -> closeSlackThreadSession (same as 'done' reply: cancels running turn, releases worktree only when pushed) + posts the same 'Done. ...' text, card re-rendered from the session log with 'Marked done by <@U>'; otherwise (closed, new session, redelivery) only re-render 'The session is closed.'
