title: Answer permission requests and questions from Slack with buttons and text
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Decisions must be answerable where the human is. When a bot session raises a pending decision, post a message in the Slack thread with one button per offered option labelled by kind and a short decision id, and accept text replies as verbs (yes, no, choose with a number, answer with free text, each followed by the id). "Always allow" appears only when the agent proposed a rule. Answers go through the same pending-decision model as the chat panel, so a decision answered in Slack disappears from the panel and vice versa, and the first answer wins. Update the Slack message to show the outcome, including timeout.
acceptance_criteria: A permission prompt posts buttons; pressing Allow continues the tool and the card in the chat panel shows answered; answering from the panel updates the Slack message; a text verb works; a timed-out decision shows refused.
notes:
Implemented (no tables, no migration). Files: apps/daemon/src/slack/decision-message.ts (Block Kit rendering, choice list, text-verb parser, outcome wording), apps/daemon/src/slack/decisions.ts (startSlackDecisions), wired in apps/daemon/src/platform.ts (startSlackDecisions before startSlackRouter; router gets interceptReply), tests in apps/daemon/src/slack/decisions.test.ts.
Flow: startSlackDecisions observes sessions.observe; on decision_opened for a session that maps to an open slack_threads row (findSlackThreadBySession) it posts the card in the thread; on decision_answered/decision_expired it chat.update's the card with the outcome (same wording as the panel card, 'Refused' on timeout). Message ref {botId, channel, ts} is kept in memory and in platform_meta key 'slack-decision:<decisionId>' (JSON), deleted once settled; on start, recover() re-renders cards whose decision settled/died while the daemon was down.
Answers go through DecisionService.answer with surface 'slack', actorId slackActorId(member) = 'slack:<member>'; first answer wins (DecisionError -> card re-rendered for button presses, 'Could not answer <id>: ...' posted for text). Membership: replier and thread opener must both pass mayMemberTalkToBot.
Text verbs: router option interceptReply(event, ref, plainText) => Promise|null runs for thread replies before 'done' and before the per-thread queue (the queued turn is waiting on the answer). Returning null passes the reply on as a normal prompt. Verbs: yes <id>, no <id> [reason], choose <id> <n> (or choose <n> <id>), answer <id> <text> (multi-field: 'Title: value' per line). Short id = first 6 hex of the decision UUID. Successful text answer gets a white_check_mark reaction.
Buttons: action_id 'cm-decision:<n>', value '<decisionId>:<n>', block_id 'cm-decision:<decisionId>'; n indexes slackDecisionChoices(decision) so buttons and 'choose' agree. allow_always appears only when the decision carries an allow_always option (i.e. the agent proposed a rule).
HOW TO ADD ANOTHER block_actions HANDLER (e.g. 7.6 'mark done' on a handoff card): there is no central interaction router. Each feature subscribes on its own: slack.subscribe(listener, { kinds: ['interactive'] }) (SlackConnections event bus, decision 46), checks event.interaction.type === 'block_actions', and handles only actions whose actionId starts with its own prefix (pick a new one, e.g. 'cm-handoff:'), ignoring the rest; other prefixes belong to other handlers. The envelope is already acked by socket.ts before emit. Use event.botId + interaction.channelId/messageTs/threadTs/userId; find the thread with findSlackThread(db, {botId, channelId, threadTs}) and apply the same mayMemberTalkToBot check. Update the card with client.call('chat.update', {channel, ts, text, blocks}) from slack.web(botId).client. Slack may redeliver an envelope, so make the handler idempotent. Start it in platform.ts next to startSlackDecisions and close it in close().
close_reason: Slack decision cards, buttons and text verbs via DecisionService; tests green (912 passed)

title: Route Slack mentions and replies to bot sessions with membership, resume and dedup
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A mention starts work; replies continue it. Build the router: a top-level mention of a bot, in a channel it answers in (anywhere, or one of its listed channel ids), by a roster member whose scope covers the bot, creates a thread-to-session mapping (bot, channel, thread timestamp, session, member) and starts a bot session with the Slack thread as holder, passing the request text wrapped as context on the first turn (who asked, where, and the message). Replies in a mapped thread continue the session; after a daemon restart the first reply resumes it. Non-members and non-listed channels get silence. A thread whose member was removed from the roster stops being answered. The word "done" alone in the thread closes the session and releases the worktree. Record every delivered Slack event id so a retried event is never processed twice. Post the agent's final text to the thread (replaced by streaming in separate work). Add an acknowledging reaction on receipt.
acceptance_criteria: A roster mention in a listed channel starts a session and a worktree; a reply continues it; a mention from a non-member or non-listed channel gets no reply; a replayed event is ignored; after restart a reply resumes the same session; "done" releases the worktree; tests cover gating and dedup.
notes:
Slack routing decisions (7.3 streaming, 7.4 decisions, 7.6 handoff card, 7.7 MCP tool build on these). How-to in apps/daemon/README.md '## Slack routing'.

FILES: apps/daemon/src/slack/{router.ts (startSlackRouter), threads.ts (slack_threads/slack_deliveries store), post.ts (postToSlackThread, splitSlackText, addSlackReaction, slackTextToPlain, mentions), router.test.ts (7 tests), index.ts (re-exports)}; src/db/schema/slack-threads.ts (+ export in schema/index.ts); src/team/service.ts gained findTeamMemberBySlackId(db, projectId, slackMemberId); src/platform.ts wires platform.slackRouter = startSlackRouter({ db, slack, botSessions, sessions }, PlatformOptions.slackRouter) after platform.slack and closes it first in close(). No REST routes, no shared types added.

MIGRATION: drizzle/0018_slack_threads.sql (journal idx 18, tag 0018_slack_threads, single entry; 0000-0017 untouched). TABLES: slack_threads (id uuid PK, project_id FK cascade, bot_id FK bots cascade, team_id nullable, channel_id, thread_ts, session_id FK agent_sessions cascade, slack_member_id = the opener, state 'open'|'closed' default open, turn_count, created_at, updated_at, closed_at; UNIQUE (bot_id, channel_id, thread_ts); index session_id). slack_deliveries (bot_id, event_id, channel_id, ts, received_at; PK (bot_id, event_id); UNIQUE (bot_id, channel_id, ts) because a mention inside a thread arrives as app_mention AND message with different event ids). claimSlackDelivery = insert onConflictDoNothing, changes>0; claimed BEFORE any work (at-most-once: a crash mid-processing drops that message rather than repeating it; same tradeoff as notifications).

ROUTING RULES (router.ts handle()): subscribes kinds app_mention+message on platform.slack. Drop: fromSelf, any subtype (edits/joins/bot_message), no user. Claim delivery; duplicate -> stop. isReply = threadTs set and != ts. Top-level counts only when mentioned (kind app_mention or '<@botUserId>' in text); DMs and unmentioned top-level messages are silence. MENTION: bots row answersIn ({anywhere:true} | channels includes channel) AND mayMemberTalkToBot(projectId, user, botId) else silence; touchMemberActivity; reactions.add 'eyes' (SlackRouterOptions.acknowledgeReaction; failure logged, needs reactions:write); botSessions.start({ botId, holder: { kind:'slack', id: slackThreadHolderId = '<botId>:<channel>:<thread_ts>' }, actorId: 'slack:<memberId>' }); BotStartError -> its message posted to the thread; else insertSlackThread then the turn. REPLY: findSlackThread(bot, channel, thread_ts) else silence; closed thread + no mention -> silence (a mention in a closed thread starts fresh: state open + new session id via reopenSlackThread); admitted() = replier passes mayMemberTalkToBot AND the opener (slack_member_id) still does (removed member -> thread stops); touch; react; botSessions.prompt(row.session_id, text); BotStartError worktree_released or SessionError not_found -> start fresh on the same holder and repoint the row; other BotStartError/SessionError (e.g. session_busy) -> message posted. Per-thread FIFO queue (enqueue keyed by holder id) so a reply never overtakes the mention's worktree cut. DONE: isDoneMessage = /^\s*[*_`~]*done[*_`~.!]*\s*$/i on the plain text of a reply; bypasses the queue; closeSlackThread then botSessions.closeSession(sessionId) (cancels a running turn, safe-rule release); posts 'Done. The worktree was released; branch X is kept.' | 'Done. The session is closed, but the worktree was kept because it holds work that is not on origin: <unpushedReason>. Branch X.' | 'Done. The session is closed.' A cancelled turn posts no text. RESUME after restart: nothing in memory; the row's session_id -> botSessions.prompt resumes in the same worktree (tested).

CONTEXT WRAPPER (slackRequestText): first turn = 'A request arrived from Slack. Work it in this worktree and reply as if answering in that thread: your final message is posted there as is.' + blank line + '<slack-request>\nfrom: <displayName> (<memberId>)\nchannel: <C..>\nthread: <ts>\nmessage:\n<text>\n</slack-request>'; replies = same block tagged <slack-reply> with no preamble. Text via slackTextToPlain: bot mention stripped, <url|label> -> 'label (url)', <url> -> url, &/</> decoded, trimmed.

FINAL TEXT: collectTurn subscribes sessions.subscribe(sessionId) before prompt, concatenates text rows role agent, settles on turn_end (or error phase start/connection, auth_required, unexpected exited -> posts 'The bot could not finish: ...'; sessions.signal/router abort -> nothing). Posted via client.call chat.postMessage with thread_ts in <=3900-char pieces (splitSlackText on newlines). SlackOperations.postMessage has no thread_ts, hence post.ts.

SEAMS: 7.3 streaming replaces turn()'s collectTurn+post (same place; persist the stream ts in slack_threads or a new column for exactly-once completion; a restart mid-turn today loses the post - text stays in the session log). 7.4 decisions: subscribe kinds ['interactive'] separately (router ignores interactive/slash); findSlackThreadBySession(db, sessionId) gives channel/thread_ts to post buttons; who pressed = interaction.userId -> findTeamMemberBySlackId / mayMemberTalkToBot; answer via platform.decisions.answer(..., surface 'slack', actorId slackActorId(user)). 7.6 handoff card: parse outcome.text in turn() before post, post blocks via client.call chat.postMessage { channel, thread_ts, blocks, text }; emit bot.handoff activity there. 7.7 MCP tool: resolve the thread from the session id with findSlackThreadBySession; the holder id parses as botId:channel:thread_ts. Test seam: startSlackRouter needs only { subscribe, web } so tests use createSlackEventBus() + createSlackClient('xoxb-test', { fetch: recording fetch }) (see fakeTransport in router.test.ts), plus the temp git repo + fake claude + startPlatform pattern from bot-threads.test.ts.

TESTS router.test.ts: e2e mention -> slack_threads row, session posture.bot.holder, actorId slack:U0JACK, active lease under paths.worktrees, eyes reaction, posted <slack-request> text with entities decoded and mention gone, last_active_at stamped; replay (same event id) and the sibling message event (same channel/ts) ignored; reply continues the same session (2 prompt rows, turn_count 2, <slack-reply>); silence for non-member, non-listed channel, unmentioned top-level, self, message_changed, non-member reply; removed member stops the thread, re-added resumes; ' Done. ' closes, lease released, dir gone, main checkout on main; plain reply after done ignored; mention after done -> new session + new active worktree. Unpushed: untracked file + done -> row closed, lease active with unpushedWork, dir kept, message names the reason. Restart: close platform, boot same data dir/key, new router+bus, reply -> same session id, cwd = lease path, echo posted. Unit: isDoneMessage, slackTextToPlain, slackRequestText, splitSlackText.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (133 files, 1267 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass. UNVERIFIED: no Slack tokens here (none created), so a live Socket Mode mention, the real event shapes for app_mention vs message in threads, reactions:write / chat:write scopes and the 3,900-char split are from docs; the agent side ran against the claude fixture, not a logged-in CLI.
close_reason: Slack router with slack_threads/slack_deliveries (0018), roster/channel gating, dedup, resume, done-close; gates green

title: Stream progress into the Slack thread with exactly-once completion
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Watching a bot work in Slack is the point. Replace the final-text post with streaming: where the Slack workspace supports native streaming, open a stream on the first text, append throttled text, add tool calls as summarised timeline updates, and stop the stream at the end of the turn; otherwise post one progress message and edit it in place with throttled updates. Persist the stream or message identity per turn so that after a daemon restart an interrupted turn is finished exactly once (the resumed turn continues the same message, never a second one).
acceptance_criteria: A turn shows live text and tool summaries in the thread; restarting the daemon mid-turn ends with exactly one completed message; the fallback path works when native streaming is unavailable; tests cover the persistence.
notes:
Slack turn progress (7.3). How-to: apps/daemon/README.md '## Slack turn progress'.

FILES: src/slack/progress.ts (createSlackProgress, SLACK_STREAM_TEXT_MAX 11500, SLACK_STREAM_MAX_AGE_MS 9min), src/slack/turns.ts (slack_turns store: openSlackTurn, listOpenSlackTurns = open|finished, finishSlackTurn, completeSlackTurn, latestSlackTurn, slackTurnMessage), src/slack/router.ts (turn/follow/settle/end/recover), src/db/schema/slack-threads.ts (slackTurns; SlackTurnState now 'open'|'finished'|'completed', type-only, no SQL change), tests src/slack/progress.test.ts (7 unit) + src/slack/streaming.test.ts (5 e2e: native stream w/ task_update timeline, fallback edit-in-place + per-bot refusal memory, restart mid-turn -> resumed into same stream exactly once, restart after stream expired -> chat.update same ts, finished-turn hook re-run). MIGRATION: 0020_slack_turns only; no 0021.

BEHAVIOUR: one message per turn. Native: chat.startStream (thread_ts, recipient_user_id = member who sent the turn's message, recipient_team_id, chunks markdown_text + task_update {id: toolCallId, title, status}) -> chat.appendStream -> chat.stopStream. startStream slack_error other than channel/token errors => fallback chat.postMessage + throttled chat.update (remembered per bot in memory). Stream >9 min or >11.5k chars, or message_not_in_streaming_state => stopStream (best effort) + continue as chat.update of the SAME ts (mode recorded as message). stopped_by_user => no more calls that turn. Throttle SlackRouterOptions.streamIntervalMs (default 1000).

EXACTLY-ONCE: slack_turns row written at the prompt row; message_ts/mode recorded the moment Slack returns the ts; sent_seq after each successful call. A message is only created while message_ts is null. On start the router queues recover() per thread before new events: turn_end in log -> end message from log; still running -> one resume prompt (<slack-resume>, slackResumeText) into the same message (resumes counted; second interruption ends with note); closed/replaced session -> ended as cancelled.

FOR 7.6 (handoff card): the turn completes in exactly one place, end(turnEnd) in router.ts, called from settle() after progress.finish() (message final, row state 'finished') and from recover() for finished rows. Hook = SlackRouterOptions.onTurnEnd(end: SlackTurnEnd { thread, sessionId, turnId, text (agent text of the turn), outcome completed|cancelled|failed, error, message: SlackTurnMessage|null {channel, threadTs, ts, mode}, client }). Row -> 'completed' after the hook returns or throws (not when the router is aborted), so it is AT LEAST ONCE: make it idempotent - preferably chat.update message.ts with {text, blocks} (replaces the streamed text; for message mode the content is plain text), or record what was posted keyed by turnId (platform_meta) before/after posting. After a restart, error is null and outcome derives from the log. Wire it in platform.ts via startSlackRouter(..., slackRouterOptions) (onTurnEnd is already plumbed through PlatformOptions.slackRouter); message null means the turn posted nothing (e.g. cancelled with no output).

UNVERIFIED (no Slack tokens): real chat.startStream/appendStream/stopStream behaviour with chunks in a thread, whether chat.update text replaces a streamed message's chunk content, the 10-min/12k limits (from docs.slack.dev). The fixture-driven tests use a filter around the claude fixture (slow/hang scenarios) written in streaming.test.ts.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: daemon vitest 93 files / 925 passed / 3 skipped; daemon tsc clean; eslint apps/daemon clean.
close_reason: Native stream + edit-in-place fallback, per-turn persistence, exactly-once completion via end()/onTurnEnd; 925 tests pass

title: Manage one Socket Mode connection per active bot
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Slack must work from a laptop with no public URL. Build a connection manager in the daemon: for every bot whose Slack bot token and app-level token are set, open a Socket Mode connection using those secrets, reconnect with backoff on failure, and track connection state (connecting, connected, disconnected with reason) exposed on the bot's REST representation. Refuse to start a bot with missing keys and report it rather than crashing. Start connections on daemon boot and when a bot's keys change; stop them when a bot is deleted or its keys removed. Deliver received events (mentions, thread messages, interactive actions) to a dispatcher that other work implements; acknowledge events promptly. Also expose a Slack Web API client per bot for posting.
acceptance_criteria: Adding valid keys shows the bot connected within seconds; invalid keys show disconnected with the reason; removing keys closes the connection; a dropped network reconnects; tests mock the Slack client.
notes:
Slack Socket Mode decisions (7.2, 7.3, 7.4, 7.7, 7.8, 10.4 depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Slack connections'.

FILES: apps/daemon/src/slack/{events.ts, socket.ts, manager.ts, routes.ts, index.ts, fake-socket-mode.ts (test support), slack.test.ts}; packages/shared/src/bot-slack.ts (exported from index). One-line wiring: platform.ts (platform.slack, PlatformOptions.slack, close), app.ts (AppDeps.slack + route mount), index.ts (createApp slack: platform.slack). No migration.

DEPENDENCY: hand-written Socket Mode client over ws@^8.22.0 (+ @types/ws dev), both already in the lockfile. Not @slack/socket-mode 3.1.0: it pulls @slack/web-api 8 (axios, p-queue, p-retry, form-data), a second Web API client next to plugins/slack's fetch client, and its own reconnect/logging state machine; the protocol is small (apps.connections.open -> WebSocket -> hello -> ack {envelope_id}) and owning it gives exact status reasons, backoff and testability. Uses ws (not Node's global WebSocket) so the client can send pings and detect a silently dead network.

WHICH BOTS: polled, not hooked (same rationale as the issue watcher): every SLACK_RECONCILE_MS=2000 (unref'd) plus platform.slack.reconcile() and on status() for an unknown id. Eligible = project not archived AND computeBotStatus(...) === 'active' computed locally with baseBranchProblem null (no Git host call, so a GitHub outage never drops Slack) AND both tokens readable. Token change (sha256 fingerprint of app+bot token) restarts that bot's connection; ineligible/deleted bot closes it. Exactly one connection per bot.

CONNECTION (socket.ts openSocketModeConnection): each attempt auth.test with the bot token (identity + validates it) then apps.connections.open with the app token, both via createSlackClient(token, {fetch, signal}); connected on 'hello'. Every envelope with envelope_id is acked ({envelope_id}) BEFORE dispatch; ack carries no payload (interactive/slash responses go via Web API/response_url). Reconnect policy: 'disconnect' envelope (refresh_requested/too_many...) -> reconnect immediately; 'warning' ignored (Slack closes itself); link_disabled -> error w/ backoff. Socket close / network error / no hello in 15s / ping (every 30s) unanswered 10s -> backoff 1s doubling to 60s, +-20% jitter, reset after a hello; HTTP 429 honours Retry-After; Slack token errors (invalid_auth, not_authed, token_revoked, token_expired, account_inactive, not_allowed_token_type, missing_scope) -> invalid_token, retry every 5 min (a new token reconnects at next poll). All tunable via SocketModeOptions (PlatformOptions.slack.socket).

BUS API (platform.slack): subscribe(listener, { botId?, kinds? }) -> unsubscribe. Listener (event: SlackBotEvent) => void|Promise; throws/rejections are logged, never affect other listeners or the ack. SlackBotEvent common fields: botId (Candy Mountain bot), projectId, envelopeId, retryAttempt (0 first delivery), retryReason|null, receivedAt ISO, botUserId (bot's Slack user from auth.test, for stripping <@U..> and ignoring self). kinds:
 - 'app_mention' | 'message': eventId (dedup key for 7.2), teamId|null, fromSelf (user===bot user or bot_id===bot's bot id), event { channel, channelType|null, user|null, senderBotId|null, subtype|null, text, ts, threadTs|null, raw }.
 - 'slash': command { command, text, userId, channelId, teamId|null, responseUrl|null, triggerId|null, raw }.
 - 'interactive': interaction { type ('block_actions', 'view_submission', ...), userId|null, channelId|null, messageTs|null, threadTs|null, actions [{actionId, blockId|null, type, value|null}], responseUrl|null, triggerId|null, raw }.
 Other events_api types (reactions etc.) and malformed envelopes are acked and dropped. NOTE for 7.2: a mention inside a thread also arrives as a separate 'message' event with a different eventId if the app subscribes to message.* events; dedupe on (channel, ts) as well as eventId, and skip fromSelf.
WEB: platform.slack.web(botId, options?) -> { client: createSlackClient(botToken), operations: createSlackOperations({}, botToken) } | null when no bot token; reads the token per call. Throws SecretsLockedError if locked.

STATUS: platform.slack.status(botId) -> BotSlackConnection (shared): { state: 'connected'|'connecting'|'disconnected', reason|null, reasonCode: 'missing_keys'|'inactive'|'archived'|'secrets_locked'|'invalid_token'|'error'|'stopped'|null, since ISO (last state/reason change), retryAt ISO|null, identity {teamId, team, userId, user}|null }. Reasons: missing_keys 'Slack app-level token is not set.' / 'Slack bot token and Slack app-level token are not set.'; inactive 'The bot is not active: <warnings>.'; invalid_token 'Slack rejected the app-level token: invalid_auth (it is invalid or has been revoked).' (or 'bot token'); error e.g. 'Could not reach Slack: fetch failed', 'Slack stopped answering pings.'.
ROUTE: GET /projects/:slug/bots/:id/slack (admin only, requireAdmin) -> BotSlackConnectionResponse { connection }; 404 not_found for unknown slug or a bot of another project; 403 non-admin. Path helper botSlackConnectionPath(slug, id) in @candy-mountain/shared. Mounted in app.ts only when AppDeps.slack is given (index.ts passes platform.slack). Not added to the Bot REST representation (would mean editing bots.ts/Bot type); 7.8 fetches this route per card.
7.8 UI: in apps/web/layers/bots/components/SlackConnection.vue fetch GET /api + botSlackConnectionPath(slug, bot.id) on an interval while mounted (e.g. 5s; status changes within one 2s poll); render reasonCode 'missing_keys' as 'Not configured', 'connected' with identity.team/@identity.user, 'connecting', 'disconnected' with reason (+ retryAt countdown when set).

CLOSE: platform.close() -> void slack.close() (clears the poll, closes every socket with 1000, terminates after 1s); status then reports 'stopped'.

TESTS: src/slack/slack.test.ts (7) against fake-socket-mode.ts: a local ws WebSocketServer (hello on connect, records acks, autoPong off so a link can go silent) + an injected fetch for auth.test/apps.connections.open; never real Slack. Covers inactive->active opens exactly one link, missing app key closes it, re-adding reconnects, archived project closes; acks for all 5 envelopes + typed app_mention/message(fromSelf)/interactive/slash events, botId filter, throwing listener isolated; reconnect after disconnect refresh_requested, after a dropped socket, after unanswered pings, and after Slack is unreachable (status error + retryAt); invalid app/bot token reasons and immediate connect after replacing the token; close() ends all links and reports stopped; web(); route 200/404/404/403 and no token in body.
VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (117 files, 1106 passed, 3 skipped), build pass. First full test run failed only src/db/schema.test.ts (DROP TABLE uptime_monitors: another agent's in-flight 0015 migration); passed on rerun. First build hit another agent's Nuxt build lock; passed on rerun. Built daemon booted with throwaway data dir, GET /projects/nope/bots/x/slack -> 404 not_found, SIGTERM exits 0.
close_reason: Socket Mode manager per active bot over ws, reconnect, event bus, status route; 7 tests

title: Show configured bots in the chat rail and run them from the panel
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack tests a bot locally before giving it Slack keys. Make each bot with a usable status (active, or warnings that only concern Slack keys) appear as an agent in the registry's chat agent list for the project, and have threads started with a bot agent use the bot session starter with the thread as holder instead of a plain project-checkout session. The chat rail needs no change beyond rendering what the registry returns; the panel shows the worktree path and branch at the top of a bot thread. Closing or archiving the thread releases the worktree.
acceptance_criteria: A bot appears in the rail; a thread with it asks it to fix a trivial issue by id, an edit prompts for confirmation, a push asks first, and after closing the thread the worktree is reclaimed only once the work is pushed; a thread with a plain Claude Code agent still uses the project checkout.
notes:
Bots in the chat rail decisions (7.x Slack, 10.8, any future project-sourced agent build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md end of '## Chat threads' (and the console paragraph of '## Bot sessions').

AGENT ID: 'bot:<botId>'. Shared (bot-sessions.ts): BOTS_CAPABILITY_ID='bots', BOT_AGENT_ID_PREFIX, botAgentId(botId), botIdOfAgent(agentId)->string|null. botAgentId moved from daemon bot-sessions/service to shared (daemon re-export removed).

REGISTRY RULE: computeRegistry adds one RegistryAgent per project bot { id: bot:<id>, capabilityId 'bots', label = bot name, description '<Family> bot, <write scope>, working in its own worktree.', family, avatar 'i-lucide-bot', kind: 'bot', bot: { id, writeScope, baseBranch|null } } (RegistryAgent gained optional kind/bot; RegistryAgentBot). Conditions: (1) bot usable = botUsableWithoutSlack (bots/status.ts): computeBotStatus with both Slack keys treated as set === 'active', i.e. family plugin stored healthy + persona verified; read synchronously by listProjectBotRefs(deps, projectId) in bots/bots.ts (no host call; a blank base branch is NOT resolved here, start fails with repository_not_configured if unreadable); RegistryInput.bots = usable refs (load.ts). (2) actor has chat on 'bots' (held + rung.chat + ready). RUNG SEMANTICS: bots ladder unchanged in names (none -> manage); manage now has chat: true ('...and run them from the chat rail'); no chat-only rung. CapabilityManifest gained projectAgents?: boolean (bots sets it) so assertCapability allows a chat rung with no declared agents. (3) actor has chat on the bot family's capability (first capability whose agent has that family: chat-claude-code / chat-codex), because the session SSE/decisions routes gate on it.

THREADS (src/threads): ChatAgent gained botId?; findThreadAgent(db, capabilities, projectId, agentId) resolves bot:<id> (bot of this project, else not_found) or a manifest agent; projectBotAgents(db, projectId) lists every bot (any status) for the unfiltered thread list. Routes gate with checkAgent = checkChat on agent.capabilityId AND, for bots, on familyCapability(family) (no longer requireCapability). POST /threads {agentId: bot:<id>} -> botSessions.start({ botId, holder: { kind: 'console', id: <new uuid> }, actorId, signal }) (worktree, persona, posture), then title reset to the given title or null so the first prompt names it; model/effort -> 400 invalid_request (create and PATCH); options route -> empty lists. ThreadService.create is now async. Prompt on a bot session -> botSessions.prompt (lease touch); on BotStartError worktree_released (closed thread) it starts a fresh session+worktree on the same thread (switchThreadSession, sessions history grows) and prompts that. BotStartError mapped in thread routes onError ({ code: reason }). ADOPT: watches map now records sessionId; list()/get() adopt any thread whose current session is not watched (threads created by POST /bots/:id/sessions, switched sessions, restart), reconciling working without setting unread. ThreadServiceOptions.bots (app.ts passes deps.botSessions). BotSessionService gained lease(sessionId) (includes released leases).

CLOSE ROUTE: POST /projects/:slug/threads/:id/close (shared threadClosePath) -> ChatThreadCloseResponse { thread, session, sessions, bot, released, keptUnpushed }; calls botSessions.closeSession(currentSessionId) (cancels a turn, safe-rule release), marks read; plain-agent thread -> 422 unsupported_agent. Every bot thread response (GET/POST/PATCH/close) carries bot: ChatThreadBot { botId, name, worktreePath, branch, baseBranch, worktree: 'active'|'released'|'none', keptUnpushed, unpushedReason }. No migration (posture JSON + existing lease columns).

UI (layers/chat): rail unchanged (bot agents render from registry.agents as chat-rail-entry-bot:<id>). New ChatBotWorktree (components/BotWorktree.vue, data-testid chat-bot-worktree/-branch/-path/-close/-unpushed/-released) mounted at the top of a thread in AgentPanel when useChatThread().bot is set: branch + worktree path (mono, truncated, title=full), 'Close thread' button while active, warning UAlert 'Unpushed work kept' with the reason while keptUnpushed, muted 'Worktree released; the branch is kept. Your next prompt starts a fresh worktree.' once released, toast on release. useChatThreads gained close(threadId); useChatThread gained bot. AgentPanel.send follows a changed session id after a prompt (remembers old events, refreshes the thread).

FOR 7.x: same session service; Slack does not use thread routes. If a Slack surface wants a chat-rail view of a Slack-held session it would need a thread row (holder kind slack has none). 10.8/platform agent start_chat does not know bot:<id> agents (findChatAgent path) - extend with findThreadAgent if bots should be startable from the platform agent.

TESTS src/threads/bot-threads.test.ts (4): registry lists a verified bot without Slack keys with the exact agent shape; unverified bot absent; developer with defaults sees it, bots none -> absent + create 403, chat-claude-code none -> absent + 403; unknown bot 404. E2E (temp git repo + bare origin, persona committed, stubHosts, fake claude): model refused, options empty, create -> worktree branch cm/bot/ana-bot/<session>, cwd = worktree, write-confirm flags --permission-mode default with no git push allow, launch argv has --agent ana, unread after turn, 'permission' prompt opens a decision while working, plain claude-code thread cwd = sourcePath(project) and close 422; close with untracked file -> keptUnpushed (uncommitted), committed-not-pushed -> kept (not on origin), pushed -> released, dir gone, main checkout status/branch unchanged; next prompt -> new session + new worktree, 2 sessions. Adopt: thread started via POST /bots/:id/sessions served by GET thread with bot info, unread after a session-route prompt; restart (same data dir/key) -> thread idle, prompt via thread resumes same session in worktree.
VERIFIED 2026-10-28: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (132 files, 1257 passed, 3 skipped), build pass. Live: built daemon (dist) on 127.0.0.1:10140 with node --import GitHub fetch stub, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR + random CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth; built web .output copy on :10141. Temp repo (bare origin, .claude/agents/ana.md, bd init --stealth, issue wt-ay3), real persona check through the stub -> verified, status warnings = Slack keys only; plugin health set in sqlite. Headless Chromium (playwright-core, chromium-1217): bot + Claude Code in rail; bot panel -> new thread 'Fix wt-ay3' streams echo; header shows branch + worktree path; session cwd = worktree, posture --permission-mode default, no push allow, --agent ana; 'permission' prompt -> decision card, denied; untracked file -> Close thread -> 'Unpushed work kept 1 uncommitted change(s)' and dir kept; commit+push -> Close -> released note + toast, dir gone, branch kept; plain claude-code thread cwd = clone; 390px no overflow; zero console errors; prompt on released thread -> 2nd session, new active worktree. Processes stopped.
UNVERIFIED (needs a real logged-in claude CLI): the actual edit-confirmation and push-asks prompts from a real model; asserted via the launched posture flags (--permission-mode default; push not pre-allowed so it asks like any Bash) and a fixture permission request rendered as a decision card.
close_reason: Bots appear in the chat rail as bot:<id> agents; threads run bot sessions in worktrees with close route; gates green

notes:
Team page decisions (all in apps/web/layers/team).
