title: Run a bot session end to end: worktree, persona, posture, instructions, decisions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

This is the real bot path, used by the console and later by Slack. Build the bot session starter in the daemon: given a bot and a holder (console thread or Slack thread), run the persona check, acquire or resume the worktree lease for the holder, compute the posture for the bot's family and scope, compose the surface instructions, apply the environment that routes `bd` to the main checkout's database, and start or resume a session through the existing session layer with the worktree as working directory and the project's plugin config home. Decisions flow through the existing pending-decision model. Closing the holder releases the lease under the safe-reclaim rule. Record failures (persona missing, worktree cap, plugin unhealthy) as typed reasons the caller can show.
acceptance_criteria: Starting a bot session creates a worktree on a new branch and a session whose working directory is that worktree; `bd create` by the agent lands in the main checkout list; the main checkout's git status is untouched; a persona-missing bot fails to start with that reason; closing releases the lease.
notes:
Bot session starter decisions (6.14 chat rail, 7.2 Slack routing, 7.7 MCP tool build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Bot sessions'.
MODULE apps/daemon/src/bot-sessions/ (errors.ts, service.ts, routes.ts, index.ts, bot-sessions.test.ts, 6 tests). Platform: platform.botSessions = createBotSessionService({ db, paths, pluginTypes, secrets, secretsReader, sessions, worktrees }); platform.close() calls botSessions.stop() before sessions.close(). App: createApp({ botSessions }) mounts botSessionRoutes on /projects; index.ts passes platform.botSessions. NO migration.
API: botSessions.start({ botId, holder, actorId, signal? }) -> { bot, session, lease (WorktreeLease), thread (ChatThread|null), resumed, neutralised, warnings }. HOLDER MODEL: holder = { kind: 'console', id: <chat thread id> } | { kind: 'slack', id: <thread key 7.2 chooses, e.g. channel:thread_ts> } (shared BotSessionHolder, BOT_SESSION_HOLDER_KINDS). The worktree lease holder stays 6.1's { kind: 'session', id: sessionId } with branch botBranchName(bot.name, sessionId); the session id is drawn before acquire (new CreateSessionInput.id) so the lease is keyed on it. Holder -> session is persisted in the session posture JSON: posture.bot = { id, name, holder }; found with json_extract on agent_sessions.posture (newest first). Resume rule: start() with a holder that already has a session whose lease worktrees.resume() still returns -> that session + lease (resumed: true), no persona re-check; a released/reclaimed lease -> a NEW session and worktree (the old conversation is gone; release keeps branches so the new branch names the new session id).
START ORDER (new session): getBot -> plugin stored health (plugin_unhealthy) -> assertBotPersonaBeforeSession (persona_missing | persona_check_failed | repository_not_configured) -> effectiveBaseBranch (null -> repository_not_configured) -> worktrees.acquire (cap_reached -> worktree_cap, other WorktreeError -> worktree_failed; awaits the dependency install) -> persona text read from the WORKTREE file .claude/agents/<name>.md | .agents/<name>.md (missing -> persona_missing; no host readFile needed, --agent reads the same file) -> beadsEnvForWorktree(main checkout) -> surfaceInstructionsForBot({ branch, baseBranch: lease.baseBranch, dependenciesInstalled: dependencyInstallState(lease.dependencies), issueTrackerNote: beads !== null }) -> resolveBotPosture({ ..., checkoutDir: lease.path, mainCheckoutDir: sourcePath(project.source), claude: beads ? { sandboxAllowWrite: [...CLAUDE_SANDBOX_DEFAULT_WRITE_PATHS, beads.beadsDir] } : undefined }) (PostureError -> posture_refused) -> assertPostureNotWidened on the exact { flags, env: { ...posture.env, ...beads.env }, codex, settingsOverrides } handed over -> sessions.create({ id, projectId, family, actorId, cwd: lease.path, posture: { flags | codex, env, bot }, bot: { id, name } }). Any failure after acquire releases the lease (non-forced; it is clean).
WHAT IS APPENDED WHERE: Claude: posture flags carry --agent <persona> and --append-system-prompt <surface instructions> (6.7 order); Codex: codex.developerInstructions = persona text + '\n\n' + surface instructions (6.8). Both families: posture.env = { BEADS_DIR, BD_NON_INTERACTIVE } (6.4); sessions/manager.ts launchFor now merges row.posture.env into startSession env for both families (Claude: { ...posture.env, ...context.env }), so it is reused on every resume. parsePosture on POST /sessions drops env/bot, so REST cannot inject env. Shared AgentSessionPosture gained env? and bot?.
ACTIVITY: sessions.create with bot -> session.started titled 'Bot "<name>" session started', payload { sessionId, family, actorId, botId, botName } (manager.ts edit; CreateSessionInput.bot).
SANDBOX WRITABLE ROOTS: Claude write-auto: beadsDir added to sandbox.filesystem.allowWrite via claude.sandboxAllowWrite (verifier does not inspect allowWrite; bd itself is excluded from the sandbox anyway). Codex: NOT done — CodexLaunchOptions has no writable-roots field and verify.ts refuses unknown codex keys; adding sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots to the CODEX_CONFIG JSON (codex-acp JSON.parses it, nested objects fine) needs edits to acp/families.ts (4.15 in flight) + posture/verify.ts; until then a bd write under workspace-write is an escalation the user answers as a decision. FOLLOW-UP bead wanted.
PROMPT: botSessions.prompt(sessionId, text) = worktrees.resume(session holder) (touches last_used_at; null -> BotStartError worktree_released 409: caller starts again) then sessions.prompt. Safety net: the service observes every session and on each 'prompt' row of a bot session calls worktrees.resume, so prompts via POST /sessions/:id/prompt (console) keep the lease fresh too.
CLOSE: botSessions.close(holder) / closeSession(sessionId) -> null if not a bot session, else cancels a prompting/queued turn, finds the session's lease via worktrees.list(projectId), worktrees.release(lease.id) (safe rule) -> { session, lease, released, keptUnpushed } (keptUnpushed = state active + unpushedWork; lease.unpushedReason has the text). Idempotent: lease null once released. The idle live process is left to the session reaper (manager has no per-session close). Thread row is kept.
CONSOLE THREAD: for holder.kind 'console' the service inserts the chat_threads row itself (threads/store insertThread; agentId 'bot:<botId>' = botAgentId(botId), title = bot name, model/effort null, chat_thread_sessions row). Starting the same thread id again after close switches it to the new session (switchThreadSession). Bot threads are NOT registry agents: /threads routes 404 them (findChatAgent); the thread service only watches them for working/unread after a restart (allThreads loop) — 6.14 should add a ThreadService adopt/watch for new bot threads (threads/service.ts, 10.7 in flight, untouched here) or reconcile on read, and extend thread routes/registry for 'bot:' agents.
HOW 6.14 CALLS IT: POST /projects/:slug/bots/:id/sessions { threadId? } (admin) -> 201 BotSessionStartResponse { session, lease: BotSessionLease { id, path, branch, baseBranch, dependencies, unpushedWork, unpushedReason }, thread, resumed, warnings } (200 + resumed:true when threadId still holds a session; threadId omitted -> a fresh uuid thread; a threadId held by another bot -> 404). Then prompt/cancel/stream/decisions on the SESSION routes with session.id (those are gated on Agent Hub chat capabilities: the module must be enabled for the project). Close: POST /projects/:slug/bots/:id/sessions/:sessionId/close -> BotSessionCloseResponse { session, lease|null, released, keptUnpushed }. Errors: code = BotStartError.reason. Shared paths botSessionsPath(slug, botId), botSessionClosePath(slug, botId, sessionId).
HOW 7.2 CALLS IT: platform.botSessions.start({ botId, holder: { kind: 'slack', id: <channel:thread_ts> }, actorId: <roster member actor id> }) on a mention (thread null); on replies platform.botSessions.find(holder) / start again (resumes while the lease is active) then botSessions.prompt(session.id, text); 'done' -> botSessions.close(holder) and report keptUnpushed. Decisions: platform.decisions as 4.7 (surface 'slack'). Map BotStartError.reason to the Slack reply.
ERROR REASONS (shared BOT_START_ERROR_REASONS, BotStartError { reason, status }): persona_missing 422, persona_check_failed 502, plugin_unhealthy 422, repository_not_configured 422, worktree_cap 409, worktree_failed 502, worktree_released 409, posture_refused 422; dependencies_failed never thrown (warnings[] + instructions).
TESTS bot-sessions.test.ts: real temp git repo with bare origin + personas committed on main + bd init --stealth in the clone (skipIf !hasBd for the e2e), stubHosts (+ override serving .agents/cody.md), healthy plugin rows written directly, fake claude fixture (claudePath) and fake ACP agent (Codex). Asserts: branch cm/bot/ana-bot/<sessionId> at origin/main, cwd = worktree, posture env/flags/instructions, console thread row, activity event naming the bot, launch argv via the session route, lease touched by the observer, a permission decision answered (deny) through platform.decisions, bd create with the session env in the main list and no .beads in the worktree, main checkout branch + porcelain status unchanged throughout, resume same session/lease, close releases (branch kept), same thread -> new session; persona missing (Codex bot with Claude-only persona) creates nothing; plugin unhealthy; non-admin 403; cap 409 with no session leaked; Codex Slack holder (developerInstructions = persona + platform text, env keys include BEADS_DIR via the fake agent, find/resume/close/worktree_released); write-auto allowWrite includes beadsDir + Bash(git push *) ask; close keeps an uncommitted worktree (keptUnpushed) then releases once clean.
VERIFIED 2026-10-28: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (127 files, 1206 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass (the SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_PATTERN build break was already fixed by its owner).
UNVERIFIED: no real claude/codex login here, so a live bot turn (sandbox + --agent + bd in a real Claude session, Codex escalation for bd writes) is measured from docs and fakes, not run.
close_reason: startBotSession/prompt/close with persona, worktree, posture, instructions, bd env; 6 tests; criteria verified

title: Register the bots and team capabilities in the Agent Hub
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Add the `bots` and `team` capabilities (module `agent-hub`) with one view each. `bots` requires the `repository` plugin and at least one of `claude-code` or `codex`; the readiness model only knows "all required plugins", so extend it with an any-of group so a capability can require one of several plugin types. `team` requires at least one bot to exist for the project, expressed as a project-fact readiness requirement. Both ladders: none then manage. Layers hold placeholder pages; the real pages are separate work.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`. Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`. Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: A project with Repository and Claude Code healthy shows Bots in the sidebar; Team shows the soft lockout until a bot exists; the any-of readiness has tests.
notes:
Bots + Team capability registration decisions (6.11, 6.12 and any capability needing an any-of plugin requirement rely on these).

MANIFESTS (apps/daemon/src/capabilities/manifests/, both in CAPABILITIES in this order):
- bots.ts botsCapability: id 'bots', label Bots, view { id 'bots', label 'Bots', icon 'i-lucide-bot', path 'bots' } -> /p/<slug>/bots. requiresPlugins ['repository'], requiresAnyPlugins [['claude-code','codex']]. No agents/jobs/tools. Ladder none -> manage (manage shows view 'bots', chat false).
- team.ts teamCapability: id 'team', view { id 'team', label 'Team', icon 'i-lucide-users', path 'team' } -> /p/<slug>/team. requiresPlugins [], requiresProjectFacts ['hasBots']. Ladder none -> manage (shows 'team').
- No tools declared yet: bot REST routes stay requireAdmin. 6.11/6.12 may add operation tools (e.g. 'bots.manage') to the manage rung if routes should be gated by rung via requireCapability.

MODULE: AGENT_HUB_MODULE.capabilities = [{bots, manage}, {team, manage}] (src/modules/definitions.ts). Chat capabilities (4.x) append here.

ANY-OF PLUGINS:
- Shared CapabilityManifest.requiresAnyPlugins?: readonly (readonly PluginTypeId[])[] (packages/shared/src/capabilities.ts; also on defineCapability's param). Each inner group is satisfied by ANY member being 'ready' (stored-healthy instance, own else global); all groups and all requiresPlugins must hold.
- assertCapability rejects: unknown type ("has unknown plugin type(s) 'x' in an any-of group."), repeats in a group, a group with <2 types ("put a single one in requiresPlugins"), a type both in requiresPlugins and a group. assertManifests' pluginTypeIds hook also checks group members.
- New ReadinessReason member { kind: 'plugin-any', plugins: string[], message } (packages/shared/src/registry.ts). Message: "Needs one of: Claude Code, Codex; none is configured and healthy." (type display names, fallback id).
- src/registry/readiness.ts: requiredPluginTypes(cap) = requiresPlugins + flattened groups; load.ts and gate.ts load readiness for that list.

HASBOTS FACT:
- PROJECT_FACT_IDS = ['hasBeads','isGitRepo','hasRemote','hasBots']. projectFacts(db, project) (signature changed: now takes db first; gate.ts updated) sets hasBots from a 1-row select on the bots table for the project. Deliberately NOT listBots: listBots is async and resolves base branches over the network, while the registry and gate are synchronous and run on every navigation/gated request. Any bot counts, whatever its status.
- Reason: "The project has no bots yet; add one on the Bots page." (kind 'project-fact', fact 'hasBots').
- Web: after creating/deleting a bot call refreshProjectRegistry(slug) so Team readiness updates.

LAYERS (placeholders; 6.11/6.12 replace the page bodies):
- apps/web/layers/bots/nuxt.config.ts (components prefix 'Bots'), app/pages/p/[project]/bots/index.vue
- apps/web/layers/team/nuxt.config.ts (prefix 'Team'), app/pages/p/[project]/team/index.vue
- Each page wraps a UDashboardPanel + UEmpty placeholder in core's <CapabilityViewGate capability="bots|team" view="bots|team"> (2.7). 6.11 replaces the bots panel with cards/editor/persona check; 6.12 replaces the team panel with the roster. Keep the gate wrapper.

FOLLOW-UP FOR 2.7 OWNER (not changed here): CapabilityViewGate offers 'Configure plugins' only for kind === 'plugin' (should include 'plugin-any') and 'Re-check the project' for every project-fact reason (wrong for hasBots; should link to the Bots page).

TESTS: src/registry/readiness.test.ts (any-of pure: any member ready, none ready names both, absent = missing, all-of still enforced, hasBots fact), src/registry/agent-hub.test.ts (real CAPABILITIES/MODULES via instanceHarness with fixture plugin types: Repository + Claude Code healthy -> Bots ready, Team not ready with hasBots reason until a bot row exists; Codex alone satisfies; neither -> plugin-any reason + degraded; developer granted agent-hub defaults gets manage, sees only Bots in groups, Team view ready false), manifest.test.ts any-of assertions, capabilities/registry.test.ts real manifests load + hook checks groups, modules/registry.test.ts agent-hub membership. capabilities/boot.test.ts and plugins/boot.test.ts now pass modules: [] since they boot with fixture capabilities only.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (80 files, 736 passed, 3 skipped), build pass. Live: built daemon :6510 + built web :6511, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR/CM_SECRETS_KEY: '2 capability manifest(s) registered'; project live + agent-hub enabled + repository and claude-code instances: untested -> bots reasons (Repository untested; 'Needs one of: Claude Code, Codex...'); after writing healthy into plugin_instances via sqlite, GET /api/projects/live/registry: agent-hub group entries /p/live/bots + /p/live/team, bots ready, team not ready with hasBots reason; POST bot -> team ready, degraded []. /p/live/bots and /p/live/team SSR 200.
close_reason: bots/team manifests, any-of readiness, hasBots fact, placeholder layers; verified live

title: Build the Bots page with cards, editor and persona check
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Build the Bots view: a card per bot showing name, family, scope, base branch, status (active, not configured, or warnings with reasons) and the Slack connection state slot (filled later); a create/edit form with name, the two Slack keys (write-only, shown as set), family (a family is disabled when its plugin is unhealthy or when the persona check found its file missing, with the reason), write scope, base branch (placeholder showing the repository default), persona name with a "check persona" button that shows which files were found, and "answers in" as anywhere or a list of channel ids each in its own input with an add button; and delete with confirmation.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a bot on a repo with only the Claude persona disables Codex with the reason after the check; saving with Claude Code, confirmation scope and base branch `main` shows an active card once Slack keys are set; channel ids can be added and removed one per input.
notes:
Bots page decisions (7.8 and later bot UI depend on these).

FILES (all in apps/web/layers/bots, plus one line in apps/web/vitest.config.ts):
- app/pages/p/[project]/bots/index.vue: gate (bots/bots) + UDashboardPanel; navbar 'New bot' sets a local ref editing (undefined closed, null new, Bot edit) passed as v-model:editing to BotsManager. No fetching in the page (gate gotcha).
- components/Manager.vue (BotsManager): loads useBots + useBotsPlugins; grid of BotsCard; UEmpty 'No bots yet'; BotsEditorModal; delete via core ProjectsConfirmModal (useOverlay); per-card check persona = POST /bots/:id/check-persona, replaces the bot in the cached list + toast. After save: if persona name set and status unverified, it auto-runs the per-bot check so a saved bot can reach 'active' without a second click. After every create/edit/delete: refresh list + refreshProjectRegistry(slug) (hasBots -> Team readiness).
- components/Card.vue (BotsCard): props bot, checkingPersona; emits edit/delete/checkPersona. Shows status badge (Active/Not configured/N warnings, data-status attr), agent, scope, base branch (effective; '(repository default)' when baseBranch null), persona + Found/Missing/Not checked, answers in (Anywhere or channel badges), Slack key set/unset badges, warnings list, BotsSlackConnection slot.
- components/EditorModal.vue (BotsEditorModal): v-model:open, props bot|null, familyReasons Record<BotFamily,string|null>, defaultBranch|null; emits saved(bot, created). zod schema mirrors shared patterns (name<=80, xoxb-/xapp- prefixes, base branch, persona name, channel ids uppercased, dupes flagged). Secrets write-only: blank keeps, 'Set' badge when stored; create sends only non-empty secrets, PATCH sends only changed fields. Family is a URadioGroup (table variant) from botsFamilyOptions; submit refuses a disabled family with its reason as field error. 'Check persona' uses POST /bots/check-persona {personaName, baseBranch|null} (preview, records nothing) and shows BotsPersonaFiles; result clears when persona name or base branch changes. Base branch placeholder '<branch> (repository default)' from the preview branch, else defaultBranch. Answers in: Anywhere | Only in these channels with one input per channel, remove button each, 'Add channel' in the field hint. Error codes: name_taken->name, family_unavailable->family, rest -> UAlert.
- components/PersonaFiles.vue (BotsPersonaFiles): prop check BotsPersonaCheck; rows per family with path + found.
- components/SlackConnection.vue (BotsSlackConnection): SLOT FOR 7.8. Props { bot: Bot }; currently renders an empty <div class='empty:hidden' data-testid='bot-slack-connection' :data-bot-id>. Rendered in each card between the details list and the warnings. 7.8 replaces this component's body (fetch/connection state keyed by bot.id); no Card/Manager change needed. If it needs a list-level fetch, add a composable in this layer (useBots... prefix).
- composables/useBots.ts: useBots() -> {bots, data, status, error, refresh} (useAsyncData key botsDataKey(slug) = 'bots:<slug>', GET /projects/:slug/bots); useBotsPlugins() -> {instances, familyReasons, status, error, refresh} (key 'bots-plugins:<slug>', GET /plugins?project=slug, admin-only like the bot routes).
- utils/bots.ts (pure, tested): botsDataKey, botsPluginsDataKey, botsFamilyPluginReason (daemon status wording), botsPersonaMissing, botsFamilyOptions({pluginReasons, personaCheck, currentFamily}) (persona-missing always disables; plugin reason disables except the saved bot's own family, matching the daemon), botsPersonaFileRows, botsStatusView, botsRepositoryDefaultBranch (repository config.defaultBranch, else a bot following the default).
- test/unit/bots.test.ts (7 tests). apps/web/vitest.config.ts include now also 'layers/*/test/**/*.test.ts' (layer-owned tests, so the boundary lint treats them as the layer's).

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (93 files, 883 passed, 3 skipped), build pass (build retried past other agents' Nuxt build lock). Live: tsx daemon :7100 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR/CM_SECRETS_KEY, node --import preload stubbing api.github.com for jack/candy with only .claude/agents/ana.md; real repository health test passed through the stub; claude-code/codex health faked in sqlite) + nuxt dev of a scratch copy of apps/web on :7101; headless Chromium 33/33: empty state; Team not ready; preview shows Claude found, Codex not found; Codex radio disabled with 'Codex persona file .agents/ana.md was not found on main'; placeholder 'main (repository default)'; result clears on branch change; channels add/invalid flagged/remove keeps others; save Claude Code + Write (confirmation prompts) + main -> card persona Found, warnings name both missing Slack keys; Team ready; wrong prefix flagged; set xoxb-/xapp- dummies -> card Active; edit shows keys Set with empty inputs; per-card check toast; name_taken on name field; keyless/personaless bot -> Not configured; delete cancel keeps, confirm removes; deleting all -> Team not ready again. Unhealthy codex plugin -> Codex disabled with 'The Codex plugin is unhealthy: Not logged in'; no horizontal overflow at 390px.
close_reason: Bots page: cards, editor, persona check, channel inputs; browser-verified 33/33

title: Compose the platform's surface instructions appended after the persona
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The persona in the repository carries personality and task knowledge; platform behaviour must come from the platform, appended at session start. Build the composer that produces this text for a bot session: the branch the bot is on and the base branch to propose against; how to deliver (commit, push the branch, and open a pull request on the repository host, with the host named); that `bd` works from this directory and issues land in the project's main list; whether dependencies were installed; and the structured handoff instruction: end every turn with the handoff block described below. Keep it short and factual; it is appended as system-level instructions after the persona for Claude Code and as developer instructions after the persona for Codex.

Shared names: The structured handoff format is fixed: a fenced code block whose info string is `handoff`, containing one `key: value` line per field with keys `outcome` (one of done, partial, blocked), `summary` (one line), `pull_request` (URL or none), `issues` (comma-separated issue ids or none), and `follow_ups` (semicolon-separated or none).
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests check the composed text for both families contains branch, base branch, host, bd note, dependency state and the handoff instruction; the text is under about forty lines.
notes:
Surface instructions (apps/daemon/src/bots/instructions.ts, re-exported from src/bots/index.ts).

EXPORTS
- composeSurfaceInstructions(input: SurfaceInstructionsInput): string — pure, ~26 lines (test asserts < 40).
  SurfaceInstructionsInput = { family: BotFamily, botName: string, personaName: string|null, branch: string, baseBranch: string, host: RepositoryHost ('github'|'bitbucket'), repository: { owner, repo }, writeScope: BotWriteScope, dependenciesInstalled: boolean|'failed' (DependencyInstallState), issueTrackerNote: boolean }.
- surfaceInstructionsForBot(deps: BotDeps, bot: Bot, runtime: BotSessionRuntime): string — reads the project's Repository plugin instance (resolvePluginInstance + repositoryConfig) for host/owner/repo; base branch = runtime.baseBranch ?? bot.effectiveBaseBranch. Throws BotError('repository_not_configured') when the Repository instance is missing or the base branch is unknown (null). No host call is made.
  BotSessionRuntime = { branch: string (worktree branch), dependenciesInstalled: boolean|'failed', issueTrackerNote: boolean (true when BEADS env points bd at the main checkout db), baseBranch?: string (pass the branch the worktree was actually cut from) }.
- HANDOFF_INSTRUCTION_FIELDS: Record<keyof Handoff, {key, value}> (wire keys outcome/summary/pull_request/issues/follow_ups + placeholder) and HANDOFF_INFO_STRING 'handoff'. Outcomes built from shared HANDOFF_OUTCOMES. shared/handoff.ts only exports HANDOFF_OUTCOMES (keys are literals inside parseHandoff), so drift is guarded by the Record<keyof Handoff> type plus a test that fills the template lines from the composed text and parses them with parseHandoff.

TEXT: '# Platform instructions', framing line (claude-code: 'These system-level instructions ...'; codex: 'These developer instructions ...'), bot/persona/family line; Workspace (branch, cut from base, stay on branch, repo owner/repo on host + URL, dependency state, bd note or 'bd is not connected'); Delivery (write-scope line; write scopes: commit, push to origin, open PR from branch into base on host, URL in handoff, fallback say so in follow_ups; read-only: no PR, pull_request none); Handoff (fenced handoff template + outcome meaning + 'none' rule).

HOW 6.13 PASSES IT
- Claude Code: forward after the shim's '--' as ['--append-system-prompt', text] in FamilyLaunchOptions.flags (persona via --agent <personaName> or equivalent stays separate, so the text lands after the persona).
- Codex: FamilyLaunchOptions.codex.developerInstructions = personaText + '\n\n' + text (apps/daemon/src/acp/families.ts sends it as CODEX_CONFIG developer_instructions).

TESTS: src/bots/instructions.test.ts (13): both families contain branch, base, host + URL, bd note, dependency state, handoff instruction, < 40 lines; framing per family; Bitbucket; each dependency state; bd off; read-only/write-auto; null persona; template round-trip through parseHandoff per family; composed text + appended sample block parses; surfaceInstructionsForBot fills from bot + Repository config, runtime baseBranch override, throws without Repository plugin or base branch.
close_reason: composeSurfaceInstructions + surfaceInstructionsForBot, 13 tests incl. parseHandoff round-trip

title: Add the per-project team roster
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Only listed people may talk to a project's bots. Add a team roster per project with REST (list, add, update, remove): display name, email, Slack member id (unique per project), and bot scope as all bots or a list of bot ids. There is no per-person agent login; sessions run under the project's plugin login. Record last-active time for later use. Provide a daemon-side lookup "may this Slack member talk to this bot?" used by routing later.
acceptance_criteria: Adding a member with a scope of one bot makes the lookup true for that bot and false for another; removing the member makes it false; a duplicate Slack id is rejected; tests cover each.
notes:
Team roster decisions (7.2 routing, 6.12 Team page rely on these). How-to in apps/daemon/README.md '## Team roster'.
TABLE team_members (src/db/schema/team-members.ts): id uuid PK, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, display_name, email nullable, slack_member_id, bot_scope JSON {all:true}|{botIds:string[]}, last_active_at nullable, created_at, updated_at. Unique index (project_id, slack_member_id); index on project_id. MIGRATION drizzle/0014_team_members.sql (tag 0014_team_members, after 0013_worktree_reclaim).
SHARED (packages/shared/src/team.ts, exported): projectTeamPath(slug), TeamBotScope, TeamMember {id, projectId, displayName, email|null, slackMemberId, botScope, lastActiveAt|null, createdAt, updatedAt}, CreateTeamMemberRequest {displayName, slackMemberId, email?, botScope?}, UpdateTeamMemberRequest=Partial, TeamMemberListResponse {members}, TeamMemberResponse {member}, SLACK_MEMBER_ID_PATTERN /^[UW][A-Z0-9]{2,}$/, TEAM_NAME_MAX_LENGTH 100, TEAM_ERROR_CODES.
ROUTES (admin only via requireAdmin, mounted on /projects via teamRoutes()): GET /projects/:slug/team -> {members} (by lower(displayName)); POST -> 201 {member} (omitted botScope = {botIds:[]}, i.e. no bots; omitted email = null); GET/PATCH/DELETE /projects/:slug/team/:id -> {member} / {member} / 204 (PATCH omitted fields unchanged, email null or blank clears, botScope replaced whole). Errors: invalid_request 400, not_found 404 (also member of another project), slack_member_taken 409 (create and patch), unknown_bot 422 (botIds not bots of this project). Non-admin 403.
SERVICE (apps/daemon/src/team): listTeamMembers(db, projectId), findTeamMember/getTeamMember(db, projectId, id), addTeamMember, updateTeamMember, removeTeamMember, touchMemberActivity(db, projectId, slackMemberId, at?) -> boolean (stamps last_active_at; false if not listed), and LOOKUP mayMemberTalkToBot(db: Db, projectId: string, slackMemberId: string, botId: string): boolean, synchronous, fails closed (unlisted member, bot outside scope -> false). 7.2 should call it with the bot's projectId and Slack user id, and touchMemberActivity on accepted messages. Stale ids: deleting a bot does not prune botIds from members (uuids never reused, harmless; lookup just never matches).
6.12 Team page: call GET/POST /api/projects/:slug/team and GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/projects/:slug/team/:id; get bot choices from GET /api/projects/:slug/bots. Tests: src/team/team.test.ts (7).
close_reason: team_members + admin REST + mayMemberTalkToBot lookup; 7 tests

title: Map write scope to agent posture per family and verify it is never widened
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Write scope is the human's promise about what a bot may do, and nothing may widen it. Build the posture mapping for a bot session: for Claude Code, read-only becomes plan mode with the tools that leave plan mode or spawn agents denied; write-with-confirmation becomes the default permission mode; write-automatically becomes accept-edits with the shell sandbox on and git push always asking. All scopes: disable every hook from the checkout, pass the persona as the CLI's agent, always allow the `bd` command, and vet the checkout's own Claude settings files so they cannot auto-approve shell commands. For Codex, map the same scopes onto its approval and sandbox settings (read-only sandbox for read-only; workspace-write with on-request approvals for both write scopes) and pass the persona as developer instructions. Refuse any resulting configuration that bypasses permissions, and refuse a persona whose front matter asks for broader permissions than the scope allows. The output is the launch flags, environment and config the harness passes through.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests assert the flags and config for every scope and family; a persona front matter requesting bypass is refused; a checkout settings file that auto-approves shell commands is neutralised; `bd` is always allowed.
notes:
Posture mapping (6.13 feeds this into startSession). Code: apps/daemon/src/posture/ (index.ts exports everything). Docs: apps/daemon/README.md '## Bot posture'. Tests: src/posture/posture.test.ts (33), verify.test.ts (8).

SIGNATURES
- resolveBotPosture({ family: BotFamily, writeScope: BotWriteScope, personaName: string, personaText: string, surfaceInstructions?: string, checkoutDir: string (absolute worktree), checkoutSettings?: CheckoutSettingsFile[] (pre-read; else read from checkoutDir), claude?: { sandboxAllowedDomains?: string[], sandboxAllowWrite?: string[] } }) -> BotPosture { family, writeScope, flags: string[], env: Record<string,string> (always {} today), codex?: CodexLaunchOptions, settingsOverrides: object|null (the object inside --settings), neutralised: { file, key, how }[] }. Pure apart from the optional settings read. Runs assertPostureNotWidened itself before returning.
- assertPostureNotWidened(posture: VerifiablePosture {family, flags, env, codex?, settingsOverrides}, writeScope) -> void; throws PostureError code 'widened' (or 'bypass'). 6.13 should call it again on the exact object it hands to the harness.
- assertPersonaWithinScope(personaName, personaText, writeScope) -> { name, front }; parsePersonaFrontMatter(text) -> { block, entries[{key,value,items}], unreadable } | null.
- readCheckoutSettings(dir) -> CheckoutSettingsFile[] ({ path, settings }); vetCheckoutSettings(files, checkoutDir, writeScope) -> { askRules, denyRules, neutralised }.
- PostureError codes: invalid_input | bypass | persona_unreadable | persona_name_mismatch | persona_widens | checkout_settings_unreadable | widened.
- personaText is REQUIRED (Claude: front matter judged, name must equal personaName since --agent matches the front-matter name; Codex: whole text becomes developer instructions). personaName must match BOT_PERSONA_NAME_PATTERN.

CLAUDE CODE FLAGS (after the shim's --, fixed order):
--permission-mode <plan|default|acceptEdits> --settings <inline JSON> --strict-mcp-config --agent <persona> [--append-system-prompt <surfaceInstructions>] --allowedTools 'Bash(bd *)' [--disallowedTools <list>]
- read-only: plan; disallowed ExitPlanMode,Agent,Workflow; settings useAutoModeDuringPlan:false (plan mode otherwise lets the auto-mode classifier approve shell commands).
- write-confirm: default; disallowed Agent,Workflow (a subagent runs in its own front-matter permissionMode under a plan/default parent, so spawning one could widen the scope; under acceptEdits the CLI forces the parent mode so write-auto keeps subagents).
- write-auto: acceptEdits; no disallowed; settings permissions.ask ['Bash(git push *)'] (ask outranks allow from any file and the sandbox auto-approval, so push always prompts); sandbox { enabled:true, failIfUnavailable:true, autoAllowBashIfSandboxed:true, allowUnsandboxedCommands:false, enableWeakerNestedSandbox:false, excludedCommands:['bd *'], filesystem.allowWrite: [~/.local/share/pnpm/store, ~/.cache/pnpm, ~/.npm] (override via claude.sandboxAllowWrite), network { allowedDomains: [github.com, api.github.com, bitbucket.org, api.bitbucket.org, registry.npmjs.org] (override via claude.sandboxAllowedDomains), allowLocalBinding:false, allowAllUnixSockets:false } }. bd is excluded from the sandbox because it writes the main checkout's issue DB; outside the sandbox the Bash(bd *) allow rule approves it. The worktree's shared .git is handled by the CLI's sandbox itself (hooks/ and config stay denied).
- every scope's --settings: disableAllHooks:true, enableAllProjectMcpServers:false, permissions { defaultMode:<same as flag>, disableBypassPermissionsMode:'disable', disableAutoMode:'disable', ask?, deny? }, sandbox { enabled:false } for read-only/write-confirm.

CHECKOUT SETTINGS VETTING (mechanism; CLI 2.1.311 docs: --settings sits above project/local for scalar keys; permission lists MERGE across files; rules evaluate deny > ask > allow regardless of file or specificity):
- permissions.allow rules -> mirrored verbatim into --settings permissions.ask (ask outranks allow). Rules equal to Bash(bd *) / Bash(bd:*) are left alone. A rule that covers bd (bare Bash or Bash(* ...)) is still mirrored and neutralised[].how says bd will prompt in that checkout.
- permissions.additionalDirectories -> --settings permissions.deny Edit(//<abs>/**) (resolved against checkoutDir; ~ kept). Write(path) rules never match, so Edit is the only path rule that works.
- hooks -> disableAllHooks:true; permissions.defaultMode -> --permission-mode + defaultMode; sandbox -> enabled:false (read-only/write-confirm) or allowUnsandboxedCommands:false (write-auto; the CLI then ignores repository excludedCommands/allowedDomains/allowWrite); agent -> --agent; enableAllProjectMcpServers/enabledMcpjsonServers -> --strict-mcp-config. Each is reported in neutralised[].
- A settings file that is not a JSON object, or a permissions/allow/additionalDirectories value of the wrong shape, is refused (checkout_settings_unreadable). Missing files are skipped.
- Note for 6.13: in a worktree the CLI reads .claude/settings.local.json from the MAIN checkout root; call readCheckoutSettings on both the worktree and the main checkout and pass the concatenation as checkoutSettings.

PERSONA FRONT MATTER (Claude only; parsed as plain top-level key: value lines plus block/flow/comma lists; a flow mapping or merge key makes it unreadable -> refused):
- any BLANKET_BYPASS_TOKEN in the block -> 'bypass'.
- permissionMode above the scope ceiling (read-only plan < write-confirm default/manual/dontAsk < write-auto acceptEdits), 'auto', or unknown -> 'persona_widens'.
- tools listing a tool the scope denies (ExitPlanMode/Agent/Workflow per scope) -> refused; disallowedTools only narrows, ignored.
- hooks, mcpServers, observer -> refused on every scope. memory: user -> refused; project/local -> only write-auto.
- Codex personas are not judged (no front matter semantics); text sent whole.

CODEX: codex = { mode: read-only -> 'read-only', write-confirm & write-auto -> 'workspace-write', developerInstructions: personaText.trim() + '\n\n' + surfaceInstructions.trim() }; flags [] and env {}. Verifier refuses any mode outside CODEX_AGENT_MODES or not the scope's, any flags, any CODEX_LAUNCHER_ENV name in env, unknown codex keys.

VERIFIER (Claude): bypass token in any flag/env (instruction text excluded) or in --settings; CLAUDE_REFUSED_FLAGS (--dangerously-skip-permissions, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions, --permission-prompt-tool, --setting-sources, --bare, --system-prompt(-file), --append-system-prompt-file, --agents, --tools, --add-dir, --mcp-config, --permission-prompts); exactly one --permission-mode equal to the scope's; exactly one inline --settings equal to settingsOverrides with every guard above (hooks off, bypass/auto disabled, no allow/additionalDirectories/hooks/apiKeyHelper/env, sandbox state per scope, git push ask for write-auto); --strict-mcp-config present; --allowedTools contains Bash(bd *) and no editing tool, bare Bash, Bash(*...) or tool-name wildcard; --disallowedTools contains the scope's denials; exactly one --agent; instruction text not starting with '-'.

HOW 6.13 USES IT
const posture = resolveBotPosture({ family: bot.family, writeScope: bot.writeScope, personaName: bot.persona.name, personaText: <read from worktree .claude/agents/<name>.md or .agents/<name>.md>, surfaceInstructions: surfaceInstructionsForBot(...), checkoutDir: worktree, checkoutSettings: [...readCheckoutSettings(worktree), ...readCheckoutSettings(mainCheckout)] })
assertPostureNotWidened(posture, bot.writeScope)
acpHarness.startSession({ family: bot.family, cwd: worktree, configHome, flags: posture.flags, env: { ...posture.env, ...beadsEnv }, codex: posture.codex, ... })
Verified in posture.test.ts that resolveFamilyLaunch accepts the result for both families. Surface posture.neutralised to the session log/UI so Jack sees what the checkout tried.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (83 files, 793 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass. Flag names checked against claude 2.1.311 --help (--permission-mode choices acceptEdits|auto|bypassPermissions|manual|dontAsk|plan; --allowedTools/--disallowedTools; --settings; --agent; --strict-mcp-config; --setting-sources exists but drops CLAUDE.md so it is refused, not used).

FOLLOW-UPS (not done here): other subagent files under .claude/agents/ and forked skills (context: fork) can run in their own permissionMode even with Agent denied; a checkout env/apiKeyHelper block in .claude/settings.json is not vetted (the shim rejects a non-firstParty provider at initialize); behaviour measured from docs, not a live run (6.13 has the first real session).
close_reason: resolveBotPosture + assertPostureNotWidened, checkout settings vetting, persona front matter check; 41 tests; gates green

title: Add the bot definition with status computation and REST
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A bot is a Slack-facing agent for a project. Add the bot table and REST (list for a project, create, update, delete): name; the Slack bot token and app-level token as secrets in the secrets store (shown only as set); agent family (Claude Code or Codex); write scope (read-only, write with confirmation prompts, write automatically); base branch (defaulting to the Repository plugin's default branch when blank); persona name; and "answers in" as either anywhere or a list of Slack channel ids. No approvals section, no keyword, no Slack team id. Validation: the family's plugin must be healthy for the project to choose it; the Repository plugin must be configured. Compute and return a status per bot: active (plugin healthy, persona verified, both Slack keys set), not configured (nothing usable yet), or warnings listing each reason (plugin unhealthy, persona missing or unverified, Slack keys missing). Deleting a bot deletes its secrets.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a bot with a missing Slack key returns status warnings naming the key; choosing a family whose plugin is unhealthy is rejected; blank base branch resolves to the repository default; secrets never appear in responses; tests cover status computation.
notes:
Bot definition decisions (6.6, 6.8, 6.9, 6.10, 6.13, 7.x depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Bots'.

TABLE bots (apps/daemon/src/db/schema/bots.ts): id uuid PK, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, name, family 'claude-code'|'codex', write_scope 'read-only'|'write-confirm'|'write-auto', base_branch nullable (null = Repository plugin default, resolved at READ time, never stored), persona_name nullable, answers_in JSON {anywhere:true}|{channels:string[]}, persona_status 'unverified'|'verified'|'missing' default 'unverified', persona_checked_at nullable, persona_reason nullable, created_at, updated_at. Index bots_project_id_idx. Name unique per project ignoring case (service check in a transaction, no unique index).
MIGRATION: apps/daemon/drizzle/0008_bots.sql (tag 0008_bots).

SHARED (packages/shared/src/bots.ts, exported from index): BOT_FAMILIES, BotFamily, BOT_FAMILY_NAMES; BOT_WRITE_SCOPES, BotWriteScope, BOT_WRITE_SCOPE_NAMES; BOT_SECRET_NAMES ['slackBotToken','slackAppToken'], BotSecretName, BOT_SECRET_LABELS, BOT_SECRET_PREFIXES (xoxb-, xapp-); BOT_NAME_MAX_LENGTH 80; BOT_PERSONA_NAME_PATTERN /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/; BOT_BASE_BRANCH_PATTERN; SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_PATTERN /^[CG][A-Z0-9]{2,}$/; BotAnswersIn; BOT_PERSONA_STATUSES, BotPersonaStatus, BotPersona {name|null, status, checkedAt|null, reason|null}; BotStatus = 'active'|'not_configured'|{warnings:string[]}; Bot {id, projectId, name, family, writeScope, baseBranch|null, effectiveBaseBranch|null, persona, answersIn, secrets: Record<BotSecretName,'set'|'unset'>, status, createdAt, updatedAt}; BotSecretValues; CreateBotRequest {name, family, writeScope? (default read-only), baseBranch?, personaName?, answersIn? (default anywhere), secrets?}; UpdateBotRequest = Partial<CreateBotRequest>; BotListResponse {bots}; BotResponse {bot}; projectBotsPath(slug); BOT_ERROR_CODES/BotErrorCode.

STATUS RULES (computeBotStatus, pure, src/bots/status.ts; input {family, familyPlugin: {health}|null, persona {name,status,reason}, secrets, baseBranchProblem}): warnings in order = family plugin (not set up / not tested since it last changed / unhealthy: <reason>), persona (No persona is set / Persona "x" has not been checked / persona_reason or "Persona "x" was not found on the base branch"), base branch problem (blank base branch and default branch unreadable), each missing key ("Slack bot token is missing", "Slack app-level token is missing"). No warnings -> 'active'. Else if NEITHER Slack key is set AND persona status != verified -> 'not_configured' (nothing usable yet). Else {warnings}. Family plugin health is the STORED test result of resolvePluginInstance(project, family) (null = untested = not healthy).

ROUTES (admin only via requireAdmin per route, mounted on /projects in app.ts via botRoutes(deps.secretsReader ?? locked); decision: bots hold Slack credentials, like /plugins):
- GET /projects/:slug/bots -> {bots} ordered by lower(name)
- POST /projects/:slug/bots CreateBotRequest -> 201 {bot}
- GET /projects/:slug/bots/:id -> {bot}
- PATCH /projects/:slug/bots/:id UpdateBotRequest (omitted fields unchanged; baseBranch/personaName null or blank clears; answersIn replaced whole) -> {bot}
- DELETE /projects/:slug/bots/:id -> 204 (deletes secrets owner)
Bot in another project -> 404. Validation: Repository plugin configured (instance exists + required secrets set) on create AND update -> else 422 repository_not_configured; family plugin stored-healthy on create and when family CHANGES (editing other fields while the plugin is unhealthy is allowed) -> else 422 family_unavailable with the reason. Errors: invalid_request 400 (bad JSON/shape/unknown field/bad channel id/empty channel list/bad branch or persona name), not_found 404 (slug or bot), family_unavailable/repository_not_configured/invalid_secrets 422 (unknown secret name or wrong xoxb-/xapp- prefix), name_taken/secrets_locked 409.
Secrets: owner botSecretOwner(id) = 'bot:<id>', names slackBotToken, slackAppToken. Non-empty string sets, omitted or '' leaves, null clears; any value while locked -> 409 before anything is written. Responses only 'set'/'unset'.
Base branch: reads call createRepositoryOperations(...).getDefaultBranch() (10 s timeout + request signal), once per project per read; failure -> effectiveBaseBranch null + status warning, never an error.
Persona reset: changing personaName, family or baseBranch (not the bot name) sets persona_status back to 'unverified' and clears checkedAt/reason.

PERSONA COLUMNS FOR 6.6: call recordBotPersonaCheck(db, botId, bot.updatedAt /*captured when the check started*/, { status: 'verified' | 'missing', reason?: string }) -> boolean (false = bot changed since, nothing stored; reason is cleared on verified). It sets persona_checked_at and does NOT bump updated_at. Use bot.effectiveBaseBranch as the branch to check. The per-family file availability (for disabling a family in the UI) is not stored; return it from 6.6's action.

SERVICE (src/bots, index re-exports bots/errors/routes/status/validation). BotDeps = PluginInstanceDeps {db, pluginTypes, secrets: SecretsWriter}; BotReadDeps = BotDeps & {secretsReader} (platform code: {...platform, secretsReader: platform.secrets}; routes: {...c.var, secretsReader}).
- listBots(readDeps, {projectId?, signal?}) -> Promise<Bot[]> (no projectId = every bot on the platform, for 7.1 Socket Mode: filter status === 'active')
- findBot(readDeps, id, {signal?}) -> Bot|null; getBot (throws BotError not_found)
- createBot(readDeps, projectId, CreateBotInput) / updateBot(readDeps, id, UpdateBotInput) (parse with parseCreateBot/parseUpdateBot)
- deleteBot(deps, id); deleteProjectBots(deps, projectId) (called by DELETE /projects/:slug before deleteProjectPluginInstances)
- botProjectId(db, id) -> string|null (cheap ownership check)
- createBotSecrets(platform.secrets, botId).get('slackBotToken'|'slackAppToken') -> plaintext, daemon-side only (7.1)
- computeBotStatus(input) pure.
6.8/6.13: bot.effectiveBaseBranch, bot.writeScope, bot.family, bot.persona.name. 6.9 team roster: reference bots.id (FK ON DELETE CASCADE or JSON list) and listBots for 'which bots'. 6.10: registry readiness can use listBots(...).length / status.

TESTS: src/bots/status.test.ts (7) + src/bots/bots.test.ts (13): instanceHarness with real repositoryPluginType + stubHosts (jack/candy default main), fixturePluginType('claude-code') tested healthy, fixturePluginType('codex') unhealthy. Covers missing-key warnings, no secret in any body, encrypted store, unhealthy/untested/missing family 422, repository_not_configured, blank base branch -> repo default (and defaultBranch override, PATCH null), unreadable default branch warning, active + persona reset + stale persona check refused, not_configured, secret update semantics, edit with unhealthy family allowed but switch refused, validation errors, locked store 409, delete + project delete remove secrets, other-project 404, non-admin 403.
VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (75 files, 683 passed, 3 skipped), build pass. Built daemon on 6235 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR + CM_SECRETS_KEY: 9 migrations applied; 422 repository_not_configured, 422 family_unavailable (not set up, then real claude-code 'Not logged in'); after simulating health in sqlite, create with bot token only -> warnings incl. 'Slack app-level token is missing' and real GitHub 401 base-branch warning; repo defaultBranch override -> effectiveBaseBranch main; PATCH '' leaves/new app token sets; 409 name_taken, 422 wrong prefix, 400 bad channel; new bot with no keys -> not_configured; no plaintext in secret files; DELETE bot and DELETE project removed bot:<id> secret dirs.
close_reason: bots table, status computation, admin REST; verified live

title: Add the persona check against the bot's base branch
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A bot's personality lives in the repository, not the platform: `.claude/agents/<name>.md` for Claude Code and `.agents/<name>.md` for Codex, on the bot's base branch. Add a check-persona action on a bot that, through the Repository plugin's host API (not a local clone), looks up both files on the base branch and records which exist and when it was last checked. The result feeds the bot's status (persona missing for the chosen family is a warning) and tells the UI which families to disable. Also run the check automatically before a bot session starts so a persona removed after setup is caught, and fail the start with a clear reason.
acceptance_criteria: For a repo with only the Claude persona the check reports Claude present and Codex missing; a bot on Codex then shows a persona warning; a session start for that bot fails naming the missing file.
notes:
Persona check decisions (6.11 and 6.13 depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Bots' (Persona check paragraph).

FILES: apps/daemon/src/bots/persona.ts (+ persona.test.ts, 9 tests); small edits to bots/routes.ts, bots/errors.ts, bots/index.ts (export * from './persona'), packages/shared/src/bots.ts, apps/daemon/README.md. No schema or migration.

SHARED (packages/shared/src/bots.ts): botPersonaPath(family, name) -> '.claude/agents/<name>.md' | '.agents/<name>.md'; botPersonaMissingReason(family, name, branch) -> 'Codex persona file .agents/ana.md was not found on main'; BOT_PERSONA_FILE_KEYS {'claude-code':'claudeCode', codex:'codex'}; BotPersonaFiles {branch, claudeCode, codex}; BotPersonaPreviewRequest {personaName, baseBranch?}; BotPersonaPreviewResponse = BotPersonaFiles; BotPersonaCheckResponse = BotPersonaFiles & {checkedAt, status: 'verified'|'missing', reason|null, bot: Bot}. New BotErrorCodes: persona_not_set 422, persona_missing 422, persona_check_failed 502.

ROUTES (admin only, same as other bot routes):
- POST /projects/:slug/bots/:id/check-persona (no body) -> 200 BotPersonaCheckResponse. Looks up BOTH files on bot.effectiveBaseBranch (re-resolves the repo default when that is null) through the Repository plugin host API, 10 s timeout + request signal. Records only the bot's own family via recordBotPersonaCheck (verified, or missing + reason naming file and branch); bot.status then carries that reason as its persona warning. Branch missing on the host -> recorded missing with reason 'Claude Code persona file .claude/agents/x.md could not be looked up: Branch 'develop' does not exist in owner/repo.'. Any other host failure (401, unavailable, timeout) -> 502 persona_check_failed, nothing recorded. No persona name -> 422 persona_not_set. No Repository plugin -> 422 repository_not_configured. If the bot changed during the check, nothing is stored (recordBotPersonaCheck guard) and the response still reports what was found.
- POST /projects/:slug/bots/check-persona {personaName, baseBranch?} -> 200 {branch, claudeCode, codex}, for an UNSAVED bot (create form); records nothing. Blank/null baseBranch = repo default. Missing branch -> both false. 400 invalid_request on bad name/branch/unknown field.

SERVICE (import from '../bots'):
- checkBotPersona(readDeps, bot, {signal?}) -> BotPersonaCheckResponse
- previewBotPersona(readDeps, projectId, personaName, baseBranch|null, {signal?}) -> BotPersonaFiles
- assertBotPersonaBeforeSession(readDeps, bot, {signal?}) -> BotPersonaCheckResponse when verified. Throws BotPersonaMissingError (extends BotError; code 'persona_missing', status 422, fields family, path e.g. '.agents/ana.md', branch; message 'Bot "Cody" cannot start: Codex persona file .agents/ana.md was not found on main'). Also throws BotError persona_not_set / persona_check_failed / repository_not_configured. readDeps = {...platform, secretsReader: platform.secrets}. Pass a freshly read bot (getBot) so the updatedAt guard lets the result be stored.

FOR 6.13: call assertBotPersonaBeforeSession first; map BotPersonaMissingError (or any BotError) to the typed failure reason, using error.message for display.
FOR 6.11: in the create form, 'check persona' calls POST /bots/check-persona with {personaName, baseBranch}; on an existing bot, POST /bots/:id/check-persona and replace the card with response.bot.
