title: Install dependencies into a new worktree and report the outcome
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Clanker's most painful open bug was worktrees without installed dependencies, which left agents unable to run tests. When a worktree is created, attempt to install the project's dependencies in it using the package manager the repository declares (detect from lockfiles; support pnpm, npm and yarn; prefer an offline install from the local store when possible, falling back to online), with a timeout. Record the outcome (installed, skipped because no manifest, or failed with the tail of the output) on the lease so the session's surface instructions can tell the agent whether dependencies are present.
acceptance_criteria: A worktree of a pnpm repo has node_modules after creation; a repo without a package manifest records skipped; a failing install records failed with output and does not block the session; tests cover detection.
notes:
Dependency installs into worktrees (6.13 and any worktrees UI build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Worktrees' (Dependencies paragraph). NO migration: columns came from 0013; schema file untouched; schema drift test + db:check clean.

MODULE apps/daemon/src/worktrees/install.ts (re-exported from worktrees/index.ts):
- detectPackageManager(dir): {kind:'install', plan:{packageManager, lockfile, commands: string[][]}} | {kind:'skip', reason}.
- installCommands(pm, {yarnBerry?}), installEnv(base?), dependencyInstallState(deps), installWorktreeDependencies(dir, {timeoutMs?, env?}) -> Promise<DependencyInstallResult {status, packageManager|null, output}> (type DependencyInstaller; never throws).
- Constants DEPENDENCY_INSTALL_TIMEOUT_MS = 300000 (5 min), DEPENDENCY_OUTPUT_TAIL_BYTES = 4096.

DETECTION (worktree root only): no package.json -> skipped 'No package.json in the worktree...'; package.json but no lockfile -> skipped (never installs unlocked: it would write a lockfile into the worktree). Lockfiles: pnpm-lock.yaml -> pnpm; package-lock.json / npm-shrinkwrap.json -> npm; yarn.lock -> yarn. Several lockfiles: packageManager field ('pnpm@9...', 'yarn@1.22+sha') picks among those PRESENT, else precedence pnpm > yarn > npm (stray package-lock.json is the usual extra). A packageManager naming a manager without its lockfile is ignored. Invalid JSON package.json still detects by lockfile.

COMMANDS (binary from the daemon's PATH, no shell): pnpm: 'pnpm install --offline --frozen-lockfile', on failure 'pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline'. npm: 'npm ci --prefer-offline --no-audit --no-fund'. yarn: Berry lockfile (contains '__metadata:') -> 'yarn install --immutable', else classic 'yarn install --frozen-lockfile --prefer-offline --non-interactive'. One deadline covers all attempts; on timeout the whole process group gets SIGKILL (detached spawn) and no further attempt runs; a missing binary (ENOENT) -> failed '<pm> is not installed or not on the daemon's PATH', not retried. stdin ignored.

ENV: AGENT_ENV_ALLOWLIST from acp/env.ts (PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL LC_CTYPE TERM TZ USER LOGNAME SHELL TMPDIR) + XDG_CACHE/CONFIG/DATA/STATE_HOME, PNPM_HOME, COREPACK_HOME, NVM_DIR, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, SSL_CERT_FILE/DIR, HTTP(S)_PROXY/NO_PROXY (both cases); fixed COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0, NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1, npm_config_update_notifier=false, NO_COLOR=1, FORCE_COLOR=0. Nothing else (no NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, CM_*, NODE_OPTIONS), so private registries needing a token env var fail -> recorded failed.

OUTPUT: '$ <command>' header per attempt + combined stdout/stderr + 'exited with code N' / 'timed out after Ns'; ANSI stripped; last 4 KB (prefixed '…' when cut). Skipped -> the reason string.

POOL (pool.ts): WorktreeLease gained dependencies: WorktreeDependencies|null = {status:'installed'|'skipped'|'failed', output: string|null, checkedAt: ISO} (null = never attempted), mapped from dependencies_status/_output/_checked_at.
- acquire({..., installDependencies? = true}): after the lease row is inserted and the project lock released, runs the install and records it (status/output/checked_at + updated_at). A failure (or an installer that throws -> failed 'Dependency install crashed: ...') is recorded, never thrown; the lease stays active.
- resume(holder, {installDependencies? = true}): reinstalls only when it re-added a vanished directory.
- pool.installDependencies(leaseId, {timeoutMs?}) -> Promise<WorktreeLease>: re-run on demand; not_found for unknown id; released lease returned untouched.
- Installs run OUTSIDE withProjectLock (they touch no git state and can take minutes). Deps: createWorktreePool({..., installer?: DependencyInstaller}) for tests; options: WorktreePoolOptions = Partial<WorktreeSettings> & { dependencyInstallTimeoutMs? } (platform passes options.worktrees through; no env var added).

FOR 6.13: lease = await worktrees.resume(holder) ?? await worktrees.acquire({...}) (acquire awaits the install, up to 5 min). Then surfaceInstructionsForBot(deps, bot, { branch: lease.branch, baseBranch: lease.baseBranch, dependenciesInstalled: dependencyInstallState(lease.dependencies), issueTrackerNote }) — installed -> true, failed -> 'failed', skipped/null -> false. lease.dependencies.output has the detail for logs/UI.

TESTS src/worktrees/install.test.ts (22): detection (no manifest, no lockfile, pnpm, npm x2, yarn classic/berry, tie-breaks, field without lockfile, bad JSON); dependencyInstallState; installEnv drops secrets; stand-in binaries on PATH: pnpm offline-fails-online-succeeds fallback, failure tail <= 4 KB, curated env (no NPM_TOKEN/CM_*), missing binary tried once, timeout kills grandchild via process group and no retry, skip runs nothing; real pnpm on temp git repos: pnpm repo with link: dep + lockfile + .gitignore -> node_modules/local-dep symlink, status installed, persisted, worktree still clean for reclaim; outdated lockfile -> failed with ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE output, lease active, listed, resumable; no manifest -> skipped; throwing installer -> failed; installDependencies:false -> null; resume of vanished dir reinstalls; pool.installDependencies re-runs. Real-pnpm cases skipIf pnpm is not on PATH.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint pass, typecheck pass (first run hit an in-flight src/slack/slack.test.ts error from 7.1, passed on rerun), test pass (116 files, 1104 passed, 3 skipped), daemon build pass; db:check ok.
RE-VERIFIED after resume (6.9/7.1 landed): root lint pass, typecheck pass, test 117/118 files pass (1 flaky timing failure in src/issues/watcher.test.ts 'within two seconds of bd create' under concurrent-agent load; passes on rerun with src/worktrees: 5 files, 65 tests), schema drift test + db:check ok. Root build FAILS outside worktrees: daemon tsdown AMBIGUOUS_EXTERNAL_NAMESPACES on SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_PATTERN (src/bots/validation.ts re-export vs packages/shared/src/bots.ts) from another agent's in-flight change; the daemon build passed with this bead's changes earlier in the session.
close_reason: Package manager detection + offline-first install recorded on the lease; 22 tests

title: Make bd inside a worktree read and write the project's main beads database
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack keeps beads on Dolt and expects issues to span branches; a bot that runs `bd` inside its worktree must land issues in the project's main checkout database, never in a copy inside the worktree. Find the mechanism `bd` 1.2.2 offers for pointing at another database (a database path flag, an environment variable, or a config setting) and produce the environment variables and/or config the daemon must apply to a bot session so every `bd` call from the worktree resolves to the main checkout's `.beads`. Provide that as a reusable function (given the project path, return the session environment additions) with a test that runs `bd create` from inside a temporary worktree and confirms the issue appears in `bd list` run in the main checkout. Document the mechanism and its limits.
acceptance_criteria: The test proves an issue created from a worktree appears in the main checkout's list and no `.beads` database is created inside the worktree; the helper is documented.
notes:
bd-from-worktree decisions (6.13 applies this). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Worktrees' (paragraph 'bd from a worktree').

HELPER apps/daemon/src/worktrees/bd-env.ts, exported from src/worktrees/index.ts:
  beadsEnvForWorktree(projectPath: string): Promise<WorktreeBeadsEnv | null>
  WorktreeBeadsEnv = { beadsDir: string (<resolved projectPath>/.beads), env: { BEADS_DIR: beadsDir, BD_NON_INTERACTIVE: '1' } }
  null when <projectPath>/.beads is not a directory. No config file is written into the worktree (a .beads/redirect file would itself create .beads in the worktree; not needed).

MECHANISM (bd 1.2.2, verified by experiment): BEADS_DIR = path of the .beads directory itself (NOT the repo root; repo root is ignored and discovery wins) and it takes precedence over discovery. BEADS_DB=<.beads>/embeddeddolt also works but BEADS_DIR is the documented one. bd ALSO natively resolves a git worktree to the main checkout's .beads via the git common dir ('bd worktree --help': worktrees share the db automatically), both when .beads is committed to the branch (worktree gets only tracked config.yaml/metadata.json/hooks, no db) and in --stealth repos (worktree has no .beads). BEADS_DIR makes it independent of that: works from a subdir, from a scratch dir outside any checkout, or if the worktree's .git link breaks. Config is read from the main .beads/config.yaml (branch copy ignored). With export.auto on, issues.jsonl export lands in the MAIN checkout's .beads (shows in main git status, not the worktree). bd init in the worktree refuses (db exists), with or without BEADS_DIR. Commits in the worktree run bd's git hooks (core.hooksPath = main .beads/hooks, absolute) and create nothing in the worktree.

ENV ALLOWLIST: src/acp/env.ts NOT edited on purpose. AGENT_ENV_ALLOWLIST is for variables inherited from the daemon's env; putting BEADS_DIR there would leak the daemon's own BEADS_DIR into agents (the issue runner strips it for the same reason). Session extras (startSession({ env })) already pass anything not denied; BEADS_DIR/BD_NON_INTERACTIVE are not denied. Test asserts curateAgentEnv({ base: { BEADS_DIR: '/elsewhere', BEADS_DB }, extra: result.env }) yields ours and drops BEADS_DB.

HOW 6.13 APPLIES IT: const beads = await beadsEnvForWorktree(sourcePath(project.source)); harness.startSession({ cwd: lease.path, env: { ...otherExtras, ...beads?.env }, ... }); surfaceInstructionsForBot(..., { issueTrackerNote: beads !== null, ... }). If the session runs in a write-confining sandbox, add beads.beadsDir as a writable root: Codex workspace-write sandbox (sandbox_workspace_write.writable_roots, via CODEX_CONFIG) / Claude Bash sandbox filesystem write allow; otherwise bd writes fail with permission errors. Claude's --allowedTools 'Bash(bd *)' is unaffected.

LIMITS: (1) one embedded Dolt store shared by the bot's bd calls and the daemon's runBd; access queues on its lock (8 concurrent creates, 4 from each side, all succeeded in ~2.5s), so a long-held lock (e.g. a long bd sql) delays the Issues page up to BD_TIMEOUT_MS 15s then tracker_timeout. (2) BEADS_DIR also wins if the bot cds into another repo with its own .beads: bd there writes to this project. (3) daemon's issue list cache (3s TTL) is not invalidated by bot writes; Issues page catches up on TTL/watcher (3.3). (4) Dolt auto-push (if configured on the main db) runs from bot writes too.

TESTS apps/daemon/src/worktrees/bd-env.test.ts (5): null without .beads; env shape + curateAgentEnv passthrough; real bd (skipIf !hasBd): createTempGitRepo + bd init in clone (committed .beads and --stealth variants) + git worktree add outside the clone, bd create in worktree with the env -> id in bd list --all in clone, no .beads/embeddeddolt|dolt in worktree, .beads presence unchanged, worktree git status clean; BEADS_DIR alone from a non-git dir (bd list fails without env, create lands in the clone).

VERIFIED: bd-env tests 5/5; root lint pass, typecheck pass, build pass (one rerun hit another agent's concurrent Nuxt build lock); root test: 990 passed, 3 failed, all in 6.2's in-flight files (config.test.ts loadConfig overrides + pool.test.ts settings cap: new idleTimeoutMs/reclaimIntervalMs fields; pool.test.ts release with deleted clone: 'active' vs 'released').
close_reason: Verified by agent; gates green except 6.2 in-flight files

title: Build the worktree pool with persisted leases and caps
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Bots must never work in the checkout Jack edits. Build a worktree pool in the daemon: the project's local path is the clone, and a bot session gets its own git worktree under the daemon's data directory on its own branch (named to identify the bot and session) cut from a given base branch after fetching it. Leases are rows in the platform database (project, holder kind and id, path, branch, base branch, state, timestamps) so a resumed session lands in the same path, which both CLIs need to find their conversation. Refuse to create a worktree on the base branch itself. Enforce a configurable cap on concurrent worktrees per project. Serialise all git operations on a clone with a per-project lock so concurrent sessions do not corrupt it. Provide acquire, resume (by holder), and release operations. Non-goals: reclaim policy and dependency installation (separate work).
acceptance_criteria: Acquiring a lease creates a worktree on a fresh branch from the base; resuming by holder returns the same path; a second acquire beyond the cap is refused; the main checkout's branch and status are unchanged after acquire and release; tests run against a temporary git repo.
notes:
Worktree pool decisions (6.2 reclaim, 6.3 deps, 6.4 bd, 6.13 bot run build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Worktrees'.

TABLE worktree_leases (apps/daemon/src/db/schema/worktree-leases.ts): id uuid PK, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, holder_kind 'session'|'bot', holder_id, path, branch, base_branch, state 'active'|'released' (default active), created_at, updated_at, last_used_at (touched on resume; 6.2 idle input), released_at nullable. Index (project_id, state); partial UNIQUE (holder_kind, holder_id) WHERE state='active'. MIGRATION apps/daemon/drizzle/0012_worktree_leases.sql (tag 0012_worktree_leases, after 0011_project_assignees).

MODULE apps/daemon/src/worktrees (index re-exports config/errors/git/lock/pool). startPlatform creates platform.worktrees = createWorktreePool({ db, paths, git?, now? }, { maxPerProject? }); PlatformOptions.worktrees; loadConfig().worktrees = resolveWorktreeSettings(env). No HTTP routes, no close() needed.

API (WorktreePool):
- acquire({ projectId, holder: { kind, id }, baseBranch, branchName? }) -> Promise<WorktreeLease>. Under the project lock: project must exist and sourcePath(project.source) must be a git repo (clone_unavailable 422); base + branch validated with git check-ref-format (invalid_request 400); refuses branch === baseBranch (base_branch_refused 422); refuses a holder that already has an active lease (lease_exists 409: call resume instead); refuses when active leases >= cap (cap_reached 409, never queued); refuses an existing local branch (branch_exists 409). Then: remote = 'origin' if present else first remote; if a remote exists 'git fetch <remote> <base>' (120s timeout; failure = fetch_failed 502, unknown remote ref = base_branch_not_found 422) and start point refs/remotes/<remote>/<base>; no remote -> refs/heads/<base> (must exist). 'git worktree add --quiet --no-track -b <branch> <path> <start>' (--no-track so a plain git push from the worktree is not refused; the agent publishes with git push -u origin <branch>). Lease row inserted after git succeeds; a failed add removes the directory (git_failed 500).
- resume(holder) -> Promise<WorktreeLease|null>: the holder's ACTIVE lease, same path; updates last_used_at. If the directory vanished: git worktree prune, then re-add on the lease branch (commits survive, uncommitted work is gone), or if the branch is gone too, cut it from the base again (fetch as in acquire). Released leases return null: the caller acquires anew.
- release(leaseId) -> Promise<WorktreeLease>: git worktree remove --force + prune (errors ignored), rm -rf path, state=released + released_at. BRANCH IS KEPT (6.2 decides when branches go). Idempotent; unknown id = not_found 404. Works when the clone is gone (just removes the directory and marks released).
- list(projectId, { includeReleased? = false }) -> WorktreeLease[] oldest first; get(leaseId) -> WorktreeLease|null.
- withProjectLock(projectId, fn) -> Promise: per-project async mutex (createKeyedLock in lock.ts; FIFO per key, keys independent, released on throw). acquire/resume/release run inside it. ANY other git command on a project's clone or worktrees (6.2 status/unpushed checks + removals, 6.3 installs if they touch git, 6.4) must run inside it; the lock is in-process only (one daemon).
- git(cwd, args, { timeoutMs? = 30s }) -> Promise<trimmed stdout> (createGitRunner({ env? }) in git.ts): spawn 'git' without a shell, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, LC_ALL=C, GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_COMMON_DIR stripped, own process group killed with SIGKILL on timeout (so git-remote-https etc. die too), 16MB output cap. Throws GitError { args, exitCode, stderr, timedOut }; ENOENT -> clear 'git is not installed' message.
WorktreeLease { id, projectId, holder: { kind, id }, path, branch, baseBranch, state, createdAt, updatedAt, lastUsedAt, releasedAt }. Errors: WorktreeError(code, message) with .status; WORKTREE_ERROR_CODES = invalid_request, not_found, lease_exists, branch_exists, cap_reached, base_branch_refused, base_branch_not_found, clone_unavailable, fetch_failed, git_failed (daemon-side only; add to shared if a route needs them).

PATH SCHEME: <paths.worktrees>/<project id>/<lease id> (project id, not slug: slugs can change). Parent dir created 0700. Deleting a project cascades the rows but leaves the directories: 6.2's startup reconcile should sweep worktrees/<project id> dirs with no project and worktrees/<project>/<lease> dirs with no active lease (git worktree prune in the clone afterwards).

BRANCH SCHEME: default cm/<holder kind>/<holder id>. Bots: botBranchName(botName, sessionId) = cm/bot/<bot name slugified a-z0-9->-, 'bot' if empty>/<session id>, so the branch names both the bot and the session. Constant WORKTREE_BRANCH_PREFIX='cm'.

HOLDER DECISION: 6.13 uses holder { kind: 'session', id: <agent session id> } and branchName: botBranchName(bot.name, session.id): a session's cwd is fixed at sessions.create and resume needs the same cwd, and one bot runs many sessions. 'bot' kind exists for a future bot-level worktree (e.g. persona checks) but nothing uses it yet. Flow for 6.13: lease = await worktrees.resume(holder) ?? await worktrees.acquire({ projectId, holder, baseBranch: bot.effectiveBaseBranch, branchName }); sessions.create({ cwd: lease.path, ... }); on thread close worktrees.release(lease.id) (or leave it for 6.2 reclaim).

CAP: CM_WORKTREES_PER_PROJECT (default 4, positive int) -> WorktreeSettings { maxPerProject }; counts ACTIVE leases per project; beyond it acquire throws cap_reached (no queue; the caller surfaces it).

TESTS apps/daemon/src/worktrees/pool.test.ts (18) against real temp repos (test-repo.ts createTempGitRepo: seed -> bare origin -> clone on main; pushToOrigin() commits via another clone so acquire must fetch; TEST_GIT_ENV pins identity and blanks global/system git config). Covers: fresh branch at the fetched origin/main commit, no upstream set, main checkout branch/HEAD/status unchanged across acquire+release with a dirty file, no-remote clone, bot branch naming, base==target refused, cap + release frees a slot, duplicate holder / existing branch, bad names / unknown project / missing base / non-git checkout, 3 concurrent acquires serialised, resume same path + last_used_at, resume recreates vanished dir on the lease branch (commit kept) and from base when the branch is gone, release keeps branch/removes dir/idempotent, release with a deleted clone, project delete cascade, GitError exit code + stderr + process-group timeout kill (sleeping pre-commit hook), keyed lock ordering, settings env parsing, platform wiring with the cap.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (103 files, 988 passed, 3 skipped), build pass; db:check ok; built daemon on a throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: '13 migration(s) applied', worktree_leases table + partial unique index present. Only non-worktree edit: src/config.test.ts expectation extended with worktrees: { maxPerProject: 4 }.
close_reason: worktree_leases, pool with per-project lock, cap, resume; 18 tests against real git

title: Reclaim idle worktrees safely and reconcile orphans at startup
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Worktrees accumulate; reclaiming one must never lose work. Add a reclaim pass to the worktree pool: a lease whose holder has been idle for a configurable period is reclaimed only if its worktree has no uncommitted changes and no commits that are not on the remote; otherwise it is kept and marked as holding unpushed work so the UI can show it. Releasing a lease explicitly follows the same safety rule. On daemon startup reconcile: leases whose paths are missing are closed, worktrees on disk with no lease are removed if clean and reported if not, and git's own worktree list is pruned.
acceptance_criteria: An idle clean worktree is reclaimed; one with an uncommitted file is kept and flagged; one with an unpushed commit is kept; after deleting a worktree directory by hand, startup closes its lease; tests cover each case.
notes:
Worktree reclaim + startup reconcile decisions (6.3, 6.11, 6.13 and any worktrees UI build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Worktrees' > 'Reclaim and reconcile'.

MIGRATION apps/daemon/drizzle/0013_worktree_reclaim.sql (after 0012_worktree_leases). Adds to worktree_leases: unpushed_work integer boolean NOT NULL default false, unpushed_reason text null, inspected_at text null (ISO). RESERVED FOR 6.3 (no logic here, 6.3 needs no migration): dependencies_status text null typed WorktreeDependenciesStatus = 'installed'|'skipped'|'failed' (exported from db/schema/worktree-leases.ts and worktrees/index.ts), dependencies_output text null, dependencies_checked_at text null (ISO text like every other timestamp in this table, not integer). The dependencies_* fields are in the Drizzle row type but NOT yet on the WorktreeLease TS type / toLease (6.3 adds them); acquire's insert sets them null.

SAFETY CHECK src/worktrees/inspect.ts inspectWorktree(git, path, { fetch? = true }) -> WorktreeInspection { path, exists, uncommitted: string[] (porcelain lines), unpushedCommits, remote, fetched, unsafeReason: string|null }. Rule: safe iff `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` is empty (gitignored files like node_modules do not count) AND `git rev-list --count HEAD --not --remotes=<remote>` is 0, where remote = origin else first remote, after `git fetch --quiet <remote>` (120s; failure -> uses last known remote-tracking refs, fetched:false). So a branch pushed under any name or merged into any remote branch counts as pushed; a branch never pushed counts commits beyond origin/<base>. No remote: `HEAD --not --exclude=<own branch> --branches` (commits must be on another local branch). Missing directory -> safe. Any git failure (not a repo, clone deleted, unborn HEAD) -> unsafe 'Cannot inspect the worktree: ...'. Reason format: '1 uncommitted change(s), 2 commit(s) not on origin'.

RELEASE: pool.release(leaseId, { force?, unusedSince? }). Under the project lock re-reads the row; unless force, inspects; unsafe -> lease stays state 'active', sets unpushed_work=true, unpushed_reason, inspected_at, updated_at and is RETURNED (no throw) — callers must check lease.state. Safe or force -> previous behaviour (worktree remove --force, prune, rm -rf, keep branch) + clears unpushed_work/reason. force is for an explicit human 'discard' only. unusedSince (ISO): return the lease untouched if last_used_at > it (reclaim vs resume race guard). WorktreeLease gained unpushedWork, unpushedReason, inspectedAt.

RECLAIMER src/worktrees/reclaim.ts startWorktreeReclaimer({ db, paths, pool, now?, log? }, { idleTimeoutMs?, reclaimIntervalMs?, reconcileOnStart? = true }) -> { ready: Promise<ReconcileReport|null>, reclaimIdle({ idleForMs? }) -> { reclaimed, kept, failed }, reconcile() -> ReconcileReport { closedLeases, removed, dirty: {path, reason}[], pruned }, close() }. Platform: startPlatform creates platform.worktreeReclaimer with PlatformOptions.worktrees (now WorktreePoolOptions & WorktreeReclaimerOptions); platform.close() calls worktreeReclaimer.close() before the DB closes. index.ts unchanged (loadConfig().worktrees carries the new settings). Interval is unref'd, skips a tick while a pass (or the startup reconcile) runs, stops between leases after close.
- reclaimIdle: active leases with last_used_at <= now - idle, oldest first, each via pool.release(id, { unusedSince: cutoff }); kept leases logged (warn) only the first time they become flagged; flagged leases are retried every interval, so a pushed branch is reclaimed on the next pass.
- reconcile (startup, does NOT block the server; ready logs 'Closed N worktree lease(s)...', 'Removed N...', warns per dirty dir): (1) active leases whose path is missing -> pool.release (released, branch kept); (2) every dir under paths.worktrees/<projectId>/ (also for deleted projects) with no active lease: empty -> removed; safe per inspectWorktree -> rm -rf + `git worktree prune` in its git-common-dir (works without the project row); unsafe -> left in place and reported in dirty; empty project dirs removed; runs under withProjectLock(dir name); (3) `git worktree prune` in every project's clone (archived included), errors ignored.

ENV: CM_WORKTREE_IDLE_TIMEOUT default 2h, CM_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_INTERVAL default 10m (duration Ns/Nm/Nh/Nd, >0, <=30d). WorktreeSettings = { maxPerProject, idleTimeoutMs, reclaimIntervalMs }.

UI CAN READ (no HTTP routes yet): pool.list(projectId) / get(id) -> lease.unpushedWork (show 'holds unpushed work'), lease.unpushedReason (human text), lease.inspectedAt (as-of), lastUsedAt (idle age), branch, path. Released leases cleared the flag. Dirty orphan directories (no lease) are only in the startup ReconcileReport/log, not persisted. A 'discard' action would call release(id, { force: true }) after confirmation.

FOR 6.13: last_used_at only moves on acquire/resume, so a long-running session holding a CLEAN worktree past CM_WORKTREE_IDLE_TIMEOUT can be reclaimed under it; call worktrees.resume(holder) per turn (it touches last_used_at). On thread close call release(id) and check state: 'active' + unpushedWork means kept until pushed. Startup reconcile releases leases whose directory vanished (resume would otherwise have recreated them); re-acquiring with the same branchName then hits branch_exists because release keeps branches.

TESTS src/worktrees/reclaim.test.ts (12) on real temp repos: inspect clean/untracked/unpushed/pushed, commits that reached the remote another way, no-remote clone, missing vs unreadable dir; release keeps+flags dirty, force releases, pushed releases + clears flag; reclaimIdle clean reclaimed, untracked kept+flagged, unpushed commit kept, fresh lease untouched, push then reclaimed, warn once; unusedSince guard; reconcile closes lease whose dir was deleted by hand, removes clean/empty unleased dirs (also under a deleted project id, project dir removed), reports dirty unleased dir, prunes a hand-deleted registered worktree; env parsing; platform: restart closes missing-path lease via ready, interval reclaims an idle lease. pool.test.ts: deleted-clone release now kept unless force; settings expectation extended. src/config.test.ts expectation extended.

title: Wire Create with Claude Code and Create with Codex to a seeded thread
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The Add Issue chooser already shows "Create with Claude Code" and "Create with Codex" when the matching chat capability is ready, through a placeholder integration point. Connect them: choosing one creates a thread with that agent and sends a seeded prompt asking the agent to interview Jack briefly about the issue he wants (title, type, priority, parent, acceptance criteria, dependencies) and then create it with `bd` in the project's checkout, replying with the new id. Open the chat panel on the thread and close the chooser. Because the Issues page watches `.beads`, the new issue appears in the list as soon as the agent creates it; no extra wiring is needed.
acceptance_criteria: Choosing Create with Claude Code opens a thread with the seeded prompt; after answering the agent's questions the new issue appears in the list without a reload.
notes:
Create with Claude Code / Codex (seeded issue-drafting thread). 5.1 Run buttons reuse the same flow.

FILES (apps/web/layers/issues/)
• app/composables/useIssuesCreateWithAgent.ts -> { options, starting, start(option) }. start: threads = useChatThreads(slug) (chat layer, auto-imported; capability -> chat is allowed) -> threads.create({ agentId: option.agentId, title: ISSUES_CREATE_THREAD_TITLE }) -> useChatPanel().showThread(option.agentId, thread.id) (opens the panel AND mirrors ?thread=<id> into the CURRENT page's URL via router.replace, keeping other query keys such as list filters; chosen over navigateTo(chatThreadLink(id)) because chatThreadLink's bare { query } drops other query keys) -> threads.prompt(id, issuesSeedCreatePrompt(registry.project.name)). Opens before prompting (like ChatAgentPanel's own send) so a refused prompt leaves the thread visible. Errors: toApiError(cause).message in an error toast titled 'Chat not started' (create failed, e.g. 409 not_ready, 403 not_granted) or 'Prompt not sent' (prompt failed; thread already shown). A second start while one is in flight is ignored (starting ref). AddButton.vue is unchanged (it closes the modal, then calls start).
• app/utils/issues-seed.ts: ISSUES_CREATE_THREAD_TITLE = 'Create an issue' (given at create, so the daemon does not retitle it from the first prompt); issuesSeedCreatePrompt(projectName) (blank name -> 'this project').
• test/unit/issues-seed.test.ts (3 tests).

SEED PROMPT (issuesSeedCreatePrompt('Acme')):
I want to add an issue to Acme. Its issues are tracked with the bd (beads) CLI in the current directory.

1. Interview me briefly: ask what the issue is about, then only what you still need, such as the title, type (task, bug, feature, epic or chore), priority (P0 critical to P4 backlog), parent epic, acceptance criteria and what it depends on. Keep it to a few short questions, and look up existing issues with bd (bd list, bd show) rather than asking me for ids.
2. If this project has a skill or guide for writing beads or issues, follow it. Otherwise write each issue so someone with no other context can do it: open with the problem and why it matters, say what to build without dictating how, state defaults and non-goals, and give acceptance criteria a person or a test can check.
3. Create the issue with `bd create --json` in the current directory, using --type, --priority, --parent, --deps, --labels, --description and --acceptance as needed. If my answers describe several issues, create each one.
4. Reply with the id of every issue you created.
('the current directory' is right because thread sessions run with cwd = sourcePath(project.source). The prompt says 'bd (beads)' once so the agent can find a beads-writing skill; UI labels still say 'issue'.)

FLOW: Add issue -> chooser -> 'Create with Claude Code' (modal closes) -> POST /projects/:slug/threads { agentId, title } -> panel opens on the thread, URL gains ?thread=<id> on the same page -> POST threads/:id/prompt { text: seed } -> agent asks its questions in the panel -> agent runs bd create in the checkout -> the daemon's .beads watcher fires 'changed' -> the list page's live refresh (3.6's useIssuesLiveRefresh) refetches -> the row appears. No daemon change.

FOR 5.1 (Run buttons): copy this composable's shape: useChatThreads(slug).create({ agentId, title: issue title or 'Run N issues' }) -> useChatPanel().showThread(agentId, id) -> prompt(id, 'Complete <id>. Check to see if you have any skills relevant to running beads.' / ids listed); same toast handling and starting guard. To land on a different page use navigateTo(chatThreadLink(id, projectPath(slug))) instead of showThread. Agent choice: issuesAgentCreateOptions-style filtering on registry.capabilities chat-claude-code/chat-codex ready && chat (or registry.agents).

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: tsx daemon 127.0.0.1:8150 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, random CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth), temp bd workspace (prefix xs) registered as project 'tmp' ('Tmp Tracker'), modules issues + agent-hub, claude-code plugin_instances row inserted healthy with config.claudePath = scratch fake claude (stream-json; answers the seed with 'What is the issue about?', then runs bd create --title=<answer> --json in its cwd and replies 'Created <id>'). Built web .output copied to scratch on :8151. Headless Chromium (playwright-core, chromium-1217), all PASS: Add issue -> Create with Claude Code -> chooser modal detached; panel open on /p/tmp/issues?thread=<id>; panel title 'Create an issue'; transcript starts with the seed and shows the question; daemon thread agentId claude-code, title 'Create an issue', session cwd = checkout; fake claude received the exact issuesSeedCreatePrompt('Tmp Tracker'); answering in the prompt bar -> 'Created xs-jx8'; the new row (href /p/tmp/issues/xs-jx8) appeared ~1.8s later with zero page loads; panel and ?thread= stayed; bd list has it; no console errors. Error path at 390px: plugin flipped unhealthy after the chooser rendered -> click -> toast 'Chat not started' with the daemon's not_ready message, no panel, no ?thread=. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (106 files, 1008 passed, 3 skipped), build pass.

With the chat panel open at 1280px the list row titles (issues-row-title) collapse to width 0 (3.6's Row layout, observed in the screenshot; not changed here). title: Record a run.started activity event with issue ids and a thread link
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The Overview feed should show when work was started on issues. When a run thread is created (from the issue detail or the bulk bar), append a `run.started` activity event to the project: title naming the agent and the issue ids, a link that deep-links to the thread in the chat panel, and the ids in the payload.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.

notes:
run.started activity event on run thread creation. DECISION: appended daemon-side inside ThreadService.create, because 2.12 has no HTTP route that creates events (by design), so a web-side append would need new surface; instead POST /projects/:slug/threads accepts optional issueIds (non-empty array of non-empty strings, else 400 invalid_request). Without issueIds (Create-with-agent, plain chats) no event. The web's useIssuesRun.run() just passes issueIds: [...ids] to threads.create (all 3 surfaces share it).
FILES: packages/shared/src/threads.ts (CreateChatThreadRequest.issueIds?, new chatThreadLink(slug, threadId) = /p/<slug>?thread=<id>, the same ?thread= the chat panel deep-links on any project page); apps/daemon/src/threads/routes.ts (optionalIssueIds + parseCreateThread, passes to service); apps/daemon/src/threads/service.ts (CreateThreadInput.issueIds, appendActivityEvent after the thread row is inserted); apps/daemon/src/threads/threads.test.ts (1 new test); apps/web/layers/issues/app/composables/useIssuesRun.ts (one-line issueIds).
EVENT SHAPE: type run.started; title '<agent label> run: id1, id2' (e.g. 'Claude Code run: rx-319, rx-bpr'); link '/p/<slug>?thread=<threadId>' (Overview page, panel opens the thread); payload { threadId, agentId, sessionId, issueIds: string[] }. Note the event is recorded at thread creation, before the prompt is sent; a refused prompt still leaves the event (thread is visible).

Headless Chromium 9/9 PASS. pnpm lint, typecheck, test (1257 pass), build all pass.

title: Render the transcript: text, reasoning, tool calls, usage and decision cards
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Raw events are not a transcript. In the chat layer render the session event stream as a conversation: user prompts, assistant text (markdown), collapsible reasoning, tool calls folded with their results (one block per call, status while running), usage and cost where the agent reports it, and decision cards for pending decisions: a permission card with Allow once, Always allow (shown only when the agent proposed a rule, listing it) and Deny, and a question card for agent questions with its options or a free-text answer. Answered and timed-out decisions show their outcome. Re-segment streamed text so partial chunks join cleanly. Decision answers go to the daemon's decision endpoint.
acceptance_criteria: Asking the agent to create a file shows a permission card; Deny leaves no file; a second attempt with Allow once writes it; tool calls show results; reasoning is collapsible; a timed-out decision shows refused.
notes:
Transcript rendering (7.4 Slack answers, 6.13/6.14 bot sessions, 10.x platform agent build on these). All in apps/web/layers/chat.

SEGMENTER (app/utils/chatTranscript.ts, pure, unit-tested in test/unit/transcript.test.ts):
• chatSegmentTranscript(rows: readonly ChatTranscriptRow[]) -> ChatTranscriptItem[]. ChatTranscriptRow = AgentSessionEvent | ChatTranscriptDivider { kind:'divider', key, label: string|null }.
• Items (all but divider carry key, seq (first row), at): prompt {text} (prompt rows and joined user text chunks); text {text} (consecutive agent chunks joined raw, ACP chunks are deltas); reasoning {text, endedAt (at of next item, null while it may grow)}; tool {toolCallId, title, toolKind, status pending|in_progress|completed|failed, running (open and turn not ended), input (rawInput), output: ChatToolOutput[] (text | diff {path, oldText, newText} | other {label}), rawOutput, locations} - one item per toolCallId, created at the first tool_call/tool_result and merged by later ones; decision {decision: Decision} at decision_opened, replaced (never mutated) by decision_answered/expired; error {title, message} from error (by phase), auth_required, exited with expected:false; turn {stopReason, usage: ChatTranscriptUsage|null} where usage = { tokens (turn_end usage: input/output/total/thought/cachedRead/cachedWrite), context {used,size} and cost {amount,currency} from the turn's latest usage row }; divider {label}. Hidden: permission_request, question, request_cancelled (their decision rows carry them), other, expected exited.
• DIVIDER HOOK (4.12 uses it): ChatTranscriptSession { id, divider: string|null, events } and chatTranscriptRows(sessions) -> rows with a divider row per session (key = session id; null label = boundary only). After a divider seqs and tool ids restart and item keys become '<session id>:<seq>', so keys stay stable as earlier sessions load in. ChatTranscript props: events, working, connected?, history?: ChatTranscriptSession[] (earlier sessions oldest first), divider?: string|null (above the current session); AgentPanel passes history from useChatSessionHistory + chatSessionDividers (4.12). Current part id is 'current'.
• Helpers: chatUsageParts(usage) -> ['1.2K in','56 out','1.5K / 200K context','$0.0123'], chatStopReasonLabel(reason), chatDecisionTool(decision) -> {title, kind, input, notes, locations}.

DECISIONS (app/utils/chatDecisions.ts, tests in test/unit/decisions.test.ts): chatQuestionForm(decision) -> { message, fields: [{key,title,description,type text|number|integer|boolean|choice|multi, choices [{value,label,description?}], freeText (from _meta['clanker-corner'].freeText, CHAT_DECISION_META_KEY), required}] }; chatQuestionAnswer(form, values) (typed, blank optional fields dropped) + chatQuestionComplete; chatDecisionOptions(decision, kind); chatProposedRule(option) (meta.rule, else label minus 'Always allow'); chatDecisionOutcome(decision, viewerId) -> {label, detail, tone}: 'Allowed once|Always allowed|Denied|Declined|Answered' + ' by you' (actorId = current user) + ' in Slack' (surface slack); expired -> 'Refused' (timeout/exited/refused) or 'Withdrawn' (cancelled) with expiry.message as detail.
COMPOSABLE: useChatDecisions(slug) -> { answer(decision, AnswerDecisionRequest) -> Decision|null, submitting, errors } (keyed by decision id). Deviation from the brief's useChatDecisions(slug, sessionId): POSTs sessionDecisionPath(slug, decision.sessionId, decision.id), since each Decision carries its session (history may hold several). The response is a receipt; the card's state comes from the stream rows, so web and Slack answers render the same.

COMPONENTS: ChatTranscript (Transcript.vue: items -> ChatModelEffortDivider | prompt bubble | ChatTranscriptMarkdown | UChatReasoning (collapsed after streaming, duration from endedAt) | ChatTranscriptTool | ChatDecisionCard | UAlert | turn line with data-testid chat-usage; auto-scroll only while pinned to bottom; children shrink-0 so cards are not squashed); ChatTranscriptMarkdown (chatRenderMarkdown in utils/chatMarkdown.ts: a copy of the issues layer's sanitised marked renderer, raw HTML escaped, only http/https/mailto/relative URLs; cross-layer import is not allowed and 3.8 kept its helper in layers/issues; a core helper could replace both later); ChatTranscriptTool (UChatTool card: icon by ACP kind, suffix waiting/running/failed/did not finish, input ('$ cmd' for command inputs, else JSON), result text, naive diff, rawOutput fallback); ChatDecisionCard (UCard, outcome badge, detail, inline error; uses useChatDecisions + useCurrentUser) -> ChatDecisionPermission (tool title/notes/input; Allow once, Deny, 'Deny with a reason' textarea -> explanation; Always allow section only when allow_always options exist, one row per proposed rule) / ChatDecisionQuestion (radio/checkbox/switch/number/textarea per field, free-text input for freeText choice fields, Answer disabled until complete, Decline = deny). Test ids: chat-decision (data-state, data-decision-kind, data-decision-id), chat-decision-tool, -allow-once, -deny, -always, -allow-always, -explanation, -outcome, -detail, -error, -message, -answer, -decline, chat-question-<key>, chat-tool (data-status, data-tool-call-id), chat-tool-output, chat-usage; data-kind on rows (prompt,text,reasoning,tool,decision,error,turn_end).
Removed chatEventSide/chatEventText (old raw transcript) and their tests; chatIsWorking stays.

FOR 7.4 (Slack): reuse the same contract: answer by option kind + optionId (never index); allow_always buttons only for offered options, labelled with chatProposedRule-style text (option.meta.rule ?? label); outcome wording/expiry reasons as chatDecisionOutcome; question forms as chatQuestionForm (freeText via _meta['clanker-corner']). These utils are web-layer only; lift them to packages/shared if Slack needs the exact functions.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: unit tests (chat layer 24). Live: daemon from source via a scratch launcher (startPlatform with acp.bins.claudeShim = a scripted ACP agent that streams reasoning, runs ls, asks permission and really writes the file on allow, asks a form question, reports usage/cost) on 127.0.0.1:7900, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR/CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth, CM_DECISION_TIMEOUT=20s, project alpha with agent-hub + healthy claude-code instance (sqlite); built web on :7901. Headless Chromium 38/38: prompt bubble; one tool block completed with input '$ ls' and result; reasoning collapsed after streaming, expands and collapses; streamed chunks joined into one markdown block, raw <b> shown as text; usage+cost on the turn line; 'create notes.txt' shows a pending permission card with Allow once/Deny and the proposed rule Write(notes.txt); tool waits; Deny -> 'Denied by you', no file, tool failed; second attempt Allow once -> 'Allowed once by you', file written, tool completed; 'touch late.txt' has no Always allow and after 20s shows 'Refused' + 'Nobody answered in time...', no file; question card -> dprint -> 'Answered by you', agent got the content; reload replays outcomes and folding; 390px no overflow; no console errors. Also deny with a reason (agent received the explanation) and Always allow ('Always allowed by you', Write(y.txt), file written). Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (118 files, 1122 passed, 3 skipped) pass; web nuxt build passed with these changes, but the final root pnpm build failed on another agent's in-flight packages/shared change (notifications.ts re-declares SLACK_MEMBER_ID_PATTERN / SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_PATTERN also exported by team.ts/bots: AMBIGUOUS_EXTERNAL_NAMESPACES in layers/team EditorModal.vue and daemon src/bots/validation.ts).
OPEN: no live Claude/Codex run (no logins); 'other' updates (plans, mode changes) are not shown; markdown helper duplicated from layers/issues.
close_reason: Transcript segmenter, markdown, tool blocks, decision cards; browser-verified 38/38

title: Add model and effort selection per thread
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack wants to pick a model and effort where the agent supports it. In the chat panel add selectors fed by the daemon's model and effort options for the agent (Claude Code exposes both through its CLI flags and session config; Codex exposes models discovered through ACP). Changing either starts a fresh session on the same thread, with a visible divider in the transcript noting the change. Default to the agent's own defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Changing the model mid-thread shows a divider and the next reply comes from a new session with that model (visible in the session record); the selectors are absent for an agent that exposes no options.
notes:
Model/effort per thread (web only; no daemon change).

COMPONENTS (apps/web/layers/chat/app/components):
- ChatModelEffort (ModelEffort.vue): two compact USelects (ghost, xs, icons cpu/gauge, menus open upward) for model and effort, each shown only when that list is non-empty. Props { options: ChatAgentOptions, model, effort, disabled? }; emits change({ model, effort }) only when something differs. The first item is 'Default model' / 'Default effort' (sentinel value CHAT_OPTION_DEFAULT 'agent-default' -> null, because select items cannot carry null). testids chat-model-effort, chat-model-select, chat-effort-select.
- ChatModelEffortDivider (ModelEffortDivider.vue): USeparator with the label, testid chat-session-divider. 4.11's Transcript renders it for 'divider' items.
- AgentPanel wiring: the ChatPromptBar #options slot holds ChatModelEffort when useChatAgentOptions(...).available. It is disabled while working or while a change is in flight. Draft (no thread yet): the choice is kept locally and sent in POST threads { agentId, model, effort }, and it resets when the thread id changes. Existing thread: useChatThreads().update(id, choice) (PATCH), then the current session's on-screen events go into the history cache, then useChatThread().refresh(), so the stream follows the new session id. Errors: thread_busy 409 -> warning toast 'The agent is still working'; anything else -> error toast 'Model or effort not changed'. The select shows the thread's value, so a refused change snaps back.

COMPOSABLES:
- useChatAgentOptions(slug, agentId) -> { options, available, status, refresh }. useAsyncData key chatAgentOptionsDataKey(slug, agentId) = 'chat-agent-options:<slug>:<agentId>' on GET chatAgentOptionsPath. A refused or failed lookup returns null, which hides the selectors.
- useChatSessionHistory(slug, sessionIds) -> { logs (sessionId -> events), remember(id, events) }. Client only. Loads each earlier session once over the existing session SSE route and closes the stream at the first 'status' event, which the route sends right after replaying the log. That works because a replaced session never runs again, so its log is final. remember() seeds the cache at switch time so nothing is fetched again.

DIVIDER MECHANISM: useChatThread().sessions (chat_thread_sessions, oldest first) -> chatSessionDividers(sessions, options) in utils/chatModelEffort.ts gives text per session id, e.g. 'New session with model Sonnet', 'New session with effort High' or 'New session with model default and effort Low', using option labels. ChatTranscript gained props history?: ChatTranscriptSession[] (earlier sessions { id, divider, events }) and divider?: string|null (above the current session). 4.11's chatTranscriptRows/chatSegmentTranscript turn those into 'divider' items. So a reload shows every session in order, with dividers between them. Unit tests: layers/chat/test/unit/modelEffort.test.ts (3).

CODEX: still exposes no options, so its selectors are absent. Not wired here because session.ts, manager.ts, families.ts and threads/* were under active concurrent edits and there is no logged-in codex-acp to verify against. Follow-up bead candy-mountain-v3-x8m.4.15 has the exact steps: capture configOptions in acp/session.ts, cache them per project in the manager, return them from the options route, apply them via CODEX_CONFIG {model, model_reasoning_effort} or set_config_option, and extend options.ts. The web side needs no change: the selectors appear when the lists are non-empty.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28:
- Setup: daemon from source on 127.0.0.1:8600 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, random CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth); project alpha with agent-hub, a claude-code instance (claudePath = a scratch fake claude that logs argv) and codex, both set healthy in sqlite; built web on :8601; headless Chromium 1217 via playwright-core.
- Selectors are shown with defaults. The first turn has no --model.
- Choosing Sonnet: divider 'New session with model Sonnet' appears, and the earlier rows stay above it. GET thread shows 2 sessions, the current posture is { flags: ['--model','sonnet'] }, and the next reply comes from a new process launched with --model sonnet.
- Effort High: a second divider, and the launch has --settings {"effortLevel":"high"}.
- Reload replays all 3 sessions in order with both dividers.
- Mocked 409 thread_busy -> toast, and the select reverts. Mid-turn the selects are disabled, and a direct PATCH gets 409 thread_busy.
- Choosing Haiku in a draft creates the thread with model haiku (no divider).
- Codex: no selectors. At 390px there is no horizontal overflow. No console errors other than the mocked 409.
- Re-ran after 4.11's new Transcript landed: all pass.
- Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (114 files, 1075 passed, 3 skipped), build: all pass. Earlier runs failed transiently on 4.11's in-flight DecisionQuestion.vue, on an issues-layer prefix lint error and on .nuxt missing during a concurrent build.

OPEN: switching model leaves the old session's process alive until the idle reaper closes it (daemon behaviour).
close_reason: Model/effort selectors with session dividers; browser-verified 23/23; Codex deferred to 4.15

title: Build the shared chat layer: rail, panel, threads and prompt bar
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Chat must be reachable from every page without leaving it. Build the shared `chat` Nuxt layer (infrastructure, not a capability) mounted by the dashboard layout: a rail on the right edge listing the agents the registry says the actor may chat with for the selected project (avatar, unread and working indicators, a "+" to start a thread), and a panel that opens from the rail with the thread list for the chosen agent, the transcript area (filled by separate work; render raw events as text for now), and a prompt bar with send and cancel. Threads are per actor and per project; switching project switches the rail. Support a deep link to a thread (query parameter) that opens the panel on load. The panel subscribes to the session's SSE stream with replay from the last seen sequence and reconnects on drop. Design the layer so bot agents and a native platform agent can appear later as entries in the same rail with no changes to the layer.
acceptance_criteria: The rail shows Claude Code and Codex for a project with both plugins healthy and nothing for a project without them; starting a thread and sending a prompt streams the reply; a reload mid-turn shows the full transcript and the turn finishes; the deep link opens the thread; lint passes.
notes:
Shared chat layer decisions (4.11 transcript, 4.12 model/effort, 5.1/5.2 seeded threads, 6.14 bots, 10.8 platform agent build on these). Layer: apps/web/layers/chat (prefix Chat; mounted by core via ONE line in app/layouts/dashboard.vue: <ChatDock /> after <slot /> inside the flex row).

COMPONENTS (layers/chat/app/components, auto-registered as Chat*):
• ChatDock (Dock.vue): the one mount point; computes rail entries once (useChatRailEntries) and runs useChatDeepLink, renders <ChatPanel :entries/> then <ChatRail :entries/> (fragment, both flex children of the dashboard row).
• ChatRail (Rail.vue): right-edge 3rem strip, data-testid chat-rail; hidden when there are no entries (no project, no chattable agents). Top '+' (chat-rail-new) = UDropdownMenu listing entries -> startThread(entry) (draft panel). One UButton per entry (chat-rail-entry-<id>, icon = entry.avatar) wrapped in UChip: shown when unread or working, color primary when working (data-working) else error (data-unread); tooltip '<label> (working|unread)'. Click toggles the panel on that entry.
• ChatPanel (Panel.vue): data-testid chat-panel; aside, fixed full-screen under md, static 26rem with border-l from md. Renders entry.panel (custom component, prop entry) or ChatAgentPanel. Escape closes. If the deep-linked entry is not (yet) in entries it falls back to { id, label: id, avatar: CHAT_DEFAULT_AVATAR, agentId: id }.
• ChatAgentPanel (AgentPanel.vue): default panel for registry agents. Header (chat-panel-title, chat-panel-back, chat-panel-new, chat-panel-close). Views: thread list (ChatThreadList) when no thread/draft; else ChatTranscript + ChatPromptBar. Draft = no thread yet: first send does POST threads {agentId} then POST prompt, then showThread. Mark-read: watch on [threadId, listed.unread] -> POST read whenever the shown thread is unread (on open and again after each turn end). Turn end (session.working true->false) -> threads.refresh() so flags/titles follow.
• ChatThreadList (ThreadList.vue): rows chat-thread-<id> with data-unread/data-working, title ?? 'Untitled thread', chatRelativeTime(lastActivityAt), spinner when working; UEmpty with 'New thread' action when empty.
• ChatTranscript (Transcript.vue) = THE 4.11 BOUNDARY. Props ChatTranscriptProps { events: readonly AgentSessionEvent[], working: boolean, connected?: boolean }. Today: one div per row (data-kind, data-seq) with chatEventText(event) (prompt/text/reasoning verbatim, every other kind as 'kind …json'), side via chatEventSide (user right / agent left / system mono), auto-scroll on new rows, 'Working' line (chat-working) while working, 'Reconnecting' when the stream dropped. 4.11 replaces this file only (and may drop the chatEvents.ts helpers); decision rows (decision_opened/answered/expired) already arrive in events, answer via sessionDecisionPath on the session id from useChatThread().session.
• ChatPromptBar (PromptBar.vue): UChatPrompt (data-testid chat-prompt lands on the textarea) + UChatPromptSubmit (chat-prompt-submit; status 'streaming' while working -> stop emits cancel). Props { working, error?: string|null }; emits send(text) (trimmed, ignored while working) and cancel. Named slot 'options' rendered inside UChatPrompt's #footer = THE 4.12 HOOK: put the model/effort USelects there; thread.model/effort are on the thread, options via GET chatAgentOptionsPath(slug, agentId) (no composable yet), change via useChatThreads().update(threadId, { model, effort }) which PATCHes, then useChatThread(...).refresh() -> new session id -> the SSE reopens from seq 0 (chat_thread_sessions history is in useChatThread().sessions for dividers). Expect thread_busy 409 while working.

COMPOSABLES (layers/chat/app/composables):
• useChatThreads(slug, agentId?) -> { threads (computed, filtered to registry.project.id and agentId, newest activity first), enabled, status, error, refresh, create({agentId,title?,model?,effort?}), prompt(id,text), cancel(id), markRead(id), update(id,{title?,model?,effort?}) }. One useAsyncData per project (key chatThreadsDataKey(slug) = 'chat-threads:<slug>'), unfiltered GET /projects/:slug/threads, run only when registry.agents is non-empty (awaits useProjectRegistry().loaded; watch: [enabled]); otherwise { threads: [] }. Every action patches the returned thread into the list so rail flags update at once.
• useChatThread(slug, threadId) -> { thread, session, sessions, status, error, refresh } (key 'chat-thread:<slug>:<id>', GET thread; null when no id; stale answers for another id are hidden).
• useChatSession(slug, sessionId) -> { events (shallowReadonly ref), status (SSE status event), connected, working (chatIsWorking(status)), close }. Client only (opens in onMounted, watches [slug, sessionId], closes on scope dispose). EventSource on '/api' + sessionEventsPath(slug, id, lastSeq); drops rows with seq <= lastSeq; on error closes and reopens itself with after=lastSeq after 1s doubling to 15s (the browser's own retry would replay from the original after). Never touches $api, so a dropped stream cannot trip useDaemonStatus.
• useChatPanel() -> { state: useState('chat-panel') { slug, entryId, threadId, draft }, open (entryId set AND state.slug === current slug), openEntry(id), startThread(id), showThread(entryId, threadId), showList(), close() }. showThread mirrors the id into ?thread= via router.replace (other query keys kept); showList/close/openEntry/startThread remove it.
• useChatDeepLink(): resets state when slug changes; on the client watches route.query.thread (immediate): GET thread -> showThread(thread.agentId, id); a failed GET (unknown id, agent no longer chattable) is ignored.
• useChatRailEntries() -> { entries, threads }: agents from chatAgentRailEntries(registry.agents, threads) (order 0) + chatRailSources() entries, flattened by order; polls threads.refresh() every CHAT_THREADS_POLL_MS 15s while enabled and the tab is visible.

RAIL ENTRY REGISTRATION POINT (6.14 bots, 10.x platform agent) in layers/chat/app/utils/chatRail.ts:
• ChatRailEntry { id (unique across sources; agents use the registry agent id, so namespace others e.g. 'bot:<id>'), label, description?, avatar (Iconify), unread?, working?, agentId? (registry agent id: the default ChatAgentPanel lists/prompts its threads), panel? (Component, markRaw; replaces the panel body, receives prop entry) }.
• chatRailRegister({ id, use: () => MaybeRefOrGetter<ChatRailEntry[]>, order? }) from a Nuxt plugin in the contributing layer, e.g. layers/bots/app/plugins/chat-rail.ts: export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => chatRailRegister({ id: 'bots', use: useBotsRailEntries })). The use() function runs once inside ChatDock's setup (so it may call useAsyncData/useSelectedProject and must be project-aware itself); order lower first, registry agents are 0, default 100. Capability -> chat imports/auto-imports are allowed by cm-layers; the chat layer never imports back.
• Platform agent (10.x): if it is a registry agent (RegistryAgent with family/avatar) it appears with NO work here; its threads go through the same thread routes. 10.8 start-chat action = useChatPanel().startThread(agentId) or showThread(agentId, threadId); navigate = navigateTo(chatThreadLink(threadId, path)).

DEEP LINK (5.1/5.2): '?thread=<threadId>' on any project page (/p/<slug>/...). Helpers in utils/chatLinks.ts: CHAT_THREAD_QUERY='thread', chatThreadLink(threadId, path?) -> RouteLocationRaw ({ query } on the current page, or { path, query }). Seeded flow: POST threads { agentId, title? } -> POST threads/:id/prompt { text } -> navigateTo(chatThreadLink(thread.id, projectPath(slug))) or, on the same page, useChatPanel().showThread(agentId, thread.id). Verified on /p/alpha/setup/plugins?thread=... (panel opens, page stays).

UTILS: chatEvents.ts (CHAT_WORKING_STATUSES queued/starting/prompting, chatIsWorking, chatEventSide, chatEventText), chatLinks.ts (above + chatThreadsDataKey/chatThreadDataKey, CHAT_THREADS_POLL_MS), chatRail.ts (above + CHAT_DEFAULT_AVATAR 'i-lucide-bot', chatAgentRailEntries, chatRailSources), chatTime.ts (chatRelativeTime). Unit tests layers/chat/test/unit/chat.test.ts (7).

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: daemon from source (tsx) on 127.0.0.1:7600 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, random CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth; projects alpha (agent-hub, claude-code instance with config.claudePath = a scratch fake claude speaking stream-json: echo, 'slow:<ms>' two-part reply, interrupt-aware; codex instance) and beta (agent-hub, no plugins); both instances set healthy in sqlite. Built web (.output copied to scratch) on :7601 with CM_DAEMON_PORT=7600. Headless Chromium (playwright-core 1.59 + chromium-1217): rail shows Claude Code + Codex (SSR too) and nothing on beta; unread chip from a thread finished while the panel was closed; '+' menu -> draft -> Enter sends: transcript shows prompt, 'echo: ...', turn_end; URL gains ?thread=; title = first prompt; shown thread is read again after its turn (daemon unread false); 'slow:9000' then reload: panel reopens from ?thread=, replay shows all rows incl. part one, Working shown, part two + turn_end arrive, seqs 1..7 unique/ordered; cancel via the stop button -> turn_end (cancelled); deep link on /p/alpha/setup/plugins opens the thread and keeps the page; back/select/Escape sync ?thread=; Codex entry opens its (empty) list; client switch to beta hides rail+panel; 390px: no horizontal overflow, panel full-width; zero console errors. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (103 files, 988 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass.

OPEN: no DELETE thread route (lists only grow); codex not prompted live (needs a logged-in codex-acp); Nuxt UI's UChatPromptSubmit types status via 'ai', which the web app does not depend on (resolves to any; harmless); the registration mechanism is a plugin-called function like core's registerPluginPanel rather than app.config, although layers/README.md still says app.config for chat contributions (README not edited: outside this bead's file scope).
close_reason: chat layer: rail, panel, threads, prompt bar, SSE replay/reconnect, deep link; browser-verified

title: Add the chat capabilities, chat agents in the registry and thread endpoints
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Chatting with Claude Code and Codex are capabilities in the Agent Hub, each requiring its plugin. Register `chat-claude-code` and `chat-codex` capabilities (module `agent-hub`, required plugin `claude-code` and `codex` respectively, no views, ladder none then chat with the chat flag on) each contributing one chat agent with an id, label, avatar and family. Extend the registry so a chat agent is listed for a project only when its capability is ready and the actor's rung allows chat. Add threads: a thread belongs to an actor, a project and an agent, wraps one session at a time (a new session when model or effort changes), has a title (first prompt, truncated) and tracks unread and working state server-side. REST: list threads for the project (with unread and working flags), create, get with its current session, mark read, send prompt (delegates to the session), and the agent's supported model and effort options where the family exposes them. Run every route through the rung gate. Working directory for these threads is the project's checkout path.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`. Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`. Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: With only the Claude Code plugin healthy the registry lists one agent; enabling Codex adds the second; creating a thread and sending a prompt produces a session whose working directory is the project path; unread and working flags change as expected; an actor below the chat rung is refused.
notes:
Chat capabilities + chat threads decisions (4.10 chat layer, 4.12 model/effort selector, 5.1/5.2 seeded threads, 6.14 bots in rail, 10.7 platform agent build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Chat threads'.

MANIFESTS (src/capabilities/manifests/chat-claude-code.ts, chat-codex.ts; appended to CAPABILITIES after bots, team; AGENT_HUB_MODULE gains {chat-claude-code, defaultRung 'chat'}, {chat-codex, 'chat'}): no views/jobs/tools; ladder none -> chat (chat: true). chat-claude-code requiresPlugins ['claude-code'], agent { id 'claude-code', label 'Claude Code', family 'claude-code', avatar 'i-lucide-sparkles' }. chat-codex requiresPlugins ['codex'], agent { id 'codex', label 'Codex', family 'codex', avatar 'i-lucide-square-terminal' }.
SHARED: AgentManifest gained optional family?: AgentSessionFamily and avatar?: string (Iconify name); RegistryAgent gained the same optional fields (registry/compute.ts copies them when present). Registry already listed agents only when rung.chat && ready; verified.

TABLES (src/db/schema/chat-threads.ts; MIGRATION drizzle/0010_chat_threads.sql, tag 0010_chat_threads, after 0009_agent_sessions):
- chat_threads: id PK, project_id FK projects CASCADE, actor_id (no FK, like agent_sessions), agent_id (registry agent id), current_session_id FK agent_sessions CASCADE, title null, model null, effort null (null = agent default), unread bool, working bool, last_read_at null, last_activity_at, created_at, updated_at. Indexes (project_id, actor_id, last_activity_at), (current_session_id).
- chat_thread_sessions: thread_id FK CASCADE, session_id FK agent_sessions CASCADE, model, effort, created_at; PK (thread_id, session_id). Every session the thread wrapped, oldest first (4.12 divider data).

SERVICE (src/threads, import from '../threads'): threadServiceFor(db, sessions) -> ThreadService (one per SessionManager via WeakMap, so building the app repeatedly never doubles subscriptions); createThreadService; chatAgents(capabilities) / findChatAgent(capabilities, id) -> { id, label, capabilityId, family } (agents with a family); threadTitle(text); familyOptions/assertModelEffort/chatPosture (options.ts). Sessions are created with sessions.create({ projectId, family, actorId, cwd: sourcePath(project.source), posture: chatPosture(...) }). Mounted in app.ts next to sessionRoutes when deps.sessions is set.

UNREAD/WORKING: the service subscribes to every thread's current session (on boot for all threads, on create/model change for the new one). On each status message it reconciles in a microtask (the manager passes through 'live' synchronously between starting and prompting): working = session.status in {queued, starting, prompting}; a working -> not-working change sets unread=true and bumps last_activity_at. So it also tracks prompts sent through /sessions routes, crashes, start failures and queued cancels. POST read clears unread and sets last_read_at. Prompt and cancel through the thread mark it read for the sender (including when the prompt fails, e.g. auth_required). On boot working is recomputed from the (reset-to-idle) session status without setting unread.

ROUTES (src/threads/routes.ts; shared paths in packages/shared/src/threads.ts: projectThreadsPath(slug, agentId?), projectThreadPath, threadReadPath, threadPromptPath, threadCancelPath, chatAgentOptionsPath(slug, agentId)). Every route except the unfiltered list runs requireCapability({ capability: <agent's capability>, chat: true }) via a per-request middleware resolving the agent; another actor's or another project's thread -> 404 not_found.
- GET /projects/:slug/threads?agent=<id> -> { threads: ChatThread[] } most recently active first (gated on that agent). Without ?agent: threads of every agent the actor may chat with; refused with the first chat capability's refusal ONLY when none is allowed (so 4.10 should call it only when registry.agents is non-empty, or per agent).
- POST /projects/:slug/threads { agentId, title?, model?: string|null, effort?: string|null } -> 201 ChatThreadResponse { thread, session, sessions }. No prompt in create: 5.1/5.2 seeded threads = POST threads { agentId: 'claude-code'|'codex', title?: issue title } then POST threads/:id/prompt { text: seeded prompt }, then deep-link the thread id.
- GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id -> { thread, session (current AgentSession), sessions: ChatThreadSession[] }
- PATCH /projects/:slug/threads/:id { title?, model?, effort? } -> same shape; model/effort change creates a NEW session (new current_session_id + chat_thread_sessions row); refused thread_busy 409 while working; title-only patch keeps the session.
- POST .../:id/read -> { thread }; POST .../:id/prompt { text } -> 202 { thread, session } (delegates to sessions.prompt; title set from the first prompt, whitespace collapsed, truncated to CHAT_THREAD_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH 80 with an ellipsis, unless given); POST .../:id/cancel -> { thread, session }.
- GET /projects/:slug/threads/agents/:agentId/options -> { options: ChatAgentOptions { agentId, family, models: ChatOption[] {value,label,description?}, efforts: ChatOption[] } }.
- Streaming: 4.10 uses the existing session SSE route sessionEventsPath(slug, thread.currentSessionId, after) (not chat-gated; any authenticated actor, as 4.6 built it). Pending decisions: whatever 4.7 exposes, keyed by the session id.
- Errors (ApiErrorBody): THREAD_ERROR_CODES invalid_request 400, not_found 404, unsupported_agent 422 (agent without a family), thread_busy 409; plus session codes (session_busy, auth_required, family_unavailable, agent_failed) and gate codes (not_enabled 404, not_granted 403, not_ready 409, capability_unknown 404).

MODEL/EFFORT CONTRACT (for 4.12):
- claude-code: models = CLI aliases opus/sonnet/haiku (resolve to the latest of each tier; a full 'claude-*' id is also accepted), sent as posture flags ['--model', m]; efforts low/medium/high sent as ['--settings', '{"effortLevel":"<e>"}'] (the CLI has no effort flag; it reads settings.effortLevel or CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; verified in the CLI source). Null = no flag = agent default. If chat ever adopts 6.7's posture (which requires exactly one --settings), merge effortLevel into that settings object.
- codex: options endpoint returns empty lists; create/patch with a model or effort -> 400. codex-acp 2.3.0 exposes models through ACP configOptions on session/new/load (config id 'model', category 'model'; 'reasoning_effort', category 'thought_level'; values are model ids, setter session/set_config_option or the legacy unstable_setSessionModel with 'model[effort]' ids). To support it, 4.12 must (a) capture configOptions from the newSession/loadSession response in the harness (acp/session.ts drops it today) and expose them (e.g. cache per project after the first session), and (b) apply the choice after start via setSessionConfigOption for 'model'/'reasoning_effort' only (never 'mode', per 4.3), or pass CODEX_CONFIG {model, model_reasoning_effort} through the launcher (families.ts). Then extend FAMILY_OPTIONS/chatPosture in src/threads/options.ts.

TESTS: src/threads/threads.test.ts (11) via startPlatform + fakeBins, healthy plugin instances written directly into plugin_instances.health: registry lists claude-code only, then both; developer with chat-claude-code none sees only codex; codex thread prompt -> session cwd = sourcePath(project) and live harness cwd = project path, working true mid-turn ('hang'), session_busy, cancel via manager -> working false + unread true, read clears, next turn unread again; cancel through the thread stays read; Claude with fake claude: options lists, create opus/high -> posture flags and launched argv contain --model opus --settings {"effortLevel":"high"}, title patch keeps session, model patch -> new session + sessions history, bad model 400; codex options empty + model refused, thread_busy mid-turn; validation/404s/per-actor lists; actor below chat rung -> 403 not_granted on list, filtered list, create, options, get/patch/read/prompt/cancel of own thread; not_ready after plugin turns unhealthy; restart clears working and resumes. src/registry/agent-hub.test.ts scoped to bots/team (filters capabilities/degraded) since the chat capabilities now share the module.
VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (93 files, 882 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass (first typecheck runs hit transient apps/web .nuxt missing and a src/decisions test type error from 4.7's in-flight work; both gone on rerun). Live: built daemon on 127.0.0.1:6619, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR + random CM_SECRETS_KEY, trusted-header auth (x-user): project + agent-hub; registry agents [] -> claude-code after sqlite health=healthy -> both after codex; unfiltered list with none ready 409 not_ready; options claude (3 models, 3 efforts) / codex (empty); create claude thread opus/high, prompt 'launch-env' (claudePath = fake claude fixture wrapper) 202 working:true title 'launch-env' cwd = project path; after the turn list shows working false unread true; session SSE replay prompt/text/turn_end; argv in the log had --model opus --settings {"effortLevel":"high"}; read -> unread false; PATCH model sonnet -> new session, 2 sessions; codex model 400; user 'dev' (role developer, chat-claude-code none): registry agents ['codex'], create claude 403 not_granted, options 403, admin's thread 404, codex thread 201, list only codex; SIGTERM exit 0, no agent processes left.

title: Add the login panels for the Claude Code and Codex plugin instances
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The Plugins page can host a type-specific panel on an instance; the two agent plugins need one for their login flows. For Claude Code: a Start login button that shows the returned URL to open, a field to paste the code, the resulting status, an alternative "paste a setup token" form, and Revoke. Login panels for claude-code and codex (core, apps/web/app).
