title: Define capability manifests validated at daemon boot
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

In Digital Hub a capability had no single home: around eight hand-maintained lists had to agree on it. In v3 the server-side manifest is the only declaration of a capability, and everything else is derived from it. Define the manifest shape in the shared contract package and a definition helper in the daemon: a capability has an id, a label, a description, views (id, label, icon, path relative to the project), agents it contributes, tools (with an optional scope), jobs, the plugin type ids it requires, and a ladder of rungs. A ladder starts at a rung named `none`, rungs are monotonic (each grants a superset of the previous rung's views, tools and chat flag), and every view and tool a rung references must exist in the manifest. The daemon holds a registry of capabilities and validates all manifests at boot (unique ids, agents, tools, views and paths across capabilities); a bad manifest must stop the daemon with a clear message. Register no real capability yet beyond what tests need.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover: ladder not starting at `none` is rejected; a non-monotonic ladder is rejected; a rung referencing an unknown view or tool is rejected; duplicate ids across manifests are rejected; a valid manifest loads; the daemon refuses to boot on a bad manifest.
notes:
Capability manifest decisions (later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Capabilities".

SHARED TYPES: import from '@candy-mountain/shared' (packages/shared/src/capabilities.ts).
- CAPABILITY_IDS (as const: overview, issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent), CapabilityId, isCapabilityId().
- NONE_RUNG = 'none'. MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN /^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[-_.][a-z0-9]+)*$/ for view/agent/job/tool/rung/plugin-type ids. VIEW_PATH_PATTERN: lowercase slug segments joined by '/', no leading/trailing slash, '' = project home (web route /p/<slug>/<path>).
- ViewManifest<V> {id,label,icon,path}; AgentManifest {id,label,description}; JobManifest {id,label,description}; TOOL_KINDS ['tool','operation'], ToolManifest<T> {id, kind, scope?: ToolScopeManifest {dimension, levels (ascending, last widest)}}; ToolPermission {scope?}; Rung<V,T,R> {name,label,description, views: V[], chat: boolean, tools: {[toolId]?: ToolPermission}}; CapabilityManifest<V,T,R> {id: CapabilityId, label, description, views, agents, jobs, requiresPlugins: string[] (plugin type ids), tools, ladder}; AnyCapabilityManifest.

DAEMON MODULE apps/daemon/src/capabilities (index.ts re-exports):
- manifest.ts: defineCapability<const V,const T,const R>({...ladder: readonly [Rung<V,T,'none'>, ...Rung<V,T,R>[]]}): CapabilityManifest<V,T,R|'none'>. Type-level: first rung must be 'none', rungs may only name declared view/tool ids. Runtime: assertCapability(cap) throws CapabilityManifestError (name 'CapabilityManifestError'). Also getRung(cap,name), rungIndex(cap,name) (0 = none, -1 unknown), topRung(cap), duplicates().
- Per-manifest checks: id in CAPABILITY_IDS; non-empty label/description; ids match pattern and are unique per kind (view/agent/job/tool/rung/required plugin); views need label+icon+valid unique path; tool kind valid, scope has dimension + unique non-empty levels; ladder starts at 'none' which grants nothing; rungs reference only own views/tools; chat needs >=1 agent; scoped tool grants must name a level, unscoped must not; monotonic: each rung keeps every view, chat, tool and scope level (>=) of the rung below.
- registry.ts: createCapabilityRegistry(manifests, { pluginTypeIds? }) -> CapabilityRegistry { list() (registration order, frozen), byId(id) -> manifest|undefined, get(id) -> manifest (throws Error "Capability 'x' is not registered."), has(id) }. assertManifests(manifests, opts) re-runs assertCapability on each (manifests may not have come through defineCapability) then checks uniqueness across manifests of capability ids, agent ids, tool ids, job ids, view ids, view paths. pluginTypeIds hook: when given (bead 2.4 should pass the plugin type registry ids), every requiresPlugins entry must be known; omitted now, so plugin refs are only format-checked.
- Error messages read like: "Capability 'uptime': the ladder must start with a rung named 'none'." / "Capability 'uptime': rung 'full' hides view(s) 'uptime-home' that 'read' shows; rungs must be monotonic." / "Capability 'uptime': rung 'full' grants unknown tool 'ghost.tool'." / "Duplicate view path(s) across capabilities: 'overview' (overview, issues)." / "Unknown capability id 'billing'; add it to CAPABILITY_IDS in @candy-mountain/shared first."

REGISTERING A CAPABILITY (file-per-capability): write apps/daemon/src/capabilities/manifests/<capability id>.ts exporting e.g. `export const issuesCapability = defineCapability({...})` (import defineCapability from '../manifest'), then append it to CAPABILITIES in manifests/index.ts (currently empty: no real capability registered). Manifests are pure data (tool ids are strings), so they import no feature code. A bad manifest throws on import (defineCapability) or in createCapabilityRegistry.

BOOT WIRING: startPlatform(dataDir, { capabilities = CAPABILITIES }) builds the registry FIRST, before ensureDataDir/DB, so a bad manifest throws CapabilityManifestError and leaves nothing on disk; index.ts lets it propagate (uncaught -> exit 1 with the message). Platform.capabilities: CapabilityRegistry. index.ts logs "N capability manifest(s) registered" and passes it to createApp. createApp deps gained optional `capabilities?: CapabilityRegistry` (defaults to createCapabilityRegistry(CAPABILITIES)); routes read c.var.capabilities (AppVariables.capabilities). No DB table/migration (none needed: manifests are code).

TESTS: src/capabilities/fixtures.ts: fixtureCapability(id, requiresPlugins?) -> valid manifest with ids prefixed by the capability id (views '<id>-home' path '<id>' and '<id>-admin' path '<id>/admin', agent '<id>-agent', job '<id>-job', tools '<id>.read' and scoped '<id>.search' (dimension project, levels own/all), ladder none/read/full with chat on full), so different-id fixtures never collide; cloneManifest(cap) -> deep mutable copy to break in tests. Build a registry with createCapabilityRegistry([fixtureCapability('overview'), fixtureCapability('issues')]) or boot with startPlatform(temp.root, { capabilities: [...] }). Test files: manifest.test.ts (per-manifest rules incl. @ts-expect-error compile-time checks), registry.test.ts (lookup, cross-manifest dups, plugin hook, real CAPABILITIES list loads), boot.test.ts (bad manifest / colliding manifests refuse startPlatform with no data dir created; valid one reaches c.var.capabilities).

VERIFIED: 31 capability tests; root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (137), build pass. Built daemon boots and logs '0 capability manifest(s) registered'; a tsx probe calling startPlatform with a bad manifest exited 1 with CapabilityManifestError and created no data dir.
close_reason: Manifest types, defineCapability, boot-validated registry; gates green

title: Add module definitions and role grants with rung resolution
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A module groups capabilities for enablement and navigation, and grants decide what a role may do. Declare the three modules in the daemon with their member capabilities and a default rung each (members are filled in by later work; an empty module is valid and renders nothing). A capability may belong to several modules. Store grants in the platform database: a grant gives a role either a module or a standalone capability at a rung per capability. Resolve permissions per actor: the admin role always resolves to the top rung of every ladder; otherwise an actor's rung for a capability is the highest across all grants of all their roles; nothing granted means `none`. Expose grants over REST (list, set) for the admin only, and seed the admin's grants on first start. Resolution must fail closed on any error.

Shared names: Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`. Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover: admin resolves to the top rung; two grants at different rungs resolve to the higher; an ungranted capability resolves to `none`; a capability in two modules resolves correctly; grants persist across restarts.
notes:
Modules and grants decisions (2.3, 2.6, 2.10 rely on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Modules and grants'.

SHARED TYPES (@candy-mountain/shared)
- modules.ts: MODULE_IDS ['issues','agent-hub','operations'], ModuleId, isModuleId(), ModuleMember { capabilityId: CapabilityId, defaultRung: string }, ModuleDefinition { id, label, description, icon, capabilities: readonly ModuleMember[] }.
- grants.ts: GRANTS_PATH '/grants', GRANT_TARGET_KINDS ['module','capability'], GrantTarget = {kind:'module',id:ModuleId} | {kind:'capability',id:CapabilityId}, CapabilityRungs = Partial<Record<CapabilityId,string>> (the resolution result shape), RoleGrant { role (slug), target, rungs: CapabilityRungs, createdAt, updatedAt }, RoleRungs { role, name, rungs }, GrantListResponse { grants, roles: RoleRungs[] }, SetGrantRequest { role, target, rungs }, GrantResponse { grant }, GRANT_ERROR_CODES / GrantErrorCode.
- auth.ts additions: FORBIDDEN_ERROR_CODE 'forbidden', isAdmin(actor) (roles includes ADMIN_ROLE).

DAEMON
- src/modules: definitions.ts MODULES = [ISSUES_MODULE, AGENT_HUB_MODULE, OPERATIONS_MODULE], all with capabilities: [] today (add members as { capabilityId, defaultRung }). registry.ts createModuleRegistry(modules, capabilityRegistry) -> ModuleRegistry { list(), byId(), get() (throws), has(), withCapability(capId) }; assertModules throws ModuleDefinitionError on unknown/duplicate module id, empty label/description/icon, unregistered member capability, default rung not on that ladder, duplicate member. Built in startPlatform right after the capability registry, before touching disk. Platform.modules; AppDeps.modules? (defaults to createModuleRegistry(MODULES, capabilities)); c.var.modules. startPlatform option modules?: ModuleDefinition[] for tests. index.ts logs 'N module(s) registered'.
- TABLE role_grants (src/db/schema/role-grants.ts): id uuid PK, role_id FK roles ON DELETE CASCADE, target_kind 'module'|'capability', target_id, rungs JSON {capabilityId: rung}, created_at, updated_at; unique index role_grants_role_target_idx (role_id, target_kind, target_id).
- MIGRATION: drizzle/0004_role_grants.sql (tag 0004_role_grants).
- src/grants: AccessDeps { db, capabilities, modules } (c.var and Platform both satisfy it). grants.ts listGrants(db, roleSlugs?), findGrant(db, role, target), normaliseGrant(deps, req), setGrant(deps, req) (upsert per role+target; module grants store EVERY member explicitly, missing ones filled with defaultRung; capability grants must name exactly their own capability), parseSetGrant(body). errors.ts GrantError(code) with status.
- RESOLVER src/grants/resolve.ts: resolveActorRungs(deps, actor) / resolveRoleRungs(deps, roleSlugs) -> CapabilityRungs with an entry for EVERY registered capability. Admin role -> topRung of every ladder (no DB read). Else per capability the highest rungIndex across all grants of all roles; module grant member rung = grant.rungs[cap] ?? member.defaultRung (so members added to a module later get their default); stale rung names, unregistered capabilities/modules are ignored (none); any thrown error -> console.error + everything 'none' (fail closed). rungOf(rungs, capId) -> rung or 'none'. Bead 2.6: call resolveActorRungs(c.var, c.var.actor) in the registry route and use rungOf/getRung(cap, rung) for views/chat/tools. Module 'held' by an actor is not modelled separately: derive from per-project enablement (2.3) plus the members' rungs.
- SEED src/grants/seed.ts seedAdminGrants(deps): runs in startPlatform after seedAuth on every start; inserts an admin module grant for each module the admin lacks (rungs = each member's top rung, {} today); onConflictDoNothing so edits are never overwritten. Not run by openTestDatabase (tests call it).
- ADMIN GUARD src/auth/admin.ts requireAdmin(): Hono middleware, mount after auth with app.use(requireAdmin()); non-admin -> 403 { error: { code: 'forbidden', message: 'Only the admin may do this' } }. Exported from src/auth.

ROUTES (admin only; browser /api/grants)
- GET /grants -> 200 GrantListResponse { grants (ordered role slug, kind, id), roles: [{ role, name, rungs }] } where rungs is the resolved rung of every registered capability for that role alone (admin = all top). Bead 2.10 can render this directly.
- PUT /grants SetGrantRequest { role, target: { kind, id }, rungs } -> 200 { grant }. rungs optional for modules ({} = all defaults). Errors: invalid_request 400 (bad JSON/shape), role_not_found 422, target_not_found 422 (unregistered module/capability), invalid_rung 422 (rung not on ladder, capability not in module, capability grant naming another capability). No DELETE: revoke by setting rungs to 'none'.

TESTS: src/modules/registry.test.ts, src/grants/{resolve,grants,routes}.test.ts (26 tests) with fixtures in src/grants/test-access.ts (TEST_CAPABILITIES issues/uptime/deployments/team, TEST_MODULES with uptime in two modules, testAccess(db), addRole(db, slug)).

VERIFIED: root lint, typecheck, build pass; root test 506/507, the one failure is src/issues/watcher.test.ts (another bead's in-flight timing test). Live: built daemon on 5622 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: 5 migrations applied, '3 module(s) registered', GET /grants shows 3 seeded admin module grants; PUT ok and error codes 400/422; restart -> 0 migrations, same 3 grants, edited updatedAt kept. trusted-header on 5623: no header 401, non-admin 'jack' 403 on GET and PUT, admin PUT 200.
close_reason: Modules, role_grants, resolver, admin-only /grants; verified incl. restart

title: A capability that needs a newer platform than the product has is refused at boot, by name
description:
Context: two repositories on this machine, both Jack's (the owner and only developer). The base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) publishes the platform as @crab-shack/platform-* packages at one shared version, all still 0.x. The capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) publishes sixteen packages, each at its own version, that products install beside the platform: capabilities (cap-*), connections (plugin-*), an ACP shim and test support. Each capability package names the platform packages as peer dependencies with the range 0.x, states the SDK major it targets, and is developed and tested against the one exact platform version the capabilities repository pins (0.8.2 at the time of writing). When a product's daemon boots, the platform refuses a capability whose SDK major is not its own, naming it. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in both repositories Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and in both that push is a release; follow AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md in each.

The problem. Nothing stops a capability from being installed into a product whose platform is too old for it. While everything is 0.x the SDK major is 0 for every release, so the boot check passes, and the peer range 0.x accepts any release. But the platform adds things capabilities rely on between minors: 0.8.0, for instance, began telling a plugin type's health check and instance actions the product's name, and two connections (plugin-netlify and plugin-repository, from 0.1.1) now build their User-Agent from it. In a product on an older platform those paths receive no name and fail at run time, in a health check, long after install and boot looked fine. Candy Mountain is such a product today (it pins 0.5.0) and is about to install these packages. The rule the published packages were shaped by is that a capability installed without something it needs fails at install or at boot with a message naming what is missing, never silently; a platform that is too old is the one case that still slips through.

What to do. Make a capability that needs a newer platform than the product has fail early and by name: at install where the package manager will really refuse it, and at boot in any case, since pnpm reports a peer that is out of range as a warning by default. Decide where the minimum is stated and how it is kept true as the capabilities repository moves its pin, so that it costs a capability author nothing to remember; say what a pin move then requires of each package. If the answer needs the platform to check something at boot that it does not check today, that is a change in the base as well as in the capabilities repository.

Because this sets a rule every future capability and every pin move will follow, stop after you have looked at both repositories and report the rule you propose, with what it would publish (which packages, which versions) and what it would do to a product already on an old platform, before building it.

Not in this bead: moving any product's platform pin, and the behaviour once the platform reaches 1.0, beyond not making it worse.
acceptance_criteria:
- A product on a platform older than a capability needs is refused at boot with a message naming the capability, the platform it needs and the platform it found; shown with a fixture product on an old release and one of the published packages.
- The same product on a platform new enough boots as it does today.
- The rule for stating the minimum, and what a pin move requires, is written where capability authors and agents will read it in both repositories.
- The gates are green in each repository changed, and the releases that carry the change are named in the closing note.
notes: Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from 94z.6.3 (platform 0.10.0): pnpm platform-list marks capabilities a product cannot take (another SDK major today). 'Needs a newer platform than this product has' belongs beside that mark: marks() in packages/platform-config/list/index.mjs. platform-add refuses what the list marks, so the same minimum should make platform-add refuse too.

title: Base: a product's daemon finds its product file whatever directory it is started from
description:
Context: the base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) publishes the platform that products are built on. A product is described by a product.yaml at its repository root; the product's daemon app finds that file at start by asking the platform to look upwards from the daemon's own module location. The capabilities repository (/home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) and Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives) are products that do this. Run bd commands from Candy Mountain and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the base Jack (the owner and only developer) has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and that push is the release; follow AGENTS.md in the base.

The problem. An agent starting the capabilities repository's daemon from a directory outside that repository reported that the daemon could not find product.yaml and threw. Its account: the helper that finds the product file (findProductFile), when handed a module's URL as a string (import.meta.url, which is what the generated daemon app passes), treats that string as a relative path, so the search really starts from the process's working directory and only succeeds when the daemon happens to be started from inside the repository. Handing it a URL object works. The same code is in the base at 0.8.0. Treat the account as a lead and reproduce it first.

Why it matters. A product's daemon is started from elsewhere in ordinary use: by a service manager, by a CLI installed on the PATH, by an agent running a script from a scratch directory. Each then fails at boot with a message about a missing product file although the file is where it should be, or worse, finds a different product's file because the working directory happens to be inside another product.

What to do. Make the product file be found from where the daemon's code is, whatever the working directory, for every form of location the helper accepts and for what the generator writes into a new product's daemon app. If it is not the cause described, find the real one.

A product started from inside its own repository must behave exactly as it does today.
acceptance_criteria:
- The closing note states what happened before the change when a generated product's daemon was started from a directory outside the product, with the command that showed it.
- Tests show the product file is found from the module's location when the working directory is elsewhere, including when the working directory is inside a different product, for each form of location the helper accepts.
- A freshly generated product's daemon starts from a working directory outside the product.
- The base's four gates are green and the release containing the change is in the registry; the closing note names the version and says whether a product on an older platform can work round it.

title: Capabilities: each package documents how its daemon half behaves
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ (capabilities cap-*, connections plugin-*, the Claude Code ACP shim and shared test support) that were moved out of the product Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3, where this bead tracker lives). Its root README is a map: what the repository is, a table of the packages, and the commands. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain; run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow AGENTS.md there.

The problem. How each capability's daemon half behaves (its routes, its background work, what it stores, what it expects of the connections it uses, its environment variables) is written down in one place only: Candy Mountain's apps/daemon/README.md, about 640 lines, written when the capabilities lived in Candy Mountain. The capabilities have left, that file did not come with them, and Candy Mountain is about to delete its copies of the packages. Someone working on a capability in the capabilities repository, or choosing one for a new product, has the code and a one-line description and nothing between.

What to do. Give that knowledge a home in the capabilities repository, next to the code it describes, so that each package explains its own behaviour and the root README leads to it. Take the content from Candy Mountain's file as it is at its current commit, but check every statement you carry over against the code as it is now in the capabilities repository: the packages have been renamed to @crab-shack, they read the product's name from the platform, and their identifiers are derived from it. Carry over what is true of a capability; leave behind what is about Candy Mountain as a product (its apps, its deployment, its own settings). Where the file describes something the platform does rather than a capability, point to the base's documentation instead of repeating it.

Do not change any code, and do not change Candy Mountain's file.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every capability and connection package that the Candy Mountain file describes has its behaviour documented in the capabilities repository, reachable from the root README.
- The bead's closing note lists each section of the Candy Mountain file and where it went, or why it was left behind.
- No carried-over statement names @candy-mountain packages or describes behaviour the current code does not have; the closing note lists the statements that had to be corrected.
- Lint is green, and Candy Mountain's working tree is untouched.
notes:
94z.3.11: package READMEs written on branch 94z-3-11 (worktree /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities-94z-3-11), one commit, lint green; READY TO LAND, WAITING FOR 94z.4.1 (not yet on origin/main). Source: apps/daemon/README.md at Candy Mountain 8f4240e, untouched.

WHERE EACH SECTION WENT (source section -> destination)
- Intro, Shape, Adding or removing a capability, Development-only capabilities: left behind. Candy Mountain's distribution wiring (its apps, product package, definitions list); the capabilities repository's root README ("New capabilities and connections") and the platform's cap-template README cover the equivalent.
- Configuration table: CM_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT, CM_SESSION_MAX_LIVE, CM_DECISION_TIMEOUT -> cap-acp. CM_UPTIME_HISTORY_MAX, CM_UPTIME_HISTORY_MAX_AGE -> cap-uptime. CM_WORKTREES_PER_PROJECT, CM_WORKTREE_IDLE_TIMEOUT, CM_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_INTERVAL -> cap-bots, as Candy Mountain wiring (see corrections). CM_DAEMON_HOST/PORT, CM_DATA_DIR, CM_SECRETS_KEY, CM_AUTH_*, CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD, CM_WEB_URL: platform variables, left behind (root README already covers the dev distribution's).
- Product settings -> cap-bots "Settings" (the mechanism is the platform's, linked).
- Data directory, Database, Adding a table, Using the database, Secrets, Mastra, Workspaces and organisations, Auth (+ Password strategy, Adding a strategy), Capabilities, Modules and grants, Workspace modules, Registry, Platform settings, Platform agent: platform, left behind; READMEs link to platform-daemon's README and docs/capability-authors.md instead. Per-capability pieces were carried (workspace facts, activity event types).

Per-type sections: Repository -> plugin-repository, Heroku -> plugin-heroku, Netlify -> plugin-netlify, Claude Code -> plugin-claude-code, Codex -> plugin-codex. The slack type (not in the source) added to plugin-slack.
- Bots, Bot sessions, Bot posture, Slack routing, Slack turn progress, Slack decisions, Slack handoffs, Worktrees, Reclaim and reconcile -> cap-bots. Slack connections, Daemon-hosted MCP tools (the post_blocks tool and Block Kit rules) -> plugin-slack; the MCP host itself is the platform's (left); bots' allowlist of wrapped tools -> cap-bots.
- Agent sessions (ACP harness), Durable agent sessions, Pending decisions -> cap-acp (the session store behind THREAD_SESSIONS is the platform's, linked).
- Chat threads: thread service/routes are the platform's (left); chat agents -> cap-chat-claude-code, cap-chat-codex; bots as chat agents -> cap-bots. Candy Mountain's module placement (Agent Hub, Operations) is product data, left.
- Root README: one paragraph linking every package's README, no change to the table. claude-acp's existing README untouched; testing has none (dev-only).

STATEMENTS CORRECTED (what the source said -> what is true now)
- Package names @candy-mountain/* -> @crab-shack/* (incl. @crab-shack/capabilities-testing for fakes, @crab-shack/claude-acp shim path).
- Repository: table "sits in the platform migration set; migration 0021_repositories created it" -> its own migration set `repository`, src/migrations/0000_init. Same pattern for every package: the 00NN migration numbers (0020 slack_turns, 0021, 0022) are gone, each set is one 0000_init.

FOR 94z.3.7: the Netlify and repository health checks and the repository branches action still send `candy-mountain`; update the sentences in plugin-repository/README.md ("The health check and the `branches` action send...") and plugin-netlify/README.md (last paragraph).

Assignee routes (GET/POST /:slug/assignees) documented (source named only the table).
- Uptime: runMonitorCheck and startUptimeScheduler gain a required productName; probes send User-Agent `<slug>-uptime`. onWorkspaceArchiveChange is a platform export, not src/workspaces/workspaces.ts. "Reads, open like the other monitor reads" -> reads need the `uptime` view, writes the admin and `uptime.manage`.
- Deployments: "reads open to any signed-in actor until a deployments capability gates them" -> the capability (manifest, ladder, deployments.manage) now exists but the routes still use requireAdmin only (documented as it behaves; see follow-up). productName is a required option of the routes, the sources' read context, and the custom-endpoint/Netlify User-Agent (slug of the product's name).

title: Capabilities: the development distribution can be exercised without outside accounts
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ (capabilities cap-*, connections plugin-*, the Claude Code ACP shim claude-acp and shared test support) for products built on the @crab-shack platform (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform), plus a development distribution under apps/ (a daemon app and a web app over a root product.yaml named Capabilities that enables everything). The packages were moved out of the product Candy Mountain. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow the agent instructions file in that repository.

The problem. The development distribution is where a capability change is tried before it is released, by a person or by an agent. But several capabilities cannot be exercised without real outside accounts: a repository connection is healthy only after a test against GitHub or Bitbucket with a real token (their API addresses are fixed in the code), and the Claude Code and Codex connections only after a real login of their command line tools. Until those are healthy the Bots, Team and Deployments pages show only their "needs setup" gate and no chat thread can be started. An agent that built the distribution could check issues and uptime for real, but had to write connection health straight into a scratch database to see the other pages, and could not start a chat or run a bot at all. So a change to those capabilities cannot be checked end to end by an agent, and a person needs real credentials on hand to check it.

What to do. Make it possible to run the development distribution, on a developer machine with no outside accounts, far enough that every capability's own pages render with data and a chat thread can be started and answered, using stand-ins for the outside services. The capabilities already have fakes for these services in their tests (a fake command line tool for the agent families, stand-in hosts); the aim is for the running distribution to be able to use stand-ins of that kind, when a developer asks for them explicitly, in a way that cannot be mistaken for the real thing and cannot be switched on in a product by accident.

What a product does when the stand-ins are not asked for must be exactly what it does today, and nothing in this bead may let a production product talk to a host other than the real one without someone having deliberately configured it.

Document how to start the distribution this way in the README.
acceptance_criteria:
- On a machine with no GitHub, Bitbucket, Claude Code, Codex, Slack, Heroku or Netlify account configured, the distribution started in the documented stand-in mode shows the Bots, Team and Deployments pages with their own content, and a chat thread can be started and receives a reply.
- Started the ordinary way, the distribution behaves as before; tests show the stand-ins are not used unless asked for.
- The README says how to start it this way and that the services are stand-ins.
- Lint, typecheck, test and build are green.
notes:
LANDED 2026-11-14 as 31b0767 on capabilities main (one commit; Release run 43581494405 published @crab-shack/capabilities-testing@0.1.1 and nothing else; CI run 43581494486 green; worktree and branch removed). The development distribution of the capabilities repository has a stand-in mode: `pnpm dev:stand-ins` (after `pnpm build` once, for the Claude Code shim). README section "Run without outside accounts" is the reference.

HOW TO USE IT TO CHECK A BEAD (agents: follow the rules file's section on running an app).
- Start: `CM_DATA_DIR=<scratch>/data CM_DAEMON_PORT=<free> NUXT_PORT=<free> NUXT_HOST=127.0.0.1 pnpm dev:stand-ins`, from the repository root, under /tmp/cm-dev-server.lock. Ready when <data>/stand-ins/seeded.json exists and the web app answers /spaces (about 15 to 40 s).
- CM_DATA_DIR must not exist, be empty, or be a directory the mode made before (it holds a STAND-INS file); anything else is refused. Without CM_DATA_DIR the data is in ~/.local/share/capabilities-stand-ins. `pnpm dev` refuses a directory holding STAND-INS.
- It refuses NODE_ENV=production, a CM_DAEMON_HOST other than loopback and CM_AUTH_STRATEGY other than development; it ignores CM_SECRETS_KEY and CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD.
- The first start seeds the space "Stand-in space" at /s/stand-in (API slug `stand-in`): six healthy connections, two bots, two team members, two environments, one monitor, three issues when bd is on PATH. Chat agents: `claude-code`, `codex`, `bot:<id>`. POST /api/workspaces/stand-in/threads {agentId}, then POST .../threads/<id>/prompt {text}; replies start "[stand-in Claude Code] " or "[stand-in Codex] echo: ". The prompts `tool-call` (Claude Code), `think` and `permission` (Codex) play fixture scenes.
- To add connections by hand: repository owner `stand-in`, repo `space`, token `stand-in-token`; Heroku app `stand-in-app`, key `stand-in-key`; Netlify site `stand-in-site`, token `stand-in-token`; Slack tokens starting `xoxb-stand-in` / `xapp-stand-in`; Claude Code and Codex with the path field blank; bot persona `stand-in` on `main`.
- The seed runs once per data directory; delete the directory to start over.

WHAT LATER BEADS NEED TO KNOW.
- No capability, connection or claude-acp main entry changed. Under packages/ only test support changed: packages/testing (fakeHosts takes {repository, token, files}; startFakeSocketMode takes {team, user}; fake-acp-agent.mjs reads FAKE_ACP_REPLY_PREFIX) and packages/claude-acp/src/test-support/claude-fixture.mjs (reads FIXTURE_REPLY_PREFIX). Both prefixes are empty unless set. Packing every package before and after showed only @crab-shack/capabilities-testing's tarball differs (seven files in dist, the copied claude fixture among them), so it alone was released, as 0.1.1 (a patch: every addition is optional and existing callers are unchanged).
- apps/daemon now has @crab-shack/capabilities-testing as a devDependency; its test capability-packages.test.ts allows exactly that. apps/daemon/src/ordinary-start.test.ts walks the import graph from every script's entry but dev:stand-ins and fails if it reaches src/stand-ins, test support or a fake: a new daemon script or a build entry has to stay clear of them.
- The outside hosts are routed by replacing globalThis.fetch in the stand-in process only (apps/daemon/src/stand-ins/hosts.ts). It fails closed: a call to api.github.com, api.bitbucket.org, api.heroku.com, api.netlify.com or slack.com that no handler answers throws "No stand-in answers <METHOD> <host><path>". A capability that starts calling a new endpoint of one of those hosts needs a handler there (GitHub and Bitbucket come from testing's fakeHosts) or its stand-in page will show that error.
- The product runs as "Capabilities (stand-ins)" in the daemon, so its database file is capabilities-stand-ins.db and identifiers derived from the product name carry it. The web app (apps/web/app/plugins/daemon-product.ts) asks the daemon's /info on each page load and shows the daemon's product name: on platform 0.7.1 and 0.8.2 alike the shell takes the name from the product file only, so the plugin rewrites the shell's product object. A platform release in which the shell reads the name from the daemon would replace it.
- The daemon and every tool it starts run with HOME=<data>/stand-ins/home, PATH led by <data>/stand-ins/bin (the stand-in claude and codex), GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file and bd metrics off. bd in a fresh HOME otherwise announces and sends usage metrics.
- Not covered: the platform agent (needs an LLM gateway), inbound Slack messages (nothing injects an event into the Socket Mode fake), and what monitors or custom deployment endpoints point at.

EVIDENCE is kept in the orchestrator's scratchpad under 94z-3-10/ (p082-explicit/out and p082-ordinary/out are the runs on platform 0.8.2: checks.txt, the page screenshots and texts, the home snapshots).

FOUND ON THE WAY, NOT FIXED HERE.
- cap-team's Team page logs "Hydration completed but contains mismatches" on every load in nuxt dev, with or without this change.
- findProductFile(import.meta.url) in the base resolves against the working directory (already filed by the orchestrator); both daemon entries are started from apps/daemon by pnpm, so they work, and the stand-in entry does not work round it.
close_reason: Landed as 31b0767 on crab-shack/capabilities main: pnpm dev:stand-ins runs the development distribution with a stand-in for every outside service, entirely in the unpublished apps plus optional parameters in the test support package (published as capabilities-testing 0.1.1 by Release run 43581494405; nothing else published; CI green). No capability, connection or claude-acp main entry changed. Shown for real with no accounts: Bots, Team and Deployments with content, chat answered for Claude Code, Codex and a bot, in the API and headless Chromium. Ordinary start unchanged apart from refusing a stand-in data directory; import-graph and real-fetch tests; unanswered stood-in hosts fail closed; the developer's real homes untouched. Not verified: a production web build of the label plugin, Bitbucket seeded, inbound Slack.

title: Capabilities: text that names the workspace uses the product's word for it, not "project"
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ (capabilities cap-*, connections plugin-*, the Claude Code ACP shim claude-acp and shared test support) for products built on the @crab-shack platform (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform), plus a development distribution under apps/ (a daemon app and a web app over a root product.yaml named Capabilities that enables everything). The packages were moved out of the product Candy Mountain. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow the agent instructions file in that repository.

The problem. A product chooses what its workspaces are called: Candy Mountain calls them projects, the development distribution here calls them spaces, and the next product may call them something else. The platform tells every capability that word when it starts (the capability context carries the scope label). But some text the capabilities show still says "project" whatever the product calls it: the descriptions in capability manifests and plugin type declarations (for instance the issues capability describing itself as "The project's issues, read and edited through its .beads tracker."), and at least the empty state of the bots page. In the development distribution these now read beside the word "space".

What to do. Find the text a person reads, in the daemon halves and in the web layers of every package, that names the workspace as a "project", and make it right in a product that uses another word. Where the text is built at run time with the context in reach, use the product's word. Where it is declared before the product is known (a manifest or plugin type description) and cannot use it, reword it so it does not name the scope at all. Keep the meaning of every sentence.

In a product whose scope label is project, text that uses the label must read exactly as it does today.

Not in this bead: ids, routes, table and column names, API field names, environment variables and anything stored, however they are spelled; the word "project" where it means something other than the product's workspace (a Netlify project, a repository project); code comments and test names.
acceptance_criteria:
- In the development distribution (scope label space), no page or description shown by a capability calls the workspace a project; the bead's closing note lists each text changed, with before and after.
- Tests show at least one run-time text carrying a scope label other than project, and the same text reading as today when the label is project.
- Lint, typecheck and test are green.

title: Capabilities: the Netlify and repository health checks and the branches action identify their product
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ (capabilities cap-*, connections plugin-*, an ACP shim and shared test support) that were moved out of the product Candy Mountain and are now meant to run in products with other names. It pins one exact version of the platform (github.com/crab-shack/platform, published as @crab-shack/platform-* packages) in every package.json. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the capabilities repository Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished; follow the agent instructions file in that repository where there is one.

The problem. An earlier bead made the capabilities identify the product they run in, rather than Candy Mountain, wherever the product's name reaches them: the identifier is the product's name turned into a slug by the platform SDK's own rule, so Candy Mountain still comes out as candy-mountain. Three paths were left behind because the platform calls them by itself and, at the time, did not tell them the product's name: the Netlify plugin type's health check, the repository plugin type's health check, and the repository plugin type's branches action. Each sends a User-Agent that still says candy-mountain in every product.

A separate bead in the base adds the product's name to what the platform passes to a plugin type's health check and to its instance actions. This bead uses it.

What to do. Move the repository's platform pin to the release that contains that base change (the base bead's closing note names the version), then make those three paths send a User-Agent derived from the product's name by the same rule the rest of the repository already uses, so there is one rule and one place it lives.

The hard requirement: in a product named Candy Mountain the User-Agent on all three paths is exactly candy-mountain, as it is today.

Moving the pin changes every package.json; follow the base's docs/upgrade-path.md and do not regenerate the lockfile.

Not in this bead: any other identifier, and temporary folder names beginning candy-mountain-, which stay.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests pin the User-Agent as the literal candy-mountain on the Netlify health check, the repository health check and the branches action for a product named Candy Mountain.
- With a product of another name, tests show each of the three carries that product's identifier and not candy-mountain.
- Searching the non-test source under packages/ for candy-mountain finds only temporary folder name prefixes.
- Every package.json pins the platform release named by the base bead, and lint, typecheck, test and build are green from a fresh clone.
notes:
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), from 94z.7 (platform 0.7.2): pnpm refuses a lockfile entry younger than a day unless the package is exempt in pnpm-workspace.yaml (minimumReleaseAgeExclude). Since 0.7.2 the generator writes the four platform packages there by name, without a version, and a pin move no longer touches the list; docs/upgrade-path.md in the base ('A release younger than a day') has the one-time edit for a repository whose entries still carry a version. The capabilities repository still has versioned entries: make that edit as part of moving its pin.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14): the base change is released as platform 0.8.0 (bead 94z.8). The field is productName, required, on both PluginHealthContext and PluginActionContext; a plugin type reads it as healthCheck({ config, secrets, signal, productName }) and run({ config, secrets, productName }). checkPluginHealth called bare in a test hands the check 'Platform'; the test kit's deps carry the booted product's name. The rule this repository already uses is the SDK's slugify(productName) (bead 94z.3.6). Moving the pin is 0.7.1 to 0.8.0, a minor: read the base's changelogs for 0.7.2 and 0.8.0 and docs/upgrade-path.md. Type actions (PluginTypeActionContext) still do not get the name: if a type action in this repository sends a User-Agent, leave it and report it.
Orchestrator note (2026-11-14), replacing the two earlier notes where they differ. (1) Pin: move to platform 0.8.2, the newest release, not 0.8.0. It contains the 0.8.0 change this bead needs (productName on the plugin health and action contexts) plus two patches (0.8.1: the web shell's dev server binds to loopback by default; 0.8.2: generator and docs only). Read the acceptance criterion's 'release named by the base bead' as 0.8.2. Read the base's changelogs for 0.7.2, 0.8.0, 0.8.1 and 0.8.2 and docs/upgrade-path.md. (2) Release age: Jack decided everything under @crab-shack is exempt from pnpm's minimum release age, and since 0.8.2 the form is one entry for the scope. In this repository's pnpm-workspace.yaml, under minimumReleaseAgeExclude, delete every @crab-shack entry (the four versioned platform entries and any pnpm appended itself) and put '@crab-shack/*' in their place; keep any other entry; do not regenerate the lockfile. Bead 94z.9's closing note has the detail, including that pnpm caches lockfile verification, so prove the install from a fresh clone with an empty pnpm cache directory. (3) Documentation: bead 94z.3.11 added a README.md to plugin-repository and plugin-netlify with a sentence each saying these three paths still send candy-mountain as the User-Agent; make those sentences true of your change. (4) Bead 94z.4.1 has landed: platform peers in the capability packages are the range 0.x, which accepts 0.8.2, so the pin move is the exact pins in devDependencies and the apps, not the peer ranges.
Draft (not final): pin 0.8.2 + one-line @crab-shack/* release-age entry committed on branch 94z-3-7 (lockfile diff only platform-* entries); UA via slugify(productName) in plugin-netlify plugin-type.ts and plugin-repository definition.ts; changeset health-user-agent.md (patch both). Not yet landed.
LANDED 13d9125 on capabilities main (pin 0.8.2 commit 1b0579a, UA commit 653d96a, release commit 13d9125). title: Base: a plugin type's health check and instance actions are told the product's name
description:
Context: the base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) is a pnpm workspace that publishes the platform as five packages under @crab-shack to GitHub Packages at one shared version: a daemon, a web shell, an SDK holding the capability contract, shared configuration and a CLI. A product is plain data (its name, theme and the lists of capabilities and plugin types it enables) joined at boot with capability definitions. Capabilities live in their own repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities) and are meant to run in products with different names. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the base Jack has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and under the fast lane that push is the release; follow AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md in the base, including the changeset rule.

The problem. When the platform starts a capability it hands it a context that includes the product's name, so that anything the capability writes or sends can name the product it is running in. But a plugin type (the thing a connection package contributes, such as the Netlify or repository plugin types) also has code the platform calls by itself, outside any capability's start: its health check, and its instance actions. The contexts the platform passes to those two do not carry the product's name. So a plugin type that identifies its product when it calls an outside service (the capabilities send it as the User-Agent) cannot do so from a health check or an action, and today those paths still say "candy-mountain" in every product.

A product can also list a plugin type directly, without any capability that contributes it being started, so the name cannot be relied on to arrive by way of a capability's start.

What to do. Give a plugin type's health check and its instance actions the product's name, the same value a capability receives at start, in every way a plugin type can come to be registered, including one a product lists directly. It is an addition: an existing plugin type that ignores it must keep working unchanged, and nothing a capability author has written needs to change.

Say so on the capability author's page where the health check and actions are described.

Not in this bead: changing the capabilities repository to use it (a separate bead does that after this is released), and any other addition to those contexts.
acceptance_criteria:
- Tests show a plugin type's health check and an instance action each receive the product's name, equal to what a capability's start receives.
- The same holds for a plugin type the product lists directly, with no capability contributing it.
- The worked examples and existing plugin types in the base build and pass unchanged.
- The capability author's documentation mentions the name where it describes health checks and actions.
- The base's four gates are green and the release containing the change is in the registry; the bead's closing note names the version.
notes: Released in platform 0.8.0 (commit b8f1aba on crab-shack/platform main; Release run 43442618490, CI run 43442618482 green; tag v0.8.0). New field: productName: string on PluginHealthContext AND on PluginActionContext (@crab-shack/platform-sdk/daemon). Always present (required, not optional) when the daemon runs the check or action: POST /plugins/:id/test, an instance action, refreshHealth, testPluginInstance. It equals CapabilityContext.productName (product.config.name), whether the type is brought by a plugin-* definition or listed directly in product.pluginTypes. A plugin type author writes healthCheck({ config, secrets, signal, productName }) and actions: { x: { method, run({ config, secrets, productName }) } }. Test-side: checkPluginHealth(type, { config, secrets }) bare hands the check 'Platform' (optional productName option overrides it); testPluginInstance/refreshPluginInstanceHealth deps now require productName, which kit.deps and instanceHarness(...).deps carry ('Test Product' for testProduct(), else the booted product's name). Type actions (PluginTypeActionContext, /plugin-types/:id/<action>) do NOT get it. Not done here: capabilities' Netlify/repository health checks and branches action (94z.3.7).
close_reason: Released as platform 0.8.0 (b8f1aba on crab-shack/platform main; minor, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks for an addition). Release run 43442618490 published all five packages, v0.8.0 tagged; CI run 43442618482 green. PluginHealthContext and PluginActionContext both carry a required productName, taken from the product's configuration, so a type brought by a definition and a type listed directly in product.pluginTypes get the same value a capability's start receives; a new test boots a product named Harbour and shows both. Orchestrator checked the commit, tag, runs, the field on both contexts and that the worktree is removed. Accepted: testPluginInstance and refreshPluginInstanceHealth now require productName in their deps (the test kit's deps carry it; no capability or Candy Mountain call builds them by hand). Not done, by the bead's scope: type actions (PluginTypeActionContext) still do not get the name. Not run: the capabilities repository against 0.8.0.

title: Bots: a reclaim interval above about 24.8 days makes the worktree reclaimer run continuously
description: The bots capability's worktreeReclaimIntervalMs setting (and the CM_WORKTREE_RECLAIM_INTERVAL environment variable that Candy Mountain's apps/daemon/src/settings.ts maps onto it) accepts values up to 30 days (2592000000 ms). The reclaimer passes the value to setInterval, whose maximum delay is 2147483647 ms (about 24.8 days); above that Node warns and uses 1 ms, so the reclaimer runs continuously. This predates the move to declared settings (bead candy-mountain-v3-8by.4.13), which kept behaviour unchanged on purpose. Fix: either cap the declared maximum for the reclaim interval at the timer limit, or have the reclaimer chain timeouts for long intervals. The idle timeout is compared against timestamps, not passed to a timer, so check it but it is probably unaffected. Where: packages/cap-bots/src/worktrees/config.ts (BOTS_SETTINGS) and worktrees/reclaim.ts in Candy Mountain today; after the shared-capabilities move (epic candy-mountain-v3-94z) the same files live in /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities as @crab-shack/cap-bots.
acceptance_criteria: A reclaim interval of 30d either is refused at boot with a message naming bots and the key, or results in the reclaimer firing once per 30 days; a test covers the chosen behaviour. No value the setting accepts makes the reclaimer fire more often than asked.

title: Base: one SDK-major range parser shared by the daemon drift check and the web layer list
description: Context: base repo crab-shack/platform (checkout /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform; phase 3 work in worktree platform-phase3). Phase 3 introduced two independent parsers of the @crab-shack/platform-sdk peer range a capability package declares: rangeMajor in packages/platform-config/eslint/package-boundaries.mjs (built on semver, used by capabilitySdkDrift, i.e. the daemon-side drift check run by apps/daemon tests) and a hand-written rangeMajor in packages/platform-web/layer-list.mjs (used by the web build's layer-list SDK-major check). They agree on 0.x, ^0.4.0, <1.0.0, 1.x || 2.x and *, but can diverge on unusual ranges, so the daemon and web could disagree on whether a package declares one major. Problem: two sources of truth for one rule. What to build: platform-web's layer list uses the platform-config helper (or both use one shared implementation in a package both already depend on at runtime; check that platform-web's runtime dependency graph allows it since layer-list.mjs runs inside a product's nuxt.config), with the existing platform-web fixture tests still passing. Non-goals: no change to the declaration form or the error messages. Gates: pnpm lint, typecheck (serial), test, build green in the base; a patch changeset for platform-web. Do not commit unless the assigner says so.
acceptance_criteria: platform-web's layer-list check and platform-config's capabilitySdkDrift resolve a range's major through the same function; the duplicated parser is gone; existing tests pass; a patch changeset is present; four gates green in the base.
close_reason: Done in shared worktree crab-shack/platform-phase3 (uncommitted): platform-web layer-list.mjs imports and re-exports rangeMajor from @crab-shack/platform-config/package-boundaries (already a runtime dep); hand-written parser removed; identity test added; .changeset/web-layer-shared-range-parser.md (patch). Four gates green.

title: platform-unlink is unreachable when the product is linked to a checkout older than the commands
description:
Context: @crab-shack/platform-config (base repo crab-shack/platform, 0.3.0 and later) ships the bins platform-link and platform-unlink, which a product runs as `pnpm platform-link [checkout]` and `pnpm platform-unlink` (see docs/linking.md in the base). Linking overrides every @crab-shack/platform-* package, platform-config included, with `link:` to the checkout's packages. The product's node_modules/.bin then resolves the bins from the checkout's platform-config.

Problem: if the checkout predates the commands (its packages/platform-config/package.json has no "bin"), linking succeeds but `pnpm platform-unlink` fails with `Command "platform-unlink" not found`. Seen in Candy Mountain linked to /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform at 83556b4. The workaround is to run the registry copy from the pnpm store: `node node_modules/.pnpm/@crab-shack+platform-config@<version>*/node_modules/@crab-shack/platform-config/bin/platform-unlink.mjs`, which restored the files byte for byte.

What to build: make this case impossible or self-explaining. For example, platform-link refuses a checkout whose packages/platform-config/package.json has no platform-unlink bin and tells the developer to update the checkout. Alternatively, the success message prints the absolute path of the unlink script it ran from. Add a row to the "When it fails" table in docs/linking.md either way.

Acceptance: linking a product to a checkout without the bins either is refused with a clear message, or leaves an unlink path that works and is printed. A unit test in packages/platform-config/test/unit/link.test.ts covers it. Base gates pass, with a patch changeset.
close_reason: Fixed in base PR https://github.com/crab-shack/platform/pull/8 (open, not merged): platform-link refuses a checkout without a platform-unlink bin and prints the checkout's unlink script path; docs row, tests, patch changeset. Ships in the next release.

title: Base: investigate one-off failure of the web app's test task in the full root test run
description: In the base (crab-shack/platform), right after merging the five phase-1 branches on 2026-11-09, the first full 'pnpm test' run on main failed on @crab-shack/web#test within about 1.6 seconds of the turbo run starting, straight after 'pnpm install' and the root typecheck. 'pnpm --filter @crab-shack/web test' alone passed, and four further uncached full runs ('pnpm exec turbo run test --force') all passed, so the failure did not reproduce and its output was not captured. Suspects: apps/web/test/unit/distribution.test.ts loads Nuxt in production and development mode and may race a sibling task (platform-web playground tests, cap-template tests, or a root postinstall 'nuxt prepare') over a shared .nuxt or .output directory, or depend on state the preceding 'nuxt typecheck' leaves behind. Reproduce by running the full gate sequence from a fresh clone (install, lint, typecheck, test) several times; if it recurs, capture the web task's output, and either isolate the test's Nuxt build directories or declare the missing task dependency in turbo.json. Acceptance: either the cause is found and fixed with the fix covered by the gates, or ten consecutive fresh-clone runs of the gate sequence pass and the bead is closed as not reproducible.
close_reason: Not reproducible: ten consecutive fresh-clone runs of install, lint, typecheck, test passed; structural suspects (OOM, shared caches, missing build dependency, concurrent processes) ruled out. Details in comments.

comments.author: kingrea
comments.text: Investigated 2026-11-09. Original run recovered from the orchestrator session transcript (09:41:21 local): lint, pnpm --recursive --workspace-concurrency=1 typecheck, pnpm test, pnpm build, each piped through tail, which is why only the summary survived; the test turbo run reported 'Cached: 0 cached, 9 total, Time: 1.608s, Failed: @crab-shack/web#test', so the web vitest process died before its Nuxt-loading test could have run (that test alone takes 3-4s). Ruled out: no OOM kill in dmesg since boot (07:43, dmesg unrestricted); jiti, Nuxt and vite caches are per package root (apps/web/node_modules/.cache vs playground/node_modules/.cache), so the platform-web and web test tasks share no cache; the fonts cache under apps/web was written by the build step after the failure; workspace exports point at source (dist only via publishConfig) so no missing-build dependency; nothing else ran in the session or its subagents during the window and the dev servers from bead 2.2 were stopped at 09:35. Reproduction: ten consecutive fresh clones of main (83556b4) each ran pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, pnpm test; all ten passed (web 4/4, platform-web 235/235 every time). Closing as not reproducible per acceptance. Suggestion for future gate scripts: tee the full output to a file and tail the file, so a one-off failure keeps its log.

title: Capability-owned test support still ships on capability root entries
description: Context: after bead ncj.5.5 every cap-*/plugin-* test takes platform test support from @candy-mountain/platform-daemon/testing. But several capabilities export their OWN test support from their production root entry so dependents' tests can use it: cap-acp (src/index.ts re-exports ./acp/test-support: fakeBins, FAKE_ACP_AGENT, createTempHome...), plugin-repository (createWorkspaceWithRepository, fakeHosts, GOOD_TOKEN, hostJson), plugin-claude-code (claudeCodeTestCapabilities), plugin-codex (codexTestCapabilities). Consumers: cap-bots, cap-chat-*, apps/daemon tests. The boundary lint (packages/platform-config/eslint/package-boundaries.mjs, cm-packages/no-subpath-import) only lets a capability import another capability's root entry, so a per-capability /testing export is refused today. Problem: these ship in production bundles (the comments say 'kept free of vitest so the root entry stays safe to bundle') and will be published with the capabilities. What to do: decide whether capabilities get a declared ./testing export the lint allows (dependency capability's root or /testing), then move each package's test support there and update consumers. title: Phase 5: Digital hub as a distribution (loose, needs its own plan)
description:
Capability: the digital hub runs as a distribution of the platform, with its capabilities ported one at a time, and the two products share one base instead of one being a fork of the other. Plan: .ai-docs/plans/platform-package/phase-5-digital-hub.md, deliberately loose; it gets its own plan when it starts. The hub is multi-scope with clients grouped by organisation, which the platform supports; its capabilities (investigator, uptime, audit, the hub agent) map onto the platform's capability, module and grant model because that is where the model came from. Decisions that plan will need: the hub's chat streams through the AI SDK's message stream from a separate Mastra server while the platform's chat is an SSE event log through the daemon; the hub's uptime is a static service list polled in process while Candy Mountain's is per-workspace monitors in the database; the hub's permission gates tokenise personal data in tool output, which the platform does not do. Each is a choice between porting the hub's version, adopting the platform's, or lifting the hub's into the platform as a standard capability (research notes: .ai-docs/research/digital-hub.md). If the hub wants uptime and Slack connections, that is the moment to move them from Candy Mountain into the base as optional packages versioned with the platform, or to copy them, which the requirements allow.

Not decomposed: write the phase's own plan first (plan-writing skill), then decompose it, after phases 3 and 4 close.

Human test: to be written with the phase's plan. At minimum the hub's existing human tests pass on the platform, and the three products run on the same base version.

title: Make agent_sessions.cwd nullable so native-family sessions store null, not ''
description: Since ncj.2.2 the thread service no longer passes a cwd; the session store asks the attached driver (SessionDriver.workingDirectory). comments.author: kingrea
comments.text: Done. Migration platform/0001_agent_session_cwd_nullable: schema change generated with drizzle-kit (snapshot 0001 + journal entry kept as generated), but the generated SQL (PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF + __new_agent_sessions rebuild + DROP TABLE) was replaced by hand: inside the migrator transaction the pragma is a no-op, so DROP TABLE cascade-deleted agent_session_events (reproduced by the new test before the swap). Native SQL instead: ALTER TABLE ADD cwd_nullable; UPDATE SET cwd_nullable = NULLIF(cwd, ''); DROP COLUMN cwd; RENAME COLUMN cwd_nullable TO cwd. No table is dropped, so agent_session_events, chat_threads, chat_thread_sessions and cap-bots slack tables keep their rows; existing '' rows become NULL. cwd is now the last column (same on fresh and upgraded DBs). db:check clean, db:generate reports no diff. comments.author: kingrea
comments.text: Mechanism: onWorkspaceDeleted(workspace, deletion) now gets a WorkspaceDeletion { afterCommit(task) } (platform-sdk daemon/capability.ts). The route (platform-daemon src/workspaces/routes.ts removeWorkspace) collects tasks during the BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, discards them on ROLLBACK, and runs them in order after COMMIT inside the same deletion queue; a failing task is console.error-logged and the delete still answers 204 (the rows are already gone). deleteWorkspacePluginInstances(deps, id, deletion) and deleteProjectBots(deps, id, deletion) register their secret deletions there; the platform stays ignorant of bots. Worktrees: new WorktreePool.removeProject(projectId, clone) rm -rf's worktrees/<project id> whatever it holds (deleting the project is the human decision) and runs git worktree prune in the clone (errors swallowed as in release); the bots definition reads the clone path in its hook (the repository row goes in the same transaction) and registers removeProject after commit. title: Offer Codex models and reasoning effort in the chat selectors
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (apps/daemon) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app (apps/web). The chat panel (apps/web/layers/chat) shows model and effort selectors (ChatModelEffort in the prompt bar) fed by GET /projects/:slug/threads/agents/:agentId/options; a change PATCHes the thread, which starts a new session and the transcript shows a divider. Claude Code offers opus/sonnet/haiku and low/medium/high (apps/daemon/src/threads/options.ts). Codex returns empty lists, so its selectors are hidden.

Wire Codex: codex-acp 2.3.0 returns configOptions on session/new and session/load (id 'model', category 'model', values are model ids with display names; id 'reasoning_effort', category 'thought_level', whose values depend on the current model). (1) Capture configOptions in the ACP harness (apps/daemon/src/acp/session.ts drops the newSession/loadSession response today) and expose them on AcpSession. (2) Cache them per project in the session manager after the first Codex session starts, and have the options route return them for Codex (empty until a Codex session has run). (3) Apply a choice: add model / reasoning effort to the Codex posture and pass them through CODEX_CONFIG {model, model_reasoning_effort} in resolveCodexLaunch (apps/daemon/src/acp/families.ts, which currently sets CODEX_CONFIG only for developer_instructions), or call session/set_config_option for 'model'/'reasoning_effort' after start (never 'mode'). (4) Extend FAMILY_OPTIONS/assertModelEffort/chatPosture in threads/options.ts to validate against the cached lists. No web change should be needed: the selectors appear once the options list is non-empty.
acceptance_criteria: With a logged-in Codex, after one Codex turn the options endpoint lists Codex models and efforts; choosing a model in the chat panel starts a new session whose launch carries that model (visible in the session posture and the adapter's startup log), and the reply comes from it; before any Codex session the selectors stay hidden.
notes:
Codex models and reasoning effort in the chat selectors (no migration, no web change).

HARNESS (apps/daemon/src/acp): AcpSession.configOptions (readonly SessionConfigOption[]) = configOptions of the session/new or session/load response, replaced by any later config_option_update (still emitted as an 'other' event). Codex launch options gain model? / reasoningEffort? (CodexLaunchOptions, shared AgentSessionPosture.codex). resolveCodexLaunch builds CODEX_CONFIG from { developer_instructions, model, model_reasoning_effort } (only the keys that are set; '' when none); the adapter merges it into thread/start AND thread/resume, so a resumed session keeps the model. Values must be plain ids (model /^[A-Za-z0-9][\w.:/-]{0,127}$/, effort /^[a-z][a-z_-]{0,31}$/) or AcpLaunchError. New export assertCodexLaunchOptions(codex) runs the mode + config checks without spawning. Mode is untouched; nothing calls session/set_config_option or set_mode.

SESSION MANAGER: create() also runs assertCodexLaunchOptions for codex postures (AcpLaunchError -> SessionError invalid_request; Claude bypass check unchanged). After a successful start it remembers acp.configOptions in memory per (projectId, family), one set per 'model'-category currentValue (efforts depend on the model), latest last: SessionManager.configOptions(projectId, family) -> SessionConfigOption[][]. Empty after a daemon restart until a session of that family starts again. sessions/routes.ts parsePosture accepts posture.codex.model / reasoningEffort (non-empty strings).

THREADS: options.ts familyOptions(family, sets=[]) / assertModelEffort(family, model, effort, sets=[], kept={model,effort}) / chatPosture. Codex models = latest set's 'model' option (groups flattened; ChatOption {value, label: name, description if any}); efforts = union of every 'thought_level' option seen (first-seen order). A choice must be in those lists, and an effort a KNOWN model does not list is refused (400). Values equal to the thread's current ones (kept) are not rechecked, so a title patch or re-sending the same model works after a restart empties the lists; changing to a new value then needs a Codex session to have run. chatPosture codex -> { codex: { model?, reasoningEffort? } } (null when both null). ThreadService.options(project, agent) feeds GET .../threads/agents/:agentId/options.

TESTS: families.test.ts (CODEX_CONFIG with persona+model+effort, read-only mode kept, injection-like/empty/dash-leading values refused); harness.test.ts (configOptions from new and load, launched model visible to the agent, FAKE_ACP_CONFIG=none -> []); sessions.test.ts (bad codex model / non-string effort -> 400); threads.test.ts new describe 'Codex models and reasoning effort': options empty before any Codex session; after one turn lists Fast/Deep + low/medium/high; PATCH model gpt-deep -> new session, posture {codex:{model:'gpt-deep'}}, agent reports model:gpt-deep/high; efforts gain xhigh; PATCH effort xhigh -> posture with reasoningEffort, child env CODEX_CONFIG {model, model_reasoning_effort} and INITIAL_AGENT_MODE read-only; unknown model, gpt-fast with xhigh, unknown effort, create with an incompatible pair -> 400; create with gpt-fast/low works; restart with an FAKE_ACP_AUTH=none adapter -> options empty, prompt 409 auth_required, options still empty, title patch keeps the session, new values refused, re-sending the kept model ok. Fake agent (test-support/fake-acp-agent.mjs) advertises codex-shaped configOptions (mode, model gpt-fast|gpt-deep, reasoning_effort per model) picked from CODEX_CONFIG; prompt 'model' echoes model/effort; FAKE_ACP_CONFIG=none hides them. README 'Agent sessions' + 'Chat threads' updated.

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: root pnpm lint pass; pnpm test pass (118 files, 1125 passed, 3 skipped; includes the real-adapter fresh CODEX_HOME auth_required check); pnpm build pass; pnpm typecheck pass (a first run failed on packages/shared SLACK_CHANNEL_ID_PATTERN / SLACK_MEMBER_ID_PATTERN duplicate exports from the concurrent slack work; gone on rerun). NOT verified: a real logged-in Codex (no login here; ~/.codex untouched), so the real adapter's model list, its Startup log line (it logs codexConfig incl. model) and a reply from the chosen model are unchecked.

OPEN: (1) the catalog is in memory, so after a restart the selectors stay hidden until a Codex session starts in that project. (2) with the default model (null) an effort is not checked against the default model's list (configOptions do not mark the default). (3) the adapter unshifts its current model into the model list when it is not listed, so such a model can appear as a choice.
close_reason: configOptions captured, cached per project/family, applied via CODEX_CONFIG; fake-agent verified; gates green

Give the title a sensible min-width with truncation (flex-1 min-w-0 truncate) and let the less important columns (assignee, chips, comment count) collapse first, so rows stay readable with the panel open at 1280px and 1024px.

Root lint/test(1139)/build pass; typecheck fails in apps/daemon/src/sessions/manager.ts (StartSessionOptions, other agent's in-flight change).

title: Vet checkout subagent files and forked skills against the bot's posture ceiling
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon, apps/daemon/src/posture (bead 6.7). The posture mapping denies the Agent tool for read-only and write-confirm scopes, but other .claude/agents/*.md files and skills with context: fork in the checkout can still declare their own permissionMode and run wider than the bot's write scope. Clanker Corner judged every subagent file against the ceiling. Extend vetCheckoutSettings (or add vetCheckoutAgents) to read .claude/agents/*.md and skill front matter in the checkout, refuse or neutralise any that request a mode or tools wider than the scope (report in neutralised[]), and cover the checkout env/apiKeyHelper block. Tests with fixture checkouts.
acceptance_criteria: A checkout containing a subagent file with permissionMode bypassPermissions is refused for every scope; a subagent requesting acceptEdits is refused under read-only and allowed under write-auto; an apiKeyHelper block is refused; existing posture tests still pass.
notes:
Checkout agent vetting. Code: apps/daemon/src/posture/checkout-agents.ts (new), front-matter.ts (shared judge), checkout-settings.ts (refused keys + mirrorAllowAsAsk), posture.ts (wiring). Tests: src/posture/checkout-agents.test.ts (17, fixture checkouts via mkdtemp). README '## Bot posture' updated.

API (additive; existing exports unchanged):
- vetCheckoutAgents(checkoutDir, writeScope) -> CheckoutVetting { askRules, denyRules (always []), neutralised }. readCheckoutAgents(checkoutDir) -> CheckoutAgentFile[] { path, kind: subagent|skill|command|codex-persona, text }. Scans .claude/agents/**/*.md, .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md (one level only), .claude/commands/**/*.md, .agents/*.md. Missing dirs skipped; a file with no front matter (or no closing fence) is skipped since it asks for nothing.
- Each file with front matter: bypass token in the block -> 'bypass'; unreadable block -> 'checkout_agent_unreadable' (also a file/dir read error); then assertFrontMatterWithinScope (same rules as the persona: permissionMode rank > scope ceiling, auto or unknown -> refused; tools/allowed-tools/allowedTools naming a scope-denied tool -> refused, Task treated as Agent, Agent(x) matched by name; hooks/mcpServers/observer always refused; memory user / project+local outside write-auto refused) with code 'checkout_agent_widens'.
- allowed-tools / allowedTools approvals (skills, commands) are mirrored as --settings ask rules (deduped) and reported in neutralised[] with key 'allowed-tools <rule>'; skipped: bd baseline forms and CLAUDE_UNPROMPTED_TOOLS (Read, Glob, Grep, LS, NotebookRead, TodoWrite, AskUserQuestion). Bash/Bash(*) notes that bd will prompt.
- Checkout settings: CLAUDE_CHECKOUT_REFUSED_SETTINGS env, apiKeyHelper, awsAuthRefresh, awsCredentialExport, otelHeadersHelper -> PostureError 'checkout_settings_widens' (empty env {} allowed).
- New PostureError codes: checkout_settings_widens, checkout_agent_unreadable, checkout_agent_widens.
- resolveBotPosture input gains optional mainCheckoutDir (absolute, else invalid_input). Claude family only: agents are vetted in checkoutDir and mainCheckoutDir; when checkoutSettings is NOT given, settings are read from both too (each resolved against its own dir). Codex ignores checkout agents. 6.13 should now pass mainCheckoutDir instead of concatenating readCheckoutSettings results.
- Persona check also gains: tool lists split on commas and whitespace outside parentheses (allowed-tools: A B form), Task alias, Agent(x) form, allowed-tools judged.

Verified 2026-10-28: posture tests 58/58; root typecheck and build pass. Root lint fails only on apps/web issues pages (vue/multi-word-component-names, another agent's in-flight files); root test fails only src/registry/agent-hub.test.ts (3 tests, new chat-claude-code/chat-codex capabilities from another agent's in-flight change).
Open: nested .claude/skills in subdirectories (monorepo discovery) and plugin skills are not scanned; behaviour of skill allowed-tools vs ask rules taken from docs, not a live run.
