title: Make the password rate-limit tests immune to scrypt cost under load
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon, apps/daemon/src/auth/password-rate-limit.test.ts and password.test.ts (beads 1.6, 10.9). Under full-suite load, tests that perform ten real scrypt logins (N=2^17) exceed vitest's 5s per-test timeout and fail, while passing alone. Make the scrypt parameters injectable (e.g. a hashing options parameter on the password strategy or a test-only low-cost preset used via createPasswordStrategy options) so tests use a cheap cost, keep one test that verifies the production cost parameters are the defaults, and raise the timeout of any remaining real-cost test explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Root pnpm test runs the auth tests in well under 5s each under parallel load (10 consecutive runs green); the production scrypt parameters are unchanged and asserted by a test.
notes: Scrypt cost injectable: passwordStrategy({hashing}) feeds verifyAgainstDummy (per-params cached dummy hash; this was the remaining 2^17 cost on unknown-user logins); setUserPassword/applyAdminPassword take hashing param. Stored hashes carry own params, format unchanged, defaults unchanged. LOW_COST_SCRYPT_PARAMS (N=2^10) exported from passwords.ts, used by password.test, password-rate-limit.test, passwords.test. passwords.test asserts defaults N=2^17,r=8,p=1 and stored hash prefix (30s timeout). Auth suite 10x under concurrent root test: all 45 pass, ~1-2s each.
close_reason: Dummy-verify cost was the culprit; injectable hashing params, 10/10 green under load

title: Make the issue watcher burst test robust under parallel test load
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon, apps/daemon/src/issues/watcher.test.ts (bead 3.3). The test 'folds a burst of ten writes into a handful of events' asserts <=5 events for ten sequential bd creates; under heavy parallel load (other vitest projects, concurrent builds) it produced 6 and once 10 events and failed, while passing alone. Either make the assertion relative to the watcher's minIntervalMs and the measured elapsed time of the burst, or use an injected clock / fake fs events for the folding assertion and keep one real-bd smoke test for latency.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes 10 consecutive runs with the whole root test suite running concurrently; the folding behaviour is still asserted.
notes: Burst test now asserts events <= floor(elapsed/minIntervalMs)+1 and consecutive events >= minIntervalMs-50ms apart, instead of fixed <=5. watcher.ts unchanged. Verified 6 runs under concurrent root pnpm test: all pass.

title: Add login rate limiting to the password strategy
description: Context: Candy Mountain v3 daemon, password auth strategy (bead 1.6) at apps/daemon/src/auth/password.ts. Login has no rate limiting; acceptable behind Tailscale today but a cheap hardening step. Add a per-username and per-IP limiter on POST /auth/login (e.g. token bucket in memory, 429 with Retry-After), tested.

title: Base: the web shell shows the name of the product its daemon is running
description:
Context: the base (github.com/crab-shack/platform, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/platform) publishes the platform, including platform-web, the web shell every product's web app extends, and platform-daemon, whose /info route describes the running product. A product is described by a product file that both its daemon app and its web app read when they start. The capabilities repository (/home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) is built on it. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: in the base Jack (the owner and only developer) has authorised agents to commit and push to main when a piece of work is finished, and that push is the release; follow AGENTS.md in the base.

The problem. The web shell shows the product's name (header, page title) from the product file it read at start, not from the daemon it is talking to. Usually they agree. They do not when one web app is pointed at a daemon running a different product description: the capabilities repository's development distribution has a stand-in mode whose daemon runs the product under the name "Capabilities (stand-ins)" precisely so that nobody mistakes stand-in connections for real ones, and an ordinary web app pointed at that daemon would show the plain name over stand-in data. To close that gap the capabilities repository carries a web plugin in its own web app that asks the daemon for its name and rewrites the shell's product object, which is not a documented extension point and may break on any shell release.

What to do. Let the name a person sees come from the daemon that is serving them, in a way the shell supports, so that a product needs no plugin of its own for it; then remove the plugin from the capabilities repository's web app once it pins a release that has this. Decide what the shell shows before the daemon has answered and when it cannot be reached, and say so in the shell's documentation.

A product whose web app and daemon read the same product file must look exactly as it does today.
acceptance_criteria:
- With a web app started on one product file and a daemon running the same product under another name, the header and page title show the daemon's name, in development and in a production build.
- A product whose two apps read the same product file renders as before; the shell's tests cover both cases and the daemon being unreachable.
- The capabilities repository's web app no longer carries its own plugin for this, pins the release that has the change, and its stand-in mode still shows the stand-in name.
- The gates are green in each repository changed and the releases are named in the closing note.

title: Capabilities: the Team page renders the same on the server and in the browser
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds capabilities for products built on the @crab-shack platform, each a package under packages/ with a daemon half and, where it has pages, a web half that is a Nuxt layer. Its development distribution (apps/ over a root product.yaml) runs every capability, and since bead 94z.3.10 can run with stand-ins for every outside service: pnpm build once, then pnpm dev:stand-ins (the README section "Run without outside accounts" has the details), which is the way to see the page below with content and no accounts. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: Jack (the owner and only developer) has authorised agents to commit and push to main in the capabilities repository; a push there is a release, so follow AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md in that repository (a change to a package's web layer needs a changeset).

The problem. The Team page of the team capability (packages/cap-team) logs a hydration mismatch in the browser console on every load under nuxt dev: what the server rendered and what the browser renders first are not the same. It was seen with and without the stand-in mode, so it is in the page, not in the stand-ins. A mismatch means the browser throws away and rebuilds part of the page, can flash wrong content, and hides any real mismatch warning that appears later.

What to do. Find what differs between the server's render and the browser's first render of that page and make them agree, without changing what the page shows once loaded. Check the other capabilities' pages for the same warning while the distribution is running and fix any that share the cause; list any with a different cause in the closing note rather than fixing them here.
acceptance_criteria:
- Loading the Team page in the development distribution's stand-in mode logs no hydration mismatch, shown from a headless browser's console for at least three loads.
- The closing note states the cause, and lists every capability page checked and what its console showed.
- Lint, typecheck, test and build are green, and the release that carries the fix is named.

title: Capabilities: the last fixed sleeps in the tests wait for their condition, and CI draws no deprecation warning
description:
Context: the capabilities repository (github.com/crab-shack/capabilities, checkout at /home/kingrea/work/crab-shack/capabilities) holds sixteen packages under packages/ and is released from every push to main, with its checks (lint, typecheck, test, build) running beside the publish on GitHub's runners. The bead tracker lives in Candy Mountain (/home/kingrea/work/candy-mountain-v3); run bd commands from there and change nothing else in it.

Commits: Jack (the owner and only developer) has authorised agents to commit and push to main in the capabilities repository when a piece of work is finished; a push there is a release, so follow AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md in that repository for how to land.

The problem. An earlier piece of work made the test suite hold on a slow or busy machine: tests that start a process got an allowance per start with its reason written down, and tests that slept and then asserted were changed to wait for the condition. The agent that did it found three more places with the same weakness that have not been seen failing yet, and left them:

- The watcher tests in the issues capability sleep for a fifth of a second so that the watcher can read its starting state before the test writes. If the write lands before that read, no change event is emitted and the test fails. A real fix needs the watcher to make known when its first read is done.
- The Codex connection's test that an attempt expires uses a short time-to-live in the same way the Claude Code one did before it was fixed, and its check of the stand-in tool's process id can pass without having checked anything.
- The CI workflow's actions are at versions that run on a Node release GitHub has deprecated, and each run carries an annotation saying so.

What to do. Remove each weakness the way the earlier work did: wait for the condition rather than for a fixed time, make a check that can pass vacuously actually check, and move the workflow's actions to versions that draw no deprecation annotation. Do not weaken what any test checks and do not remove a gate from the workflow.

Not in this bead: raising the per-start allowance for tests that start the Claude Code shim. It has about twice the headroom over the slowest time seen on a runner; leave it unless it is seen to fail.
acceptance_criteria:
- The watcher tests no longer depend on a fixed sleep for the watcher's first read; a forced full test run passes on a machine pinned to two busy cores.
- The Codex expiry test waits for the expiry rather than racing it, and its process check fails when the process is not what it expects (shown by breaking it once).
- A CI run on main for the landing commit is green and shows no deprecation annotation from the workflow's actions.
- Lint, typecheck, test and build are green.
